knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral and diameter propagation condition measures
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph with diameter \(D_G\), Laplacian \(L\), and eigenvalues \(0=\lambda_1(L)<\lambda_2(L)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(L)\). Let \(W\) be a symmetric doubly stochastic mixing matrix compatible with \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed connected undirected networks; conditioning is summarized by graph diameter, Laplacian spectral ratios, or mixing contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The graph diameter is \[D_G:=\max_{i,j\in V}\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j).\] The Laplacian spectral gap is \(\gamma_L:=\lambda_2(L)\), and the positive-spectrum condition number is \[\kappa_L:=\frac{\lambda_n(L)}{\lambda_2(L)}.\] For symmetric mixing, the disagreement factor and mixing condition scale are \[\rho_W:=\|W-J\|_2=\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i(W)|,\qquad \tau_W:=\frac1{1-\rho_W}\quad\text{when }\rho_W<1.\] These are network-propagation conditioning measures, not one interchangeable scalar definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Network propagation can be conditioned by several related quantities. Diameter measures the longest shortest path. The Laplacian gap measures algebraic connectivity, while the ratio of largest to smallest positive Laplacian eigenvalue is a spectral condition number. For symmetric averaging, the norm of W minus the averaging projector measures one-round disagreement contraction, and its inverse gap gives a mixing scale.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, undirected, and connected.
\(W=W^\top\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\mathbf1^\top W=\mathbf1^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_G\), \(\gamma_L\), \(\kappa_L\), \(\rho_W\), and \(\tau_W\) are defined by the displayed path-length and spectral formulas.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(D_G\) is the least integer \(D\) such that every vertex pair is joined by a path of at most \(D\) edges.
\(\gamma_L=\min_{x\perp\mathbf1,\,x\ne0}x^\top Lx/\|x\|_2^2\).
special_cases_latex: For the complete graph with unweighted Laplacian, \(D_G=1\) and \(\kappa_L=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Smaller \(\rho_W\) gives stronger one-round Euclidean disagreement contraction.
Disconnected graphs have \(\lambda_2(L)=0\), so \(\kappa_L\) is not finite under this definition.
boundary_notes: For nonsymmetric directed mixing, eigenvalue moduli alone need not determine transient contraction.
Diameter and spectral conditioning capture different propagation features and should not be conflated.
review_flags: The node groups several conditioning families; no inspected source identified a single canonical choice or supported all displayed measures together.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral and diameter propagation condition measures
Spectral-Gap Measures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute spectral gap is one minus the largest nonconsensus eigenvalue magnitude; it quantifies Euclidean contraction of disagreement by one symmetric mixing step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order the eigenvalues of \(W\) as \(1=\lambda_1(W)\geq\lambda_2(W)\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n(W)\geq-1\). Define \[\rho_\perp=\|W-J\|_2=\max\{|\lambda_2(W)|,|\lambda_n(W)|\},\qquad \gamma=1-\rho_\perp.\] For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\|(W-J)x\|_2\leq\rho_\perp\|(I-J)x\|_2\). Hence \(\gamma>0\) exactly when one mixing step is a strict Euclidean contraction on the disagreement subspace. If \(W\) is positive semidefinite, then \(\rho_\perp=\lambda_2(W)\) and \(\gamma=1-\lambda_2(W)\).
assumptions_latex: The matrix \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and doubly stochastic.
The eigenvalue \(1\) of \(W\) is simple.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The absolute spectral gap \(\gamma=1-\rho_\perp\) measures one-step contraction on the disagreement subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric doubly stochastic mixing; the absolute gap handles possible negative eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Network Condition Numbers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The network condition number is the ratio of the largest Laplacian eigenvalue to algebraic connectivity, measuring the spectral difficulty of reducing disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(G\) is connected, its Laplacian eigenvalues satisfy \(0=\lambda_1(L)<\lambda_2(L)\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n(L)=\lambda_{\max}(L)\). The Laplacian network condition number is \[\kappa_G=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(L)}{\lambda_2(L)}.\] Equivalently, \(\kappa_G\) is the spectral condition number of the restriction of \(L\) to \(\mathbf{1}^{\perp}\). It is invariant under uniform rescaling of all edge weights. For a mixing matrix of the form \(W=I-\eta L\), the admissible step size and resulting disagreement contraction depend on these two extreme nonzero eigenvalues.
assumptions_latex: The graph \(G\) is finite, connected, undirected, and has weighted Laplacian \(L\).
Edge weights are nonnegative and \(L\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The network condition number is \(\kappa_G=\lambda_{\max}(L)/\lambda_2(L)\), with larger values indicating worse propagation conditioning.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laplacian condition number for a connected undirected weighted graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Diameter–Mixing Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local communication has finite speed: diameter-separated agents cannot influence each other before D rounds, and their mixing distributions remain disjoint for fewer than half that many rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After \(t\) synchronous neighbor-communication rounds, the state at vertex \(i\) can depend only on initial data at vertices in \(\{j:d_G(i,j)\leq t\}\). Consequently, information from one endpoint of a diameter-realizing path cannot affect the other endpoint before \(D\) rounds. If \(P\) is any row-stochastic matrix supported on self-loops and edges of \(G\), and \(u,v\) satisfy \(d_G(u,v)=D\), then for \(2t<D\) the supports of \(e_u^{\mathsf T}P^t\) and \(e_v^{\mathsf T}P^t\) are disjoint. Their total-variation distance is therefore \(1\), precluding uniform pairwise mixing before \(\lceil D/2\rceil\) rounds.
assumptions_latex: Communication in one round crosses at most one edge of a fixed connected graph \(G\).
The graph diameter is \(D=\max_{i,j}d_G(i,j)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global influence requires at least \(D\) rounds, and pairwise distributional mixing requires at least \(\lceil D/2\rceil\) rounds in the worst case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-speed relation between graph diameter and local synchronous mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Poor-Connectivity Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connected path networks become increasingly ill-conditioned: their gap shrinks quadratically, and ordinary local mixing needs quadratically many rounds even for constant-factor disagreement reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the path family \((P_n)_{n\geq2}\), the nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues scale as \(\lambda_2(L)=\Theta(n^{-2})\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(L)=\Theta(1)\). Hence \(\kappa_G=\Theta(n^2)\). A symmetric lazy nearest-neighbor mixing matrix with uniformly comparable edge probabilities likewise has absolute spectral gap \(\gamma=\Theta(n^{-2})\). Its disagreement contraction factor is \(1-\Theta(n^{-2})\), so reducing Euclidean disagreement by a factor \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) requires \(\Theta(n^2\log(1/\varepsilon))\) rounds. Thus connectivity alone does not provide dimension-independent propagation or consensus rates.
assumptions_latex: The network is the path graph \(P_n\) with \(n\geq2\).
Mixing uses a symmetric lazy nearest-neighbor stochastic matrix with edge probabilities bounded above and below by positive constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For paths, \(\gamma=\Theta(n^{-2})\), \(\kappa_G=\Theta(n^2)\), and constant-factor disagreement reduction requires \(\Theta(n^2)\) rounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path graphs exhibit a canonical vanishing-gap, ill-conditioned connectivity regime.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The path-graph asymptotics are plausible, but the cited general mixing-matrix section is not confirmed to support the spectral asymptotics or the claimed round complexity. Moreover, the lower-bound wording must specify worst-case initial disagreement (or operator-norm contraction). A more specific theorem, example, or page locator is required before fixing the mathematical version.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint-Connectivity Windows
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every block of a fixed number of consecutive topologies must have a connected union, although individual graphs may be disconnected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The graph sequence \((G_t)_{t\geq0}\), with \(G_t=(V,E_t)\), is uniformly jointly connected with window \(B\) when, for every \(t\geq0\), the union graph \(G_{[t,t+B-1]}=\bigl(V,\bigcup_{s=t}^{t+B-1}E_s\bigr)\) is connected. For directed graphs, the corresponding uniform joint strong-connectivity condition requires every such union digraph to be strongly connected. Individual graphs \(G_t\) may be disconnected; the condition requires paths to be available collectively within every window of the same finite length \(B\).
assumptions_latex: \((G_t)_{t\geq0}\) is a sequence of graphs on a fixed finite vertex set \(V\).
\(B\geq1\) is an integer window length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(t\), the union graph \(\bigl(V,\bigcup_{s=t}^{t+B-1}E_s\bigr)\) is connected, or strongly connected in the directed version.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform sliding-window connectivity for undirected or strongly connected directed graph sequences.

notation.meaning: Union graph over the window starting at t
Edge or arc set active at time s

children.title: Neighbor Communication Model
children.top_down_role: Local information-exchange interfaces available to network agents.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At round \(k\), let \(G_k=(V,E_k)\) be a directed communication graph. Agent \(i\) has local state \(s_i^k\in\mathcal S_i\), emits messages in spaces \(\mathcal M_{ij}\), and has in-neighborhood \(N_i^-(k):=\{j:(j,i)\in E_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-based deterministic communication with arbitrary local state and edge-indexed message spaces; computation is local after reception.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A neighbor communication round consists of local encoders and update maps \[m_{ji}^k=E_{ji}^k(s_j^k)\in\mathcal M_{ji}\quad((j,i)\in E_k),\] \[s_i^{k+1}=U_i^k\!\left(s_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i^-(k)}\right).\] The locality condition is that \(E_{ji}^k\) depends only on sender \(j\)'s locally available information and \(U_i^k\) depends only on agent \(i\)'s prior local information and messages received along edges entering \(i\) at round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a neighbor communication model, the graph determines which directed messages may be delivered in each round. Every message is encoded from information locally available to its sender, and every new agent state is computed only from that agent's old state and the messages arriving from its current in-neighbors.
assumptions_latex: Agents are indexed by the fixed finite set \(V\).
An edge \((j,i)\in E_k\) authorizes a message from \(j\) to \(i\) during round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Messages and state transitions factor through the edge-local encoders \(E_{ji}^k\) and receiver-local update maps \(U_i^k\) shown above.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The global transition map has component \(i\) measurable only with respect to \(s_i^k\) and data received from \(N_i^-(k)\), once any protocol randomness is included in the local state.
special_cases_latex: Linear mixing has \(m_{ji}^k=s_j^k\) and \(s_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}^ks_j^k\).
Broadcast, pairwise gossip, and edge-specific message passing arise by restricting the encoders and active edges.
immediate_consequences_latex: Information from a nonneighbor cannot influence agent \(i\) in one round unless it was previously relayed through local states.
boundary_notes: This definition does not impose bandwidth, delay, loss, privacy, or quantization constraints.
Asynchronous execution requires an event- or delay-indexed interface rather than this synchronous round model.

children.title: Neighborhood Broadcast Communication
children.top_down_role: A common message delivered to available neighbors.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Broadcast Communication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agent forms one message and sends that identical payload to all currently available neighbors; receivers may still process received messages differently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A neighborhood broadcast by agent \(i\) at round \(k\) consists of forming one payload \(m_i^k=\phi_i(x_i^k)\) and delivering that identical payload to every \(j\in N_i^{\mathrm{out}}(k)\). The encoder \(\phi_i\) cannot tailor the payload to the recipient within the same broadcast action. After reception, each agent \(j\) may apply a recipient-specific update \(x_j^{k+1}=\psi_j^k(x_j^k,(m_i^k)_{i\in N_j^{\mathrm{in}}(k)})\). Thus broadcast restricts message formation, not how receivers aggregate the messages they obtain.
assumptions_latex: At round \(k\), agent \(i\) has state \(x_i^k\) and available out-neighbors \(N_i^{\mathrm{out}}(k)\).
A transmitted message is delivered reliably to every currently available out-neighbor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One broadcast action sends the same message \(m_i^k\) to every agent in \(N_i^{\mathrm{out}}(k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous reliable local broadcast with identical payloads for all available recipients.

notation.meaning: message formed by agent i at round k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous one-to-many communication in which a sender cannot tailor payloads to individual recipients during the same broadcast.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A neighborhood broadcast protocol uses, for each sender \(j\) and round \(k\), one encoder \[m_j^k=B_j^k(s_j^k)\in\mathcal M_j\] and delivers the identical payload \(m_j^k\) to every receiver \(i\in N_j^+(k)\). Each receiver updates by \[s_i^{k+1}=U_i^k\!\left(s_i^k,(m_j^k)_{j\in N_i^-(k)}\right).\] The defining broadcast constraint is \(m_{ji}^k=m_j^k\) for all \(i\in N_j^+(k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neighborhood broadcast is a one-to-many interface: during one round, each sender forms one message from its local state, and exactly that same message is made available to all of its active out-neighbors. Receivers may still process received messages differently through their own local update maps.
assumptions_latex: The graph specifies the active recipients of each sender at each round.
A broadcast payload has a common message space \(\mathcal M_j\) for all recipients of sender \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every sender \(j\), round \(k\), and recipients \(i,i'\in N_j^+(k)\), \(m_{ji}^k=m_{ji'}^k=B_j^k(s_j^k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The family of edge encoders leaving \(j\) factors through one common encoder: \(E_{ji}^k=B_j^k\) on every active outgoing edge.
special_cases_latex: Broadcasting the current iterate uses \(B_j^k(s_j^k)=x_j^k\).
A wireless broadcast may realize the common-message constraint physically, while a wired system may emulate it by repeated identical transmissions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The sender-side payload cannot contain recipient-specific information unless that information is encoded in a common message delivered to all recipients.
boundary_notes: Different delivery times, erasures, or receiver noise require additional channel variables.
Sending separately tailored messages on distinct outgoing edges is edge-local message passing, not broadcast under this definition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Center-originated flooding with stale-message suppression, recovery exchange, and a transmission-count bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After each change of the center value V, the center sends the new value with an incremented sequence number to all its neighbors. A processor accepts and forwards a received value to neighbors other than its sender only if its sequence number exceeds the locally stored number; otherwise it discards the message. When a failed link becomes operational, its endpoints exchange their stored values and sequence numbers. If |A| is the number of bidirectional network links, the scheme uses fewer than 2|A| messages per new value and does not require links to preserve transmission order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The center floods each new value with a larger sequence number. Nodes forward only messages newer than their stored version, and endpoints exchange stored versions when a link recovers. An update uses fewer than twice the number of bidirectional links in messages, and FIFO delivery is unnecessary.

|A|\text{ is the number of bidirectional network links}
\text{Endpoints exchange stored values and sequence numbers when a failed link recovers}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{messages per new value of }V<2|A|,\qquad\text{order-preserving link delivery is unnecessary}.

children.title: Pairwise Gossip Communication
children.top_down_role: Selected pairs exchange and combine information.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Gossip Communication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, one selected neighboring pair replaces both values by their average while all other agents remain unchanged; adequate repeated edge activation yields average consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize arbitrary states \(x_1^0,\ldots,x_n^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At round \(k\), select an edge \(\{i_k,j_k\}\) according to a specified schedule or probability distribution and perform \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{j_k}^{k+1}=\frac{x_{i_k}^k+x_{j_k}^k}{2},\qquad x_\ell^{k+1}=x_\ell^k\ \text{for }\ell\notin\{i_k,j_k\}.\] Stop under a prescribed round budget or disagreement tolerance and output the current local states. Every update preserves \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k\); convergence to the initial average additionally requires a selection rule that activates sufficient edges repeatedly.
assumptions_latex: At round \(k\), an edge \(\{i_k,j_k\}\) is selected from an undirected graph.
Only the selected endpoints communicate during that round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected pair replaces its values by their average, preserving the global sum and contracting their local disagreement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical randomized or scheduled pairwise averaging update on an undirected graph.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). At round \(k\), an edge \(e_k=\{i_k,j_k\}\in E\) is selected, and agents hold states \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pairwise averaging gossip step with parameter \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\) is \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)x_{i_k}^k+\alpha_kx_{j_k}^k,\qquad x_{j_k}^{k+1}=\alpha_kx_{i_k}^k+(1-\alpha_k)x_{j_k}^k,\] with \(x_\ell^{k+1}=x_\ell^k\) for \(\ell\notin\{i_k,j_k\}\). In stacked form, \[X^{k+1}=(W_{e_k}(\alpha_k)\otimes I_d)X^k,\quad W_{\{i,j\}}(\alpha)=I_n-\alpha(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^\top.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pairwise gossip round selects one communication edge. Its two endpoints exchange their states and replace them by symmetric convex combinations, while every other agent remains unchanged. The corresponding matrix is identity except on the selected two-agent block.
assumptions_latex: The selected pair \(\{i_k,j_k\}\) is an edge of the communication graph.
\(0\le\alpha_k\le1\), and both endpoints use the same parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only the selected endpoint states change, according to the displayed symmetric averaging equations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The selected two-state sum is invariant: \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}+x_{j_k}^{k+1}=x_{i_k}^k+x_{j_k}^k\).
\(W_e(\alpha)\) is doubly stochastic for \(\alpha\in[0,1]\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\alpha_k=1/2\), both endpoints adopt their arithmetic mean.
For \(\alpha_k=0\), the selected communication produces no state change.
immediate_consequences_latex: The global arithmetic average is preserved at every pairwise step.
Randomized gossip is obtained by sampling \(e_k\) from a specified distribution on \(E\).

Convergence requires persistent edge activation or suitable probabilistic assumptions, which are not part of the communication primitive.

children.title: Edge-Local Message Passing
children.top_down_role: Distinct messages associated with edges or coupling constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Local Message Passing
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each active edge may carry its own recipient-specific message, allowing agents to communicate edge variables, coupling information, or distinct residuals to different neighbors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In an edge-local message-passing round, each active directed edge \((i,j)\in E_k\) carries a payload \(m_{i\to j}^k=\phi_{ij}^k(x_i^k,z_{ij}^k)\), where \(z_{ij}^k\) is optional edge-local state. Payloads associated with two different outgoing edges may differ even when they have the same sender. Agent \(j\) updates according to \(x_j^{k+1}=\psi_j^k(x_j^k,(m_{i\to j}^k)_{i:(i,j)\in E_k})\). This model represents edge-specific coupling data, dual variables, or residuals and strictly contains identical-payload neighborhood broadcast as a special case.
assumptions_latex: Each directed edge \((i,j)\) active at round \(k\) can carry one edge-indexed payload.
Agent updates use only their local state and payloads received on incident active edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Edge-local communication permits distinct payloads \(m_{i\to j}^k\) for different neighbors \(j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous edge-indexed messages with recipient-dependent payloads.

notation.meaning: message sent from i to j at round k

children.title: Stateful Neighbor Communication

knowledge_statements.title: Stateful Neighbor Communication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents retain auxiliary state between rounds and use it when forming messages and updates; trackers, cached estimates, and error-feedback residuals are instances of this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stateful neighbor-communication mechanism has the local state-space form \[m_{i\to j}^k=H_{ij}^k(x_i^k,z_i^k),\qquad (x_i^{k+1},z_i^{k+1})=F_i^k\left(x_i^k,z_i^k,(m_{j\to i}^k)_{j\in N_i^{\mathrm{in}}(k)}\right).\] The auxiliary variable \(z_i^k\) persists between rounds and is initialized by a specified value \(z_i^0\). Memoryless communication is recovered when \(z_i^k\) is absent or constant. Gradient trackers, compression residuals, and cached neighbor estimates fit this representation by choosing the state space and maps \(H_{ij}^k\) and \(F_i^k\) appropriately.
assumptions_latex: Each agent \(i\) stores a persistent local memory \(z_i^k\) in addition to its primary state \(x_i^k\).
Messages are exchanged only along edges active at round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stateful communication updates both the primary state and persistent memory from current local information and received neighbor messages.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic state-space representation encompassing trackers, memories, residual accumulators, and error-feedback states.

notation.meaning: message sent from i to j

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G_k=(V,E_k)\) be a communication graph at round \(k\), with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Agent \(i\) has local state \(s_i^k\in\mathcal S_i\), receives messages from \(N_i^-(k)=\{j:(j,i)\in E_k\}\), and may use local data \(d_i^k\in\mathcal D_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time, synchronous, deterministic stateful communication; randomized and asynchronous variants require an explicit probability space or event schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stateful neighbor-communication process consists of message maps \(M_{ij}^k:\mathcal S_i\times\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal M_{ij}\) and transition maps \(T_i^k:\mathcal S_i\times\mathcal D_i\times\prod_{j\in N_i^-(k)}\mathcal M_{ji}\to\mathcal S_i\) such that, for every \(k\ge0\), \(m_{ij}^k=M_{ij}^k(s_i^k,d_i^k)\) is sent only when \((i,j)\in E_k\), and \(s_i^{k+1}=T_i^k(s_i^k,d_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i^-(k)})\). It is stateful when some admissible future output or transition depends on \(s_i^k\) beyond the current input and received-message tuple.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, every agent forms edge-local messages from its retained state and current data, receives messages only from in-neighbors, and updates its retained state through a local transition map. The model is stateful precisely when retained information can affect a later message or transition beyond what current inputs and current received messages determine.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordination architecture of a distributed optimization system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index computing agents, let \(C\) be a possibly empty set of coordinator processes, and let \(P=V\cup C\). At round \(k\), process \(p\in P\) has state \(s_p^k\in\mathcal S_p\), receives messages along a directed graph \(G^k=(P,E^k)\), and applies a state-transition map.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The object defined is the information-flow and authority structure of an iterative optimization system, independently of the particular objective, update formula, synchronization convention, or convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordination architecture is a tuple \[\mathfrak A=(P,V,C,(G^k)_{k\ge0},(\mathcal M_{pq})_{p,q\in P},(U_p^k)_{p\in P,k\ge0}),\] where a message \(m_{pq}^k\in\mathcal M_{pq}\) may be sent only if \((p,q)\in E^k\), and every process evolves according to \[s_p^{k+1}=U_p^k\!\left(s_p^k,\{m_{qp}^k:(q,p)\in E^k\}\right).\] Its architectural class is determined by which processes may aggregate information and issue coordination variables: centralized when one distinguished \(c\in C\) mediates all inter-agent coordination, peer-to-peer when \(C=\varnothing\), hierarchical when coordinator processes form multiple tiers, and federated when a coordinator exists but each agent's raw local dataset is excluded from the permitted message spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordination architecture specifies the processes, time-indexed communication edges, permitted message spaces, and local state-transition maps of a distributed optimization system. Centralized, peer-to-peer, hierarchical, and federated architectures are distinguished by the presence and organization of coordinators and by the information that messages are allowed to disclose.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak A\) is classified by \(C\), the coordinator subgraph, and the admissible message spaces \((\mathcal M_{pq})\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For synchronous deterministic systems, all maps \(U_p^k\) may be combined into one global transition \(s^{k+1}=U^k(s^k)\) whose block-sparsity is prescribed by \(G^k\).
special_cases_latex: A star graph with one center in \(C\) gives centralized aggregation.
Taking \(C=\varnothing\) and allowing only neighbor messages gives a peer-to-peer architecture.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two algorithms with identical numerical updates can have different coordination architectures if their allowed information paths differ.
The architecture alone does not determine communication complexity because message sizes and activation schedules remain separate data.
boundary_notes: A logical coordinator may be implemented by several machines; the definition concerns roles and information flow rather than physical hardware.
Privacy, security, and fault tolerance are not implied merely by restricting message spaces.

notation.meaning: State-transition map of process \(p\) at round \(k\).

children.title: Centralized Aggregation Architectures
children.top_down_role: Optimization organized around a distinguished aggregation service.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,ldots,m\}\) be worker agents and let \(c\notin V\) be a distinguished aggregation process. Worker \(i\) has state \(x_i^k\), produces an uplink message \(u_i^k\), and receives a downlink message \(d_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a logical star-coordination model. It permits parallel local computation but requires all cross-worker coordination to pass through a distinguished service.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed iterative system has a centralized aggregation architecture if, for every round \(k\), there are maps \(P_i^k\), \(A^k\), and \(Q_i^k\) such that \[u_i^k=P_i^k(x_i^k),\qquad a^k=A^k(u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k),\qquad d_i^k=Q_i^k(a^k),\] and each worker updates by \[x_i^{k+1}=U_i^k(x_i^k,d_i^k),\] with no worker-to-worker message entering any \(U_i^k\) directly. Equivalently, after deleting self-loops, every directed communication path from one worker to another contains \(c\). The aggregate \(a^k\) may be a sum, average, model parameter, dual variable, or other sufficient coordination object.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a centralized aggregation architecture, each worker sends a locally produced message to one distinguished service. That service combines the worker messages and returns coordination information used in the next local updates. No direct worker message participates in another worker's update; every cross-worker information path passes through the aggregator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall i\ne j)\), every information path from worker \(i\) to worker \(j\) passes through \(c\), and the round transition factors through \(A^k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The communication graph is a directed subgraph of the bidirected star on \(V\cup\{c\}\), possibly with self-loops.
The global worker transition factors as \(x^{k+1}=U^k(x^k,Q^k(A^k(P^k(x^k))))\) with block-separable \(P^k,Q^k,U^k\).
special_cases_latex: Parameter-server averaging uses \(a^k=\sum_i w_i u_i^k\) with \(w_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_iw_i=1\).
A master process that allocates a shared resource via a dual price is a centralized aggregation architecture.
immediate_consequences_latex: The aggregator is an articulation point of the logical inter-worker information graph.
Centralization of coordination does not require centralization of local objective evaluation.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require workers to participate synchronously.
Replication of the aggregation service for availability is compatible only when replicas collectively implement the same distinguished logical role.

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Coordinator Architectures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers compute local messages from the shared state, while a persistent coordinator aggregates every contribution and broadcasts the next state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A central-coordinator architecture consists of workers \(1,\ldots,m\), a coordinator state \(x^k\), worker message maps \(M_i^k\), and a coordinator aggregation map \(A^k\). At round \(k\),
\[u_i^k=M_i^k(x^k;\mathcal D_i),\qquad x^{k+1}=A^k(x^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k),\]
after which the coordinator broadcasts \(x^{k+1}\) or designated blocks to the workers. Workers need not communicate directly; every contribution to the shared iterate passes logically through the persistent coordinator.
assumptions_latex: Worker \(i\) has local information \(\mathcal D_i\).
The coordinator is the unique logical aggregation point for the shared iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=A^k(x^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k)\) characterizes centralized aggregation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-based distributed architecture in which one persistent coordinator aggregates all worker messages and broadcasts the next shared state.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Server Architectures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Servers own parameter blocks; workers pull parameter versions, compute local-data updates, and push them for barrier-synchronized batch application or asynchronous application that may accept stale reads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A parameter-server architecture maintains server-resident parameter blocks \(x_{(1)},\ldots,x_{(q)}\). Worker \(i\) pulls a version \(x^{\tau_i(k)}\), computes \(u_i^k=U_i(x^{\tau_i(k)};\mathcal D_i)\), and pushes the update to the responsible server blocks. A server may apply one received update as
\[x^{k+1}=S^k(x^k,u_i^k)\]
or aggregate a batch of concurrently received updates. Execution is synchronous when workers use the designated round-\(k\) version and update application is separated by a round barrier; it is stale-read asynchronous when updates computed from \(\tau_i(k)<k\) may be accepted without such a global barrier.
assumptions_latex: Every parameter block has a designated server owner.
Worker \(i\) computes from local data \(\mathcal D_i\) and a pulled parameter version.
Synchronous execution uses a round barrier in addition to current-version reads.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^{\tau_i(k)},u_i^k,S^k)\), together with the update-application schedule, specifies the pull-compute-push parameter-server cycle.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Server–worker architecture whose central service stores parameter blocks and applies worker-generated updates.

notation.meaning: version timestamp read by worker i

knowledge_statements.title: Worker–Aggregator Topologies
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bipartite graph specifies worker-to-aggregator communication; one aggregator gives a star, while multiple aggregators require reconciliation of their outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W\) be a set of workers and \(A\) a set of aggregators. A worker–aggregator topology is the bipartite graph \(G=(W\cup A,E)\), where \((i,a)\in E\) exactly when worker \(i\) may send a local message to aggregator \(a\). For messages \(u_i^k\), aggregator \(a\) computes
\[v_a^k=\mathcal A_a^k\bigl((u_i^k)_{i\in N(a)}\bigr).\]
A single-star topology has \(|A|=1\) and \(N(a)=W\); multiple aggregators partition or overlap worker neighborhoods and require an additional rule to reconcile \((v_a^k)_{a\in A}\).
assumptions_latex: Messages travel only along edges in \(E\).
Every participating worker has at least one adjacent aggregator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=(W\cup A,E)\) determines the admissible aggregation neighborhoods \(N(a)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Service Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because every worker message crosses one service, fixed service bandwidth and processing capacity force synchronous round time to grow at least linearly with workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(m\) workers each send and receive \(s\) bits through one central service during every synchronous round. The service must process at least \(2ms\) incident bits per round. If its aggregate ingress-plus-egress rate is at most \(B\) bits per unit time and it processes at most \(P\) worker messages per unit time, then the round duration satisfies
\[T_{\mathrm{round}}\ge\max\left\{\frac{2ms}{B},\frac{2m}{P}\right\}.\]
Consequently, with fixed \(B\), \(P\), and \(s\), central-service communication time grows at least linearly with the worker count.
assumptions_latex: Every synchronous round requires one upload and one download of \(s>0\) bits per worker.
The central service has total traffic rate \(B>0\) and message-processing rate \(P>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{round}}\ge\max\{2ms/B,2m/P\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-round communication and service-time lower bounds caused by routing all worker traffic through one central service.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the bottleneck leaf and the counting argument is plausible under the stated capacity model, but the cited architecture sections do not establish the exact max lower bound or clarify that P counts both uploads and downloads. A direct locator supporting this capacity model is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Peer-to-Peer Decentralized Architectures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each peer stores and updates a local state using local information and neighbor messages, while no distinguished permanent service exclusively performs global aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a communication graph and let iterations be indexed by \(k\in\mathbb{N}\). A peer-to-peer decentralized architecture assigns a state \(x_i^k\) and local information \(\mathcal D_i\) to each node \(i\in V\), with updates of the form
\[x_i^{k+1}=U_i^k\bigl(x_i^k,(x_j^{\tau_{ij}(k)})_{j\in N_i};\mathcal D_i\bigr),\qquad 0\le\tau_{ij}(k)\le k.\]
Nodes exchange states only along edges of \(G\), and no distinguished permanent service has exclusive responsibility for aggregating all contributions or determining a global iterate. In linear mixing,
\[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j\in V}w_{ij}x_j^k,\qquad w_{ij}=0\quad\text{whenever }j\notin N_i\cup\{i\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) specifies admissible peer-to-peer communication.
\(k\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(0\le\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\) for every received neighbor state.
Each update uses only the node's local information and received neighbor states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The architecture has no distinguished permanent aggregation service, and communication is local to \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighbor-exchange architecture with local states and no permanent node responsible for global aggregation.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be agents and let \(G^k=(V,E^k)\) be the directed communication graph at round \(k\). Agent \(i\) holds state \(x_i^k\in\mathcal X_i\) and local information \(\xi_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns absence of a permanent coordinating process and neighbor-local information dependence; it allows synchronous or asynchronous and static or time-varying communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed iterative system has a peer-to-peer decentralized architecture if its process set is exactly \(V\), no process has a distinguished global aggregation role, and for every \(i\) and \(k\), \[x_i^{k+1}=U_i^k\!\left(x_i^k,\xi_i,\{m_{ji}^k:j\in N_i^{-,k}\}\right),\qquad N_i^{-,k}=\{j:(j,i)\in E^k\},\] where every message \(m_{ji}^k\) is generated from information locally available at \(j\). Global dependence may arise only by composing such neighbor exchanges over multiple rounds. No single vertex is required to lie on every information path between all distinct agent pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A peer-to-peer decentralized architecture contains only agents, without a permanent global coordinator. Each agent updates from its own state and information received from current in-neighbors. Information about distant agents can influence an update only after being relayed through a sequence of neighbor exchanges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^{k+1}\) is measurable with respect to agent \(i\)'s local information and messages from \(N_i^{-,k}\), for every \(i,k\), with no distinguished coordinator process.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In a deterministic synchronous system, the global update map \(U^k\) is graph-local: its \(i\)-th block depends only on blocks indexed by \(\{i\}\cup N_i^{-,k}\).
special_cases_latex: Consensus iterations \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j\in N_i^{-,k}\cup\{i\}}w_{ij}^kx_j^k\) are peer-to-peer.
Gossip schemes are peer-to-peer when the activated node or edge is selected without becoming a permanent coordinator.
immediate_consequences_latex: A change at agent \(j\) cannot affect agent \(i\) before a time-respecting path carries information from \(j\) to \(i\).
Decentralization does not imply that all agents have equal computational or communication capabilities.
boundary_notes: Temporary leaders or token holders are allowed if no permanent process mediates every round.
A star-shaped peer graph is not automatically centralized unless its center has the distinguished aggregation role required by the algorithm.

children.title: Multi-Tier Coordination Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Coordination across clusters, edge tiers, or regional aggregators.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite set of processes partitioned into nonempty tiers \(P_0,\ldots,P_L\), where \(P_0\) contains leaf agents and \(L\ge2\). Let \(\pi:P_0\cup\cdots\cup P_{L-1}\to P_1\cup\cdots\cup P_L\) assign each nonroot process a parent in the next tier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition models logical aggregation and dissemination across at least two coordinator levels; tiers may represent clusters, edge servers, regions, or organizational domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordination architecture is an \(L\)-tier hierarchy if \(L\ge2\), \(\pi(P_\ell)\subseteq P_{\ell+1}\), repeated application of \(\pi\) reaches a root in \(P_L\), and inter-tier messages follow parent-child edges. For each coordinator \(q\in P_{\ell+1}\), its upward summary has the form \[u_q^k=A_q^k\!\left(s_q^k,\{u_p^k:\pi(p)=q\}\right),\] while downward coordination is recursively disseminated by \[d_p^k=D_p^k(s_p^k,d_{\pi(p)}^k,u_{\pi(p)}^k).\] Thus information from distinct leaves is first combined at their least common ancestral coordinator before reaching higher tiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-tier hierarchy partitions processes into leaf and coordinator levels connected by a parent map. Local summaries move upward and are aggregated at each successive level, while coordination information moves downward through the same hierarchy. There must be at least two coordinator levels, distinguishing this family from a single centralized aggregator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi(P_\ell)\subseteq P_{\ell+1}\) and every leaf-to-root coordination path traverses the successive tiers \(P_1,\ldots,P_L\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The parent edges form a rooted forest whose leaves contain \(P_0\), whose roots lie in \(P_L\), and whose internal vertices occupy the intermediate tiers.
special_cases_latex: Clients, edge servers, and a cloud service form a two-coordinator-tier hierarchy with \(L=2\).
Regional aggregators followed by a national aggregator constitute a hierarchy when regional summaries, rather than all raw leaf messages, enter the top-tier update.
immediate_consequences_latex: A coordinator can aggregate a subtree without exposing each descendant's individual message to higher tiers.
Communication and aggregation delays can differ by tier without changing the architecture's defining parent relation.
boundary_notes: A flat star with only one coordinator tier is excluded by \(L\ge2\).
Cross-tier or peer links may supplement the hierarchy, but if they replace the parent-mediated coordination structure the system falls outside this definition.

notation.meaning: Parent map from each nonroot process to the next coordination tier.

review_flags: No inspected source supports this exact tiered aggregation formalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-tier coordination hierarchy
Clustered Coordination Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents are partitioned into clusters; cluster coordinators aggregate locally and communicate through a top-level coordinator to solve a shared optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A clustered coordination hierarchy is a communication architecture \(\mathcal H=(V,\{c_k\}_{k=1}^K,c_0)\) in which every agent \(i\in V_k\) exchanges optimization messages only within \(V_k\) or with its cluster coordinator \(c_k\), while each \(c_k\) exchanges aggregate messages with the top-level coordinator \(c_0\). Intercluster information used by an agent in \(V_k\) must therefore traverse a path through \(c_k\), \(c_0\), and the destination cluster coordinator. The associated global problem is \(\min_x\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in V_k}f_i(x)\), with local computations performed at agents and aggregation performed at the two coordinator tiers.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite set of agents partitioned as \(V=V_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}V_K\).
Each agent stores a local objective \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal H=(V,\{c_k\}_{k=1}^K,c_0)\) is a clustered coordination hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite, two-level coordinator model with cluster-mediated inter-agent communication.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the cited general architecture section does not inspectably support the specific two-level message restrictions, mandatory routing through c_k and c_0, or the stated optimization decomposition. A hierarchy-specific source with a section or page locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Edge–Cloud Coordination
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cloud broadcasts a model, selected edge devices compute local messages, and the cloud aggregates them without directly accessing local objectives or data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Edge-cloud coordination for \(\min_x\sum_{i\in E}F_i(x)\) is represented roundwise by a cloud broadcast \(x^t\), local edge computations \(m_i^t=\Phi_i(x^t;F_i,\xi_i^t)\) for participating devices \(i\in S_t\), and a cloud update \(x^{t+1}=\Psi_t(x^t,\{m_i^t:i\in S_t\})\). The maps \(\Phi_i\) may encode gradients, proximal points, or model increments. The defining architectural boundary is that the cloud accesses each local objective \(F_i\) only through \(m_i^t\); objective data and local state need not be transferred to the cloud.

A cloud coordinator can broadcast model states and receive finite-dimensional device messages.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Aggregator Architectures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each region aggregates its agents' messages locally; regional aggregators then coordinate over a separate network and return region-specific feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regional aggregator architecture for \(\min_x\sum_{r=1}^R\sum_{i\in V_r}f_i(x)\) assigns each region \(V_r\) an aggregator \(a_r\). At iteration \(t\), agents in \(V_r\) send local messages \(m_i^t\) to \(a_r\), which forms \(z_r^t=A_r^t(\{m_i^t:i\in V_r\})\). The aggregators then exchange messages only along edges of \(G_A\) and compute \((y_1^t,\ldots,y_R^t)=B^t(z_1^t,\ldots,z_R^t;G_A)\). Regional feedback to agent \(i\in V_r\) depends on \(y_r^t\), so all interregional influence is mediated by regional aggregators.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is partitioned into nonempty regions \(V_1,\ldots,V_R\).
Each region has an aggregator \(a_r\), and aggregators communicate over a graph \(G_A\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Tier Information Flow
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hierarchical information flow is cross-tier when every upward aggregate and downward feedback message factors through adjacent tiers, with no nonadjacent bypass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cross-tier information flow is admissible when optimization information moves only through adjacent-tier maps. For upward messages, \(s_{l+1}^t=U_l^t(s_l^t)\) for \(l=0,\ldots,L-1\); for downward messages, \(q_l^t=D_l^t(q_{l+1}^t,s_l^t)\). Thus the upward dependence factors through \(U_{L-1}^t\circ\cdots\circ U_0^t\), and downward feedback factors through \(D_0^t\circ\cdots\circ D_{L-1}^t\). No state at tier \(l\) may directly influence a nonadjacent tier except through these compositions. This condition distinguishes genuine hierarchical flow from a nominal hierarchy containing bypass communication links.
assumptions_latex: The coordination system has tiers \(0,1,\ldots,L\), with tier \(0\) lowest.
Messages passed between adjacent tiers belong to specified finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid cross-tier flow factors as \(U=U_{L-1}\circ\cdots\circ U_0\) upward and \(D=D_0\circ\cdots\circ D_{L-1}\) downward.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adjacent-tier factorization condition for hierarchical optimization messages.

notation.meaning: Upward aggregation from tier l to tier l+1

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Agents \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) seek to minimize \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n q_i f_i(x)\) over \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), where \(q_i>0\) and \(\sum_iq_i=1\). Agent \(i\) stores a primal copy \(x_i^k\) and communicates over \(G_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-space methods using local first-order oracles and neighbor communication; auxiliary local states are permitted, but explicit dual optimization variables are not the defining decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decentralized primal first-order method is a collection of local recursions \((x_i^{k+1},z_i^{k+1})=\Phi_i^k(x_i^k,z_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i^-(k)},g_i^k)\), where \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(\xi_i^k)\) for a locally available query point \(\xi_i^k\), every message \(m_{ij}^k\) is computed from agent \(i\)'s local history, and no update uses another agent's objective or state except through received neighbor messages. Its primal output is the block vector \(X^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_n^k)\); solving the decentralized problem means driving \(X^k\) toward the consensual solution set \(\{\mathbf1\otimes x:x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X}F(u)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family comprises neighbor-local algorithms whose decision outputs are agent-held primal copies, whose objective information comes from local first-order oracles, and whose nonlocal information arrives only through graph edges. Auxiliary trackers or memories may be used. The target is consensus of all primal copies at a minimizer of the aggregate objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{target}(X^k)=\{\mathbf1\otimes x:x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X}\sum_{i=1}^nq_if_i(u)\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: In stacked form, \((X^{k+1},Z^{k+1})=\Phi^k(X^k,Z^k,G^k)\), with the \(i\)-th component measurable with respect to agent \(i\)'s local history and received neighbor messages.
special_cases_latex: Consensus descent, diffusion, gradient tracking, exact decentralized correction, and projected primal methods fit the family when their communicated variables are locally maintained.
immediate_consequences_latex: A centralized update depending directly on all \(f_i\) or all \(x_i^k\) is outside this family unless that information has been obtained through the allowed communication process.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert convergence or prescribe a mixing matrix.
Primal-dual saddle methods may produce primal iterates but are not classified here when dual variables define the core recursion.

children.top_down_role: Consensus mechanisms used alone or inside optimization methods.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\) agents hold inputs \(a_i\in\mathbb R^d\). Their states \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) evolve using messages exchanged along a graph sequence \((G_k)_{k\ge0}\). Define \(\bar a=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^na_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact arithmetic and uniform arithmetic averaging; weighted averaging replaces the uniform target by a specified positive weight vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed averaging method is a neighbor-local state evolution initialized from \(x_i^0=a_i\) whose designated outputs satisfy \(\lim_{k\to\infty}x_i^k=\bar a\) for every agent \(i\) and every admissible input tuple \((a_1,\ldots,a_n)\). Finite-time averaging is the stronger property that, for every admissible input tuple, some finite \(K\) satisfies \(x_i^k=\bar a\) for all \(i\) and all \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent begins with a local vector and uses only neighbor communication. The process performs distributed averaging if every designated local output converges to the arithmetic mean of all initial vectors for every admissible input. Finite-time averaging requires exact agreement with that mean after a finite round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^0=a_i\ (1\le i\le n),\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty}x_i^k=\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^na_j\ (1\le i\le n).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(X^k=(x_1^k;\ldots;x_n^k)\) and \(J=n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), distributed averaging is \(X^k\to(J\otimes I_d)X^0\).
It is equivalently the conjunction of consensus, \(\|(I-J)\otimes I_d\,X^k\|\to0\), and correctness, \((J\otimes I_d)X^k\to(J\otimes I_d)X^0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(d=1\), the process computes the scalar arithmetic mean.
Weighted averaging targets \(\sum_iq_ia_i\) and is distinct unless \(q_i=1/n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If the iteration preserves \(\sum_i x_i^k\), then consensus at any limit implies that the common limit equals \(\bar a\).
boundary_notes: Agreement at an input-dependent value without mean correctness is consensus but not distributed averaging.
The definition alone supplies no rate or connectivity condition.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the consensus subspace in agent coordinates

children.title: Linear Consensus Methods
children.top_down_role: Deterministic averaging over fixed or switching networks.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Matrix Consensus Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixing residual vanishes exactly at consensus, and the spectral gap bounds distance to consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\ge0\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\). If \(\lambda_2(W)\) is the largest eigenvalue below one, then \[(I-W)X=0\iff X=JX,\qquad \|(I-J)X\|_F\le\frac{\|(I-W)X\|_F}{1-\lambda_2(W)}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\ge0\) and \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
\(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_F(X,\operatorname{range}J)\le \|(I-W)X\|_F/(1-\lambda_2(W))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus certificate for fixed symmetric nonnegative mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Need Not Preserve the Arithmetic Average
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primitive row-stochastic mixing reaches Perron-weighted consensus and preserves the arithmetic average only when it is doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W\ge0\) is primitive and row stochastic, there is a unique \(\pi>0\) with \(\pi^{\mathsf T}W=\pi^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\pi^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=1\), and \[W^k\to\mathbf1\pi^{\mathsf T},\qquad X^k\to\mathbf1\pi^{\mathsf T}X^0.\] This equals arithmetic-average consensus for every \(X^0\) if and only if \(\pi=\mathbf1/n\), equivalently \(W\) is also column stochastic.
assumptions_latex: \(W\ge0\) is primitive.
\(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}W^kX^0=\mathbf1\pi^{\mathsf T}X^0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit selected by primitive unbalanced deterministic mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Characterization and Linear Rate of Fixed Consensus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric average-preserving mixing reaches average consensus exactly when every nonconsensus eigenvalue lies inside the unit disk; the largest modulus is the linear factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and let \(1=\lambda_1>\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n>-1\). For \(X^{k+1}=WX^k\), \[(I-J)X^k=(W-J)^k(I-J)X^0,\qquad \|(I-J)X^k\|_2\le\rho^k\|(I-J)X^0\|_2,\] where \(\rho=\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i|<1\). Conversely, convergence to \(JX^0\) for every initial state requires all nonconsensus eigenvalues to have modulus below one.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) and \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
Eigenvalue one is simple and \(\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i(W)|<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed symmetric deterministic mixing; gossip and polynomial acceleration are excluded.

notation.meaning: Largest modulus of a nonconsensus eigenvalue.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Consensus Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents repeatedly replace their states by weighted neighbor averages. Doubly stochastic weights preserve the initial average, and contracting matrix products drive all agents to that average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given initial states \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\), stack them as rows of \(X^0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\). At each round choose the prescribed graph-compatible mixing matrix \(W_k\) and update \[X^{k+1}=W_kX^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n (W_k)_{ij}x_j^k.\] Stop after a fixed budget or when \(\|(I-J)X^k\|\) is below a stated tolerance, and output each row. Row stochasticity preserves consensus states; column stochasticity preserves \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}X^k\). If \(\|W_{k-1:0}-J\|\to0\), then \(X^k\to JX^0\), whose rows equal \(n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^0\).
assumptions_latex: Each \(W_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is compatible with the communication graph and satisfies \(W_k\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\).
For average preservation, also \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}W_k=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\).
The matrix products contract the disagreement subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration \(X^{k+1}=W_kX^k\) converges to the rowwise initial average under doubly stochastic mixing and disagreement contraction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous deterministic linear consensus with fixed or switching doubly stochastic weights.

notation.meaning: matrix whose rows are agent states

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(n\) agents with states \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\), let \(W_k=[w_{ij}^k]\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) respect \(G_k\): \(w_{ij}^k=0\) whenever \(j\ne i\) and \((j,i)\notin E_k\). Stack states as \(X^k=(x_1^k;\ldots;x_n^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous deterministic linear mixing on fixed or switching graphs; affine, quantized, and randomized gossip updates are outside the formal core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear consensus method is an iteration \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^nw_{ij}^kx_j^k\), equivalently \(X^{k+1}=(W_k\otimes I_d)X^k\), with graph-sparse weights. It is average preserving when \(\mathbf1^\top W_k=\mathbf1^\top\) for every \(k\), consensus preserving when \(W_k\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and doubly stochastic when both identities hold and \(W_k\ge0\). It solves average consensus on an admissible matrix sequence when \((W_{k-1}\cdots W_0)\to J=n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear consensus method replaces each local state by a graph-sparse linear combination of current states. Row stochasticity preserves common states, column stochasticity preserves the aggregate, and convergence of the matrix product to the averaging projector makes the iteration solve arithmetic average consensus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{k+1}=(W_k\otimes I_d)X^k,\qquad W_{k-1}\cdots W_0\longrightarrow \frac1n\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a fixed matrix \(W\), average consensus for all initial states is equivalent to \(W^k\to J\).
For fixed doubly stochastic \(W\), the disagreement recursion is \(X^{k+1}-(J\otimes I_d)X^k=((W-J)\otimes I_d)X^k\).
special_cases_latex: A fixed connected undirected graph commonly admits a symmetric doubly stochastic \(W\).
A switching method uses a nonconstant graph-compatible sequence \((W_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If every \(W_k\) is doubly stochastic, both the consensus subspace and the initial arithmetic mean are invariant.
boundary_notes: Row-stochastic mixing alone generally converges to a nonuniform weighted average.
Negative weights are permitted by linearity but excluded by the stated doubly-stochastic convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence characterization for linear decentralized averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions for convergence to the arithmetic average from every initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $x_i\in\mathbb R^p$, let $\mathbf{x}^0=\operatorname{stack}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, and consider $\mathbf{x}^{k+1}=W\mathbf{x}^k$, where $W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ is a decentralized mixing matrix. If the eigenvalues are ordered so that $|\lambda_1|\ge\cdots\ge|\lambda_n|$, then the iteration converges for every $\mathbf{x}^0$ to consensus at $\bar x=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$ if and only if $W\mathbf1=\mathbf1$, $\mathbf1^\top W=\mathbf1^\top$, and $1=|\lambda_1|>|\lambda_2|\ge\cdots\ge|\lambda_n|$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear decentralized averaging converges from every initial state to the arithmetic average exactly when the mixing matrix fixes consensus vectors, preserves the mean, and has every nonconsensus eigenvalue strictly inside the unit circle.
assumptions_latex: x_i\in\mathbb R^p\quad(i=1,\ldots,n)
W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\text{ is a decentralized mixing matrix}
\mathbf{x}^{k+1}=W\mathbf{x}^k
\mathbf{x}^0=\operatorname{stack}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)
|\lambda_1|\ge\cdots\ge|\lambda_n|
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf{x}^k\to\mathbf1\bar x\ \text{for every }\mathbf{x}^0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad W\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\ \mathbf1^\top W=\mathbf1^\top,\ 1=|\lambda_1|>|\lambda_2|\ge\cdots\ge|\lambda_n|.

children.title: Gossip Averaging Methods
children.top_down_role: Randomized averaging driven by local activations.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Mean-Square Gossip Contraction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise gossip contracts mean-square disagreement geometrically at a rate governed by the probability-weighted graph's algebraic connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let edge \(e=\{i,j\}\) be sampled independently with probability \(p_e\), let \(W_e=I-\tfrac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^{\mathsf T}\), and define \(L_p=\sum_ep_e(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^{\mathsf T}\). For \(Z^k=(I-J)X^k\), \[\mathbb E[\|Z^{k+1}\|_F^2\mid Z^k]\le\left(1-\tfrac12\lambda_2(L_p)\right)\|Z^k\|_F^2.\] Hence \(k=O(\lambda_2(L_p)^{-1}\log(1/\varepsilon))\) activations suffice for relative mean-square error \(\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: Edges are sampled independently with probabilities \(p_e\).
The positive-probability support graph is connected.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral rate for independent pairwise edge sampling.

knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Activation-Support Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise gossip cannot reach global average consensus when the edges that can activate form a disconnected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_+=\{e:p_e>0\}\). If \((V,E_+)\) is disconnected, every gossip update preserves each connected component's average independently. Initial component averages that differ can never converge to one global average.
assumptions_latex: Only edges with \(p_e>0\) can activate.
The positive-probability support graph is disconnected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Universal global average consensus is impossible.}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp reachability boundary for independent pairwise gossip.

knowledge_statements.title: Gossip Averaging Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly selected neighbors replace their vector values by their mean. The network average is preserved, and independent positive-probability edge activations yield average consensus almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let each agent hold \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\), and let \(X^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) have rows \((x_i^k)^\top\). At iteration \(k\), independently sample an edge \(e_k=\{i,j\}\) with probability \(p_{ij}>0\), and set \[x_i^{k+1}=x_j^{k+1}=\frac{x_i^k+x_j^k}{2},\qquad x_\ell^{k+1}=x_\ell^k\quad(\ell\notin\{i,j\}).\] Equivalently, \(X^{k+1}=W_{e_k}X^k\), where \(W_{\{i,j\}}=I_n-\tfrac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^\top\) and \(e_i\) is the ith standard basis vector of \(\mathbb R^n\). After a prescribed number \(K\) of activations, output \(x_i^K\). Every activation preserves the network average, and connectivity with positive edge probabilities gives almost-sure convergence to that average.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(p_{ij}>0\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in E\).
The edge samples are independent across iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^k\to \bar x^0:=n^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^n x_r^0\) almost surely for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise randomized gossip on a fixed connected undirected graph.

notation.meaning: Matrix whose ith row is the state held by agent i at iteration k.
Pairwise averaging matrix associated with edge e.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected communication graph. Agents hold \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\). At round \(k\), an edge \(e_k=\{i_k,j_k\}\in E\) is sampled according to a specified stochastic process.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical synchronous pairwise randomized gossip with exact arithmetic; block, broadcast, asynchronous, and lossy variants require modified activation maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pairwise gossip averaging method is the random linear iteration \(X^{k+1}=(W_{e_k}\otimes I_d)X^k\), where for \(e=\{i,j\}\), \(W_e=I-\tfrac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^\top\). Thus \(x_i^{k+1}=x_j^{k+1}=\tfrac12(x_i^k+x_j^k)\) on the activated edge and every other state is unchanged. More generally, a gossip averaging family consists of random graph-local matrices \(W_{\xi_k}\) satisfying \(W_{\xi_k}\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\mathbf1^\top W_{\xi_k}=\mathbf1^\top\); it solves averaging when \(X^k\to(J\otimes I_d)X^0\) in the declared stochastic mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round a local random activation selects an edge, and the two endpoints replace their values by their pairwise mean while all other values remain fixed. The resulting random graph-local matrix preserves both consensus and the global arithmetic mean. A complete specification states whether convergence is almost sure, in probability, or in mean square.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\{i,j\}}=I-\frac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^\top,\qquad X^{k+1}=(W_{e_k}\otimes I_d)X^k.\)

special_cases_latex: Uniform-edge gossip samples each edge with probability \(1/|E|\).
Nonuniform gossip assigns positive edge probabilities \(p_e\) with \(\sum_ep_e=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For every realization, \(\sum_i x_i^{k+1}=\sum_i x_i^k\).
Only the activated endpoints can change during a pairwise round.

children.title: Accelerated Consensus Methods
children.top_down_role: Polynomial and multi-step acceleration of disagreement contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Interval Misspecification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimating the nonconsensus spectral interval can make a Chebyshev filter noncontractive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter designed for \([-\beta,\beta]\) controls a mode \(\lambda\) only through \(|q_K(\lambda)|\). If an actual nonconsensus eigenvalue satisfies \(|\lambda|>\beta\), the minimax bound gives no contraction guarantee and \(|q_K(\lambda)|\) can exceed one.
assumptions_latex: The filter uses a declared spectral bound \(\beta\).
An actual nonconsensus eigenvalue may lie outside that interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\lambda|>\beta\not\Rightarrow |q_K(\lambda)|<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability boundary for Chebyshev consensus filters.

knowledge_statements.title: Chebyshev Minimax Optimality and Accelerated Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized Chebyshev filter is minimax-optimal among degree-K average-preserving polynomial filters and yields inverse-square-root-gap communication scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\beta<1\). Among real polynomials \(p\) of degree at most \(K\) satisfying \(p(1)=1\), \[q_K(t)=\frac{T_K(t/\beta)}{T_K(1/\beta)}\] minimizes \(\max_{|t|\le\beta}|p(t)|\), with optimal value \(|T_K(1/\beta)|^{-1}\). Moreover, \[|T_K(1/\beta)|^{-1}\le2\left(\frac{\beta}{1+\sqrt{1-\beta^2}}\right)^K.\]
assumptions_latex: The nonconsensus spectrum is contained in \([-\beta,\beta]\), \(0<\beta<1\).
Filters are real polynomials of degree at most \(K\) satisfying \(p(1)=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal degree-limited contraction on a known symmetric spectral interval.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Consensus Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized degree-K Chebyshev filter of a symmetric mixing matrix preserves the average and contracts every nonconsensus eigenmode by at most the reciprocal of the normalization factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and doubly stochastic, suppose that its eigenvalue \(1\) is simple, and suppose every other eigenvalue lies in \([-\beta,\beta]\) for some \(0<\beta<1\). For an integer \(K\ge1\), define \[q_K(t)=\frac{T_K(t/\beta)}{T_K(1/\beta)},\qquad x^K=q_K(W)x^0,\] where \(T_K\) is the degree-\(K\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind and \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\). The filtered state is computable by a three-term Chebyshev recurrence using one multiplication by \(W\) per degree. Since \(q_K(1)=1\), it preserves \(\bar x^0=n^{-1}\mathbf1^\top x^0\), and its disagreement satisfies \[\|x^K-\mathbf1\bar x^0\|_2\le \frac{1}{|T_K(1/\beta)|}\|x^0-\mathbf1\bar x^0\|_2.\]
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and doubly stochastic.
The eigenvalue \(1\) of \(W\) is simple.
\(\operatorname{spec}(W)\setminus\{1\}\subseteq[-\beta,\beta]\) for some \(0<\beta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x^K-\mathbf1\bar x^0\|_2\le |T_K(1/\beta)|^{-1}\|x^0-\mathbf1\bar x^0\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chebyshev polynomial acceleration for symmetric average-preserving mixing.

notation.meaning: Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.
Uniform magnitude bound for nonconsensus eigenvalues.
Average of the entries of the initial state.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a fixed symmetric averaging matrix with \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and let \(J=n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\). For a polynomial \(p_t\) of degree at most \(t\), multiplication by \(p_t(W)\) can be implemented using \(t\) graph-local mixing rounds and finite local memory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed undirected network with symmetric mixing; acceleration is defined relative to ordinary repeated application of the same mixing operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A degree-\(t\) polynomial accelerated-consensus operator is \(P_t=p_t(W)\) with the normalization \(p_t(1)=1\), acting as \(X^t=(P_t\otimes I_d)X^0\). The normalization preserves the consensus component. Its worst-case disagreement contraction on a spectral set \(\Lambda\) containing the nonconsensus eigenvalues of \(W\) is \(\rho_t=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}|p_t(\lambda)|\). The operator is accelerated relative to \(t\) ordinary mixing rounds when \(\rho_t<\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}|\lambda|^t\). A multi-step recurrence is an accelerated consensus method when its induced input-output operator has this polynomial form and strict contraction improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accelerated consensus replaces the monomial produced by repeatedly applying the mixing matrix with a normalized polynomial of the same communication degree. The polynomial equals one at the consensus eigenvalue and is designed to be uniformly smaller on all disagreement eigenvalues than ordinary mixing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_t=p_t(W),\quad p_t(1)=1,\quad \rho_t=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}|p_t(\lambda)|<\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}|\lambda|^t.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: A three-term recurrence using current and previous mixed states defines a polynomial \(p_t(W)\) and is accelerated when the displayed spectral inequality holds.
The disagreement satisfies \(\|(I-J)P_t\|_2=\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(W)\setminus\{1\}}|p_t(\lambda)|\) when \(W\) is symmetric.
special_cases_latex: Chebyshev filtering chooses a scaled Chebyshev polynomial minimizing a uniform bound on a known disagreement interval.
immediate_consequences_latex: The condition \(p_t(1)=1\) gives \(P_t\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
boundary_notes: Acceleration depends on the comparison class, degree, and spectral interval.
For nonsymmetric or time-varying matrices, eigenvalue polynomial bounds may not control the operator norm.

children.title: Distributed Descent Methods
children.top_down_role: Classical consensus-descent families and their bias regimes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Agents minimize \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^nq_if_i(x)\) over \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), retain \(x_i^k\in X\), and use graph-compatible weights \(w_{ij}^k\). Let \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(x_i^k)\) or \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal consensus-descent recursions without a separate dynamic estimator of the aggregate gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed descent method is a local recursion formed by a consensus operation and a local first-order displacement. In mix-then-descend form, \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k\) and \(x_i^{k+1}=\mathcal R_i^k(v_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k)\), where \(\mathcal R_i^k\) is the identity, a projection, or another specified primal feasibility map. Descend-then-mix uses \(u_i^k=x_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k\) and \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}^ku_j^k\). The family is characterized by direct mixing of primal states and use of the current local first-order direction, without a tracker enforcing the aggregate-gradient identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These methods alternate or compose neighbor averaging of primal copies with a local gradient or subgradient step. A feasibility map may follow the displacement. They are distinguished from gradient tracking by the absence of a separate state whose aggregate equals the current aggregate gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\mathcal R_i^k(v_i^k-\alpha_kg_i^k).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: In stacked form, \(V^k=(W_k\otimes I_d)X^k\) and \(X^{k+1}=\mathcal R^k(V^k-\alpha_kG^k)\).
special_cases_latex: Identity \(\mathcal R_i^k\) gives unconstrained distributed gradient or subgradient descent.
Euclidean projection gives a projected distributed descent method.
Constant and diminishing stepsizes define distinct bias and convergence regimes.
immediate_consequences_latex: With \(\alpha_k=0\), the recursion reduces to distributed consensus.
With \(W_k=I\), agents perform uncoupled local descent.
boundary_notes: The update template is a family definition, not a convergence guarantee.
Diffusion orderings can differ because mixing and adaptation need not commute.

notation.meaning: local primal feasibility or retraction map

review_flags: No inspectable exact source locator was available for this family-level template.
