children.title: Diminishing-Stepsize Distributed Subgradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Classical nonsmooth consensus optimization with vanishing steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Ergodic Subgradient Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A horizon-tuned vanishing step gives the standard order-one-over-square-root-K ergodic objective rate with a network-dependent constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under fixed primitive doubly stochastic mixing and uniformly bounded subgradients, run the distributed subgradient recursion for a known horizon \(K\) with \(\alpha_k=c/\sqrt K\) for \(0\le k<K\), and form \[\widehat x_K=\frac1{nK}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k.\] If an aggregate minimizer exists, constants independent of \(K\) satisfy \[\sum_i f_i(\widehat x_K)-\sum_i f_i(x^\star)\le\frac{C}{\sqrt K}.\] The constant depends on initialization, the subgradient bound, \(c\), and network mixing.
assumptions_latex: Local objectives are convex with uniformly bounded subgradients.
Mixing is fixed, primitive, and doubly stochastic.
The aggregate minimizer set is nonempty.
\(\alpha_k=c/\sqrt K\) during the length-\(K\) run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\widehat x_K)-F(x^\star)=O(K^{-1/2})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex Lipschitz rate under fixed balanced mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable-Stepsize Stalling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite total step length can make subgradient descent stop short of the minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=1\), \(f(x)=|x|\), choose \(x^0>\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k>0\), and use \(g^k=1\in\partial f(x^k)\). Then \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_k,\qquad x^k\to x^0-\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k>0.\] Thus positive but summable steps can fail to reach the minimizer even without network error.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_k>0\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k<\infty\).
\(x^0>\sum_k\alpha_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_kx^k=x^0-\sum_k\alpha_k>0\notin\operatorname*{argmin}|x|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-agent boundary showing why nonsummability is essential.

knowledge_statements.title: Diminishing-Stepsize Distributed Subgradient Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent averages neighboring iterates and takes a diminishing local subgradient step. Standard nonsummable, square-summable steps yield consensus at a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Agent \(i\) initializes \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and, for \(k\ge0\), selects \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(x_i^k)\) and updates \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha_k g_i^k.\] Here \(W=(w_{ij})\) is a fixed doubly stochastic mixing matrix and \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\). Stop using a prescribed iteration budget or tolerance and return the local iterates. If the aggregate objective has a minimizer and all subgradients are uniformly bounded, then consensus and convergence to a common minimizer follow.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is convex and has uniformly bounded subgradients.
\(W\) is nonnegative, primitive, and doubly stochastic.
\(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_i f_i(x)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^k-x_j^k\to0\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x_i^k,X^\star)\to0\) for all \(i,j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-subgradient iteration for an unconstrained convex sum objective.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Each agent has a convex function \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), a state \(x_i^k\), graph-compatible weights \(w_{ij}^k\), and a selected subgradient \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(v_i^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic convex nonsmooth consensus optimization with a common scalar stepsize; convergence conditions are recorded as the standard diminishing schedule but no convergence theorem is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A diminishing-stepsize distributed subgradient method has the recursion \(v_i^k=\sum_{j=1}^nw_{ij}^kx_j^k\), \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(v_i^k)\), and \(x_i^{k+1}=v_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k\), or its explicitly projected counterpart. Its defining stepsize satisfies \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\alpha_k\to0\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\). The frequently imposed square-summability condition \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2<\infty\) identifies the classical stochastic-approximation schedule but is an additional analytic condition rather than part of mere vanishing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents first average neighboring primal copies, evaluate a local subgradient at the mixed point, and take a subgradient displacement. The method is diminishing-step when positive steps vanish but have an infinite total sum. Classical analyses often additionally require the squared steps to be summable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k,\quad g_i^k\in\partial f_i(v_i^k),\quad x_i^{k+1}=v_i^k-\alpha_kg_i^k,\quad \alpha_k\downarrow0,\quad \sum_k\alpha_k=\infty.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: A projected version replaces the last update by \(x_i^{k+1}=P_X(v_i^k-\alpha_kg_i^k)\) for a common closed convex set \(X\).
special_cases_latex: The schedule \(\alpha_k=a/(k+b)^p\) with \(a>0\), \(b>0\), and \(1/2<p\le1\) is diminishing, nonsummable, and square summable.
immediate_consequences_latex: A positive constant stepsize is excluded because it does not converge to zero.
A summable schedule is excluded by \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\).
boundary_notes: Vanishing alone does not imply convergence.
Subgradients may be set-valued, so their selection is part of the algorithm.

notation.meaning: selected local subgradient at the mixed point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ergodic Subgradient Rate on a Fixed Connected Network
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order bound for convex Lipschitz objectives under fixed balanced mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under fixed primitive doubly stochastic mixing and uniformly bounded subgradients, run distributed subgradient descent for a known horizon \(K\) with \(\alpha_k=c/\sqrt K\), and form the network-time average \[\widehat x_K=\frac1{nK}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k.\] If \(x^\star\) is an aggregate minimizer, then constants \(C_0,C_1<\infty\), depending on initialization, the subgradient bound, \(c\), and the mixing contraction but not on \(K\), satisfy \[\sum_i f_i(\widehat x_K)-\sum_i f_i(x^\star)\le\frac{C_0+C_1}{\sqrt K}.\] The network-dependent term grows as mixing becomes poorly connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With horizon-tuned order-one-over-square-root-K steps, the averaged distributed subgradient method has the standard order-one-over-square-root-K objective rate, with a network-dependent constant.
assumptions_latex: All local objectives are convex with uniformly bounded subgradients.
The fixed mixing matrix is primitive and doubly stochastic.
The aggregate minimizer set is nonempty.
\(\alpha_k=c/\sqrt K\) for \(0\le k<K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(\widehat x_K)-F(x^\star)=O(K^{-1/2}).

knowledge_statements.title: Plain Constant-Stepsize Distributed Gradient Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent mixes current states and subtracts a fixed local-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For differentiable local objectives and \(\alpha>0\), \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha\nabla f_i(x_i^k),\qquad X^{k+1}=WX^k-\alpha\nabla F(X^k),\] where \(F(X)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\). Each round uses one neighbor-mixing operation and one local gradient evaluation.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
\(W\) respects the communication graph.
\(\alpha>0\) is constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{k+1}=WX^k-\alpha\nabla F(X^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncorrected fixed-step consensus-gradient descent on a fixed network.

notation.meaning: Separable lifted objective over local copies.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Stability Test for Quadratic DGD
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For quadratic objectives, fixed-step DGD is globally stable exactly when its affine iteration matrix has spectral radius below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f_i(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}H_ix-b_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\), with \(H_i=H_i^{\mathsf T}\), and set \(H=\operatorname{blkdiag}(H_1,\ldots,H_n)\). Then \[x^{k+1}=(W\otimes I-\alpha H)x^k+\alpha b.\] It converges to a unique fixed point for every initialization if and only if \(\rho(W\otimes I-\alpha H)<1\).
assumptions_latex: Each local objective is quadratic.
The stacked iteration has the displayed affine form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\) converges uniquely for every \(x^0\) if and only if \(\rho(W\otimes I-\alpha H)<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient linear stability condition for quadratic local objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized-Objective Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plain fixed-step DGD is gradient descent on a quadratic-penalty relaxation whose penalty strength is inversely proportional to the stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) and \(I-W\succeq0\), then \(X^{k+1}=WX^k-\alpha\nabla F(X^k)\) is gradient descent with stepsize \(\alpha\) on \[\Phi_\alpha(X)=F(X)+\frac1{2\alpha}\langle X,(I-W)X\rangle.\] Thus every fixed point satisfies \((I-W)X+\alpha\nabla F(X)=0\), the stationarity equation of a quadratic-penalty relaxation rather than generally the exact consensus problem.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\).
\(I-W\succeq0\).
Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla\Phi_\alpha(X)=\nabla F(X)+\alpha^{-1}(I-W)X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric-mixing representation explaining constant-step network bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Stepsize Distributed Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-agent quadratic example shows that constant-step distributed gradient descent can converge to nonconsensual local states, with disagreement proportional to the stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two agents, scalar states, \(W=\tfrac12\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), \(f_1(x)=\tfrac12(x-a)^2\), and \(f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x-b)^2\), where \(a\ne b\). Constant-step distributed gradient descent is \[x^{k+1}=Wx^k-\alpha\bigl(x^k-(a,b)^\top\bigr),\qquad 0<\alpha<1.\] It converges to a unique fixed point whose average equals the aggregate minimizer \(x^\star=(a+b)/2\), but whose disagreement is \[x_1^\infty-x_2^\infty=\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}(a-b)\ne0.\] Thus a fixed positive step does not generally produce exact consensus, even for smooth strongly convex quadratic objectives and complete averaging.
assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb R\) with \(a\ne b\).
\(W=\tfrac12\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_1^\infty-x_2^\infty=\alpha(a-b)/(1+\alpha)\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent disagreement in constant-step decentralized gradient descent.

notation.meaning: Minimizer of the sum of the two local objectives.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let differentiable local objectives \(f_i:\mathbb R^d	o\mathbb R\) be held by \(n\) agents. Let \(W=[w_{ij}]\) be a fixed graph-compatible mixing matrix, \(X^k=(x_1^k;\ldots;x_n^k)\), and \(
abla f(X^k)=(
abla f_1(x_1^k);\ldots;

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth unconstrained consensus-gradient methods with one fixed positive stepsize and no gradient tracker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constant-stepsize distributed gradient method is the recursion \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^nw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\) for every agent and round, where \(\alpha\in(0,\infty)\) is independent of \(k\). In stacked form, \(X^{k+1}=(W\otimes I_d)X^k-\alpha\nabla f(X^k)\). The defining persistent-step property is \(\inf_k\alpha_k=\sup_k\alpha_k=\alpha>0\); consequently the local gradient perturbation is not forced to vanish by the schedule itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each round mixes the current primal copies and subtracts the current local gradient multiplied by the same positive stepsize at every iteration. This persistent local displacement distinguishes the method from diminishing-step recursions and may couple disagreement with optimization error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{k+1}=(W\otimes I_d)X^k-\alpha\nabla f(X^k),\qquad \alpha>0\text{ independent of }k.\)

special_cases_latex: When all local gradients vanish at a common optimizer, that consensual optimizer is a fixed point.
When local minimizers differ, the displayed fixed-step recursion need not have the exact aggregate minimizer as a consensual fixed point.
immediate_consequences_latex: Setting \(W=I\) yields independent constant-step gradient methods.
Setting \(\alpha=0\) would yield consensus but is excluded by the definition.

Gradient tracking and exact correction add states or memory absent from this recursion.

children.top_down_role: Consensus-gradient methods for common or agent-local feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Distributed Subgradient Method with Agent-Local Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent projects onto its own set; intersection regularity and standard diminishing steps yield common feasible optimal cluster points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agent \(i\) know a nonempty closed convex set \(C_i\), with \(C=\bigcap_iC_i\ne\varnothing\). Set \[v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=P_{C_i}(v_i^k-\alpha_kg_i^k),\quad g_i^k\in\partial f_i(v_i^k).\] Under primitive doubly stochastic mixing, bounded subgradients, nonsummable square-summable steps, existence of a constrained aggregate minimizer, bounded iterates, and bounded linear regularity of \(\{C_i\}\) on the iterate region, feasibility errors and disagreement vanish and every cluster point is an aggregate minimizer over \(C\).
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(C=\cap_iC_i\ne\varnothing\).
The iterate sequence is bounded and the sets are boundedly linearly regular on its region.
Mixing is primitive and doubly stochastic.
Subgradients are bounded and the stepsizes are nonsummable but square summable.
A constrained aggregate minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i\operatorname{dist}(x_i^k,C)\to0\), \(\max_{i,j}\|x_i^k-x_j^k\|\to0\), and every cluster point lies in \(X_C^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-constraint variant complementing the shared-set seed.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Feasibility and Consensus Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero local-feasibility and edge-disagreement residuals certify a common point in every local set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a connected undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), define \[r_{\mathrm{feas}}(X)=\max_i\operatorname{dist}(x_i,C_i),\qquad r_{\mathrm{cons}}(X)=\max_{\{i,j\}\in E}\|x_i-x_j\|.\] Then both residuals vanish if and only if \(x_i=x\) for every agent for some \(x\in\bigcap_iC_i\).
assumptions_latex: The communication graph is connected.
Each \(C_i\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{feas}}(X)=r_{\mathrm{cons}}(X)=0\iff X=\mathbf1x^{\mathsf T}\) for some \(x\in\cap_iC_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for agent-local feasibility on a connected graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Intersection Boundary for Local Projections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With empty set intersection, bounded iterates cannot become both locally feasible and consensual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bigcap_iC_i=\varnothing\), no bounded sequence can satisfy both \(\max_i\operatorname{dist}(x_i^k,C_i)\to0\) and \(\max_{i,j}\|x_i^k-x_j^k\|\to0\). Hence convergence to a common feasible optimizer is impossible regardless of the gradient or stepsize rule.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is closed.
\(\cap_iC_i=\varnothing\).
The iterate sequence is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\neg(r_{\mathrm{feas}}(X^k)\to0\land r_{\mathrm{cons}}(X^k)\to0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility obstruction for agent-local constraint sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Distributed Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents average neighboring feasible states, take local gradient steps, and project onto a shared closed convex set. Under the stated mixing, bounded-gradient, minimizer-existence, and diminishing-stepsize assumptions, they approach constrained minimizers and consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and define \(X_C^\star:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Agent \(i\) initializes \(x_i^0\in C\) and iterates \[v_i^k=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}x_j^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=P_C\bigl(v_i^k-\alpha_k\nabla f_i(v_i^k)\bigr).\] The method stops after a prescribed budget or when feasibility and consensus residuals meet specified tolerances, and it returns the local states. If the local objectives are differentiable and convex with gradients uniformly bounded on \(C\), \(W=(w_{ij})\) is nonnegative, primitive, and doubly stochastic, \(X_C^\star\neq\varnothing\), and \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then the local iterates asymptotically agree and approach \(X_C^\star\).
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and convex, with gradients uniformly bounded on \(C\).
\(W\) is nonnegative, primitive, and doubly stochastic.
\(X_C^\star:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) is nonempty.
\(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x_i^k,X_C^\star)\to0\) and \(\|x_i^k-x_j^k\|\to0\) for all \(i,j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected consensus-gradient iteration over a shared convex feasible set.

notation.meaning: Minimizer set of the aggregate objective over C.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Agents have differentiable objectives \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), nonempty closed convex feasible sets \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), states \(x_i^k\), and graph-compatible weights \(w_{ij}^k\). The common-set case has \(X_i=X\) for all \(i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A projected distributed gradient method forms \(v_i^k=\sum_{j=1}^nw_{ij}^kx_j^k\) and updates \(x_i^{k+1}=P_{X_i}(v_i^k-\alpha_k\nabla f_i(v_i^k))\), where \(P_{X_i}(y)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_i}\|x-y\|_2\). For closed convex \(X_i\), this projection is single valued and the update guarantees \(x_i^{k+1}\in X_i\). With a common set \(X\), all post-update iterates are feasible for the same constraint; with heterogeneous sets, local feasibility does not by itself imply membership in \(\bigcap_iX_i\) for any individual mixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent averages neighbor states, takes a local gradient step from the mixed point, and projects the result onto its closed convex feasible set. Projection makes every new local state feasible for that agent. Common and agent-specific constraint sets lead to different feasibility interpretations.

Convexity and closedness ensure uniqueness of each Euclidean projection.

Nonconvex projections may be multivalued and are outside this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Perron-Weighted Stationarity of Diffusion Fixed Points
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perron weights and local stepsizes determine ATC fixed-point stationarity; a consensual CTA fixed point requires every local gradient to vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the seed orientation and set \(B=A^{\mathsf T}\), so the combination is \(x^+=B\psi\). If \(B\) is primitive and row stochastic and \(\pi^{\mathsf T}B=\pi^{\mathsf T}\), then any consensual deterministic ATC fixed point satisfies \[\sum_i\pi_i\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0.\] A consensual CTA fixed point satisfies the stronger componentwise equations \(\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\), and hence also the displayed weighted equation. The unweighted aggregate stationarity equation is ensured for ATC when \(\pi_i\mu_i\) is constant.
assumptions_latex: The effective combination matrix is primitive and row stochastic.
Local gradients are exact.
The fixed point is consensual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i\pi_i\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0\) for ATC, while CTA additionally requires \(\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary stationarity condition under primitive combination weights and heterogeneous stepsizes.

notation.meaning: Stationary left distribution of the effective combination matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Small-Stepsize Stochastic Diffusion Neighborhood
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small constant-step stochastic diffusion is mean-square stable, with order-step optimization error and order-step-squared disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the Perron-and-stepsize-weighted aggregate objective is strongly convex, local gradients are Lipschitz, the combination matrix is primitive, and sampled gradients are conditionally unbiased with uniformly bounded conditional second moments. For sufficiently small positive constant stepsizes, ATC and CTA are mean-square stable. With \(\mu=\max_i\mu_i\), \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\sum_i\mathbb E\|x_i^k-x^\star\|^2=O(\mu),\qquad \limsup_{k\to\infty}\sum_i\mathbb E\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|^2=O(\mu^2).\] Persistent gradient noise therefore prevents exact last-iterate convergence at a fixed positive stepsize.
assumptions_latex: The weighted aggregate objective is strongly convex.
Local gradients are Lipschitz.
Samples are conditionally unbiased with uniformly bounded conditional second moments.
Mixing is primitive and all constant stepsizes are sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_k\sum_i\mathbb E\|x_i^k-x^\star\|^2=O(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative constant-step mean-square stability for ATC and CTA diffusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Diffusion Adaptation Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diffusion methods either adapt locally before mixing or mix before adapting. Both use neighborhood-weighted combinations and local exact or sampled gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=(a_{\ell i})\) be nonnegative with \(\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}=1\) and \(a_{\ell i}=0\) outside agent \(i\)'s neighborhood. Adapt-then-combine diffusion uses \[\psi_i^k=x_i^k-\mu_i g_i(x_i^k),\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}\psi_\ell^k.\] Combine-then-adapt diffusion instead uses \[\phi_i^k=\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}x_\ell^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\phi_i^k-\mu_i g_i(\phi_i^k).\] Here \(g_i\) may be an exact or sampled local gradient. Initialize arbitrary local states, stop under a prescribed budget or residual rule, and output the final local states.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) is a local gradient or stochastic gradient oracle.
\(A\) respects the communication graph and has unit column sums.
\(\mu_i>0\) is agent i's stepsize.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursions respectively define the adapt-then-combine and combine-then-adapt diffusion families.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapt-then-combine and combine-then-adapt diffusion recursions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Agents \(i=1,\ldots,n\) hold differentiable risks \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\). Let \(A=[a_{\ell i}]\ge0\) have \(a_{\ell i}=0\) for nonneighbors and \(\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}=1\). Each agent has iterate \(w_i^k\) and stepsize \(\mu_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order diffusion with a fixed convex-combination matrix; stochastic-gradient diffusion replaces exact gradients by local oracle samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adapt-then-combine diffusion recursion is \(\psi_i^k=w_i^k-\mu_i\nabla f_i(w_i^k)\), followed by \(w_i^{k+1}=\sum_{\ell=1}^na_{\ell i}\psi_\ell^k\). A combine-then-adapt diffusion recursion is \(\phi_i^k=\sum_{\ell=1}^na_{\ell i}w_\ell^k\), followed by \(w_i^{k+1}=\phi_i^k-\mu_i\nabla f_i(\phi_i^k)\). The two orderings define distinct methods because local adaptation and network combination generally do not commute.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diffusion methods use a convex neighbor-combination operator and a local adaptation step. Adapt-then-combine first moves each local iterate using its own gradient and then blends adapted values. Combine-then-adapt first blends neighbor iterates and then takes a local gradient step. These orderings are generally different.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{ATC: }\psi_i^k=w_i^k-\mu_i\nabla f_i(w_i^k),\quad w_i^{k+1}=\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}\psi_\ell^k;\qquad \text{CTA: }\phi_i^k=\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}w_\ell^k,\quad w_i^{k+1}=\phi_i^k-\mu_i\nabla f_i(\phi_i^k).\)
special_cases_latex: Using a stochastic gradient \(g_i(w_i^k;\xi_i^k)\) in place of \(\nabla f_i(w_i^k)\) gives stochastic diffusion.
If \(A=I\), both orderings reduce to uncoupled local adaptation.

ATC and CTA coincide in special commuting or zero-adaptation cases, but not generally.

This definition does not include exact-diffusion correction variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decentralized Gradient Descent as Consensus-Penalty Gradient Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combine-then-adapt DGD, including its decentralized implementation and its fixed-stepsize convergence boundary: the stated guarantee concerns the quadratic-penalty problem rather than the original exact-consensus problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}} h(\mathbf{x})+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|\mathbf{x}\|_{I-W}^{2}\), where \(\|\mathbf{x}\|_{I-W}^{2}=0\) if and only if \(\mathbf{x}\) is in consensus. Gradient descent with stepsize \(\alpha\) yields decentralized gradient descent (combine-then-adapt): \(\mathbf{x}^{k+1}=W\mathbf{x}^{k}-\alpha\nabla h(\mathbf{x}^{k})\). If the penalty problem has a solution, the local functions satisfy the source's standing convexity assumptions and are \(L\)-smooth, and \(0<\alpha<(1+\lambda_n(W))/L\), then \(\mathbf{x}^{k}\) converges to a solution of the penalty problem. When \(W\) is a decentralized mixing matrix, multiplication by \(W\) uses neighbor communication and all remaining operations are local. For fixed \(\alpha\), this is not an asserted convergence guarantee for the exact-consensus problem; small \(\alpha\) only motivates the penalty approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient descent on the quadratic consensus-penalty formulation produces DGD, also called combine-then-adapt: mix with W and subtract the local gradient step. Under the stated smoothness, solvability, and stepsize assumptions, the iterates converge to a solution of the penalty problem. A decentralized mixing matrix permits neighbor-only communication. The extract does not claim exact convergence to the original consensus problem for a fixed positive stepsize.

I-W\succeq0
\|\mathbf{x}\|_{I-W}^{2}=0\iff \mathbf{x}\text{ is in consensus}
\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf{x}}\left(h(\mathbf{x})+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|\mathbf{x}\|_{I-W}^{2}\right)\neq\varnothing
h_1,\ldots,h_n\text{ satisfy the standing convexity assumptions and are }L\text{-smooth}
0<\alpha<\frac{1+\lambda_n(W)}{L}
W\text{ is a decentralized mixing matrix for the decentralization claim}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf{x}^{k+1}=W\mathbf{x}^{k}-\alpha\nabla h(\mathbf{x}^{k}),\qquad \mathbf{x}^{k}\to\mathbf{x}^{\star}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf{x}}\left(h(\mathbf{x})+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|\mathbf{x}\|_{I-W}^{2}\right).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordinary adapt-then-combine diffusion, its penalty representation, decentralized implementation, and convergence to the penalty solution rather than an exact-diffusion bias-corrected solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the source's standing mixing-matrix assumptions, further suppose \(\min\{\lambda_2(W),\ldots,\lambda_n(W)\}>0\), so that \(W\) is positive definite and invertible, and consider \(\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}} h(\mathbf{x})+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|\mathbf{x}\|_{W^{-1}-I}^{2}\). Forward-backward splitting with \(\mathbb{A}=\nabla h\) and \(\mathbb{B}=\alpha^{-1}(W^{-1}-I)\) yields the diffusion (adapt-then-combine) iteration \(\mathbf{x}^{k+1}=W(\mathbf{x}^{k}-\alpha\nabla h(\mathbf{x}^{k}))\). Although \(W^{-1}\) occurs in the penalty representation, it is not evaluated by the iteration. If the penalty problem has a solution, the local functions satisfy the standing convexity assumptions and are \(L_h\)-smooth, and \(0<\alpha<2/L_h\), then \(\mathbf{x}^{k}\) converges to a solution of the penalty problem. When \(W\) is a decentralized mixing matrix, the iteration is decentralized. This is ordinary diffusion, not the exact-diffusion bias-correction method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite mixing matrix, forward-backward splitting of the quadratic-penalty formulation gives ordinary diffusion, or adapt-then-combine: take a gradient step and then mix with W. The inverse of W appears only in the formulation and analysis. Under the stated solvability, smoothness, and stepsize assumptions, the iterates converge to a penalty-problem solution. This is not an exact-diffusion convergence result.

h_1,\ldots,h_n\text{ satisfy the standing convexity assumptions and are }L_h\text{-smooth}

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Offset under Incorrect Tracker Initialization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced mixing cannot repair a wrong aggregate tracker initialization; the permanent offset can drive motion on a zero objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For doubly stochastic \(W\), the tracker recursion preserves
\[
\sum_i y_i^k-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)=\sum_i y_i^0-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^0)=:\delta.
\]
Thus exact tracking requires \(\delta=0\). In the one-agent case with \(f_1\equiv0\), \(y_1^0=c\ne0\), and fixed \(\alpha>0\), one has \(y_1^k=c\) and \(x_1^k=x_1^0-k\alpha c\), although the true gradient is zero.
assumptions_latex: The tracker uses gradient differences and doubly stochastic mixing.
For the explicit example, \(n=1\), \(f_1\equiv0\), \(y_1^0=c\ne0\), and \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta\ne0\text{ persists};\qquad f_1\equiv0\Rightarrow x_1^k=x_1^0-k\alpha c.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of exact tracking despite balanced mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Average Dynamics and Disagreement Error
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The network average takes a centralized gradient step evaluated at local states, with error relative to the gradient at the average controlled by disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the immutable balanced gradient-tracking recursion,
\[
\bar x^{k+1}=\bar x^k-\alpha\bar y^k
=\bar x^k-\alpha{1\over n}\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k).
\]
If every \(\nabla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz and \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\), then
\[
\|\bar y^k-\nabla F(\bar x^k)\|\le {1\over n}\sum_iL_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|.
\]
assumptions_latex: The immutable recursion uses a doubly stochastic matrix.
\(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\).
Each \(\nabla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz for the error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x^{k+1}=\bar x^k-\alpha\bar y^k,\qquad\|\bar y^k-\nabla F(\bar x^k)\|\le n^{-1}\sum_iL_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centralized descent law followed by the network average, perturbed by disagreement.

notation.meaning: network averages of decisions and trackers

abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x_i^k).\] Stop at a prescribed iteration or when optimization and consensus residuals are small. Double stochasticity and the initialization imply the exact invariant \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i
abla f_i(x_i^k)\), so the average tracker equals the average current gradient.

\(W\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic.
\(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Failure without Joint Connectivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without joint connectivity, agents can remain at distinct local minimizers even though every mixing matrix is doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_k=I_2\) for every \(k\), \(f_1(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), and \(f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x-2)^2\). Initialize \(x_1^0=0\), \(x_2^0=2\), and \(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)=0\). The time-varying tracking recursion then remains at \(x_1^k=0\), \(x_2^k=2\), although the minimizer of \(\tfrac12(f_1+f_2)\) is \(x^*=1\).
assumptions_latex: The disconnected sequence \(W_k=I_2\) is used.
The local quadratic objectives and stated exact tracker initialization are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_1^k=0,\quad x_2^k=2\quad\forall k,\qquad x^*=1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-agent obstruction showing that per-round double stochasticity cannot replace information flow across graph windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient Tracking on Time-Varying Networks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Time-varying balanced gradient tracking uses a symmetric doubly stochastic mixing matrix at each round. Uniform positive communication and self-weights together with bounded-window connectivity provide disagreement contraction, while the tracker-sum invariant survives every topology change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(k\ge0\), let \(W_k\in\mathbb R^{n	imes n}\) be a nonnegative symmetric doubly stochastic matrix associated with an undirected communication graph. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient tracking over a time-varying network
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((G_k)_{k\ge0}\) be a graph sequence and let \(W_k\ge0\) be graph compatible and doubly stochastic for every \(k\). Agents hold \(x_i^k,y_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) and differentiable local functions \(f_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous time-varying balanced networks; joint connectivity is included as an admissibility condition, while convergence is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Gradient tracking on a time-varying network is \(X^{k+1}=(W_k\otimes I_d)X^k-\alpha_kY^k\) and \(Y^{k+1}=(W_k\otimes I_d)Y^k+
abla f(X^{k+1})-
abla f(X^k)\), initialized by \(Y^0=
abla f(X^0)\). A graph sequence is \(B\)-jointly connected when, for every \(k\ge0\), the union graph \((V, igcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}E_t)\) is connected. Because each \(W_k\) preserves sums, the aggregate tracking identity holds at every round despite switching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal and tracker mixers may change at every iteration but must respect the current graph. Uniform joint connectivity requires every window of a fixed length to have a connected union. With doubly stochastic mixers and gradient initialization, switching does not disturb the equality between the aggregate tracker and aggregate current gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{k+1}=(W_k\otimes I_d)X^k-\alpha_kY^k,\quad Y^{k+1}=(W_k\otimes I_d)Y^k+\nabla f(X^{k+1})-\nabla f(X^k),\quad \bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}G_t\text{ is connected for every }k.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Uniform joint connectivity is also called \(B\)-connectivity for the graph sequence.
The tracking invariant is \((\mathbf1^\top\otimes I_d)Y^k=(\mathbf1^\top\otimes I_d)\nabla f(X^k)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(G_k=G\) and \(W_k=W\) for all \(k\), the method reduces to fixed-network balanced gradient tracking.
immediate_consequences_latex: Individual graphs in the sequence may be disconnected while every length-\(B\) union is connected.
boundary_notes: Joint connectivity alone does not give a quantitative contraction without weight lower bounds and self-loop conditions.
Directed switching requires asymmetric normalization beyond this definition.

children.top_down_role: Tracking with sampled gradients and local finite-sum structure.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Agent \(i\) has a finite-sum objective \(f_i(x)=m_i^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{m_i}f_{i,r}(x)\), a primal copy \(x_i^k\), a tracker \(y_i^k\), and an estimator state \(h_i^k\). Let \(W\) be graph compatible and doubly stochastic, and let \(\xi_i^k\) denote a locally sampled index or minibatch.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous finite-sum or stochastic-oracle tracking; the estimator construction is abstracted but its sampling filtration and conditional target must be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sampled gradient-tracking method consists of a local gradient estimator \(v_i^k=V_i(x_i^k,h_i^k,\xi_i^k)\), an estimator-state transition \(h_i^{k+1}=H_i(x_i^{k+1},h_i^k,\xi_i^k)\), and the network recursion \(X^{k+1}=(W\otimes I_d)X^k-\alpha Y^k\), \(Y^{k+1}=(W\otimes I_d)Y^k+V^{k+1}-V^k\), initialized by \(Y^0=V^0\). Here \(V^k=(v_1^k;\ldots;v_n^k)\). The tracker exactly follows the aggregate estimator, \((\mathbf1^\top\otimes I_d)Y^k=(\mathbf1^\top\otimes I_d)V^k\); estimator unbiasedness, variance reduction, or consistency is an additional declared property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent replaces its exact local gradient with a sampled or variance-reduced estimator and retains any memory needed by that estimator. The tracker adds the estimator increment rather than the exact-gradient increment. With sum-preserving mixing and matching initialization, the aggregate tracker equals the aggregate current estimator. Whether that estimator is unbiased or variance reduced must be stated separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{k+1}=(W\otimes I_d)X^k-\alpha Y^k,\quad Y^{k+1}=(W\otimes I_d)Y^k+V^{k+1}-V^k,\quad (\mathbf1^\top\otimes I_d)Y^k=(\mathbf1^\top\otimes I_d)V^k.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an unbiased estimator, \(\mathbb E[v_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\); this condition is not automatic from sampling.
A minibatch estimator uses \(v_i^k=|B_i^k|^{-1}\sum_{r\in B_i^k}\nabla f_{i,r}(x_i^k)\).
special_cases_latex: Full-batch sampling \(B_i^k=\{1,\ldots,m_i\}\) reduces the method to deterministic gradient tracking.
Memoryless single-sample estimators and memory-based variance-reduced estimators are distinct members of the family.
immediate_consequences_latex: The aggregate tracking identity remains exact pathwise for estimator values even when the estimator is random.
Sampling error enters through \(V^k-\nabla f(X^k)\), not through failure of the tracker-sum identity.
boundary_notes: An oracle distribution, filtration, and estimator update are required for any probabilistic guarantee.
Biased compression and intermittent communication require additional correction states or assumptions.

Stochastic Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent tracks changing stochastic gradients while mixing with neighbors. The tracker sum exactly matches the current sampled-gradient sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At agent \(i\), let \(g_i(x;\xi_i)\) be a stochastic gradient. Draw \(\xi_i^0\), initialize \(x_i^0\) arbitrarily and \(y_i^0=g_i(x_i^0;\xi_i^0)\). At iteration \(k\), compute \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha_k y_i^k,\] draw \(\xi_i^{k+1}\), set \(g_i^{k+1}=g_i(x_i^{k+1};\xi_i^{k+1})\), and update \[y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+g_i^{k+1}-g_i^k.\] Stop after a prescribed sample budget and output local or averaged iterates. The tracker sum equals the sum of current sampled gradients pathwise.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic.
\(\mathbb E[g_i(x;\xi_i)\mid x]=\nabla f_i(x)\).
The stochastic gradients have finite conditional second moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i g_i(x_i^k;\xi_i^k)\) for every \(k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient tracking driven by unbiased sampled local gradients.

knowledge_statements.title: SAGA-Type Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAGA-type tracking uses a local component-gradient table to obtain an unbiased estimator without periodic full-gradient snapshots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f_i=m_i^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{m_i}f_{ir}\), agent \(i\) stores points \(\phi_{ir}^k\) and their component gradients. Given \(x_i^k\), sample \(r_i^k\) uniformly and set \[v_i^k=
abla f_{i r_i^k}(x_i^k)-
abla f_{i r_i^k}(\phi_{i r_i^k}^k)+ rac1{m_i}\sum_{r=1}^{m_i}
abla f_{ir}(\phi_{ir}^k).\] Replace \(\phi_{i r_i^k}^k\) by \(x_i^k\), leaving other entries unchanged. With balanced mixing, use \[x^{k+1}=Wx^k-\alpha y^k,\qquad y^{k+1}=Wy^k+v^{k+1}-v^k,\] and initialize \(y^0=v^0\). Then \(\mathbb E[v_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=
abla f_i(x_i^k)\) and \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i v_i^k\).
assumptions_latex: Each local objective is a finite average of differentiable components.
The sampled component is conditionally uniform.
\(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(y^0=v^0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[v_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k),\qquad\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i v_i^k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Table-based unbiased variance reduction embedded in balanced tracking.

notation.meaning: stored evaluation point for local component r

knowledge_statements.title: SARAH-Type Recursive Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SARAH-type tracking recursively uses same-component gradient differences and periodically resets estimator error with a full local gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a refresh iteration, agent \(i\) sets \(v_i^k=
abla f_i(x_i^k)\). Between refreshes it samples \(r_i^k\) uniformly and uses \[v_i^k=v_i^{k-1}+
abla f_{i r_i^k}(x_i^k)-
abla f_{i r_i^k}(x_i^{k-1}).\] Embed the estimator sequence in \[x^{k+1}=Wx^k-\alpha y^k,\qquad y^{k+1}=Wy^k+v^{k+1}-v^k,\] with doubly stochastic \(W\) and \(y^0=v^0\). Then \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i v_i^k\), although \(v_i^k\) is generally not conditionally unbiased for \(
abla f_i(x_i^k)\).
assumptions_latex: Each local objective has a finite-sum representation.
The same sampled component is evaluated at successive local points.
Exact local gradients are computed at refresh iterations.
\(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(y^0=v^0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i v_i^k,\quad\text{while }\mathbb E[v_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\text{ need not hold}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive, generally conditionally biased local variance reduction with periodic exact refreshes.

knowledge_statements.title: SVRG Variance Collapse at the Snapshot
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SVRG estimator's variance is controlled by the distance to its snapshot and vanishes at the snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(v_i=
abla f_{ir}(x)-
abla f_{ir}(\widetilde x)+
abla f_i(\widetilde x)\), suppose every component gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(r\) is uniform. Then \[\mathbb E\|v_i-
abla f_i(x)\|^2\le \mathbb E\|
abla f_{ir}(x)-
abla f_{ir}(\widetilde x)\|^2\le L^2\|x-\widetilde x\|^2.\] In particular, the estimator variance is zero at \(x=\widetilde x\).
assumptions_latex: Every local component has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
The component index is sampled uniformly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E\|v_i-\nabla f_i(x)\|^2\le L^2\|x-\widetilde x\|^2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional mean-square bound for the immutable SVRG estimator.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Reduced Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SVRG estimator replaces raw stochastic gradients inside the tracking recursion, reducing sampling variance through periodically refreshed local snapshots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f_i(x)=m_i^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{m_i}f_{ir}(x)\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) samples \(r_i^k\) uniformly and forms the snapshot estimator \[v_i^k=
abla f_{i r_i^k}(x_i^k)-
abla f_{i r_i^k}(\widetilde x_i)+
abla f_i(\widetilde x_i).\] With \(y_i^0=v_i^0\), update \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha y_i^k,\qquad y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+v_i^{k+1}-v_i^k.\] Refresh each snapshot and its full local gradient periodically, stop after a prescribed component-gradient budget, and output the final local states. Conditionally, \(v_i^k\) is unbiased for \(
abla f_i(x_i^k)\).
assumptions_latex: Each local objective is a finite average of differentiable component functions.
Each component index is sampled uniformly, conditionally on the current history.
\(W\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[v_i^k\mid x_i^k,\widetilde x_i]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\) and \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i v_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SVRG-type local estimators embedded in balanced gradient tracking.

knowledge_statements.title: Common Noise Defeats Network Variance Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly correlated local noises are not attenuated by adding agents, so the average tracker retains the full noise variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon_i^k=z^k\) for every agent, where \(\mathbb E[z^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\|z^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\sigma^2>0\). Then \[\frac1n\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k=z^k,\qquad \mathbb E\left[\left\|\frac1n\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k\right\|^2\middle|\mathcal F_k\right]=\sigma^2,\] independently of \(n\).
assumptions_latex: All agents receive the same conditionally centered square-integrable noise realization.
Its conditional second moment is \(\sigma^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E\left[\left\|\bar y^k-n^{-1}\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\right\|^2\middle|\mathcal F_k\right]=\sigma^2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp correlated-noise example for the average tracker.

notation.meaning: common noise shared by all agents

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Agent Noise Covariance Controls Averaging
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Network averaging reduces gradient-noise variance only to the extent that cross-agent covariances cancel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\varepsilon^k=n^{-1}\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k\), with conditionally centered square-integrable vector noises. Then \[\mathbb E[\|\bar\varepsilon^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbb E[\langle\varepsilon_i^k,\varepsilon_j^k\rangle\mid\mathcal F_k].\] Hence the \(1/n\) variance reduction in the seed follows from vanishing cross terms and does not follow from centered marginals alone.
assumptions_latex: Each noise is square integrable and conditionally centered.
No conditional independence assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\|\bar\varepsilon^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=n^{-2}\sum_{i,j}\mathbb E[\langle\varepsilon_i^k,\varepsilon_j^k\rangle\mid\mathcal F_k].
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-moment representation replacing the independent-noise simplification.

knowledge_statements.title: Tracking under Gradient Noise
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient tracking preserves the sum of noisy gradients, not true gradients. Independent centered noise leaves average tracker variance of order one over the network size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)+\varepsilon_i^k\), initialize \(y_i^0=g_i^0\), and use \[y^{k+1}=Wy^k+g^{k+1}-g^k\] with a doubly stochastic \(W\). Then the telescoping identity \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i g_i^k\) holds pathwise. Consequently, the average tracker equals \[\bar y^k=\frac1n\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)+\frac1n\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k,\] rather than the exact average gradient. If the noises are conditionally independent, centered, and satisfy \(\mathbb E[\|\varepsilon_i^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2\), then the mean-square average tracking noise is at most \(\sigma^2/n\).
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(y^0=g^0\).
\(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) and noises are conditionally independent across agents.
\(\mathbb E[\|\varepsilon_i^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\|\bar y^k-n^{-1}\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2/n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tracking invariant and residual variance under additive gradient noise.

notation.meaning: History conditioning the iteration-k noise model.

knowledge_statements.title: Random Reshuffling Is Not Per-Step Unbiased
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random reshuffling is uniform over the remaining components, so its within-epoch gradient is generally not conditionally unbiased for the full local gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
During a random-reshuffling epoch, let \(S_k\) be the component indices not yet visited. Conditional on the within-epoch history, \[\mathbb E[
abla f_{i\xi_i^k}(x_i^k)\mid\mathcal F_k]= rac1{|S_k|}\sum_{j\in S_k}
abla f_{ij}(x_i^k),\] which generally differs from \(
abla f_i(x_i^k)=m_i^{-1}\sum_j
abla f_{ij}(x_i^k)\). Thus with-replacement martingale-difference arguments do not apply stepwise without modification.
assumptions_latex: A uniformly random permutation is traversed without replacement within each epoch.
The conditioning history reveals the indices already visited.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]\ne\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\quad\text{in general within an epoch}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-bias boundary within a without-replacement epoch.

notation.meaning: indices remaining in the current reshuffling epoch

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Variance of Importance-Weighted Component Sampling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Importance sampling is unbiased, and probabilities proportional to nonzero component-gradient norms minimize its conditional second moment at a fixed iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At fixed \(x\), write \(a_j=\nabla f_{ij}(x)\), \(\bar a=m_i^{-1}\sum_j a_j\), and sample \(J\) with \(p_j>0\). For \(g=a_J/(m_ip_J)\), \[\mathbb E\|g-\bar a\|^2=\frac1{m_i^2}\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}\frac{\|a_j\|^2}{p_j}-\|\bar a\|^2.\] If every \(a_j\ne0\), this is minimized by \(p_j=\|a_j\|/\sum_\ell\|a_\ell\|\). If some \(a_j=0\) while strict positivity is required, the same value is an infimum approached by assigning those indices arbitrarily small positive mass.
assumptions_latex: The component gradients exist at the fixed iterate.
Sampling probabilities are strictly positive and sum to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_j\ne0\ \forall j\Longrightarrow p_j^*=\frac{\|a_j\|}{\sum_\ell\|a_\ell\|}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-sample variance formula and variance-minimizing probabilities at a fixed local iterate.

notation.meaning: component gradient at the fixed local iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Sampling Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local finite sum may be sampled using conditionally independent draws, shared randomness, or random reshuffling. For a draw having the stated conditional probabilities, importance weighting makes the sampled gradient conditionally unbiased.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agents be indexed by \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Agent \(i\) holds \(m_i\) differentiable component functions \(f_{ij}:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) and has local objective \(f_i(x)=m_i^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}f_{ij}(x)\). Let \(\mathcal F_k\) denote the history before iteration-\(k\) sampling, with \(x_i^k\) measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_k\). Independent sampling uses indices that are conditionally independent across agents, with fresh draws over iterations. Common-randomness sampling uses a shared random variable or seed that may induce dependence among the agents' indices. Random reshuffling draws a permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,m_i\}\) for each local epoch and visits every component once in that order. If \(\mathbb P(\xi_i^k=j\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_{ij}>0\), then the importance-weighted estimator \(g_i^k=(m_i p_{i\xi_i^k})^{-1}\nabla f_{i\xi_i^k}(x_i^k)\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\).
assumptions_latex: \(n,d,m_i\) are positive integers, and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
Each \(f_{ij}:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
The iterate \(x_i^k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and \(\mathbb P(\xi_i^k=j\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_{ij}>0\) with \(\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}p_{ij}=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampling conventions for local finite-sum objectives in gradient-tracking methods.

notation.meaning: history available immediately before iteration-k sampling
component index sampled by agent i at iteration k

children.title: Exact Decentralized Correction Methods
children.top_down_role: Bias-correction families that support exact optimization with persistent steps.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\), and let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a mixing matrix satisfying \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\). Consensus is \((I-W)X=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic constant-stepsize decentralized first-order schemes whose additional state removes the fixed-point bias of plain consensus-plus-local-gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An exact decentralized correction method is an iteration on a primal state \(X^k\) and correction state \(C^k\) of the form \(X^{k+1}=\mathcal M_W(X^k-\alpha G(X^k))+C^k\), \(C^{k+1}=\mathcal U_W(C^k,X^{k+1},X^k,G(X^k),G(X^{k-1}))\), with fixed \(\alpha>0\), where \(G(X)=(
abla f_1(x_1),\ldots,
abla f_n(x_n))\). It is exact when every fixed point reachable under its initialization satisfies \((I-W)X^\infty=0\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^n
abla f_i(x_i^\infty)=0\); hence \(X^\infty=\mathbf1(x^\star)^	op\) with \(x^\star\) stationary for \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact decentralized correction method augments mixed local-gradient descent with a correction state. Exactness means that its fixed-point equations enforce both consensus and the unweighted aggregate first-order condition, so a persistent stepsize does not leave the network-dependent steady-state bias of ordinary decentralized gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness is the fixed-point implication \(X^\infty\in\ker(I-W)\) and \(\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^\infty)=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(F\) is convex and differentiable, the fixed-point condition is equivalent to \(X^\infty=\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\) for some \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\).
special_cases_latex: Gradient tracking, EXTRA-type successive-difference recursions, and exact diffusion can realize the correction state in different coordinates.
immediate_consequences_latex: The defining property excludes a nonzero constant-stepsize neighborhood error at an attracting fixed point.
boundary_notes: Exactness is a fixed-point property, not by itself a convergence theorem.
Weighted objectives require a correspondingly weighted aggregate stationarity condition.

notation.meaning: A communication mixing operation induced by the network weights.
Auxiliary state producing the bias correction.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\), \(G(X^k)\) stack local gradients, \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\alpha>0\). Define a provisional mixed-gradient update \(Z^{k+1}=WX^k-\alpha G(X^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural family definition covering two-step primal recursions whose correction is the difference of consecutive provisional network updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A successive-difference exact-correction method is a second-order recursion initialized by \(X^1=Z^1\) and, for \(k\ge1\), defined by \(X^{k+1}=X^k+Z^{k+1}-\widetilde Z^k\), where \(Z^{k+1}=A X^k-\alpha G(X^k)\) and \(\widetilde Z^k=B X^{k-1}-\alpha G(X^{k-1})\) for network-compatible linear maps \(A,B\). Equivalently, \(X^{k+1}=(I+A)X^k-BX^{k-1}-\alpha\bigl(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\bigr)\). The family is exact-correcting when its stationary equations imply consensus and aggregate stationarity rather than the biased equation \((I-W)X+\alpha G(X)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family consists of two-step decentralized recursions that add the difference between a current provisional network-gradient update and a preceding provisional update. The resulting recursion contains a difference of successive local gradients, and its admissible network operators are chosen so that stationary states satisfy consensus and aggregate stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining recurrence is \(X^{k+1}=(I+A)X^k-BX^{k-1}-\alpha(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1}))\), together with the exact fixed-point conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing \(Z^{k+1}=AX^k-\alpha G(X^k)\) rewrites the two-step recursion as the correction form \(X^{k+1}=X^k+Z^{k+1}-\widetilde Z^k\).
special_cases_latex: Choices of \(A\) and \(B\) derived from symmetric mixing matrices produce EXTRA-like or diffusion-like recursions.
immediate_consequences_latex: At a stationary trajectory the successive-gradient difference vanishes, so exactness must be encoded by the network operators and initialization invariant.
boundary_notes: Arbitrary \(A\) and \(B\) do not guarantee exactness or convergence.
This definition excludes one-state consensus-gradient iterations lacking a successive-difference correction.

Explicit Unstable Quadratic EXTRA Instance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with two connected agents and identical strongly convex quadratics, canonically initialized EXTRA diverges or oscillates when its stepsize is too large.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two agents use \(W=\tfrac12\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\), \(\widetilde W=(I+W)/2\), and \(f_i(x)=\tfrac q2x^2\) with \(q>0\). Initialize \(X^0=c\mathbf1\), \(c\ne0\), and set \(X^1=WX^0-\alpha\nabla f(X^0)=(1-\alpha q)c\mathbf1\). The EXTRA recurrence remains in the consensus subspace and satisfies \(X^k=(1-\alpha q)^kc\mathbf1\). Therefore \(\alpha q>2\) gives divergence, while \(\alpha q=2\) gives a nonconvergent sign oscillation.
assumptions_latex: \(W=\tfrac12\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\widetilde W=(I+W)/2\).
\(f_i(x)=qx^2/2\) for both agents.
The canonical first-step initialization is used.
\(X^0=c\mathbf1\) with \(c\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha q>2\Longrightarrow\|X^k\|\to\infty,\qquad \alpha q=2\Longrightarrow X^k=(-1)^kc\mathbf1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of canonically initialized EXTRA when its constant stepsize exceeds the stable consensus-mode range.
review_flags: This establishes a necessary consensus-mode restriction, not the sharp full-network EXTRA stepsize theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correct fixed-point equations do not stabilize EXTRA; the mixing pair and stepsize must also stabilize its two-step dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For quadratic objectives, EXTRA induces a linear augmented error recurrence \(e^{k+1}_{\rm aug}=M_{\rm EXTRA}e^k_{\rm aug}\). Correct consensus and aggregate-stationarity equations do not ensure convergence: if \(\rho(M_{\rm EXTRA})\ge1\), some initial augmented errors fail to converge to zero.
assumptions_latex: The local objectives are quadratic.
The EXTRA recurrence is represented on its augmented two-step error state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(M_{\rm EXTRA})\ge1\Longrightarrow\text{failure for some initial augmented error}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between correct limiting equations and convergence of the two-step iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: EXTRA Limit-Point Optimality Equations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every limit of a canonically initialized EXTRA trajectory is consensual and aggregate-stationary, provided the mixing matrix has only the consensus fixed space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the canonical EXTRA trajectory converges to \(X^\star\), then \((I-W)X^\star=0\) and \(\mathbf1^\top\nabla f(X^\star)=0\). Hence, when \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\), \(X^\star=\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\) and \(\sum_i\nabla f_i(x^\star)=0\).

The canonical first-step initialization is used.
\(X^k\to X^\star\), and every \(f_i\) is differentiable.

knowledge_statements.title: EXTRA Method Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical smooth unconstrained EXTRA recursion on a static undirected network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(X)=\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x_i)\), let \(W\) and \(\widetilde W\) be symmetric mixing matrices, and write \(\mathbf W=W\otimes I_d\) and \(\widetilde{\mathbf W}=\widetilde W\otimes I_d\). From arbitrary \(X^0\), set
\[
X^1=\mathbf W X^0-\alpha\nabla F(X^0),
\]
and, for \(k\geq0\), update
\[
X^{k+2}=(I+\mathbf W)X^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf W}X^k-\alpha\bigl(\nabla F(X^{k+1})-\nabla F(X^k)\bigr).
\]
The standard choice is \(\widetilde W=(I+W)/2\). The successive gradient difference supplies the correction absent from ordinary decentralized gradient descent; output the local blocks of the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: EXTRA combines two mixing terms with a successive gradient difference to remove the fixed-stepsize bias of decentralized gradient descent.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable for every \(i\).
\(W\) and \(\widetilde W\) are symmetric and preserve \(\mathbf1\).
Their consensus nullspaces satisfy the standard EXTRA compatibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates are generated by the displayed two-step exact-correction recursion.

notation.meaning: stacked vector of all local iterates

Even for quadratic objectives, convergence additionally requires the companion matrix of the linear error recurrence to have spectral radius strictly below one; an inadmissible stepsize or mixing pair can violate this condition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-gradient extension of EXTRA derived from Condat–Vũ splitting and implemented without the square-root network operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\mathbf w^0=0\) and choose \(\mathbf x^0\) arbitrarily. PG-EXTRA iterates
\[
\mathbf x^{k+1}=\operatorname{Prox}_{\alpha f}\!\left(W\mathbf x^k-\alpha\nabla h(\mathbf x^k)-\mathbf w^k\right),
\qquad
\mathbf w^{k+1}=\mathbf w^k+\tfrac12(I-W)\mathbf x^k.
\]
It is decentralized when \(W\) is a decentralized mixing matrix. If total duality holds, \(h_1,\ldots,h_n\) are \(L\)-smooth, and \(0<\alpha<(1+\lambda_{\min}(W))/L\), then \(\mathbf x^k\to\mathbf x^\star\). EXTRA is the special case \(f=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from w^0 = 0 and arbitrary x^0, PG-EXTRA performs a proximal-gradient network update followed by an accumulated disagreement correction. It is decentralized when W is a decentralized mixing matrix. Under total duality, L-smoothness of the local smooth terms, and the stated network-dependent stepsize bound, x^k converges to x*. Setting f = 0 yields EXTRA.

Total duality holds
\(h_1,\ldots,h_n\) are \(L\)-smooth
\(0<\alpha<(1+\lambda_{\min}(W))/L\)
For decentralization, \(W\) is a decentralized mixing matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Stationarity Need Not Mean Minimization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact correction guarantees first-order stationarity only; without convexity the exact point can be a maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every agent have f_i(x)=-x^2. The consensual point X^\star=\mathbf1\,0 satisfies (I-W)X^\star=0 and \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(X^\star)=0, yet x^\star=0 is a strict maximizer of the aggregate objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Optimality Upgrade for an Exact Fixed Point
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex objectives an exact stationary fixed point is globally optimal; aggregate strong convexity makes its primal value unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the accepted exact-correction fixed-point conditions, if every f_i is convex, then F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i is convex and \nabla F(x^\star)=0 implies x^\star\in\arg\min F. If F is strongly convex, its minimizer and the consensual primal fixed point are unique.
assumptions_latex: The accepted exact-correction fixed-point conditions hold.
Each f_i is convex.
For uniqueness, F is strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\arg\min F;\qquad F\text{ strongly convex}\Rightarrow\arg\min F=\{x^\star\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Update Differences Are Not an Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero update difference can occur at a nonconsensual or nonstationary state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condition \(X^{k+1}-X^k\to0\) alone implies neither \((I-W)X^k\to0\) nor \(\mathbf1^\top G(X^k)\to0\). A constant nonconsensual sequence has zero update differences, and a constant consensual sequence can have nonzero aggregate first-order information.

knowledge_statements.title: Telescoping Successive-Correction Identity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive first-order differences telescope to an endpoint difference but do not alone imply stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Delta G^k=G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\), \[\sum_{k=1}^{K}\Delta G^k=G(X^K)-G(X^0).\] Thus accumulation of a successive-difference correction depends only on endpoint first-order maps; aggregate stationarity still requires a method-specific initialization invariant.
assumptions_latex: All \(G(X^k)\) belong to the same vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{k=1}^{K}\Delta G^k=G(X^K)-G(X^0).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic mechanism supplied by consecutive first-order differences.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact State-Difference Normal Form
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-step correction becomes a first-order system in the current state and its successive difference; the current-state coefficient is A1 minus A0 minus the identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \[X^{k+1}=A_1X^k-A_0X^{k-1}-\alpha\bigl(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\bigr)\] and define \(S^k=X^k-X^{k-1}\). Then the equivalent first-order system is \[S^{k+1}=(A_1-A_0-I)X^k+A_0S^k-\alpha\bigl(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\bigr),\qquad X^{k+1}=X^k+S^{k+1}.\] This coordinate change alone supplies no aggregate-stationarity invariant.
assumptions_latex: \(A_0\) and \(A_1\) are linear operators on the state space.
All displayed first-order-map values belong to the same vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S^{k+1}=(A_1-A_0-I)X^k+A_0S^k-\alpha\bigl(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\bigr).

knowledge_statements.title: Successive-Update Difference Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic mechanism underlying two-step exact decentralized corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) collect agent iterates, let \(G^k=\nabla F(X^k)\), and let \(W,\widetilde W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) preserve consensus. A successive-difference correction has the form \[X^{k+1}=(I+W)X^k-\widetilde W X^{k-1}-\alpha(G^k-G^{k-1}).\] At any convergent trajectory, the gradient-difference term vanishes while summing the fixed-point equation against the consensus left eigenvector yields aggregate stationarity. Thus the retained second-order state can cancel the persistent network disagreement that causes constant-step decentralized gradient descent to converge to a biased neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-step recursion uses differences of consecutive gradients and iterates so that its fixed points satisfy both consensus and aggregate first-order stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(W\mathbf 1=\widetilde W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\).
\(F(X)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\) is differentiable.
The displayed iteration converges to a consensus limit.

knowledge_statements.title: Common Local Minimizers Are Not Required

For f_1(x)=\tfrac12(x-1)^2 and f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x+1)^2, the local minimizer sets are disjoint, but their average has the unique minimizer x^\star=0, where the local gradients cancel.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Correction Applicability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions supporting exact constant-step correction on an undirected network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) over a fixed connected undirected network. Successive-difference exact correction is applicable when agents use a consensus-preserving mixing matrix \(W\) whose eigenvalue \(1\) is simple, exchange compatible primal states synchronously, and evaluate deterministic local gradients. For standard linear-convergence guarantees, additionally require each \(f_i\) to have a Lipschitz gradient, the aggregate objective to be strongly convex, and the constant step size \(\alpha\) to lie below the method-dependent stability threshold. Directed, time-varying, delayed, or stochastic settings require modified correction or tracking mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard exact correction applies to connected undirected mixing with compatible synchronous updates; smoothness, aggregate strong convexity, and a sufficiently small step yield the usual linear regime.

Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable with Lipschitz gradient.
\(f=\sum_i f_i\) is strongly convex and \(0<\alpha<\bar\alpha\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a nonnegative network mixing matrix and \(\bar A=(I+A)/2\). Agent \(i\) holds \(w_i^k,\psi_i^k,\phi_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\), a local loss \(f_i\), and a stepsize \(\mu_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapt-then-correct-then-combine exact-diffusion structure; deterministic gradients and unbiased stochastic gradients are both admitted through the oracle symbol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact diffusion is the three-stage recursion, for \(k\ge0\), \(\psi_i^{k+1}=w_i^k-\mu_i g_i(w_i^k;\xi_i^{k+1})\), \(\phi_i^{k+1}=\psi_i^{k+1}+w_i^k-\psi_i^k\), and \(w_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n\bar a_{ji}\phi_j^{k+1}\), with an initialization such as \(\psi_i^0=w_i^0\). The middle equality is the exact-diffusion correction: it retains the increment between consecutive adapted states while adding the preceding primal state before combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact diffusion is an adapt-correct-combine decentralized method. Each agent first takes a local gradient or sampled-gradient step, then forms a corrected state from the new adapted point, the current primal point, and the previous adapted point, and finally combines corrected states using the averaged network weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method is defined by the ordered adapt, correction, and combination equations with \(\bar A=(I+A)/2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Stacking agent variables gives \(\Psi^{k+1}=W^k-MG(W^k;\xi^{k+1})\), \(\Phi^{k+1}=\Psi^{k+1}+W^k-\Psi^k\), and \(W^{k+1}=\bar A^\top\Phi^{k+1}\).
special_cases_latex: Setting \(g_i(w;\xi)=\nabla f_i(w)\) gives deterministic exact diffusion.
Using an unbiased sampled gradient gives stochastic exact diffusion.
immediate_consequences_latex: The correction stage disappears only if consecutive adapted states coincide; it is distinct from ordinary adapt-then-combine diffusion.
boundary_notes: The recursion alone does not guarantee convergence; graph, weight, objective, and stepsize conditions are separate.
Transpose placement depends on whether agent states are stacked by rows or columns.

notation.meaning: Weight with which agent i combines the corrected state received from agent j.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Exact Diffusion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic exact diffusion applies a local gradient step, a one-step bias correction, and neighbor averaging at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a symmetric doubly stochastic mixing matrix and \(\bar A=(I+A)/2\). Each agent initializes \(x_i^0\), computes \(\psi_i^0=x_i^0-\alpha\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\), sets \(\phi_i^0=\psi_i^0\), and combines \(x_i^1=\sum_j\bar a_{ij}\phi_j^0\). For \(k\ge1\), it performs \[\psi_i^k=x_i^k-\alpha\nabla f_i(x_i^k),\qquad \phi_i^k=\psi_i^k+x_i^k-\psi_i^{k-1},\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_j\bar a_{ij}\phi_j^k.\] Stop when the consensus residual and successive-step norm satisfy prescribed tolerances; output the agents' final iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^\top\), \(A\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and the induced graph is connected.
Each \(f_i\) is differentiable and its exact gradient is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_j\bar a_{ij}\bigl(\psi_j^k+x_j^k-\psi_j^{k-1}\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapt-correct-combine exact diffusion with deterministic local gradients.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the adapt-correct-combine recurrence is the canonical deterministic exact-diffusion form

However, the initialization and index convention must be matched to a primary exact-diffusion source, and the orientation of the coefficients in the combine step must be consistent with that source's stochasticity convention. The missing source makes the precise algorithm unreliable.

children.title: Stochastic Exact Diffusion
children.top_down_role: Exact diffusion with sampled local information.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Exact Diffusion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic exact diffusion replaces each exact local gradient by an unbiased bounded-variance sample while retaining adapt-correct-combine updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the deterministic exact-diffusion initialization and mixing matrix, but at iteration \(k\) let agent \(i\) obtain \(g_i^k=g_i(x_i^k,\xi_i^k)\). It updates \[\psi_i^k=x_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k,\qquad \phi_i^k=\psi_i^k+x_i^k-\psi_i^{k-1},\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_j\bar a_{ij}\phi_j^k.\] The oracle must satisfy \(\mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|g_i^k-\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma_i^2\). Stop at a prescribed iteration budget or residual tolerance and output the last iterate or a specified time average.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\).
\(\mathbb E[\|g_i^k-\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma_i^2<\infty\).
The mixing matrix satisfies the deterministic exact-diffusion connectivity conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_j\bar a_{ij}\bigl(\psi_j^k+x_j^k-\psi_j^{k-1}\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact diffusion using conditionally unbiased sampled local gradients.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unbiased bounded-variance substitution is the canonical stochastic specialization

children.title: Primal-Dual Views of Exact Correction
children.top_down_role: Constraint-dual interpretations of exact decentralized methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Constraints Yield Only Componentwise Correction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a connected consensus operator, primal-dual correction enforces componentwise consensus and stationarity rather than the intended global problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \ker B\supsetneq\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}, then BX=0 permits distinct constants on different connected components. Moreover, G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0 implies G\perp\ker B, imposing zero gradient sum on each component rather than only globally.
assumptions_latex: \ker B strictly contains the global-consensus subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: BX=0\not\Rightarrow X\in\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\},\qquad G\in\operatorname{range}(B^{\mathsf T})\Rightarrow G\perp\ker B.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity boundary for interpreting correction states as global-consensus multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Correction Exists Exactly for Zero Aggregate Gradient
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a connected consensus operator, a multiplier cancels heterogeneous local gradients exactly when they sum to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n} satisfy \ker B=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}. For G\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}, \exists Y\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}:G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0 if and only if \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}G=0.
assumptions_latex: \ker B=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -G\in\operatorname{range}(B^{\mathsf T})\iff\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}G=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range characterization explaining how a multiplier balances heterogeneous local gradients.

notation.meaning: stacked local gradients at a consensual state

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Gauge Freedom
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant consensus constraints make the correction state nonunique without altering primal stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Y satisfies G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0, then Y+H satisfies it for every H\in\ker(B^{\mathsf T}). Thus the correction state is unique only modulo \ker(B^{\mathsf T}) unless a gauge or full-row-rank constraint representation is imposed.
assumptions_latex: A multiplier Y satisfying G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0 exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{\widetilde Y:G+B^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Y=0\}=Y+\ker(B^{\mathsf T}).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of correction states under redundant consensus constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Views of Exact Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-constrained saddle representation of exact decentralized correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\), let \(F(X)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\), and choose a linear map \(B\) satisfying \(\ker B=\{\mathbf1\otimes x:x\in\mathbb R^d\}\). The decentralized problem is equivalently \[\min_X F(X)\quad\text{subject to}\quad BX=0,\] with Lagrangian \(L(X,Y)=F(X)+\langle Y,BX\rangle\) and optimality inclusion \[0\in \begin{pmatrix}\partial F&B^\top\\-B&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}X\\Y\end{pmatrix}.\] Exact-correction state variables can therefore be interpreted as transformed dual variables accumulating consensus-constraint violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus optimization is a linearly constrained problem whose dual variable accumulates disagreement; exact-correction memory can be viewed as a transformed dual state.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\ker B\) equals the consensus subspace.
A saddle point of \(L\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consensus optimality is equivalent to the displayed primal-dual monotone inclusion.
