knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual representation of exact decentralized correction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal F(X)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) on \(\mathbb R^{n\times d}\). Let \(V\) be a graph operator with \(\ker V=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\), so consensus is \(VX=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-dual interpretation of exact decentralized methods on a fixed connected network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal-dual view of exact correction represents the decentralized problem as \(\min_X\mathcal F(X)\) subject to \(VX=0\), with Lagrangian \(\mathcal L(X,\Lambda)=\mathcal F(X)+\langle\Lambda,VX\rangle\). The associated optimality system is \(0=\nabla\mathcal F(X^\star)+V^\top\Lambda^\star\) and \(VX^\star=0\). A correction state is primal-dual when there exists an invertible or explicitly specified linear coordinate map relating it to \(V^\top\Lambda^k\), and elimination of \(\Lambda^k\) from the primal-dual iteration yields the stated exact-correction primal recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual view lifts one decision variable per agent and imposes consensus as a linear equality constraint. A dual multiplier supplies the correction needed to balance heterogeneous local gradients. A decentralized correction state has this view when it is a linear coordinate representation of the multiplier action and eliminating the multiplier recovers the primal exact-correction recursion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining saddle system is \(\nabla\mathcal F(X^\star)+V^\top\Lambda^\star=0\) and \(VX^\star=0\), with the correction state representing \(V^\top\Lambda^k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The system is the monotone inclusion \(0\in(\nabla\mathcal F(X)+V^\top\Lambda,-VX)\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(V=(I-W)^{1/2}\) for a symmetric mixing matrix expresses graph consensus through the mixing operator.
immediate_consequences_latex: Summing the primal stationarity equations over agents cancels the dual graph term and yields aggregate stationarity.
boundary_notes: Not every algebraic auxiliary variable is a dual multiplier without a valid coordinate map.
Directed graphs may require nonsymmetric constraints or weighted inner products.

notation.meaning: Multiplier for the lifted consensus constraint.

review_flags: General primal-dual facts are standard, but no inspected source tied this formulation to the exact-correction family.

children.title: Operator-Splitting Views of Exact Correction
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point and monotone-inclusion interpretations of exact methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Naive Forward Treatment of Skew Consensus Coupling Is Expansive
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero skew consensus coupling cannot be used naively as the forward component of ordinary forward-backward splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal K be a nonzero bounded skew-adjoint linear operator. For every \gamma>0 and z, \|(I-\gamma\mathcal K)z\|^2=\|z\|^2+\gamma^2\|\mathcal Kz\|^2. Thus the forward map is expansive on every direction for which \mathcal Kz\ne0.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal K^*=-\mathcal K and \mathcal K\ne0.
\gamma>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal Kz\ne0\Longrightarrow\|(I-\gamma\mathcal K)z\|>\|z\|;\text{ a separate splitting or preconditioner analysis is required}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting the consensus primal-dual inclusion as ordinary forward-backward splitting.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Splitting Views of Exact Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone-inclusion and fixed-point representation of consensus correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the consensus-constrained convex problem, define on the primal-dual product space \[\mathcal A(X,Y)=(\partial F(X),0),\qquad \mathcal B(X,Y)=(B^\top Y,-BX).\] Then the optimality system is \(0\in(\mathcal A+\mathcal B)(X,Y)\). Whenever the chosen preconditioner \(P\) makes the relevant resolvents well defined, a splitting method generates a fixed-point iteration \[Z^{k+1}=T(Z^k),\qquad \operatorname{Fix}T=\operatorname{zer}(\mathcal A+\mathcal B).\] Eliminating or linearly transforming the dual component of such an iteration produces the two-step correction memory appearing in several exact decentralized primal recursions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact decentralized corrections can arise by splitting the primal-dual consensus inclusion and eliminating the dual state, leaving a two-step primal fixed-point iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(B\) is linear and its kernel is the consensus subspace.
The preconditioned splitting operator \(T\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\operatorname{zer}(\mathcal A+\mathcal B)\), and its primal fixed points solve consensus optimization.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=(\mathbb R^d)^n\), let \(C=\{X:x_1=\cdots=x_n\}\), and let \(N_C\) denote its normal-cone operator. Let \(A=\partial\mathcal F+N_C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point and monotone-inclusion interpretation for convex lifted consensus optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An operator-splitting view of exact correction expresses the decentralized optimality condition as the monotone inclusion \(0\in\partial\mathcal F(X)+N_C(X)\) and represents the algorithm, possibly after adding auxiliary coordinates, as \(Z^{k+1}=T(Z^k)\), where \(T\) is a composition or averaged combination of resolvents and explicit forward steps associated with the objective and consensus operators. The representation is exact when \(P_X(\operatorname{Fix}T)=\operatorname*{zer}(\partial\mathcal F+N_C)\), where \(P_X\) projects the lifted state onto its primal coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The operator-splitting view regards consensus optimization as finding a zero of the sum of the lifted objective subdifferential and the normal cone to the consensus subspace. An exact-correction algorithm is then a fixed-point iteration on primal and auxiliary coordinates whose fixed points project precisely onto solutions of that inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness is the fixed-point identity \(P_X(\operatorname{Fix}T)=\operatorname*{zer}(\partial\mathcal F+N_C)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For proper closed convex \(\mathcal F\), \(0\in\partial\mathcal F(X)+N_C(X)\) is equivalent to \(X\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Z\in C}\mathcal F(Z)\).
special_cases_latex: Forward-backward, Douglas-Rachford, and primal-dual splittings correspond to different choices of lifted operator \(T\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A spurious fixed point whose primal projection is not consensual violates exactness.
boundary_notes: A claimed splitting identity requires specification of the metric and auxiliary-coordinate transformation.
Nonconvex objectives generally replace maximal-monotone theory with a different fixed-point framework.

children.title: Directed-Network Distributed Optimization Methods
children.top_down_role: Normalization and mixed-stochasticity methods for asymmetric networks.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G^k=(V,E^k)\) be a directed communication graph on \(n\) agents, and let agent \(i\) know only local \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\). The global objective is \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-family definition for asymmetric communication using normalization or distinct stochastic mixing operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A directed-network optimization method is a distributed iteration in which each agent updates finite-dimensional local states from its own oracle and messages received along incoming directed edges, and whose communication operators need not be doubly stochastic. To target the unweighted objective \(F\), the iteration includes either a positive normalization state \(s_i^k\) with a ratio \(x_i^k=z_i^k/s_i^k\), or distinct primal and tracking operators \(R^k,C^k\) satisfying \(R^k\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\mathbf1^\top C^k=\mathbf1^\top\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed-network optimization comprises decentralized methods for asymmetric communication graphs. Because one mixing matrix generally cannot preserve both consensus and the unweighted sum, these methods use either push-sum normalization or separate row-stochastic and column-stochastic operators for the primal and tracking states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining structure combines directed-edge-local communication with either ratio normalization or mixed stochasticity that preserves the intended unweighted aggregate objective.
special_cases_latex: Push-sum methods use a column-stochastic mass update and normalize by an accompanying scalar mass.
Push-pull methods use a row-stochastic primal operator and a column-stochastic gradient-tracking operator.
immediate_consequences_latex: A plain consensus-gradient method using only a generic asymmetric stochastic matrix may optimize a stationary-distribution-weighted objective instead of \(F\).
boundary_notes: Directedness alone does not imply time variation.
Convergence additionally requires connectivity, positivity, oracle, and stepsize conditions.

notation.meaning: Row-stochastic primal and column-stochastic tracking operators.

children.title: Push-Sum Consensus
children.top_down_role: Ratio-based averaging under mass-preserving directed communication.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Hull Certificate for the Conserved-Mass Ratio
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conserved target is a positive weighted average of the current ratios, so an exact global ratio spread bounds every node's error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_i^k>0\), \(x_i^k=s_i^k/w_i^k\), and suppose numerator and denominator masses are conserved. Then \[\bar x=\frac{\sum_i s_i^k}{\sum_i w_i^k}=\frac{\sum_i w_i^k x_i^k}{\sum_i w_i^k}\in[\min_i x_i^k,\max_i x_i^k].\] Hence an exact global-extrema computation satisfying \(\max_i x_i^k-\min_i x_i^k\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(|x_i^k-\bar x|\le\varepsilon\) for every node.
assumptions_latex: The push-sum states are scalar.
\(w_i^k>0\) for every node.
Numerator and denominator masses are conserved.
The extrema refer to one common snapshot and are computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_i x_i^k-\min_i x_i^k\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow\max_i|x_i^k-\bar x|\le\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Snapshot ratio-spread certificate for scalar push-sum states with positive denominator masses.

notation.meaning: conserved numerator mass divided by conserved denominator mass

review_flags: For vector states, a coordinatewise or separately justified convex-hull diameter certificate is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Matrix Push-Sum Communication Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric push-sum contraction gives logarithmic round complexity in inverse accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(e_k\le C'\rho^k\), then \(e_k\le\varepsilon\) whenever \(k\ge\left\lceil\log(C'/\varepsilon)/(-\log\rho)\right\rceil\). With one directed exchange stage per iteration, this is also the communication-round bound.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration has one directed communication stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_\varepsilon=O\left(\frac{\log(C'/\varepsilon)}{-\log\rho}\right).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication rounds implied by geometric ratio contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Unnormalized Directed Mixing Is Generally Biased
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column-stochastic directed mixing alone approaches a nonuniform Perron profile; push-sum denominators remove that bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be primitive and column-stochastic with \(A^k\to\pi\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\). Unless \(\pi=\mathbf1/n\), \(A^ks^0\to\pi\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0\), whose components are unequal for generic nonzero total mass. Division by \(A^kw^0\) cancels this Perron profile.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is primitive and column-stochastic.
Its normalized right Perron vector is nonuniform.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^ks^0\not\to\mathbf1(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0/n)\) for generic \(s^0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of ratio normalization on unbalanced directed graphs.

notation.meaning: normalized positive right Perron vector of A

knowledge_statements.title: Mass Conservation and Scale Invariance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push-sum conserves numerator and denominator mass separately, and common positive rescaling leaves all ratios unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s^{k+1}=As^k\) and \(w^{k+1}=Aw^k\) with column-stochastic \(A\), \[\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^k=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0,\qquad \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^k=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0.\] Replacing \((s^0,w^0)\) by \((cs^0,cw^0)\), \(c>0\), leaves every defined ratio \(s_i^k/w_i^k\) unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is column-stochastic.
Ratios are evaluated only where denominators are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^k=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0\), \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^k=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0\), and the ratios are scale invariant.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining algebraic invariants of push-sum normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Fixed-Matrix Ratio Consensus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perron convergence yields geometric convergence of fixed-matrix push-sum ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be primitive and column-stochastic, \(A^k=\pi\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}+R_k\), and \(\|R_k\|\le C\rho^k\) with \(0<\rho<1\). For \(s^k=A^ks^0\), \(w^k=A^kw^0\), and \(w^0>0\), there are \(C'>0\) and \(k_0\) such that \(\max_i\|s_i^k/w_i^k-(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0)/(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0)\|\le C'\rho^k\) for \(k\ge k_0\).
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is primitive and column-stochastic.
The displayed Perron remainder bound holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_i\left\|x_i^k-\frac{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0}{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0}\right\|=O(\rho^k).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-time convergence consequence for fixed primitive column-stochastic push-sum dynamics.
review_flags: Constants depend on the Perron vector and denominator lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Push-Sum Consensus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio consensus for a fixed directed column-stochastic network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R_+^{n\times n}\) be column stochastic and primitive. Initialize \(s_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and positive \(q_i^0\), and for \(k\ge0\) update \[s_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}s_j^k,\qquad q_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}q_j^k,\qquad z_i^{k+1}=s_i^{k+1}/q_i^{k+1}.\] Stop at a prescribed tolerance or iteration limit and output \(z_i^k\). Then every ratio converges to \[\lim_{k\to\infty}z_i^k=\frac{\sum_j s_j^0}{\sum_j q_j^0}.\] In particular, \(q_j^0=1\) yields the arithmetic average of the initial vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents propagate a vector mass and a positive scalar mass through column-stochastic directed mixing; their ratio converges to the normalized global sum.
assumptions_latex: \(A\ge0\), \(\mathbf1^\top A=\mathbf1^\top\), and \(A\) is primitive.
\(q_i^0>0\) for every agent \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_i^k\to(\sum_j s_j^0)/(\sum_j q_j^0)\) for every \(i\).
review_flags: A directed-consensus source with a precise push-sum convergence theorem is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and ratio limit are mathematically standard for a primitive column-stochastic matrix with positive initial weights, and the algorithm kind fits the leaf. However, the nontrivial convergence guarantee has no cited source.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For each \(k\), let \(A^k=[a_{ij}^k]\ge0\) be column stochastic, \(\mathbf1^\top A^k=\mathbf1^\top\), and compatible with a directed graph. Let \(z_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(s_i^0>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio-based averaging under mass-preserving directed communication; convergence conditions are separated into their own slot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Push-sum consensus is the coupled linear recursion \(z^{k+1}=A^kz^k\), \(s^{k+1}=A^ks^k\), together with the componentwise normalized estimate \(x_i^{k+1}=z_i^{k+1}/s_i^{k+1}\), for every agent \(i\) with \(s_i^{k+1}>0\). With the canonical initialization \(s^0=\mathbf1\), the two transported quantities have conserved totals \(\mathbf1^\top z^k=\mathbf1^\top z^0\) and \(\mathbf1^\top s^k=n\); the ratio removes the nonuniform right-eigenvector scaling caused by directed column-stochastic mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push-sum consensus transports a vector numerator and a positive scalar mass through the same column-stochastic directed mixing matrices. Each agent divides its numerator by its mass. With unit initial masses, the conserved numerator and denominator totals encode the arithmetic average even though the individual masses need not converge uniformly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The push-sum estimate is defined by \(x_i^k=z_i^k/s_i^k\) after identical column-stochastic updates of \(z^k\) and \(s^k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Let \(S^k=\operatorname{diag}(s^k)\); then \(x^{k+1}=(S^{k+1})^{-1}A^kS^kx^k\) whenever all masses are positive.
special_cases_latex: If every \(A^k\) is doubly stochastic and \(s^0=\mathbf1\), then \(s^k=\mathbf1\) and push-sum reduces to ordinary linear consensus.
immediate_consequences_latex: Column stochasticity preserves total numerator and total mass at every iteration.
boundary_notes: The recursion is well-defined only where denominators remain positive.
Mass conservation alone does not guarantee ratio consensus without connectivity and weight conditions.

notation.meaning: Numerator, normalization mass, and normalized estimate at agent i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-time convergence consequence for fixed primitive column-stochastic push-sum dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be primitive and column-stochastic, let \(A^k=\pi\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}+R_k\) with \(\|R_k\|\le C\rho^k\), \(0<\rho<1\), and initialize \(w^0>0\). For \(s^k=A^ks^0\), \(w^k=A^kw^0\), and \(x_i^k=s_i^k/w_i^k\), there exist finite \(C'>0\) and \(k_0\) such that \[\max_i\left\|x_i^k-\frac{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0}{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0}\right\|\le C'\rho^k\qquad(k\ge k_0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perron convergence of a fixed primitive column-stochastic matrix yields geometric convergence of every push-sum ratio.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is primitive and column-stochastic.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Bias Without Push-Sum Normalization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without normalization, directed mixing can optimize a Perron-weighted objective instead of the intended uniform aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let directed mixing have nonuniform stationary influence weights \(\pi_i>0\). Without normalization or an equivalent correction, a directed descent method may target \(F_\pi(x)=\sum_i\pi_i f_i(x)\) rather than \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\). For \(f_i(x)=\tfrac12(x-a_i)^2\), the respective minimizers are \(\sum_i\pi_i a_i\) and \(n^{-1}\sum_i a_i\), which differ for suitable \(a_i\).
assumptions_latex: The directed influence vector \(\pi\) is nonuniform.
No normalization or stationary-distribution correction is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_i\pi_i f_i(x)\ne\operatorname*{argmin}_x n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\) for some quadratic local objectives.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed-objective weighting error caused by omitting ratio correction.

knowledge_statements.title: Push-Sum Optimization Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed distributed descent normalized by push-sum weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_{ij}]\) be a primitive column-stochastic mixing matrix. Initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\), \(q_i^0=1\), and \(z_i^0=x_i^0\). For \(k\ge0\), agent \(i\) computes a local gradient or subgradient \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(z_i^k)\) and updates \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_j a_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha_k g_i^k,\qquad q_i^{k+1}=\sum_j a_{ij}q_j^k,\qquad z_i^{k+1}=x_i^{k+1}/q_i^{k+1}.\] Stop according to a declared criterion and output the terminal or weighted-average ratio iterate. The normalization compensates for non-doubly-stochastic directed mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push-sum optimization combines column-stochastic mixing, local descent, and ratio normalization to compensate for directed-network imbalance.
assumptions_latex: \(A\ge0\), \(\mathbf1^\top A=\mathbf1^\top\), and \(A\) is primitive.
Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is convex and admits the selected subgradient.
\(\alpha_k>0\) follows the convergence regime specified for the chosen variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs a normalized local estimate \(z_i\) of a minimizer of \(\sum_i f_i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Push-Pull Optimization Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents use a row-stochastic operator for primal mixing and a column-stochastic operator for gradient tracking, thereby accommodating directed communication without a common doubly stochastic matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a stepsize \(\alpha>0\), initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\). Stack the local variables as \(x^k\) and \(y^k\). The push-pull iteration is
\[
x^{k+1}=Rx^k-\alpha y^k,\qquad y^{k+1}=Cy^k+\nabla f(x^{k+1})-\nabla f(x^k),
\]
where the gradient map is applied blockwise. The row-stochastic operator forms primal averages, while the column-stochastic operator preserves the sum of tracking variables. Stop under a prescribed consensus-stationarity tolerance or budget and return the agent states.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.
The primal matrix \(R\) is row-stochastic and the tracking matrix \(C\) is column-stochastic.
All products and communicated entries are well defined on the directed graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration couples row-stochastic primal mixing with column-stochastic tracking of the aggregate gradient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-matrix push-pull gradient method with separate directed mixing operators.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R\ge0\) be row stochastic, \(R\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and let \(C\ge0\) be column stochastic, \(\mathbf1^\top C=\mathbf1^\top\). Stack primal states in \(X^k\) and trackers in \(Y^k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A push-pull optimization method is the coupled recursion \(X^{k+1}=RX^k-\Alpha Y^k\) and \(Y^{k+1}=CY^k+G(X^{k+1})-G(X^k)\), initialized by \(Y^0=G(X^0)\), where \(G(X)\) stacks local gradients and \(\Alpha\) is a nonnegative diagonal stepsize matrix. The row-stochastic operator pulls primal information toward consensus, while the column-stochastic operator pushes tracking mass so that \(\mathbf1^\top Y^k=\mathbf1^\top G(X^k)\) under the stated initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push-pull optimization uses two distinct directed mixing matrices. A row-stochastic matrix mixes primal states, and a column-stochastic matrix transports gradient trackers. The tracker is corrected by successive local-gradient differences and initialized at the local gradients, which preserves its aggregate-gradient identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining push-pull structure is \(X^{k+1}=RX^k-\Alpha Y^k\), \(Y^{k+1}=CY^k+G(X^{k+1})-G(X^k)\), with \(Y^0=G(X^0)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tracker invariant is \(\mathbf1^\top Y^k=\mathbf1^\top G(X^k)\) for all \(k\ge0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(R=C=W\) is doubly stochastic, the recursion becomes standard gradient tracking on a balanced network.
immediate_consequences_latex: No explicit push-sum ratio is required because stochasticity is split between the two state channels.
boundary_notes: Compatibility and connectivity of the graphs induced by \(R\) and \(C\) are needed for convergence but are not part of the recursion alone.
Some conventions transpose both operators depending on state stacking.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Fixed-Point Boundary of Combine-Then-Proximal Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consensual fixed point of plain constant-step proximal consensus must solve every local composite problem, which is stronger than solving their sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(\alpha>0\) and row-stochastic \(W\), a consensual state \(x_i=x^*\) is a fixed point of the accepted update exactly when, for every agent,
\[
x^*=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r_i}(x^*-\alpha\nabla f_i(x^*))
\iff0\in\nabla f_i(x^*)+\partial r_i(x^*).
\]
Aggregate stationarity does not generally imply these agentwise conditions.
assumptions_latex: The accepted combine-then-proximal recursion uses fixed \(\alpha>0\).
\(W\) is row-stochastic.
Each \(r_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, and each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf1\otimes x^*\text{ is fixed}\iff0\in\nabla f_i(x^*)+\partial r_i(x^*)\ \forall i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact obstruction to aggregate optimality for the accepted uncorrected constant-step recursion.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Consensus Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent averages neighboring iterates, takes a local gradient step, and applies its local proximal map to handle nonsmooth structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) forms the consensus point \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k\), obtains \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(v_i^k)\), and computes
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k r_i}\!\left(v_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k\right),
\qquad
\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(u)=\mathop{\arg\min}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\{r(x)+\frac{\lVert x-u\rVert^2}{2\alpha}\right\}.
\]
Agents exchange the new iterates and repeat. Stop under a prescribed consensus-optimality residual or budget and return the local states.
assumptions_latex: Each agent has a proper closed convex proximable function \(r_i\) and a convex differentiable function \(f_i\).
The mixing matrix \(W=[w_{ij}]\) is nonnegative and row-stochastic.
The stepsize \(\alpha_k>0\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each new local iterate is a proximal correction of a consensus-mixed point using local first-order information.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic combine-then-proximal-gradient consensus scheme for composite convex objectives.

The proximal map is \(\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(v)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\{r(x)+(2\alpha)^{-1}\|x-v\|^2\}\), interpreted as set-valued when the minimizer is not unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal consensus method first combines neighboring states and optionally applies a smooth first-order displacement, then evaluates a local proximal map. The proximal map handles a nonsmooth regularizer or constraint while communication drives local copies toward agreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Tracker-Initialization Bias in Proximal Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incorrect tracker initialization creates a permanent aggregate offset and shifts the fixed-point stationarity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For doubly stochastic mixing and the gradient-difference tracker recursion, define
\[
\delta=\sum_i y_i^0-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^0).
\]
Then
\[
\sum_i y_i^k-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)=\delta
\]
for every \(k\). At a consensual fixed point with tracker consensus, the proximal condition is therefore shifted to
\[
0\in\nabla F(x^*)+{\delta\over n}+\partial r(x^*),
\]
so true composite stationarity is not guaranteed unless \(\delta=0\).
assumptions_latex: The tracker update uses doubly stochastic mixing and gradient differences.
A consensual fixed point with tracker consensus exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta\ne0\Longrightarrow\text{the fixed-point condition is generally }0\in\nabla F(x^*)+\delta/n+\partial r(x^*).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent aggregate offset caused by incorrect tracker initialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensual Fixed Points Are Composite Stationary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any consensual fixed point of correctly initialized proximal gradient tracking is stationary for the aggregate smooth objective plus the common regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\). Suppose the fixed mixing matrix \(W\) is doubly stochastic with \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\), the tracker invariant \(\sum_i y_i=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i)\) holds, and the displayed proximal gradient-tracking recursion has a fixed point with \(x_i=x^*\) for every \(i\). The tracker fixed-point equation then makes all \(y_i\) equal to \(\nabla F(x^*)\), and
\[
x^*=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(x^*-\alpha y_i)
\iff0\in\nabla F(x^*)+\partial r(x^*).
\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is differentiable and \(r\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(W\) is doubly stochastic and has only consensus fixed vectors.
The tracker-sum invariant and the fixed-point equations of the common-regularizer recursion hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i=x^*\ \forall i\text{ at a fixed point}\Longrightarrow0\in\nabla F(x^*)+\partial r(x^*).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness property of a correctly initialized common-regularizer proximal gradient-tracking recursion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)+r(x)\), initialize \(x_i^0\in\operatorname{dom}r\) and \(y_i^0=
abla f_i(x_i^0)\). With a fixed doubly stochastic mixing matrix \(W\) and \(\alpha>0\), iterate \[v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(v_i^k-\alpha y_i^k),\] \[y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+
abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x_i^k).\] Stop when consensus and composite stationarity residuals are below specified tolerances, and output the local iterates or their average.

\(W\) is graph-compatible, primitive, and doubly stochastic.
The stepsize \(\alpha\) is chosen within the method's stability range.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, synchronous composite optimization with a proximal step and dynamic tracking of the aggregate smooth gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proximal gradient-tracking method is an iteration with local primal states \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) and trackers \(y_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) satisfying, for every agent \(i\) and iteration \(k\), \[z_i^k=\sum_{j=1}^m w_{ij}^k x_j^k-\alpha_k y_i^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k r}(z_i^k),\] \[y_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^m w_{ij}^k y_j^k+
abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x_i^k),\qquad y_i^0=
abla f_i(x_i^0),\] where \(\alpha_k>0\) and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(v)=\arg\min_u\{r(u)+(2\alpha)^{-1}\|u-v\|^2\}\). The defining feature is the simultaneous proximal composite update and gradient-increment tracking recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent mixes neighboring primal states, subtracts a local estimate of the network-average gradient, applies the proximal map of the common nonsmooth term, and updates that gradient estimate by mixing old trackers and adding its own gradient increment. Initialization sets each tracker to the corresponding local gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is defined by the displayed proximal primal recursion and dynamic gradient-tracking recursion for every \(i\) and \(k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With stacked variables and componentwise proximal mapping, the recursion can be written as \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k R}(W^k x^k-\alpha_k y^k)\) and \(y^{k+1}=W^k y^k+\nabla f(x^{k+1})-\nabla f(x^k)\), where \(R(x)=\sum_i r(x_i)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(r\equiv0\), the proximal map is the identity and the method reduces to smooth gradient tracking.
If \(W^k=J:=m^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\) and the states are consensual, the primal step coincides with centralized proximal-gradient descent.
immediate_consequences_latex: If every \(W^k\) is doubly stochastic, then \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\) for every \(k\), provided the stated initialization is used.
boundary_notes: Variants may reverse the order of mixing and the proximal map, use agent-specific regularizers, or employ push-sum weights; those variants require separate definitions.
No convergence claim is included.

notation.meaning: Network mixing matrix at iteration k.

children.title: Distributed Non-Euclidean Descent Family
children.top_down_role: Network methods adapted to non-Euclidean decision geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed and convex. Agent \(i\) holds a convex function \(f_i:X\to\mathbb R\). Let \(h:X\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and strictly convex on the relevant domain, with Bregman divergence \(D_h(x,z)=h(x)-h(z)-\langle\nabla h(z),x-z\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional distributed convex optimization in a common non-Euclidean geometry; stochastic subgradients and time-varying mixing are allowed at the definitional level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed non-Euclidean descent method is a network iteration in which each agent forms a mixed reference point \(v_i^k\in X\), commonly \(v_i^k=\sum_j w_{ij}^k x_j^k\), chooses \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(v_i^k)\), and sets \[x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x\rangle+D_h(x,v_i^k)\right\},\qquad \alpha_k>0.\] More generally, the linear term may contain a locally available unbiased stochastic subgradient. Membership in the family requires that communication supplies the reference or dual-coordinate aggregation and that the local descent step is regularized by \(D_h\), rather than necessarily by squared Euclidean distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents communicate to form local reference points and then minimize a first-order model of their local objective plus a Bregman divergence from the reference point. The divergence, generated by a strictly convex distance-generating function, determines the non-Euclidean geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is characterized by a network-generated reference \(v_i^k\) and a Bregman-regularized local first-order update for every agent and iteration.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When the minimizer lies in the relative interior and no constraint normal is active, optimality is equivalent to \(\nabla h(x_i^{k+1})=\nabla h(v_i^k)-\alpha_k g_i^k\).
special_cases_latex: For \(h(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\), the update is projected distributed subgradient descent.
On the probability simplex with negative entropy as \(h\), the local step is an exponentiated-gradient or multiplicative-weights update.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing \(h\) changes the local geometry while leaving the separable first-order model and communication layer conceptually distinct.
boundary_notes: Averaging primal points need not preserve the natural dual geometry; variants that mix \(\nabla h(x_i^k)\) instead require an explicitly dual-space formulation.
The definition alone imposes no connectivity, stepsize, or convergence conditions.
review_flags: The supplied source hints did not provide an inspectable locator supporting this precise distributed Bregman update.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Bregman-Descent Family
Objective–Disagreement Decomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate suboptimality is bounded by averaged local first-order terms plus a disagreement penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\), \(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\), and \(\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i\). If every \(f_i\) is convex and \(G\)-Lipschitz on \(X\), then for every \(x\in X\),
\[
F(\bar x)-F(x)\le {1\over n}\sum_i\langle g_i,x_i-x\rangle+{G\over n}\sum_i\|x_i-\bar x\|.
\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex and \(G\)-Lipschitz on \(X\).
\(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\), and \(x,x_i,\bar x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(\bar x)-F(x)\le n^{-1}\sum_i\langle g_i,x_i-x\rangle+Gn^{-1}\sum_i\|x_i-\bar x\|.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connects local mirror-descent inequalities to aggregate suboptimality while exposing disagreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Mirror-Step Inequality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every well-defined local distributed mirror step satisfies a three-point descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x\rangle+D_h(x,v_i^k)\},
\]
then every \(x\in X\) satisfies
\[
\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x_i^{k+1}-x\rangle\le D_h(x,v_i^k)-D_h(x,x_i^{k+1})-D_h(x_i^{k+1},v_i^k).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on the relevant domain.
The displayed minimizer exists, \(\alpha_k>0\), and \(g_i^k\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in X:\ \alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x_i^{k+1}-x\rangle\le D_h(x,v_i^k)-D_h(x,x_i^{k+1})-D_h(x_i^{k+1},v_i^k).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local descent inequality once a network-generated mirror center is well defined.

notation.meaning: well-defined mirror center produced by the network step

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Mirror Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-coupled mirror descent on a common closed convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed and convex, and let \(\psi\) be differentiable and strongly convex on the working domain. Agent \(i\) chooses \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(x_i^k)\), forms \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k\), and computes \[x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x\rangle+D_\psi(x,v_i^k)\right\},\qquad D_\psi(x,v)=\psi(x)-\psi(v)-\langle\nabla\psi(v),x-v\rangle.\] Initialize all states in the differentiability domain of \(\psi\); after \(K\) iterations output local weighted averages or the network average, according to the prescribed consensus protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents average neighbor states and solve a mirror-geometry linearized local objective at each iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and all iterates lie where \(\nabla\psi\) exists.
\(\psi\) is strongly convex relative to the selected norm.
\(W^k\) is graph-compatible and row-stochastic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x\rangle+D_\psi(x,v_i^k)\}\).

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence generated by the mirror function

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Proximal Three-Point Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact Bregman proximal point satisfies the three-point inequality against every feasible comparator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(x^+=P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)\), then for every \(x\in X\),
\[
\alpha\bigl(\phi(x^+)-\phi(x)\bigr)\le D_h(x,v)-D_h(x,x^+)-D_h(x^+,v).
\]
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the Bregman proximal-map definition hold.
\(x^+=P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in X:\ \alpha(\phi(x^+)-\phi(x))+D_h(x,x^+)+D_h(x^+,v)\le D_h(x,v).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact variational certificate for a local Bregman proximal solve.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Proximal Map and Optimality Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman proximal point uniquely minimizes a convex function plus a Bregman distance and is characterized by a normal-cone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha>0\), define
\[
P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\alpha\phi(x)+D_h(x,v)\},\qquad D_h(x,v)=h(x)-h(v)-\langle\nabla h(v),x-v\rangle.
\]
If the minimum is attained and the convex subdifferential sum rule applies, strong convexity of \(h\) makes the minimizer unique, and
\[
x^+=P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)\iff0\in\alpha\partial\phi(x^+)+\nabla h(x^+)-\nabla h(v)+N_X(x^+).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\phi\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on the relevant domain.
The minimum is attained and a standard convex subdifferential sum qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^+=P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)\iff0\in\alpha\partial\phi(x^+)+\nabla h(x^+)-\nabla h(v)+N_X(x^+).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Bregman proximal operation underlying distributed implementations; no network recursion is selected.

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Reduction of the Bregman Proximal Map
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With squared-Euclidean geometry, the constrained Bregman proximal map is the ordinary Euclidean proximal map of the objective plus the feasible-set indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(h(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\), \(D_h(x,v)=\tfrac12\|x-v\|_2^2\), and therefore
\[
P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\alpha\phi(x)+\tfrac12\|x-v\|_2^2\right\}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha(\phi+\iota_X)}(v).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\phi\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha(\phi+\iota_X)}(v).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Euclidean specialization of the locally owned Bregman proximal operation.

notation.meaning: convex indicator of the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Bregman Proximal Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A network Bregman-proximal update retaining a local nonsmooth term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For local composite objectives \(f_i+h_i\) on a common convex set \(X\), initialize \(x_i^0\) in the differentiability domain of \(\psi\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) forms \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k\), selects \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(v_i^k)\), and updates \[x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x\rangle+\alpha_k h_i(x)+D_\psi(x,v_i^k)\right\}.\] A finite run outputs the final local states or prescribed ergodic averages; a residual-based run stops when both network disagreement and the Bregman-proximal optimality residual satisfy their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neighbor averaging is followed by a Bregman proximal subproblem containing a local subgradient and nonsmooth term.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) and \(h_i\) is proper and convex on \(X\), with the required subgradients and subproblem solutions available.
\(\psi\) is differentiable and strongly convex on the working domain.
\(W^k\) respects the communication graph and is row-stochastic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^{k+1}\) satisfies the displayed Bregman-proximal minimization rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Map Scaling Invariance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive rescaling changes Bregman distance and curvature equally, leaving the standard geometry score unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\widetilde h=ch\) for \(c>0\), then \(D_{\widetilde h}=cD_h\) and \(\widetilde h\) is \(c\mu\)-strongly convex whenever \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. Hence
\[
{G^2D_{\widetilde h}(x^*,x^0)\over c\mu}={G^2D_h(x^*,x^0)\over\mu}.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the selected norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rules out artificial improvement of the geometry-selection score by scalar rescaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Euclidean and Entropic Geometries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared Euclidean and negative-entropy geometries provide canonical norm-divergence pairings for Euclidean domains and probability simplices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For Euclidean geometry, \(h(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\) is one-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|_2\) and \(D_h(x,y)=\tfrac12\|x-y\|_2^2\). On the simplex \(\Delta_d\), negative entropy \(h(x)=\sum_jx_j\log x_j\) is one-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|_1\); for \(y\) with positive coordinates,
\[
D_h(x,y)=\sum_jx_j\log(x_j/y_j),
\]
and at \(u=\mathbf1/d\), \(\sup_{x\in\Delta_d}D_h(x,u)=\log d\). Entropic geometry therefore pairs a logarithmic simplex Bregman radius with the dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_\infty\).
assumptions_latex: For entropy geometry, the second argument has strictly positive coordinates.
The convention \(0\log0=0\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_{\|\cdot\|_2^2/2}(x,y)=\tfrac12\|x-y\|_2^2,\qquad\sup_{x\in\Delta_d}D_{\mathrm{ent}}(x,\mathbf1/d)=\log d.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical choices illustrating feasible-set, primal-norm, dual-norm, and Bregman-radius matching.

knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Geometry Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the norm and mirror map together to reduce the product of squared dual-gradient scale and Bregman distance relative to strong convexity, while retaining tractable distributed updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a positive integer \(T\), constant stepsize \(\alpha>0\), and the standard weighted or averaged mirror-descent output, the optimization bound has the form
\[
\frac{D_h(x^*,x^0)}{\alpha T}+\frac{\alpha G^2}{2\mu}.
\]
Balancing these terms gives
\[
\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{2\mu D_h(x^*,x^0)}{G^2T}}.
\]
Thus a mirror geometry should be selected jointly with its norm to control the Bregman distance to an optimizer, the dual-norm scale of admissible subgradients, and the strong-convexity modulus. In a distributed implementation, mirror-coordinate aggregation and local mirror or proximal subproblems should also remain computationally tractable.
assumptions_latex: The objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty and convex, and \(x^*\in\mathop{\arg\min}_{x\in X}f(x)\).
Every employed subgradient satisfies \(\lVert g\rVert_*\leq G\) with respect to the dual of the selected norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\).
The selected differentiable mirror map \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), and \(D_h(x^*,x^0)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Within a candidate family of mirror geometries, the standard bound favors choices jointly controlling \(G^2D_h(x^*,x^0)/\mu\) while keeping mirror and proximal operations tractable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry-selection principle derived from the standard convex mirror-descent bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean and Entropic Barycenters Differ
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropy mirror averaging gives a geometric mean rather than the arithmetic mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h(t)=t\log t\), equal weights, and \(x_1=1,x_2=4\), the arithmetic barycenter is \(5/2\), while the mirror-coordinate barycenter is \[\exp\!\left(\tfrac12(\log1+\log4)\right)=2.\]
assumptions_latex: Both points lie in the positive entropy domain.
The weights are \(1/2,1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tfrac12(1+4)=\tfrac52\ne2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete instance of the averaging incompatibility in the accepted seed.

knowledge_statements.title: Mirror Barycenter Existence Requires Dual-Range Closure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror-coordinate averaging is well defined only when the mixed dual coordinate remains in the mirror map's range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The expression \((
abla h)^{-1}(\sum_jw_{ij}
abla h(x_j))\) is defined only when every mirror coordinate exists and the mixed coordinate belongs to \(\operatorname{ran}(
abla h)\). If the range is not closed under the selected convex mixing, no corresponding primal barycenter exists.
assumptions_latex: \(w_{ij}\ge0\) and \(\sum_jw_{ij}=1\).
\(\nabla h\) is injective on the selected interior domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain boundary for averaging mirror coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Divergence Is Not a Metric
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman divergence is a directed discrepancy, so metric consensus arguments do not transfer automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Although \(D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle\ge0\), it is generally asymmetric and need not satisfy the triangle inequality. For \(h(t)=t\log t\), \(D_h(1,2)=1-\log2\ne2\log2-1=D_h(2,1)\).
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on the relevant interior domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_h(x,y)\ne D_h(y,x)\text{ in general, and }D_h\text{ need not satisfy a triangle inequality}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on treating Bregman disagreement as an ordinary network distance.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman-Geometry Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropy mirror coordinates are undefined at zero coordinates, and ordinary convex averaging generally differs from averaging in mirror coordinates and mapping back.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the entropy generator \(h(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^d x_\ell\log x_\ell\), the mirror coordinate satisfies \(\nabla h(x)=\mathbf{1}+\log x\) on the positive orthant and is not finite when a coordinate of \(x\) is zero. Consequently, an iterate or communicated center on the boundary makes a gradient-based mirror update undefined unless a suitable extension or limiting convention is specified. Moreover, because \(\nabla h\) is nonlinear, the primal average \(\sum_jw_{ij}x_j\) generally differs from the mirror-coordinate barycenter
\[
(\nabla h)^{-1}\!\left(\sum_jw_{ij}\nabla h(x_j)\right),
\]
whenever the inverse is defined. Thus replacing mirror-coordinate aggregation by ordinary primal consensus generally changes the intended Bregman geometry.
assumptions_latex: The entropy generator is \(h(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^d x_\ell\log x_\ell\) on the nonnegative orthant, with gradient defined on its positive interior.
For each agent \(i\), the mixing coefficients satisfy \(w_{ij}\geq0\) and \(\sum_jw_{ij}=1\).
Whenever a mirror-coordinate barycenter is invoked, \(\sum_jw_{ij}\nabla h(x_j)\) lies in the range of \(\nabla h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundary points can make entropy mirror coordinates undefined, and primal averaging generally differs from averaging in mirror coordinates followed by the inverse mirror map.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain and averaging failures specific to non-Euclidean distributed updates.

notation.meaning: negative entropy on the nonnegative orthant
Bregman divergence generated by the mirror map
convex mixing coefficient from agent j to agent i

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Corrected-Surrogate Fixed-Point Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact correction for the other agents' gradients, a surrogate best-response fixed point is exactly a composite stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi(x)=\sum_jf_j(x)+r(x)\) on \(X\), and define
\[
\widehat x_i(z)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\widetilde f_i(x;z)+\left\langle\sum_{j\ne i}\nabla f_j(z),x-z\right\rangle+r(x)\right\}.
\]
If the surrogate is differentiable, strongly convex, and first-order consistent, and the convex sum rule applies, then
\[
z=\widehat x_i(z)\iff0\in\sum_j\nabla f_j(z)+\partial r(z)+N_X(z).
\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_j\) is differentiable.
\(r\) is proper, closed, and convex; \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) is differentiable, strongly convex, and first-order consistent.
A standard convex subdifferential sum qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z=\widehat x_i(z)\iff0\in\sum_j\nabla f_j(z)+\partial r(z)+N_X(z).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity certificate using an exact aggregate-gradient correction, independent of its network implementation.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order-Consistent Strongly Convex Surrogate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed SCA uses strongly convex local models matching the local gradient at the base point; majorization is optional and variant-specific.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A surrogate \(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) is admissible when it is strongly convex on \(X\), its gradient is continuous in the relevant arguments, and
\[
\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(z;z)=\nabla f_i(z).
\]
Global majorization \(\widetilde f_i(x;z)\ge f_i(x)\) is an additional variant-specific condition and does not follow from first-order consistency.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is convex.
\(f_i\) is differentiable on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\text{ is strongly convex},\qquad\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(z;z)=\nabla f_i(z).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining local model used in distributed successive convex approximation.

notation.meaning: agent i surrogate at base point z

knowledge_statements.title: Descent Property of an Exact Corrected Surrogate Direction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact gradient-corrected surrogate with strongly monotone model gradient produces a quantitatively descending displacement unless it is already at a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_i(z)=\widehat x_i(z)-z\), where \(\widehat x_i(z)\) is the exact corrected surrogate best response. If \(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) has \(\tau\)-strongly monotone gradient and is first-order consistent, then
\[
\left\langle\sum_j\nabla f_j(z),d_i(z)\right\rangle+r(\widehat x_i(z))-r(z)\le-\tau\|d_i(z)\|^2.
\]
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the accepted exact corrected-surrogate fixed-point certificate hold.
For fixed \(z\), \(\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) is \(\tau\)-strongly monotone for \(\tau>0\).
\(\widehat x_i(z)\) is the exact surrogate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left\langle\sum_j\nabla f_j(z),d_i(z)\right\rangle+r(\widehat x_i(z))-r(z)\le-\tau\|d_i(z)\|^2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local descent property of the SCA best-response direction, independent of its network implementation.

notation.meaning: strong-monotonicity modulus of the surrogate gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Successive Convex Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A gradient-consistent strongly convex surrogate template for network nonconvex optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x)+r(x)\) over a closed convex set \(X\), agent \(i\) constructs at \(x_i^k\) a strongly convex surrogate \(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;x_i^k)\) satisfying value-gradient consistency there. Given a tracker \(y_i^k\) of the aggregate gradient, compute \[z_i^k\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{\widetilde f_i(x;x_i^k)+\langle y_i^k-\nabla f_i(x_i^k),x-x_i^k\rangle+r(x)\right\},\] then set \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}^k(x_j^k+\gamma_k(z_j^k-x_j^k))\) and update \(y_i^k\) by dynamic gradient tracking. knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let agents minimize \(U(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)+G(x)\) over a closed convex set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), where the \(f_i\) are differentiable and possibly nonconvex and \(G\) is convex, possibly nonsmooth. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous distributed composite nonconvex optimization using strongly convex local surrogates and network tracking or estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed successive convex-approximation method assigns to each agent \(i\), point \(z\in K\), and iteration \(k\) a convex surrogate \(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) that is strongly convex in its first argument and is first-order consistent at \(z\): \(\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(z;z)=\nabla f_i(z)\). The agent computes \[\widehat x_i^k=\arg\min_{x\in K}\left\{\widetilde f_i(x;x_i^k)+\langle\pi_i^k,x-x_i^k\rangle+G(x)\right\},\] forms \(z_i^k=x_i^k+\gamma_k(\widehat x_i^k-x_i^k)\), and obtains \(x_i^{k+1}\) by mixing neighboring \(z_j^k\). The auxiliary network recursion defining \(\pi_i^k\) must estimate the missing aggregate-gradient contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, every agent replaces its own possibly nonconvex objective by a strongly convex first-order-consistent local model, adds an estimate of all other agents' gradients and the common convex term, solves that convex subproblem, relaxes toward its solution, and mixes the result over the network.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method family consists of the displayed surrogate subproblem together with relaxation, neighbor mixing, and estimation of the missing aggregate gradient.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The linear correction may be written using a tracker \(y_i^k\) as \(\langle m y_i^k-\nabla f_i(x_i^k),x-x_i^k\rangle\) when \(m y_i^k\) estimates \(\sum_j\nabla f_j(x_i^k)\).
special_cases_latex: A quadratic linearization \(\widetilde f_i(x;z)=f_i(z)+\langle\nabla f_i(z),x-z\rangle+\tfrac{\tau_i}{2}\|x-z\|^2\) yields a proximal-gradient-type local subproblem.
If \(f_i\) is convex, it may itself be retained as part of the surrogate.
immediate_consequences_latex: The defining first-order consistency preserves stationary-point information at the current local state, while strong convexity makes the local best response single-valued.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert global optimality for nonconvex objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SONATA distributed SCA iteration over time-varying digraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local surrogate minimization followed by push-sum averaging and gradient tracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\mathbf x_{(i)}^0\in X\), \(\phi_{(i)}^0=1\), and \(\mathbf y_{(i)}^0=\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^0)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,I\), with \(\gamma^k\in(0,1]\). At iteration \(k\), each agent computes
\[\widetilde{\mathbf x}_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf x_{(i)}\in X}\left\{\widetilde f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}\mid\mathbf x_{(i)}^k)+\bigl(I\mathbf y_{(i)}^k-\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^k)\bigr)^T(\mathbf x_{(i)}-\mathbf x_{(i)}^k)+G(\mathbf x_{(i)})\right\},\]
\[\mathbf x_{(i)}^{k+1/2}=\mathbf x_{(i)}^k+\gamma^k(\widetilde{\mathbf x}_i^k-\mathbf x_{(i)}^k).\]
After exchanging variables with its in-neighbors, it updates
\[\phi_{(i)}^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^I a_{ij}^k\phi_{(j)}^k,\qquad \mathbf x_{(i)}^{k+1}=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^I a_{ij}^k\phi_{(j)}^k\mathbf x_{(j)}^{k+1/2}}{\phi_{(i)}^{k+1}},\]
\[\mathbf y_{(i)}^{k+1}=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^I a_{ij}^k\phi_{(j)}^k\mathbf y_{(j)}^k+\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^{k+1})-\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^k)}{\phi_{(i)}^{k+1}}.\]
The iterations continue until the termination criterion is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SONATA alternates an agent-local surrogate minimization and relaxed update with push-sum averaging and gradient tracking over the current directed communication graph.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf x_{(i)}^0\in X,\quad \phi_{(i)}^0=1,\quad \mathbf y_{(i)}^0=\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^0),\quad i=1,\ldots,I
\gamma^k\in(0,1]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\phi_{(i)}^{k+1},\mathbf x_{(i)}^{k+1},\mathbf y_{(i)}^{k+1})\text{ are generated by the stated local-SCA, push-sum, and gradient-tracking recursions.}

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), with each \(f_i\) twice differentiable on an open set containing the iterates. Agent \(i\) stores a primal state \(x_i^k\), a gradient estimate \(g_i^k\), and a local or tracked curvature model \(B_i^k\in\mathbb S^d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth network optimization; the definition covers Newton, quasi-Newton, and Hessian-tracking constructions without asserting a convergence regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed curvature method is a network algorithm whose local search direction \(d_i^k\) is determined by a second-order model \[d_i^k\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathbb R^d}\left\{\langle g_i^k,d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle d,B_i^k d\rangle\right\},\] or by a regularized version with \(B_i^k+\mu_k I\succ0\), and whose state update combines \(x_i^k+\alpha_k d_i^k\) with information received from neighbors. The curvature matrix must represent local curvature \(\nabla^2f_i(x_i^k)\), a secant approximation, or a network-tracked estimate of aggregate curvature; merely scaling a first-order direction by a fixed scalar does not define membership in this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent constructs a Newton-like local quadratic model using a Hessian, a quasi-Newton secant matrix, or a tracked estimate of global curvature. It solves or approximately solves that model for a direction and combines the resulting trial point with neighbor information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership requires an iteratively generated matrix-valued curvature model that determines the local direction and a communication step coupling agents' states or curvature information.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(B_i^k\succ0\), the exact model minimizer is \(d_i^k=-(B_i^k)^{-1}g_i^k\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(B_i^k=\nabla^2 f_i(x_i^k)+\mu_kI\) gives a regularized local Newton method.
A positive-definite matrix satisfying a secant equation gives a distributed quasi-Newton variant.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of the employed model makes the exact direction a descent direction for the linear model whenever \(g_i^k\ne0\).
boundary_notes: How linear systems are solved and how Hessians are tracked are variant-defining mechanisms.
No superlinear, quadratic, or global convergence claim follows from this definition.

notation.meaning: Agent i's local or tracked curvature model.

review_flags: No supplied locator was inspectable and none was shown to support this broad distributed curvature-family definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Curvature-Based Optimization Method
Inexact Distributed Newton Residual
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Newton-equation residual verifies the local estimated solve but not consensus or global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For derivative estimates \(\widehat H_i^k,\widehat g_i^k\), define \[\eta_i^k=\frac{\|\widehat H_i^kp_i^k+\widehat g_i^k\|}{\max\{1,\|\widehat g_i^k\|\}}.\] A small \(\eta_i^k\) certifies only the estimated linear solve; distributed optimality additionally requires small derivative-estimation error, primal disagreement, and aggregate-gradient residual.
assumptions_latex: The derivative estimates and direction are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta_i^k\le\varepsilon_N\text{ certifies the estimated solve only}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for an estimated aggregate Newton solve.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation Certificate for an Estimated Aggregate Newton Direction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed distributed direction is close to the aggregate Newton direction when derivative-estimation and linear-solve errors are small relative to aggregate curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\succeq\mu I\), \(\mu>0\), \(p=-H^{-1}g\), \(\widehat H=H+E_H\), and \(\widehat g=g+e_g\). If \(\|E_H\|\le\varepsilon_H<\mu\), \(\|e_g\|\le\varepsilon_g\), and \(\|\widehat H\widehat p+\widehat g\|\le\rho\), then
\[
\|\widehat p-p\|\le\frac{\rho+\varepsilon_g+\varepsilon_H\|p\|}{\mu-\varepsilon_H}.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(H\succeq\mu I\) for some \(\mu>0\).
\(\|\widehat H-H\|\le\varepsilon_H<\mu\).
\(\|\widehat g-g\|\le\varepsilon_g\).
\(\|\widehat H\widehat p+\widehat g\|\le\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\widehat p-p\|\le(\rho+\varepsilon_g+\varepsilon_H\|p\|)/(\mu-\varepsilon_H).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates derivative-aggregation error from the estimated Newton-solve residual.

notation.meaning: aggregate Hessian, gradient, and exact Newton direction

knowledge_statements.title: Averaging Local Newton Directions Is Generally Biased
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix inversion does not commute with averaging, so naive averaging of local Newton directions is not the aggregate Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In general, \[\frac1n\sum_iH_i^{-1}g_i\ne\left(\frac1n\sum_iH_i\right)^{-1}\left(\frac1n\sum_i g_i\right).\] For scalar data \((H_1,g_1)=(1,1)\) and \((H_2,g_2)=(3,1)\), the average local direction is \(-2/3\), whereas the aggregate Newton direction is \(-1/2\).
assumptions_latex: Every local Hessian is nonsingular.
Agents compute \(p_i=-H_i^{-1}g_i\) independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline{H^{-1}g}\ne\bar H^{-1}\bar g\quad\text{in general}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncommutativity boundary for naive distributed Newton averaging.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Newton Equation in Consensus Coordinates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed Newton methods approximate the Newton equation formed from the aggregate gradient and average Hessian at a common point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), define \(\bar g(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i\nabla f_i(x)\) and \(\bar H(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i\nabla^2f_i(x)\). When \(\bar H(x)\) is nonsingular, the aggregate Newton direction satisfies \[\bar H(x)p_N(x)=-\bar g(x).\]
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is twice differentiable at \(x\).
\(\bar H(x)\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_N(x)=-\bar H(x)^{-1}\bar g(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order equation that distributed Newton methods seek to reproduce.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A consensus-based Newton template using distributed gradient and Hessian aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), agents maintain approximately consensual states \(x_i^k\) and obtain aggregate estimates \(g_i^k\approx n^{-1}\sum_j\nabla f_j(x_j^k)\) and \(H_i^k\approx n^{-1}\sum_j\nabla^2f_j(x_j^k)\) through communication. With regularization \(\lambda_k\ge0\), agent \(i\) solves \[(H_i^k+\lambda_k I)p_i^k=-g_i^k\] and updates \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k+t_kp_i^k\), where \(t_k>0\) is fixed or selected by globalization. Stop when consensus and Newton residuals meet prescribed tolerances; output the final local states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents aggregate gradients and Hessians, solve regularized local Newton systems, and combine the resulting steps with consensus.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable on the working region.
\(H_i^k+\lambda_k I\) is positive definite.
The communication procedure supplies the stated gradient and Hessian aggregate estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((H_i^k+\lambda_k I)p_i^k=-g_i^k\) and \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k+t_kp_i^k\).

notation.meaning: local estimate of the aggregate gradient
local estimate of the aggregate Hessian

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Average of Local Newton Directions Is Generally Not Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncommutativity boundary for naive local Newton averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In general, \[\frac1n\sum_i H_i^{-1}g_i\ne\left(\frac1n\sum_iH_i\right)^{-1}\left(\frac1n\sum_i g_i\right).\] For example, in one dimension with \((H_1,g_1)=(1,1)\) and \((H_2,g_2)=(3,1)\), the average local direction is \(-2/3\), whereas the aggregate Newton direction is \(-1/2\). Thus averaging independently computed local Newton steps does not reproduce the centralized Newton step except under additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix inversion does not commute with network averaging, so naive averaging of local Newton directions is biased.
assumptions_latex: Local Hessians are nonsingular.
Agents compute directions \(p_i=-H_i^{-1}g_i\) independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline{H^{-1}g}\ne\bar H^{-1}\bar g\quad\text{in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Average of Local Newton Directions Is Generally Not Newton

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Centralized Newton Equation in Consensus Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order equation that distributed Newton approximations seek to reproduce.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\frac1n\sum_i f_i(x)\), the centralized Newton direction at a common point \(x\) is \[p_N(x)=-\left(\frac1n\sum_i\nabla^2f_i(x)\right)^{-1}\left(\frac1n\sum_i\nabla f_i(x)\right).\] A distributed Newton method is exact at that iteration only if its communicated derivative information and linear solve reproduce this aggregate equation, up to a declared solve residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed Newton methods approximate the Newton equation formed from the aggregate gradient and the average Hessian at a common point.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is twice differentiable at \(x\).
The aggregate Hessian is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar H(x)p_N(x)=-\bar g(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Centralized Newton Equation in Consensus Coordinates
Positive Hessian Samples Can Produce an Indefinite Local Tracker
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing positive samples and adding their temporal differences can make a local Hessian tracker negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the scalar two-agent recursion with \(W=J\), initialize \(S^0=Q^0=(100,1)^\top\) and take \(Q^1=(1,100)^\top\). Then \(S_1^1=50.5+(1-100)=-48.5\), although every entry of \(Q^0\) and \(Q^1\) is positive. Thus dynamic Hessian tracking does not preserve agentwise positive definiteness.
assumptions_latex: The scalar tracker uses \(S^{1}=JS^0+Q^1-Q^0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_i^k>0\ \forall i,k\not\Rightarrow S_i^k>0\ \forall i,k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit boundary between the aggregate invariant and agentwise positive definiteness.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian-Tracking Disagreement Recursion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hessian-tracking disagreement is a stable consensus filter driven by changes in local Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S^{k+1}=WS^k+Q^{k+1}-Q^k\), \(J=n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), and consistently initialized aggregate components, the disagreement \(E^k=(I-J)S^k\) satisfies \[E^{k+1}=(W-J)E^k+(I-J)(Q^{k+1}-Q^k).\] If \(\|W-J\|=\sigma<1\), then \[\|E^k\|\le\sigma^k\|E^0\|+\sum_{t=0}^{k-1}\sigma^{k-1-t}\|(I-J)(Q^{t+1}-Q^t)\|.\]
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(\|W-J\|=\sigma<1\) in a compatible norm.
Trackers and samples use a common vectorized or Frobenius-space representation.
The aggregate tracker component is initialized consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|E^k\|\le\sigma^k\|E^0\|+\sum_{t=0}^{k-1}\sigma^{k-1-t}\|(I-J)\Delta Q^{t+1}\|.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic-average-consensus error dynamics for matrix-valued Hessian samples.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Hessian Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic average consensus applied to time-varying local Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_i^k=\nabla^2f_i(x_i^k)\). Initialize \(H_i^0=Q_i^0\), and for a graph-compatible doubly stochastic matrix \(W^k\) update \[H_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}^kH_j^k+Q_i^{k+1}-Q_i^k.\] If necessary, use \(\widehat H_i^k=H_i^k+\lambda_k I\) with \(\lambda_k\) large enough to ensure invertibility before computing a curvature step. For every \(k\), the recursion preserves the aggregate identity \(\sum_iH_i^k=\sum_iQ_i^k\). A finite run outputs the current local Hessian estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic average consensus tracks the network-average Hessian by mixing old estimates and adding each local Hessian change.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is twice differentiable at every local iterate used by the recursion.
\(W^k\) is graph-compatible and doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_iH_i^k=\sum_i\nabla^2f_i(x_i^k)\) for every \(k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hessian Tracking Does Not Preserve Positive Definiteness Agentwise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between an exact aggregate invariant and usable local Newton models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when every sample \(Q_i^k\succ0\) and the network sum of the trackers equals the sum of current samples, the correction \(Q_i^{k+1}-Q_i^k\) is indefinite in general. Consequently, a local tracker \(S_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}S_j^k+Q_i^{k+1}-Q_i^k\) need not remain positive definite. A Newton implementation must therefore impose a spectral safeguard, regularization, or projection onto a positive-definite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic Hessian tracking preserves an aggregate quantity but can produce indefinite local curvature estimates.
assumptions_latex: The local Hessian samples are symmetric positive definite.
No positivity-preserving correction is added to the tracking recursion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_i^k\succ0\ \forall i,k\ \not\Rightarrow\ S_i^k\succ0\ \forall i,k.
knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Tracking Does Not Preserve Positive Definiteness Agentwise
Distributed Secant Curvature Safeguard
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed BFGS needs an explicit curvature safeguard because observed secant curvature can become nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direct BFGS update preserves positive definiteness when \(B_i^k\succ0\) and \((s_i^k)^\top y_i^k>0\). Because network and tracking errors can violate this inequality, a distributed implementation must damp, skip, or regularize pairs failing a declared bound such as \((s_i^k)^\top y_i^k\ge c\|s_i^k\|^2\), \(c>0\).
assumptions_latex: A BFGS-type direct update is applied only to accepted pairs.
\(B_i^k\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_i^k\succ0\land(s_i^k)^\top y_i^k>0\Longrightarrow B_i^{k+1}\succ0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition preserving a positive-definite local BFGS model.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Quasi-Newton Secant Data
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed secant pairs may use local or tracked gradients, and the choice determines the curvature being approximated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Agent \(i\) forms \(s_i^k=x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k\) and \(y_i^k=q_i^{k+1}-q_i^k\), where \(q_i^k\) is either a local gradient or a tracked aggregate-gradient estimate. A direct model imposes \(B_i^{k+1}s_i^k=y_i^k\); an inverse model imposes \(H_i^{k+1}y_i^k=s_i^k\). Local and tracked choices generally approximate different curvature.
assumptions_latex: Successive displacements and the selected first-order estimates are available locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_i^{k+1}s_i^k=y_i^k\quad\text{or}\quad H_i^{k+1}y_i^k=s_i^k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local and tracked secant pairs used by decentralized curvature models.

notation.meaning: local displacement and selected first-order difference

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Mixing Generally Breaks Local Secant Equations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging positive-definite quasi-Newton matrices preserves positivity but usually destroys each agent's current secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each \(B_j\succ0\) satisfies \(B_js_j=y_j\) and \(\widetilde B_i=\sum_jw_{ij}B_j\) with convex weights, then \(\widetilde B_i\succ0\), but generally \(\widetilde B_is_i\ne y_i\) because neighboring matrices correspond to different secant pairs.
assumptions_latex: \(w_{ij}\ge0\) and \(\sum_jw_{ij}=1\).
Every \(B_j\) is symmetric positive definite and satisfies its own secant equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde B_i\succ0,\qquad \widetilde B_is_i=y_i\text{ need not hold}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility boundary between curvature-matrix averaging and agent-specific secant data.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative inverse-BFGS method with consensus and gradient tracking on a fixed undirected network.

Initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^p\), \(y_i^0=
