knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition ensuring well-defined local descent metrics despite noisy or inconsistent secant pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local BFGS-type update preserves positive definiteness when its accepted pair satisfies \((s_i^k)^\top y_i^k>0\). In distributed implementations, tracking and consensus errors can violate this inequality even for a strongly convex aggregate objective. A valid safeguard must therefore damp, skip, or regularize any pair failing a prescribed lower bound such as \[(s_i^k)^\top y_i^k\ge c\|s_i^k\|^2\quad(c>0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed secant updates require an explicit curvature safeguard because network errors can make the observed secant curvature nonpositive.
assumptions_latex: The current curvature model is symmetric positive definite.
A BFGS-type direct update is applied only to accepted pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_i^k\succ0\ \land\ (s_i^k)^\top y_i^k>0\ \Longrightarrow\ B_i^{k+1}\succ0.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Curvature Safeguard

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consensus Mixing Does Not Preserve the Secant Equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility boundary between mixing curvature matrices and local secant conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each agent has \(B_i s_i=y_i\), and form \(\widetilde B_i=\sum_jw_{ij}B_j\). In general \(\widetilde B_i s_i\ne y_i\), because the neighboring matrices satisfy secant equations for different pairs \((s_j,y_j)\). Thus direct averaging of quasi-Newton matrices preserves symmetry and positive definiteness under convex weights, but generally destroys each agent's current secant condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging positive-definite quasi-Newton matrices preserves positivity but usually breaks their local secant equations.
assumptions_latex: \(w_{ij}\ge0\) and \(\sum_jw_{ij}=1\).
Each \(B_j\) is symmetric positive definite and satisfies its own secant equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde B_i\succ0,\qquad \widetilde B_i s_i=y_i\ \text{need not hold}.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Mixing Does Not Preserve the Secant Equation
Aggregate Positive Curvature Does Not Imply Local Positive Curvature
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly convex aggregate can contain a locally concave objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar quadratic Hessians \(H_1=-1\) and \(H_2=3\), \(\bar H=1>0\), although \(H_1<0\). Thus aggregate strong convexity does not make every local Newton system positive definite.
assumptions_latex: Two scalar quadratic local objectives are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar H\succ0\not\Rightarrow H_i\succ0\ \forall i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar cancellation example for heterogeneous Hessians.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute and Relative Hessian Heterogeneity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hessian heterogeneity measures local curvature deviation absolutely or relative to the aggregate strong-curvature scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_i(x)=\nabla^2f_i(x)\) and \(\bar H(x)=n^{-1}\sum_iH_i(x)\). Define \(\delta_H=\sup_{x\in\mathcal D}\max_i\|H_i(x)-\bar H(x)\|_2\). When \(\bar H(x)\succ0\), a relative regime satisfies \(\|H_i(x)-\bar H(x)\|_2\le\eta\lambda_{\min}(\bar H(x))\). If \(\eta<1\), then \((1-\eta)\bar H(x)\preceq H_i(x)\preceq(1+\eta)\bar H(x)\).
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is twice differentiable on \(\mathcal D\).
The relative regime assumes \(\bar H(x)\succ0\) throughout \(\mathcal D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta<1\Longrightarrow(1-\eta)\bar H(x)\preceq H_i(x)\preceq(1+\eta)\bar H(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise disagreement of local Hessians from aggregate curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Heterogeneity Controls Local Newton-Direction Error
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Newton-direction error scales with Hessian heterogeneity and inverse local curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bar H\bar p=-g\), \(H_ip_i=-g\), and both Hessians are positive definite, then \[p_i-\bar p=H_i^{-1}(\bar H-H_i)\bar p,\qquad \|p_i-\bar p\|\le\|H_i^{-1}\|\,\|H_i-\bar H\|\,\|\bar p\|.\]
assumptions_latex: \(H_i\) and \(\bar H\) are symmetric positive definite.
Both systems use the same gradient vector \(g\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation relation for local and aggregate Newton systems sharing a gradient.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Heterogeneity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hessian-disagreement classification for smooth finite-sum objectives over a specified domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) on a nonempty domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), where every \(f_i\) is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(D\). Define the curvature-heterogeneity modulus by \[\delta_H(D)=\sup_{x\in D}\max_{1\le i\le n}\|\nabla^2f_i(x)-\nabla^2F(x)\|_2.\] The instance is curvature-homogeneous on \(D\) when \(\delta_H(D)=0\), uniformly curvature-heterogeneous when \(0<\delta_H(D)<\infty\), and unboundedly curvature-heterogeneous when \(\delta_H(D)=\infty\). A family indexed by a parameter is asymptotically homogeneous when its corresponding modulus converges to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature heterogeneity is measured by the largest local-to-average Hessian discrepancy and classified as zero, bounded positive, unbounded, or asymptotically vanishing.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty.
\(f_i\) is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(D\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_H(D)\in[0,\infty]\) determines the stated curvature-heterogeneity regime.

notation.meaning: Domain on which curvature is compared.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The modulus is mathematically well-defined, but the named regime classification and asymptotically homogeneous family terminology are noncanonical and have no cited domain-specific source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal Aggregate Curvature Does Not Imply Benign Local Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar example showing cancellation of curvature heterogeneity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In one dimension let \(H_1=-1\) and \(H_2=3\). Their average is \(\bar H=1>0\), although the first local Hessian is negative. Hence positive-definite aggregate curvature does not imply positive-definite local curvature; local Newton systems can be indefinite even when the aggregate objective is strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature can cancel across agents: a strongly convex aggregate may contain a locally concave objective.
assumptions_latex: Two scalar twice-differentiable quadratic local objectives are considered.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus, coupling-feasibility, and stationarity residuals jointly certify a convex constrained distributed solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(Bx=0\) and \(Ax=b\), define \[r_{\rm con}=Bx,\quad r_{\rm cpl}=Ax-b,\quad r_{\rm stat}=\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\nabla f(x)+B^\top\lambda+A^\top\nu+N_X(x)\right).\] Under convexity and a constraint qualification, vanishing residuals certify global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable.
\(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
A constraint qualification guarantees multiplier existence and KKT sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\rm con}=r_{\rm cpl}=r_{\rm stat}=0\Longrightarrow x\text{ is globally optimal}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for convex distributed problems with consensus and affine coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Heterogeneous Local Feasibility Does Not Survive Averaging
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging points feasible for different local sets need not produce a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From \(x_i\in X_i\) it does not follow that \(\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i\in\bigcap_iX_i\). For \(X_1=\{0\}\), \(X_2=\{2\}\), \(x_1=0\), and \(x_2=2\), the average is \(1\), which belongs to neither local set.

knowledge_statements.title: Local, Common, and Coupled Constraint Classes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agentwise projections handle Cartesian constraints, while genuine coupling constraints require coordinated or dualized handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Distributed constraints separate into local Cartesian constraints \(x_i\in X_i\), a common constraint \(x_i\in X\), and coupled constraints such as \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\). Projections onto \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_n\) separate agentwise, whereas projection onto a genuine coupling set is generally nonseparable and requires coordination, auxiliary variables, or multipliers.
assumptions_latex: Projection statements use nonempty closed convex sets and a separable positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{X_1\times\cdots\times X_n}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=(P_{X_1}x_1,\ldots,P_{X_n}x_n),\quad P_{\{x:\sum_iA_ix_i=b\}}\text{ is generally nonseparable}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical partition of constraint structures requiring different distributed handling.

notation.meaning: agent-local block of a coupling operator

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Constraint-Handling Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative projected-consensus method for agent-specific closed convex constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) subject to \(x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^nX_i\), initialize \(x_i^0\in X_i\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) forms \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k\) and updates \[x_i^{k+1}=P_{X_i}\!\left(v_i^k-\alpha_k\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\right).\] Agents exchange the new iterates with their neighbors. Stop when \(\max_i\|x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k\|\), \(\max_{i,j}\|x_i^k-x_j^k\|\), and \(\max_i\operatorname{dist}(\bar x^k,X_i)\) are below prescribed tolerances. Output \(\bar x^k=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^k\) together with these residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent averages neighboring iterates, takes a local gradient step, and projects onto its own constraint set; termination checks movement, consensus, and feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, with \(\bigcap_iX_i\ne\varnothing\).
\(f_i:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable.
\(W\) is a graph-compatible nonnegative mixing matrix and \(\alpha_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x^k=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^k\) and the feasibility-consensus residuals constitute the output.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto agent i's constraint set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If agents maintain \(x_i\in X_i\) with different closed convex sets, their arithmetic average need not belong to any \(X_i\) or to \(\bigcap_iX_i\). For example, with \(X_1=\{0\}\), \(X_2=\{2\}\), and \(x_1=0,x_2=2\), the average is \(1\), which belongs to neither set and the intersection is empty. Thus feasibility of the reported average follows automatically only for a common convex set containing every local iterate.

Tracker–Consensus Stationarity Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The aggregate gradient is bounded by the average tracker plus a Lipschitz-weighted disagreement term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If every \(\nabla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz and \(\sum_i y_i=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i)\), then with \(\bar y=n^{-1}\sum_i y_i\) and \(\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i\),
\[
\|\nabla F(\bar x)\|\le\|\bar y\|+{1\over n}\sum_iL_i\|x_i-\bar x\|.
\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) has an \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradient.
\(\sum_i y_i=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\nabla F(\bar x)\|\le\|\bar y\|+n^{-1}\sum_iL_i\|x_i-\bar x\|.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative stationarity certificate using an exact tracker-sum invariant and disagreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Does Not Certify Global Optimality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero aggregate gradient can identify a local maximum rather than a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If every agent has \(f_i(x)=(x^2-1)^2\), then \(F(x)=(x^2-1)^2\). The consensual state \(x_i=0\) satisfies \(\nabla F(0)=0\), but
\[
F(0)=1>0=F(1)=F(-1),
\]
and \(0\) is a strict local maximum.
assumptions_latex: All agents use \(f_i(x)=(x^2-1)^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla F(0)=0\quad\text{but}\quad0\notin\operatorname*{argmin}F.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation boundary for generic nonconvex network outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus First-Order Stationarity for Smooth Nonconvex Networks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generic smooth nonconvex target is consensus plus a small aggregate gradient, not global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), a product state is consensual first-order stationary when
\[
x_1=\cdots=x_n=x^*,\qquad\nabla F(x^*)=0.
\]
It is \((\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_s)\)-approximately stationary when
\[
{1\over n}\sum_i\|x_i-\bar x\|\le\varepsilon_c,\qquad\|\nabla F(\bar x)\|\le\varepsilon_s.
\]
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i=x^*\ \forall i,\qquad\nabla F(x^*)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic target of smooth unconstrained distributed nonconvex methods, independent of a particular recursion.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Nonconvex Network Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative gradient-tracking scheme for smooth nonconvex finite-sum optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x)\), initialize arbitrary \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(y_i^0=
abla f_i(x_i^0)\). With a graph-compatible mixing matrix \(W\), iterate \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha_k y_i^k,\qquad y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+
abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x_i^k).\] Stop when both \(\max_i\|x_i^k- ar x^k\|\le\varepsilon_c\) and \(\|n^{-1}\sum_i y_i^k\|\le\varepsilon_s\). Output \( ar x^k=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^k\) and the two residuals; no global-optimality claim is attached to this stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient tracking combines neighbor averaging with local nonconvex gradients and returns an approximately consensual, approximately stationary network-average iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable with Lipschitz gradient.
\(F\) is bounded below.
\(W\) is doubly stochastic and represents a connected undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|\le\varepsilon_c\) and \(\|n^{-1}\sum_i y_i^k\|\le\varepsilon_s\) define termination.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^m X_i\) and \(Y\) be convex sets, and let \(L(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^m L_i(x_i,y)+C(x,y)\) be convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\). Coupling may arise from a constraint \(\sum_i A_i x_i=b\), consensus, or a monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-concave distributed optimization represented through dualization, saddle structure, augmented Lagrangians, or operator splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed saddle-decomposition method is an iteration that seeks a saddle point \((x^\star,y^\star)\in X\times Y\) satisfying \[L(x^\star,y)\le L(x^\star,y^\star)\le L(x,y^\star)\quad\text{for all }(x,y)\in X\times Y,\] while assigning separable primal computations involving \(L_i\) to agents and coordinating the shared or replicated dual variable through communication. Its update is obtained from alternating, simultaneous, proximal, or split applications of the primal and dual saddle operators, possibly after adding an augmentation term that preserves the target saddle set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family rewrites a coupled optimization problem as a convex-concave saddle problem. Agents perform separable primal computations, while shared or local-copy multipliers coordinate the coupling; primal and dual operators may be updated directly, proximally, or through splitting and augmentation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining object is a network-realized primal-dual iteration whose target is the displayed saddle inequality and whose agent computations exploit separability of the Lagrangian or saddle operator.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For closed proper convex-concave \(L\), the saddle condition is equivalently \(0\in\partial_xL(x^\star,y^\star)\) and \(0\in-\partial_yL(x^\star,y^\star)\).
special_cases_latex: Dual decomposition minimizes the Lagrangian separately in each \(x_i\) and coordinates multipliers.
Distributed ADMM is obtained from an augmented Lagrangian and alternating primal and dual updates.
Primal-dual splitting applies resolvents and forward steps to the associated monotone inclusion.
immediate_consequences_latex: Separable dependence on \(x_i\) permits local primal subproblems once the required multiplier information is available.
boundary_notes: Nonconvex-nonconcave games are outside this stated convex-concave definition.
The communication architecture and precise splitting order distinguish subclasses.

children.title: Distributed Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of coupled problems through coordinated multiplier variables.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\), where each \(X_i\) is nonempty and convex and each \(f_i\) is proper convex. Let \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\) be the multiplier for the coupling equality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable convex programs coupled by a finite-dimensional linear equality, with coordination performed in dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Distributed dual decomposition is the method family induced by the separable Lagrangian \[L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,A_i x_i\rangle\bigr)-\langle\lambda,b\rangle\] and dual function \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i(\lambda)-\langle\lambda,b\rangle,\qquad q_i(\lambda)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,A_i x_i\rangle\}.\] At iteration \(k\), agents solve or approximate their independent \(q_i(\lambda^k)\) subproblems and a coordinating mechanism updates the multiplier using the aggregate residual \(\sum_i A_i x_i^k-b\), for example \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_k(\sum_iA_i x_i^k-b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual decomposition dualizes the coupling equality, causing the Lagrangian minimization to separate into one local problem per agent. The agents return local minimizers or resource contributions, and a coordinator or peer-to-peer mechanism changes the multiplier using the aggregate constraint residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is defined by separable local minimization at a common multiplier and multiplier coordination driven by the coupling residual.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The residual \(\sum_iA_i x_i(\lambda)-b\) is a supergradient of the concave dual function \(q\) at \(\lambda\) whenever the local infima are attained.
special_cases_latex: Inequality coupling uses a multiplier constrained to the nonnegative orthant and a projected dual update.
Resource allocation corresponds to \(A_i=I\) and an aggregate supply vector \(b\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Given \(\lambda^k\), all local Lagrangian subproblems can be solved in parallel.
boundary_notes: Primal iterates produced by local minimization need not be feasible before convergence.
A nonzero duality gap or unattained local infimum limits primal interpretation.

Multiplier for the aggregate coupling constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Coordinated Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master broadcasts prices, agents solve separable Lagrangian subproblems in parallel, and the master updates prices using the aggregate coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\). Initialize a master multiplier \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R^m\). At iteration \(k\), broadcast \(\lambda^k\); each agent returns \[x_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+(\lambda^k)^\top A_ix_i\bigr).\] The master forms \(r^k=\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b\) and updates \[\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_kr^k),\] where \(\Lambda=\mathbb R^m\) for equality constraints. Stop when \(\lVert r^k\rVert\) and the dual improvement are below tolerances; output the multiplier and a primal recovery derived from the local solutions.
assumptions_latex: Every local subproblem attains its minimum.
The coupling constraint is affine and separable by agent.
For convergence, strong duality holds and the projected dual-subgradient steps obey a valid diminishing-stepsize rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^k\) is a supergradient of the concave dual function at \(\lambda^k\), so the master update is projected dual ascent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central multiplier update with parallel solutions of separable Lagrangian subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus-Based Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent maintains a local price, solves its own Lagrangian subproblem, then mixes prices with neighbors while adding its local coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let there be \(n\geq1\) agents. For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_i}\), \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\), \(A_i:\mathbb R^{d_i}\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(b_i\in\mathbb R^m\), with \(\sum_{i=1}^n b_i=b\). Let \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a nonempty closed convex multiplier set, and initialize \(\lambda_i^0\in\Lambda\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) computes \[x_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+(\lambda_i^k)^\top(A_ix_i-b_i)\bigr),\] exchanges multiplier copies with its neighbors, and updates \[\lambda_i^{k+1}=\Pi_\Lambda\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}^k\lambda_j^k+\alpha_k(A_ix_i^k-b_i)\right).\] Stop when neighboring multiplier copies agree within a prescribed tolerance and the aggregate residual \(\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^n(A_ix_i^k-b_i)\right\rVert\) is small. Return the common price estimate together with an ergodically recovered primal allocation.
assumptions_latex: For every iterate, each local Lagrangian subproblem attains a minimum.
The local dual supergradients are uniformly bounded on the nonempty closed convex multiplier set \(\Lambda\).
Each \(W^k\) is doubly stochastic, the mixing sequence is uniformly connected, and its positive weights satisfy the method's required uniform lower bound.
The steps satisfy \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update combines consensus of the local multiplier copies with a local dual-supergradient innovation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Peer-to-peer dual ascent using local multiplier copies and consensus mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Primal Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted averages of local primal responses provide a recoverable decision; its coupling residual and primal–dual gap certify feasibility and, when feasible, suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dual-decomposition iterates \(x_i^t\) and positive weights \(\alpha_t\), define \(S_k=\sum_{t=0}^k\alpha_t\) and \[\bar x_i^k=S_k^{-1}\sum_{t=0}^k\alpha_tx_i^t.\] Agents can average their local residuals to evaluate \(r^k=\sum_iA_i\bar x_i^k-b\). Given any dual-feasible \(\lambda^k\) with dual value \(q(\lambda^k)\), the pair is an \((\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_g)\)-certificate when \[\lVert r^k\rVert\leq\varepsilon_f,\qquad \sum_if_i(\bar x_i^k)-q(\lambda^k)\leq\varepsilon_g.\] The first inequality certifies approximate coupling feasibility; weak duality makes the second a verifiable upper bound on primal suboptimality whenever \(\bar x^k\) is feasible.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is convex and each averaged local point remains in its convex set \(X_i\).
\(q(\lambda^k)\) is a valid dual lower bound.
Agents can aggregate the local residuals and objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual and gap constitute a distributedly aggregable certificate for the recovered primal point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ergodic primal recovery and computable feasibility–duality-gap certification.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the decomposed problem \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), let \(x_i^k\) be local Lagrangian minimizers generated from multiplier iterates \(\lambda^k\). Let \(\omega_{t,k}\ge0\) with \(\sum_{t=0}^k\omega_{t,k}=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of candidate primal decisions from distributed dual-decomposition iterates, including ergodic averaging and feasibility certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed primal-recovery scheme is a family of locally computable maps producing \(\bar x_i^k\in X_i\) from dual-algorithm data such that the assembled vector \(\bar x^k=(\bar x_1^k,\ldots,\bar x_m^k)\) is evaluated by both its objective value and coupling residual. The canonical ergodic recovery is \[\bar x_i^k=\sum_{t=0}^k\omega_{t,k}x_i^t,\qquad e^k=A\bar x^k-b.\] A recovery is exact at iteration \(k\) when \(e^k=0\); it is \(\varepsilon_k\)-feasible when \(\|e^k\|\le\varepsilon_k\). If the raw local minimizer is unique and compatible with an optimal multiplier, direct recovery \(\bar x_i^k=x_i(\lambda^k)\) is also included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal recovery converts the local minimizers generated by a dual method into an assembled primal candidate, commonly by weighted time averaging. The recovered point is accompanied by its aggregate coupling residual and objective value; feasibility is not inferred from dual progress alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovery object is the assembled local map \(\bar x^k\) together with the explicit residual \(e^k=A\bar x^k-b\) and a stated feasibility tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For affine coupling, the residual of ergodic recovery satisfies \(e^k=\sum_{t=0}^k\omega_{t,k}(Ax^t-b)\).
special_cases_latex: Uniform averaging uses \(\omega_{t,k}=1/(k+1)\).
Stepsize-weighted averaging uses \(\omega_{t,k}=\alpha_t/\sum_{s=0}^k\alpha_s\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Convexity of each \(X_i\) ensures that convexly averaged local iterates remain in \(X_i\).
boundary_notes: Dual convergence does not by itself guarantee convergence of raw primal minimizers when the Lagrangian minimizer is nonunique.
Nonaffine coupling requires a recovery residual defined for the original constraint map.

notation.meaning: Recovered primal decision of agent i.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A distributed resource-allocation method addresses \[\min_{x_i
i X_i}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^m x_i=b,\] or the inequality-capacity analogue, by assigning \(x_i\), \(f_i\), and \(X_i\) to agent \(i\) and generating local states using only local data and received messages. Membership requires that the algorithm explicitly coordinate the aggregate balance, either by preserving it in primal space, by updating a price multiplier for it, or by jointly evolving allocation and multiplier states. A generic distributed consensus optimizer is not a resource-allocation method unless its state and invariants encode this aggregate constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent controls a local allocation subject to its own capacity set, while all allocations must sum to a prescribed resource vector. Distributed methods coordinate this balance through feasibility-preserving exchanges, dual prices, or joint primal-dual dynamics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is defined by a separable allocation objective, local capacity sets, an aggregate balance constraint, and a distributed mechanism that explicitly coordinates that balance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing a multiplier \(\lambda\) gives the separable Lagrangian \(L(x,\lambda)=\sum_i(f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,x_i\rangle)-\langle\lambda,b\rangle\).
special_cases_latex: Scalar economic dispatch has \(p=1\) and interval sets \(X_i=[\underline x_i,\overline x_i]\).
Network-flow allocation replaces the simple sum by an incidence-matrix conservation equation.
immediate_consequences_latex: For equality balance, any primal exchange direction \(d=(d_i)_i\) with \(\sum_i d_i=0\) preserves aggregate feasibility.
boundary_notes: Consensus constraints \(x_i=x_j\) are structurally different from resource balance \(\sum_i x_i=b\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Price Coordination
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents respond to local price estimates and adjust those prices by mixing with neighbors plus their individual supply–demand imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_ix_i=d\), and choose shares \(d_i\) satisfying \(\sum_id_i=d\). Initialize local prices \(\lambda_i^0\in\mathbb R^p\). Each agent computes \[x_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+(\lambda_i^k)^\top x_i\bigr),\] then updates \[\lambda_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}^k\lambda_j^k+\alpha_k(x_i^k-d_i).\] Stop when neighboring prices agree and \(\lVert\sum_ix_i^k-d\rVert\) is small. Output the local allocations and their common limiting price, using ergodic primal recovery if instantaneous allocations oscillate.
assumptions_latex: Every local price-response problem attains a solution.
The mixing matrices are doubly stochastic and uniformly connected.
A diminishing nonsummable, square-summable stepsize sequence is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The innovation \(x_i^k-d_i\) is a local supergradient of the decomposed dual objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed price consensus for equality-constrained separable resource allocation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex resource allocation coordinated through a common or consensus-tracked dual price.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual-price coordination is the allocation mechanism in which each agent's demand or supply response at price \(\lambda^k\) is \[x_i^k\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda^k,x_i\rangle\},\] and the price is adjusted from excess aggregate allocation, canonically as \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_k\left(\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k-b\right).\] In a peer-to-peer implementation, agents maintain \(\lambda_i^k\), mix neighboring price copies, and add a local contribution whose network sum represents \(\sum_i x_i^k-b\). The defining separation is that allocation responses are local functions of price, whereas balance is coordinated in dual space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents independently choose allocations minimizing local cost plus the current resource price. The price then rises or falls according to aggregate excess allocation. A decentralized implementation replaces the single price by local copies coordinated through consensus or tracking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual-price coordination consists of local price-response minimizations and a dual update driven by aggregate balance mismatch.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The price update is an ascent step on the concave dual function whose supergradient is \(\sum_i x_i(\lambda)-b\).
special_cases_latex: For scalar allocation, \(\lambda\) is a scalar marginal price.
Inequality supply constraints use a nonnegative price and projected ascent.
immediate_consequences_latex: If each local response is unique, the aggregate mismatch becomes a single-valued function of price.
boundary_notes: Raw price responses need not satisfy balance before convergence.
Nondifferentiable dual objectives permit set-valued responses and require a subgradient interpretation.

children.title: Primal Feasibility-Preserving Allocation

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility-Preserving Allocation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a balanced allocation, agents exchange marginal costs and move resources along graph edges; the Laplacian update preserves total resource exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar allocations, solve \(\min_x\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\mathbf1^\top x=d\). Choose a feasible initialization \(x^0\) with \(\mathbf1^\top x^0=d\), and let \(L_G\) be the Laplacian of a connected undirected communication graph. Iterate \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_kL_G\nabla f(x^k).\] Equivalently, each agent exchanges marginal costs and applies \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k-\alpha_k\sum_ja_{ij}(f_i'(x_i^k)-f_j'(x_j^k))\). Stop when neighboring marginal costs agree within tolerance; output \(x^k\). Since \(\mathbf1^\top L_G=0\), every iterate satisfies the resource balance exactly.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
The communication graph is connected, undirected, and has nonnegative symmetric edge weights.
The initial allocation satisfies \(\mathbf1^\top x^0=d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf1^\top x^k=d\) for every \(k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laplacian-gradient allocation preserving an equality resource balance at every iteration.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The Laplacian identity does establish exact preservation of the initial resource balance, but the cited general decentralized-consensus locator is not specific enough to support this marginal-cost resource-allocation algorithm or its stopping criterion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed allocation algorithms that maintain aggregate equality feasibility at every iterate by balanced primal exchanges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal feasibility-preserving allocation method generates \(x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k\) with distributedly constructed exchange directions satisfying \[\sum_{i=1}^m d_i^k=0,\qquad x_i^k+d_i^k\in X_i\quad\text{for every }i,k.\] Consequently, its defining invariant is \(x^k\in\mathcal X\) for every \(k\). In an edge-based realization, oriented transfers \(s_{ij}^k=-s_{ji}^k\) yield \(d_i^k=\sum_{j\in N_i}s_{ij}^k\); pairwise antisymmetry enforces zero aggregate change. Transfer magnitudes may depend on local gradients, marginal costs, or proximal subproblems, but feasibility preservation is mandatory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a balanced allocation, agents exchange resource only through zero-sum transfers. Every local update respects its capacity set, and the sum of all allocations remains exactly equal to the prescribed resource at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method is defined by local capacity preservation and the zero-sum direction condition \(\sum_i d_i^k=0\), which maintains the aggregate balance invariant.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With an oriented incidence matrix \(B\), every update of the form \(x^{k+1}=x^k+(B\otimes I_p)s^k\) has zero aggregate change.
special_cases_latex: Pairwise trading updates only agents \(i\) and \(j\) with \(d_i^k=-d_j^k\).
For unconstrained local sets, projected capacity safeguards are unnecessary.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every iterate is aggregate-feasible when \(x^0\) is aggregate-feasible and all displayed conditions hold.
boundary_notes: Finding a feasible initializer may itself require a distributed procedure.
Local projection performed independently can destroy the zero-sum invariant unless transfers are coordinated.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Resource Allocation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocations descend on local Lagrangians while price copies mix and integrate local imbalance, jointly seeking stationarity, price consensus, and resource balance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_if_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_ix_i=d\), select shares \(d_i\) with \(\sum_id_i=d\), initialize \(x_i^0\in X_i\) and local prices \(\lambda_i^0\). With a mixing matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\), perform \[x_i^{k+1}=P_{X_i}\!\left(x_i^k-\alpha_k(\nabla f_i(x_i^k)+\lambda_i^k)\right),\] \[\lambda_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}\lambda_j^k+\beta_k(x_i^{k+1}-d_i).\] Stop when primal changes, price disagreement, and the aggregate balance residual are below tolerances. Output \((x_i^k,\lambda_i^k)\); at a fixed point, allocations satisfy local stationarity and prices agree.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and each \(f_i\) is convex and differentiable.
The communication graph is connected and \(W\) is doubly stochastic.
Stepsizes are chosen to satisfy the stability conditions of the selected primal-dual discretization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any converged fixed point with zero aggregate residual satisfies the KKT conditions for the convex resource-allocation problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected primal descent coupled to distributed price consensus and balance innovations.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: For the displayed iteration, a fixed point with consensual prices forces \(x_i=d_i\) for every agent, not merely aggregate balance. Conversely, zero aggregate residual at an arbitrary fixed point does not imply price consensus. Thus the stated fixed-point and KKT conclusion is not justified; an exact sourced primal-dual discretization is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Splitting Iteration for Resource Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives an allocation-specific proximal iteration whose coupling step projects onto the nonnegative fixed-budget allocation set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
\mathcal C=\left\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\mid x_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=b\right\}.
\]
The iteration is
\[
x_i^{k+1}:=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f_i}\!\left(x_i^k-(z^k)_i-(u^k)_i\right),\qquad i=1,\ldots,N,
\]
\[
z^{k+1}:=\Pi_{\mathcal C}(x^{k+1}+u^k),
\]
\[
u_i^{k+1}:=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-(z^{k+1})_i,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,N.
\]
Projection onto \(\mathcal C\) separates by resource coordinate into \(n\) independent projections in \(\mathbb R^N\) onto nonnegative simplices having the corresponding fixed sums \(b_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update each activity block using its local proximal map, project the assembled vector onto the nonnegative fixed-budget allocation set, and update the auxiliary block by the discrepancy between the local and projected allocations. The allocation-set projection decomposes across resource coordinates into n independent fixed-sum simplex projections in R^N.
assumptions_latex: \lambda>0
\mathcal C=\left\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\mid x_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=b\right\}
x^k,z^k,u^k\in(\mathbb R^n)^N
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}x_i^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f_i}\left(x_i^k-(z^k)_i-(u^k)_i\right),\\ z^{k+1}&=\Pi_{\mathcal C}(x^{k+1}+u^k),\\ u_i^{k+1}&=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-(z^{k+1})_i,\end{aligned}\qquad \Pi_{\mathcal C}\text{ separates into }n\text{ fixed-sum simplex projections in }\mathbb R^N.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let agents cooperatively solve \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)+g(Kx)\), or equivalently seek a saddle point of \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\). The primal and dual variables may be partitioned or replicated across a communication graph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex-concave network optimization with joint primal and multiplier evolution; proximal and projected variants are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed primal-dual algorithm is a network iteration maintaining primal states \(x_i^k\) and dual states \(y_i^k\) and applying locally computable forward, backward, projected, or proximal steps to the saddle operator \[\mathcal T(x,y)=\begin{pmatrix}\partial f(x)+K^\top y\\ \partial g^*(y)-Kx\end{pmatrix},\] together with communication that enforces agreement or coupling consistency among replicated components. A canonical simultaneous form is \[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^\top y^k),\qquad y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^{k+1}),\] with each global operation implemented by local blocks and neighbor exchanges. The defining property is joint evolution toward a zero of \(\mathcal T\), rather than complete elimination of either primal or dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The network stores and updates both decisions and multipliers. Local proximal, projected, or gradient operations act on the two blocks of a saddle-point operator, while communication reconciles replicated variables or evaluates coupling blocks. Neither primal nor dual variables are eliminated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family consists of distributed joint updates of primal and dual blocks targeting the zero set of the displayed saddle operator, with communication realizing nonlocal coupling or agreement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\) is a target exactly when \(0\in\partial f(x^\star)+K^\top y^\star\) and \(0\in\partial g^*(y^\star)-Kx^\star\).
special_cases_latex: If \(g\) is an indicator of a coupling constraint, \(y\) is its Lagrange multiplier.
Distributed primal-dual hybrid gradient uses extrapolated \(\bar x^{k+1}\); projected saddle-gradient methods arise when the proximal maps are projections or explicit gradients.
immediate_consequences_latex: Separable \(f\) and \(g^*\), together with sparse \(K\), permit block-local proximal computations and neighbor-only exchanges.
boundary_notes: The displayed iteration is representative; update order, extrapolation, preconditioning, and consensus corrections define distinct algorithms.
No stepsize or convergence guarantee is asserted.

notation.meaning: Current or extrapolated primal point used by the dual step.

review_flags: The hinted primal-dual source could not be inspected, so the representative splitting form and distributed interpretation need verification.

children.title: Primal-Dual Consensus Methods
children.top_down_role: Consensus mechanisms applied to primal and multiplier variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Consensus Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update edge multipliers from disagreement, update each primal variable proximally using neighboring multipliers, and stop when consensus and stationarity residuals are small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the replicated consensus problem \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(Bx=0\), initialize \(x^0,x^{-1}\) and \(y^0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), agents and edges perform
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\sigma B\bar x^k,\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}\!\left(x^k-\tau B^\top y^{k+1}\right),\qquad \bar x^{k+1}=2x^{k+1}-x^k.
\]
The proximal map separates across agents, while multiplication by \(B\) and \(B^\top\) uses only incident-edge messages. Stop when both \(\lVert Bx^k\rVert\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x^k)+B^\top y^k)\) meet prescribed tolerances; otherwise output the latest primal-dual pair.
assumptions_latex: The communication graph is connected and has oriented incidence matrix \(B\).
Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Step sizes satisfy \(\tau\sigma\lVert B\rVert^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every fixed point satisfies \(Bx^\star=0\) and \(0\in\partial f(x^\star)+B^\top y^\star\), hence its primal components agree and solve the consensus problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous incidence-based primal-dual consensus with proximal primal updates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected graph with \(|V|=m\), let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in(\mathbb R^d)^m\), and let \(B\) be an oriented incidence matrix. The consensus constraint is \((B\otimes I_d)x=0\). For proper closed convex \(f_i\), set \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) and define \(L(x,y)=F(x)+\langle y,(B\otimes I_d)x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex consensus optimization on a fixed connected undirected graph; the definition describes a method class rather than a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal-dual consensus method is an iteration producing \((x^k,y^k)\) for the saddle problem \(\min_x\max_y L(x,y)\), with updates of the form \[x^{k+1}=\mathcal P_k\!\left(x^k-(T_k\otimes I_d)(B^\top\otimes I_d)y^k\right),\qquad y^{k+1}=\mathcal D_k\!\left(y^k+(S_k\otimes I_d)(B\otimes I_d)\widetilde x^{k+1}\right),\] where \(T_k,S_k\) are positive step or metric operators, \(\mathcal P_k\) applies local primal operations associated with the \(f_i\), \(\mathcal D_k\) applies edge-local dual operations, and \(\widetilde x^{k+1}\) is a specified current or extrapolated primal state. It is distributed when each node computes its component using local data and messages from neighbors, and each edge multiplier uses only its endpoints. Consensus and optimality are represented jointly by \[(B\otimes I_d)x^\star=0,\qquad 0\in\partial F(x^\star)+(B^\top\otimes I_d)y^\star.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual consensus method maintains one primal copy at every node and multipliers for graph-consensus constraints. Each primal update uses the node's local objective and incident multipliers; each dual update uses disagreement across an edge. A target state simultaneously has zero edge disagreement and satisfies the stationarity inclusion for the replicated consensus problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^k,y^k)\) is a primal-dual consensus iteration precisely when its local primal and edge-dual operations address the saddle system \(0\in\partial F(x)+(B^\top\otimes I_d)y\), \((B\otimes I_d)x=0\) using only graph-local information.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(G\) is connected, \((B\otimes I_d)x=0\) is equivalent to \(x_1=\cdots=x_m\).
special_cases_latex: With a single global auxiliary variable \(z\), the equivalent constraints \(x_i=z\) yield a node-to-center consensus formulation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every saddle point has \(x_i^\star=\bar x^\star\) for all \(i\), where \(\bar x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u}\sum_i f_i(u)\).
boundary_notes: Directed or time-varying graphs require modified mixing, incidence, or weighting conventions.
The definition alone imposes no stepsize condition or convergence guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Saddle-Point Dynamics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal variables descend the network Lagrangian while edge multipliers ascend it; Euler discretization yields a local-message primal-dual iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The continuous-time network saddle dynamics for \(L\) are
\[
\dot x(t)=-\nabla_xL(x(t),y(t))=-\nabla f(x(t))-B^\top y(t),\qquad \dot y(t)=\nabla_yL(x(t),y(t))=Bx(t).
\]
Given \((x^0,y^0)\), the forward-Euler realization is
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k-h\bigl(\nabla f(x^k)+B^\top y^k\bigr),\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+hBx^k.
\]
Each derivative or update uses local gradients and incident-edge communication. A continuous trajectory is reported at a prescribed horizon; the discrete method stops at a horizon or when its consensus and stationarity residuals satisfy selected tolerances.
assumptions_latex: The graph incidence matrix is \(B\), and \(f\) is convex and continuously differentiable.
A saddle point of \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Bx\rangle\) exists.
For the displayed Euler discretization, a step size \(h>0\) is chosen for the desired stability regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equilibria of the flow, and fixed points of its Euler discretization, are precisely primal-dual solutions satisfying \(Bx=0\) and \(\nabla f(x)+B^\top y=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth convex consensus saddle flow and its forward-Euler discretization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Z=\prod_i Z_i\) be a finite-dimensional product Hilbert space and consider \(0\in A z+Bz\), where \(A\) is maximally monotone and block-separable and \(B\) is monotone, Lipschitz, and graph-local. Let \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic synchronous predictor-corrector splittings for monotone network saddle inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed predictive-corrective method is an iteration with a predicted state and a corrected state, \[p^k=J_{\gamma_k A}(z^k-\gamma_k Bz^k),\qquad z^{k+1}=p^k-\gamma_k(Bp^k-Bz^k),\] or a metrically equivalent block form. It is distributed when \(J_{\gamma_k A}\) decomposes into local resolvents and each block \((Bz)_i\) can be evaluated from agent \(i\)'s data and current neighbor states. The first line predicts a proximal primal-dual state from one network evaluation; the second corrects it using the change of the coupled saddle operator between \(z^k\) and \(p^k\). A fixed point obeys \(p^\star=z^\star\) and hence \(0\in Az^\star+Bz^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method first predicts a local proximal primal-dual state using the coupled operator at the current network state. It then corrects the prediction using the difference between coupled-operator evaluations at the prediction and the old state. Local resolvents and neighbor-only coupled evaluations make the scheme distributed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predictive-corrective family consists of graph-local two-evaluation splittings whose fixed points solve \(0\in A+B\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The displayed update is the forward-backward-forward fixed-point map \(T_\gamma z=p-\gamma(Bp-Bz)\), where \(p=J_{\gamma A}(z-\gamma Bz)\).
special_cases_latex: When \(A=N_C\), the prediction is a projection onto \(C\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(z^\star=T_\gamma z^\star\), then \(z^\star=J_{\gamma A}(z^\star-\gamma Bz^\star)\) and therefore \(0\in Az^\star+Bz^\star\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert convergence or prescribe a Lipschitz-dependent stepsize.
Methods using a single forward evaluation belong instead to the forward-backward subclass.

notation.meaning: Resolvent of the monotone operator A.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Predictive-Corrective Primal-Dual Method
Distributed Extragradient Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mix neighboring iterates, predict with one operator evaluation, and correct from the same mixed base using an evaluation at the predictor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(z^0\in K\) and choose \(\alpha>0\). At iteration \(k\), compute the distributed predictor and corrector
\[
u^k=\Pi_K\!\left(\mathcal Wz^k-\alpha F(z^k)\right),\qquad z^{k+1}=\Pi_K\!\left(\mathcal Wz^k-\alpha F(u^k)\right).
\]
Each block of \(\mathcal Wz\) is obtained from neighbor messages, and each block of \(F\) is evaluated locally. The second evaluation at \(u^k\) corrects the first-order step without an implicit solve. Stop when a prescribed network variational-inequality residual and the disagreement \(\lVert (I-\mathcal W)z^k\rVert\) are below tolerance; output \(z^k\) or an ergodic average.
assumptions_latex: The closed convex set \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_n\) is nonempty.
The block operator \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^{nd}\) is monotone and Lipschitz.
The mixing matrix \(W\) respects a connected graph and is doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any fixed point lying in consensus solves the variational inequality \(\langle F(z^\star),z-z^\star\rangle\ge0\) for every consensus-feasible \(z\in K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous projected extragradient with one mixing operation at each evaluation stage.

Plain mixing without a consensus constraint, tracking variable, or correction mechanism can converge to a problem different from the aggregate variational inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Optimistic Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimistic method predicts the next operator value by extrapolating the two latest evaluations, then combines this correction with neighbor mixing and projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(z^{-1}=z^0\in K\) and \(\alpha>0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), each agent exchanges its current block, evaluates its local operator block, and performs
\[
q^k=2F(z^k)-F(z^{k-1}),\qquad z^{k+1}=\Pi_K\!\left(\mathcal Wz^k-\alpha q^k\right).
\]
The stored value \(F(z^{k-1})\) makes the iteration a one-new-evaluation predictive correction. Stop when both \(\lVert z^{k+1}-z^k\rVert\) and \(\lVert(I-\mathcal W)z^k\rVert\) meet prescribed tolerances, or after a fixed horizon; output the final or averaged iterate according to the convergence guarantee being used.
assumptions_latex: The closed convex set \(K\) is a Cartesian product across agents.
The operator \(F\) is monotone and Lipschitz on \(K\).
The matrix \(W\) is graph-compatible and doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A consensual fixed point satisfies the network variational inequality, while the correction \(2F(z^k)-F(z^{k-1})\) uses one new operator evaluation per iteration after initialization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected one-call optimistic method with synchronous graph mixing.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cited material does not specifically support the displayed distributed optimistic iteration. A one-call optimistic operator step combined only with mixing generally needs additional structural assumptions or tracking machinery to represent the intended aggregate network problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictive–Corrective Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a consistent small-step trajectory, extragradient evaluation and optimistic extrapolation approximate the same future operator value to first order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Taylor expansion at \(z^k\) gives the extragradient evaluation
\[
F(u^k)=F(z^k)-\alpha JF(z^k)F(z^k)+O(\alpha^2).
\]
The displacement assumption gives
\[
F(z^{k-1})=F(z^k)+\alpha JF(z^k)F(z^k)+O(\alpha^2),
\]
and therefore
\[
2F(z^k)-F(z^{k-1})=F(z^k)-\alpha JF(z^k)F(z^k)+O(\alpha^2)=F(u^k)+O(\alpha^2).
\]
Thus the extragradient evaluation at a predicted point and the optimistic extrapolation from stored evaluations implement locally matching predictive-corrective information through first order.
assumptions_latex: The operator \(F\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(z^k\), with locally bounded second derivative.
The recent displacement satisfies \(z^k-z^{k-1}=-\alpha F(z^k)+O(\alpha^2)\).
Projection and network-mixing errors are absent or themselves \(O(\alpha^2)\) in the local comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Extragradient and optimistic corrections evaluate the same first-order prediction of the future operator, differing by \(O(\alpha^2)\) under the stated local trajectory relation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local first-order relation; it does not assert exact trajectory equivalence.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The local asymptotic relation is plausible under the stated trajectory assumption, but the cited general splitting section does not specifically support it. The statement also presents a derivation rather than a proof-free knowledge statement.

knowledge_statements.title: Network Saddle Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard network saddle regime combines connected doubly stochastic mixing, a positive consensus gap, and a monotone Lipschitz saddle operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A static network saddle regime is admissible when
\[
W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1,\qquad \mathbf 1^\top W=\mathbf 1^\top,\qquad W_{ij}=0\ \text{for nonedges},\qquad \rho=\lVert W-J\rVert_2<1,
\]
and the stacked saddle operator \(F\) satisfies, for all domain points \(z,z'\),
\[
\langle F(z)-F(z'),z-z'\rangle\ge0,\qquad \lVert F(z)-F(z')\rVert\le L\lVert z-z'\rVert.
\]
Here \(\rho<1\) makes disagreement contract under mixing, while monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity specify the operator regime addressed by distributed extragradient or optimistic corrections.
assumptions_latex: The matrix \(W\) is nonnegative, graph-compatible, and doubly stochastic.
The fixed-point space satisfies \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1\}\).
Each local saddle operator is monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz on the common domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((L,\delta)\) separates operator difficulty from network difficulty; predictive-corrective step restrictions and rates may depend on both quantities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static connected-network regime for monotone Lipschitz saddle operators.

children.top_down_role: Penalty-enhanced decompositions for consensus and general coupling.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in X}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), with block-sparse \(A\) conforming to a communication graph. For \(\rho>0\), define \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax-b\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-coupled optimization using augmented-Lagrangian penalties and decomposable block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed augmentation-splitting method is an iteration obtained by splitting the saddle optimality system of \(\mathcal L_\rho\) into locally solvable primal blocks and graph-local multiplier blocks. In a representative block form, \[x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u_i\in X_i}\mathcal L_\rho(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},u_i,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots;x^k,y^k)+r_i^k(u_i),\] followed by \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b),\] where \(r_i^k\) is an optional local proximal regularizer. The defining features are a positive quadratic penalty on coupling violation, alternating or otherwise split primal processing, and multiplier ascent. Distribution requires each block to access only the rows of \(A\), residual components, and neighboring variables incident to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family augments an equality-constrained Lagrangian with a quadratic coupling penalty, splits the primal minimization into local blocks, and updates multipliers from the coupling residual. The method is distributed when the coupling matrix is graph sparse and every block update uses only incident residuals and neighbor variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An iteration belongs to this family when its local split steps act on the augmented Lagrangian and its dual step accumulates the graph-local feasibility residual \(Ax-b\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The quadratic term may be written \(\frac12\|Ax-b\|_R^2\) for a positive definite or semidefinite graph-local penalty metric \(R\).
special_cases_latex: Consensus ADMM results when \(Ax=b\) encodes equality of replicated variables.
immediate_consequences_latex: At any fixed point with unchanged multiplier, \(Ax^\star=b\).
boundary_notes: A pure dual-decomposition method with \(\rho=0\) is not augmentation-based.
Multi-block update order and regularization materially affect convergence but are not fixed by this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus ADMM alternates parallel local proximal solves, averaging into a shared variable, and scaled-dual updates enforcing agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Rewrite \(\min_z\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(z)\) as \(\min_{x,z}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i=z\). Initialize \(z^0\) and \(u_i^0\). Scaled ADMM performs, in parallel,
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{f_i/\rho}(z^k-u_i^k),
\]
followed by
\[
z^{k+1}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k),\qquad u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-z^{k+1}.
\]
Stop when the primal residuals \(x_i^k-z^k\) and dual residual \(\rho(z^k-z^{k-1})\) satisfy prescribed tolerances; output \(z^k\).
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The consensus problem has a primal-dual solution.
The penalty parameter satisfies \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every fixed point satisfies \(x_i^\star=z^\star\) for all \(i\) and the optimality conditions for \(\min_z\sum_i f_i(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled two-block ADMM for a centralized replicated-variable consensus model.

notation.meaning: Agent replicas and shared consensus variable

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Centralized consensus ADMM and equivalent DRS iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-server ADMM for a sum of closed proper convex functions represented using replicated variables constrained to consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^p}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), introduce replicated variables satisfying \(x_i=y\). With \(\alpha>0\), ADMM yields local primal updates, a centralized averaging update, and dual updates. Once the dual variables have zero mean, the iteration simplifies to \(x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{Prox}_{(1/\alpha)f_i}(\bar x^k-(1/\alpha)u_i^k)\) and \(u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+\alpha(x_i^{k+1}-\bar x^{k+1})\). Its convergence is inherited from ADMM whenever the applicable ADMM convergence hypotheses hold. Equivalently, DRS applied to \(\delta_C(x_1,\ldots,x_n)+\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) gives \(x_i^{k+1/2}=\operatorname{Prox}_{(1/\alpha)f_i}(z_i^k)\) and \(z_i^{k+1}=z_i^k-\bar z^k+2\bar x^{k+1/2}-x_i^{k+1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replicate the common decision and enforce equality with a central consensus variable. Agents perform local proximal and dual updates, while a central reduction computes the average. After the dual variables acquire zero mean, the displayed simplified iteration applies. Its convergence is conditional on the hypotheses of the underlying ADMM convergence result. Douglas–Rachford splitting of the consensus-indicator formulation gives an equivalent iteration.
assumptions_latex: f_i:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is closed, convex, and proper for every }i
\alpha>0
\text{For the convergence conclusion, the hypotheses of the applicable ADMM convergence theorem hold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{Prox}_{(1/\alpha)f_i}\!\left(\bar x^k-\frac1\alpha u_i^k\right),\qquad u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+\alpha\left(x_i^{k+1}-\bar x^{k+1}\right),\quad\text{after the dual variables have zero mean; convergence then follows conditionally from ADMM, and the stated DRS iteration is equivalent.}

With zero-sum dual initialization, the dual variables remain zero-sum.

knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Based ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge-based ADMM gives each edge a coupling variable, alternates local node solves with edge averaging, and updates one multiplier per incidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent consensus by \(x_i=z_e\) for every incidence \(i\in e\). Given \((z^0,u^0)\), scaled ADMM performs
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\arg\min_x\left\{f_i(x)+\frac\rho2\sum_{e\in E_i}\lVert x-z_e^k+u_{ie}^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
then, for each edge \(e=\{i,j\}\),
\[
z_e^{k+1}=\frac{x_i^{k+1}+u_{ie}^k+x_j^{k+1}+u_{je}^k}{2},\qquad u_{ie}^{k+1}=u_{ie}^k+x_i^{k+1}-z_e^{k+1}.
\]
The analogous multiplier update is made for \((j,e)\). Stop when all incidence primal and dual residuals meet tolerance; output the node variables.
assumptions_latex: The undirected communication graph is connected.
Every local objective \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The edge penalty satisfies \(\rho>0\), and a primal-dual solution exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At a fixed point, every incidence constraint holds; graph connectivity then implies \(x_1=\cdots=x_n\), and the common value minimizes \(\sum_i f_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled ADMM on node-edge incidence constraints for an undirected graph.

children.title: Regularized Distributed ADMM Family
children.top_down_role: Regularized variants that simplify local subproblems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), where \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex and the block structure of \(A,B\) follows a communication graph. Let \(P_k\succeq0\) and \(Q_k\succeq0\) be block-diagonal local metrics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous proximal or linearized distributed ADMM; regularizers are algorithmic quadratic terms, not objective modifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regularized distributed ADMM iteration is \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2+\frac12\|x-x^k\|_{P_k}^2\right\},\] \[z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z\left\{g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2+\frac12\|z-z^k\|_{Q_k}^2\right\},\] \[u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.\] It is distributed when the metrics and coupling permit the two minimizations to decompose by agents or edges. A linearized member replaces a difficult quadratic coupling term by its affine expansion at the current iterate plus a local positive quadratic majorizer. Setting \(P_k=Q_k=0\) recovers unregularized ADMM whenever those subproblems are well posed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized distributed ADMM adds local proximal quadratic terms to one or both ADMM minimizations. These terms stabilize or separate the subproblems without changing the underlying constrained objective. Linearized variants replace hard coupled terms with a local first-order model and a majorizing quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is defined by ADMM residual accumulation together with block-local proximal or majorizing regularization in its primal subproblems.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A term \(\frac12\|x-x^k\|_{P_k}^2\) is a variable-metric proximal regularizer.
special_cases_latex: \(Q_k=0\) and \(P_k\succ0\) gives one-sided proximal ADMM.
immediate_consequences_latex: The regularization vanishes at a fixed point because \(x^{k+1}=x^k\) and \(z^{k+1}=z^k\).
boundary_notes: Indefinite proximal metrics require separate conditions and are excluded.
Regularizing the original objective permanently is not the same construction.
review_flags: An inspected source for the exact proximal/linearized distributed family is needed.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Distributed ADMM
Linearized Distributed ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearized distributed ADMM replaces one quadratic augmented-Lagrangian subproblem by a proximal gradient step, reducing local solve cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \((x^0,z^0,u^0)\). Linearize the quadratic penalty in the \(x\)-block and iterate
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}\!\left(x^k-\tau\rho A^\top r^k\right),
\]
\[
z^{k+1}=\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
In a distributed model, separability of \(f\), \(g\), and the incidence structure makes these updates local after neighbor communication. Stop using standard primal and dual residual tolerances; output \((x^k,z^k)\).
assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), with proper closed convex \(f,g\).
A primal-dual solution exists and \(\rho>0\).
The parameter satisfies \(\tau^{-1}I-\rho A^\top A\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linearized primal subproblem is proximal and separable whenever \(f\) is separable; fixed points satisfy the original ADMM optimality system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-linearized scaled ADMM for a separable linearly constrained convex problem.

notation.meaning: Current constraint residual before the primal update

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Distributed ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal distributed ADMM stabilizes or simplifies local subproblems by adding positive-semidefinite distances to the previous block iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,z}f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), initialize \((x^0,z^0,u^0)\) and iterate
\[
x^{k+1}=\arg\min_x\left\{f(x)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_P^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}=\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert z-z^k\rVert_Q^2\right\},
\]
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
Distributed implementation uses block-diagonal \(P,Q\) and graph-sparse constraints. Stop at prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances.
assumptions_latex: The linearly constrained convex problem has a primal-dual solution.
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex, and \(\rho>0\).
The regularization matrices satisfy \(P\succeq0\) and \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The additional proximal terms vanish from the fixed-point equations, so fixed points satisfy the KKT conditions of the unregularized constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block scaled ADMM with explicit proximal regularization of both subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Regularized ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid regularized ADMM linearizes a smooth objective component while retaining proximal metrics and exact augmented coupling in distributed subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \((x^0,z^0,u^0)\). A hybrid regularized ADMM step is
\[
x^{k+1}=\arg\min_x\left\{f(x)+\langle\nabla h(x^k),x-x^k\rangle+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_P^2+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}=\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert z-z^k\rVert_Q^2\right\},
\]
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
Choose graph-compatible block metrics for distributed local solves. Stop when primal and dual residuals meet tolerance; output the latest primal blocks.
assumptions_latex: The objective is \(h(x)+f(x)+g(z)\), where \(h\) is convex with \(L_h\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(f,g\) are proper closed convex.
The constraint is \(Ax+Bz=c\), and a primal-dual solution exists.
The metric satisfies \(P- L_h I/2\succeq0\), with \(Q\succeq0\) and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed points satisfy the KKT conditions for the original composite problem; smooth terms are linearized while nonsmooth terms and coupling penalties remain implicit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite ADMM combining smooth linearization with proximal regularization.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The hybrid update is mathematically recognizable, but the exact condition P-L_h I/2 positive semidefinite is version-dependent and is explicitly marked unresolved. The cited broad sections must be inspected before accepting this parameter condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Subproblem Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact local solves cost more per round; proximal or linearized solves reduce local work but impose regularization or stepsize restrictions. Their converged fixed points still satisfy the unregularized problem’s KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex problem \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\). A regularized ADMM local step has the form \[x^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_x\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax+Bz^k-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_P^2\right\},\] where \(P\succeq0\). Choosing \(P=0\) retains the exact augmented-Lagrangian subproblem; a positive block-diagonal \(P\) can make local solves separable or strongly convex; choosing \(P\) to majorize and cancel difficult quadratic curvature yields a linearized step. These choices change per-iteration computation and admissible stepsizes, but any converged fixed point satisfying the unchanged dual and constraint updates obeys the original KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(\rho>0\) and \(P\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^k,z^k,y^k)\to(x^\star,z^\star,y^\star)\) implies \(Ax^\star+Bz^\star=c\), \(0\in\partial f(x^\star)+A^*y^\star\), and \(0\in\partial g(z^\star)+B^*y^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares exact, proximal, and linearized local solves within two-block distributed ADMM.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cited augmented-Lagrangian section does not specifically support the proximal-curvature cancellation, admissible-stepsize, and fixed-point claims for this regularized ADMM variant. The plain statement also asserts that exact solves cost more, whereas the mathematical statement makes no universal ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Augmented-Lagrangian Frameworks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable network problem can be represented by an augmented Lagrangian whose sparse coupling operator permits local and neighbor computations, followed by multiplier ascent on the coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X_1,\ldots,\mathcal X_m\) and \(\mathcal Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathcal X_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal X_m\), and define \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\). Let \(K:\mathcal X_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal X_m\to\mathcal Y\) be a bounded linear network-coupling operator and let \(b\in\mathcal Y\). For \(y\in\mathcal Y\) and \(\rho>0\), the augmented Lagrangian is \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\langle y,Kx-b\rangle_{\mathcal Y}+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Kx-b\rVert_{\mathcal Y}^2.\] A distributed augmented-Lagrangian framework performs an exact or specified inexact minimization of \(\mathcal L_\rho(\cdot,y^k)\), using the sparsity of \(K\), and updates \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Kx^{k+1}-b).\] When \(K\) is induced by a graph incidence operator, each component of \(Kx\) can be evaluated using endpoint or neighbor exchanges.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X_1,\ldots,\mathcal X_m\) and \(\mathcal Y\) are real Hilbert spaces.
Each \(f_i:\mathcal X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(K:\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal Y\) is bounded and linear, and \(\{x:Kx=b\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L_\rho\) combines separable agent objectives with sparse network coupling, and \(y^{k+1}-y^k=\rho(Kx^{k+1}-b)\) accumulates the coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space augmented-Lagrangian representation of separable objectives with network coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmentation–Splitting Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equality-split convex problem, primal ADMM and Douglas–Rachford splitting of the dual optimality inclusion generate equivalent iterates after a standard variable identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper closed convex \(f,g\) and the split problem \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(x=z\), the Fenchel dual optimality condition can be written \[0\in \partial f^*(-y)-\partial g^*(y).\] Applying Douglas–Rachford splitting to the two maximal monotone operators \(A:y\mapsto-\partial f^*(-y)\) and \(B=\partial g^*\), with resolvent parameter \(\rho>0\), is equivalent, after the standard affine identification of the splitting and scaled-multiplier variables, to ADMM applied to the primal equality split. Thus quadratic augmentation produces the proximal resolvents, while operator splitting permits alternating evaluation of the two component subproblems.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Strong duality holds and the primal-dual solution set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ADMM multiplier sequence is an affine shadow of the Douglas–Rachford sequence for \(0\in A(y)+B(y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus ADMM viewed as Douglas–Rachford splitting of the associated dual inclusion.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of the primal objective terms.
Dual maximal monotone operators used by Douglas–Rachford splitting.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\prod_i\mathcal H_i\), \(\mathcal G=\prod_e\mathcal G_e\), and consider \(\min_x f(x)+h(x)+g(Kx)\), where \(f=\sum_i f_i\) and \(g=\sum_e g_e\) are proximable, \(h\) is convex differentiable, and the block sparsity of \(K\) follows a graph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex composite optimization represented as a structured primal-dual monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A distributed primal-dual splitting is a fixed-point iteration for \[0\in\partial f(x)+
abla h(x)+K^	op y,\qquad 0\in\partial g^*(y)-Kx,\] that evaluates the resolvents of \(\partial f\) and \(\partial g^*\) separately and applies \(K,K^	op\), and \(
abla h\) explicitly. A representative preconditioned form is \[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{Tf} igl(x^k-T(
abla h(x^k)+K^	op y^k) igr),\] \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{Sg^*} igl(y^k+SK(2x^{k+1}-x^k) igr),\] where \(T,S\) are positive block-diagonal metrics. It is distributed when every proximal map decomposes into node or edge blocks and every multiplication by \(K\) or \(K^	op\) requires only messages along incident graph edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed primal-dual splitting rewrites a composite network problem as coupled primal and dual monotone inclusions. It applies local proximal operations to nonsmooth terms, explicit local gradients to smooth terms, and graph-sparse linear coupling operations between node and edge blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method class consists of graph-local operator splittings whose fixed points satisfy the displayed primal-dual optimality system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The system is equivalent to \(0\in Az+Bz\) on \(z=(x,y)\), with \(A=(\partial f,\partial g^*)\) and \(B(x,y)=(\nabla h(x)+K^\top y,-Kx)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(h=0\), only proximal and sparse linear operations remain.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any fixed point yields a primal minimizer and a compatible dual solution when standard convex qualification holds.
boundary_notes: Stepsize and qualification conditions are not part of this method definition.
Nonseparable proximal maps may destroy distributability even when the abstract splitting is valid.
