children.title: Exact-Diffusion Bias-Correction Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence families explaining removal of steady-state network bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Diffusion Bias-Correction Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With smooth strongly convex objectives and a small constant step, deterministic exact diffusion converges linearly to the exact consensual optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, smooth, and strongly convex, and let the fixed undirected communication graph admit a symmetric doubly stochastic matrix \(A\) with \(\ker(I-A)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\). For deterministic exact diffusion with a sufficiently small constant step size \(\alpha>0\), there exist \(C<\infty\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \[\|X^k-\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\|^2\le C\rho^k,\] where \(x^\star\) is the unique minimizer of \(n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\). Hence the limiting consensus point is \(x^\star\), with no nonzero steady-state network bias.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is smooth and strongly convex.
\(A=A^\top\), \(A\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\ker(I-A)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).
\(\alpha>0\) satisfies the method-specific stability bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|X^k-\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\|^2\le C\rho^k\longrightarrow0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic convergence statement emphasizing removal of constant-step network bias.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: linear exact convergence is the canonical strongly-convex deterministic result

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is correct for this convergence leaf, but a linear-convergence theorem cannot be accepted from standard-field rationale alone. The exact admissible step-size and any additional eigenvalue, weighting, initialization, or objective assumptions must be taken from a method-specific theorem. No supporting source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(W^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) be the stacked exact-diffusion iterates for minimizing \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x)\), and let \(W^\star=\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\) for a solution \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the convergence property that distinguishes exact diffusion from neighborhood convergence; it is not a theorem supplying sufficient hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact-diffusion trajectory has bias-correction convergence when its optimization and disagreement errors vanish at a persistent stepsize: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|\bar w^k-x^\star\|=0\) and \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|W^k-\mathbf1(\bar w^k)^\top\|_F=0\). Equivalently, \(W^k\to W^\star\). In a stochastic constant-stepsize regime, the corresponding mean-square property is separated into a noise term and a network-bias term: bias correction means the deterministic network-heterogeneity contribution to \(\limsup_k n^{-1}\mathbb E\|W^k-W^\star\|_F^2\) is zero, although an oracle-noise floor may remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bias-correction convergence means that deterministic exact-diffusion iterates reach the common optimizer rather than a network-dependent neighborhood despite a nonvanishing stepsize. In stochastic operation, it means the persistent error contains no deterministic network-heterogeneity bias, although sampling noise can still cause a nonzero mean-square floor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining deterministic property is \(W^k\to\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\); the stochastic property removes the deterministic network-bias component from the limiting mean-square error.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(W^k\to W^\star\) is equivalent to simultaneous convergence of the network average to \(x^\star\) and disappearance of consensus disagreement.
special_cases_latex: With zero oracle variance, the stochastic formulation reduces to deterministic exact convergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: A positive limiting error caused solely by heterogeneous local gradients violates this property.
boundary_notes: The definition does not specify a rate or sufficient stepsize bound.
An oracle-noise floor is not classified as network bias.
review_flags: The exact decomposition of stochastic steady-state error requires a source; none was inspectable.

children.title: Directed-Graph Push-Sum Convergence Conditions
children.top_down_role: Connectivity, normalization, and stability families for directed convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Perturbations Generally Shift the Push-Sum Limit
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable numerator disturbances preserve agreement under stable fixed mixing but generally shift the common value by their total injected mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed primitive column-stochastic \(A\), let \(z^{k+1}=Az^k+e^k\), \(w^{k+1}=Aw^k\), \(w^0>0\), and \(\sum_k\|e^k\|<\infty\). Then the common ratio limit is \[\frac{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z^0+\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}e^k}{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0}.\] It equals the unperturbed value only when the total injected mass is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is primitive and column-stochastic.
\(\sum_k\|e^k\|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_i^k/w_i^k\to(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z^0+\sum_k\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}e^k)/(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction to the deferred claim that summability preserves the unperturbed average.

knowledge_statements.title: Lack of Recurrent Directed Reachability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push-sum cannot guarantee global agreement when directed information flow is permanently reducible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If after some finite time a directed graph sequence is reducible across a nontrivial ordered partition, compatible column-stochastic push-sum products cannot force every initialization to one common ratio. In particular, a fixed reducible mixing matrix cannot guarantee global ratio consensus.
assumptions_latex: Mixing matrices are graph-compatible and column-stochastic.
The graph sequence is eventually reducible across a nontrivial partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Universal push-sum ratio consensus fails.}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity obstruction to universal push-sum agreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Time-Varying Push-Sum Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform positivity, self-loops, and bounded-window strong connectivity keep push-sum normalization valid and yield geometric ratio consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^k\) be column-stochastic matrices with positive diagonals, every positive entry at least \(\eta>0\), and graph unions over every \(B\) consecutive iterations strongly connected. For \(z^{k+1}=A^kz^k\), \(w^{k+1}=A^kw^k\), and \(w^0>0\), all denominators remain positive and there exist \(C<\infty\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \[\max_i\left\|\frac{z_i^k}{w_i^k}-\frac{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z^0}{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0}\right\|\le C\rho^k\|z^0\|.\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(A^k\) is column-stochastic and graph-compatible.
Every positive entry is at least \(\eta>0\), including a positive diagonal entry.
Every union of \(B\) consecutive directed graphs is strongly connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_i^k/w_i^k\to(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z^0)/(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0)\) geometrically for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unperturbed push-sum convergence under regular directed graph products.

notation.meaning: uniform lower bound on positive mixing weights

knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Graph Push-Sum Convergence Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard time-varying, column-stochastic push-sum consensus conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^k=[a_{ij}^k]\) be column-stochastic, with every positive entry at least \(\eta>0\), and let each diagonal entry be positive. Suppose the union of every \(B\) consecutive communication graphs is strongly connected. Initialize \(s^0\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(w^0=\mathbf 1\), and iterate \(s^{k+1}=A^ks^k\), \(w^{k+1}=A^kw^k\). Then every \(w_i^k\) remains positive and the normalized states satisfy \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{s_i^k}{w_i^k}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n s_j^0\quad\text{for every }i.\] Uniform positivity and bounded-window strong connectivity are the stability and information-flow conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive column-stochastic weights, self-loops, and repeated strong connectivity make every push-sum ratio converge to the initial network average.
assumptions_latex: \(A^k\ge 0\), \(\mathbf 1^\top A^k=\mathbf 1^\top\), and \(a_{ij}^k>0\Rightarrow a_{ij}^k\ge\eta\).
Every diagonal entry is positive, and each union graph over \(B\) consecutive times is strongly connected.
\(w^0=\mathbf 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i^k/w_i^k\to n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n s_j^0\) for every agent \(i\).

notation.meaning: column-stochastic mixing matrix at iteration k
numerator and normalization weight of agent i
connectivity-window length and positive-weight lower bound

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A^k\ge0\) be column-stochastic matrices compatible with directed graphs \(G^k\), and let \(z^{k+1}=A^kz^k\), \(s^{k+1}=A^ks^k\), \(x_i^k=z_i^k/s_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A condition family for time-varying directed push-sum; it defines the standard uniform connectivity, positivity, normalization, and denominator-stability requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The directed push-sum sequence satisfies uniform convergence conditions when there exist integers \(B\ge1\) and a constant \(\eta>0\) such that: \(A^k\) is column stochastic for every \(k\); every positive entry obeys \(a_{ij}^k\ge\eta\); every diagonal entry obeys \(a_{ii}^k\ge\eta\); and for every \(t\ge0\), the union graph \((V,\bigcup_{k=t}^{t+B-1}E^k)\) is strongly connected. With \(s^0\succ0\), denominator stability additionally requires constants \(0<\underline s\le\overline s<\infty\) such that \(\underline s\le s_i^k\le\overline s\) for all \(i,k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard push-sum convergence-condition family requires column-stochastic mass preservation, uniformly positive active and self-loop weights, repeated strong connectivity over bounded time windows, and normalization masses uniformly bounded away from zero and infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition family is the conjunction of uniform column stochasticity, positive weights, bounded-window strong connectivity, and stable positive denominators.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Bounded-window strong connectivity is also called uniform joint strong connectivity.
special_cases_latex: For a fixed graph and fixed matrix, the connectivity condition reduces to strong connectivity, with a positive diagonal ensuring aperiodicity.
immediate_consequences_latex: The normalized matrices \((S^{k+1})^{-1}A^kS^k\) are well-defined when denominator stability holds.
boundary_notes: These are condition definitions, not a convergence theorem.
Alternative push-sum analyses may derive denominator bounds from connectivity and positivity rather than assume them separately.

notation.meaning: Uniform lower bound on positive communication weights.

children.title: Resource-Allocation Dual Convergence Conditions
children.top_down_role: Convergence families for prices, allocations, and balance residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Allocation Dual Convergence Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong duality, network connectivity, bounded residuals, and standard diminishing stepsizes, local prices agree at a dual optimum and ergodic allocations become optimal and balanced.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex allocation problem \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_if_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_ix_i=d\), and the consensus-based dual-price iteration with local residuals \(x_i^k-d_i\). Suppose strong duality holds, the dual solution set is nonempty, residuals are uniformly bounded, the doubly stochastic graph sequence is uniformly connected, and \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\). Then every local price copy converges to a common dual-optimal multiplier. Moreover, weighted ergodic primal averages have coupling residual converging to zero and objective values converging to the primal optimum. If the primal optimizer is unique, the recovered allocations converge to it.
assumptions_latex: The local objectives and constraint sets define a convex problem satisfying strong duality with attained primal and dual optima.
Dual supergradients are uniformly bounded along the iterates, and the mixing sequence is doubly stochastic and uniformly connected.
\(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_i^k\to\lambda^\star\) for all \(i\), while \(\lVert\sum_i\bar x_i^k-d\rVert\to0\) and \(\sum_if_i(\bar x_i^k)\to p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of distributed dual subgradient prices and ergodically recovered allocations.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cited broad sections do not identify a theorem supporting all three asserted conclusions. Convergence of every price iterate to one multiplier and convergence of ergodic primal objective values and allocations require an exact recovery construction and additional regularity or boundedness hypotheses not stated here. The theorem cannot be accepted from these generic locators.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-Convergence Condition Package for Resource Allocation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be the concave dual function of a convex resource-allocation problem, \(\Lambda^\star=\arg\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\), and let \(r^k\) be the balance residual used as a dual supergradient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A definitional condition package under which distributed price iterations are normally analyzed; this slot states conditions, not a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard resource-allocation dual-convergence condition package consists of: \((i)\) a nonempty primal feasible set and finite optimum; \((ii)\) zero duality gap and nonempty \(\Lambda^\star\); \((iii)\) well-posed local price-response problems and uniformly bounded dual supergradients on the iterates; \((iv)\) network mixing that asymptotically coordinates local price copies, typically through repeated connectivity and stochastic-weight conditions; \((v)\) errors or delays whose weighted effect is summable; and \((vi)\) stepsizes satisfying either \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), or a separately specified constant-stepsize accuracy regime. Primal convergence additionally requires uniqueness, regularity, or an explicit ergodic recovery rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This condition package combines primal feasibility and strong duality, existence of optimal prices, bounded and well-defined local responses, sufficient network mixing, controlled errors, and an admissible stepsize policy. Convergence of prices does not automatically imply convergence of raw allocations, so primal regularity or recovery is listed separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The package is the conjunction of optimization regularity, bounded dual information, network coordination, controlled perturbations, and a declared stepsize regime, with an additional recovery condition for primal conclusions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When the dual is differentiable with Lipschitz gradient, bounded-supergradient and diminishing-stepsize clauses may be replaced by smooth dual-gradient conditions and a compatible fixed stepsize.
special_cases_latex: Strong convexity of every \(f_i\) commonly makes local price responses unique.
For a static connected undirected graph, a fixed doubly stochastic mixing matrix with a spectral gap supplies a standard coordination condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: Without a primal-recovery clause, the condition package supports only dual-variable and dual-value conclusions.
boundary_notes: This is a definition of a hypothesis package, not an assertion that every listed condition is necessary.
Constant-stepsize methods may converge only to a neighborhood unless their algorithm includes an exact correction.
review_flags: The node requests convergence conditions, but no inspectable source supports this combined package; individual algorithms may require different hypotheses.

children.title: Distributed Saddle-Residual Convergence
children.top_down_role: Gap, residual, ergodic, and last-iterate convergence families.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Saddle-Residual Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ergodic saddle gap is bounded by the centralized cumulative constant plus accumulated network errors, divided by the iteration count. Summable errors preserve an order-one-over-K rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\ge 1\), let \(\bar z^K=K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}z^k\), and define \(G_Z(w)=\sup_{z\in Z}\langle F(z),w-z\rangle\). If, for every \(z\in Z\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\langle F(z^k),z^k-z\rangle\le C+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\varepsilon_k\), then
\[
G_Z(\bar z^K)\le \frac{C+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\varepsilon_k}{K}.
\]
If \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), then \(G_Z(\bar z^K)=O(K^{-1})\). If only \(K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\varepsilon_k\to0\), then \(G_Z(\bar z^K)\to0\).
assumptions_latex: The set \(Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is nonempty, compact, and convex, and contains a solution.
The operator \(F:Z\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is monotone, and \(z^k\in Z\) for every \(k\).
The constant satisfies \(C\ge0\), the errors satisfy \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), and the displayed cumulative inequality holds for every integer \(K\ge1\) and every \(z\in Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(K\ge1\), \(G_Z(\bar z^K)\le\bigl(C+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\varepsilon_k\bigr)/K\); summable errors yield \(G_Z(\bar z^K)=O(K^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract ergodic gap bound exposing accumulated distributed error.

notation.meaning: Minty-type gap on the test set

children.title: Distributed Primal-Dual Convergence Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Convergence, stability, certificate, and complexity families for primal-dual methods.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a distributed algorithm generate \(z^k=(x^k,y^k)\) for a network saddle problem with solution set \(Z^\star\). Let \(R(z)\ge0\) be a specified certificate and let \(C_K\) count communication rounds or transmitted messages through iteration \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal umbrella definition for convergence, stability, certificate, and communication-complexity claims; it does not assert any particular guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed primal-dual guarantee is a quantified implication \[\mathsf H_{\mathrm{prob}}\wedge\mathsf H_{\mathrm{graph}}\wedge\mathsf H_{\mathrm{alg}}\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathsf Q(\{z^k\},Z^\star,R,C),\] where the hypotheses explicitly state the problem regularity, graph connectivity or mixing regime, and algorithm parameters, and where \(\mathsf Q\) is at least one of: \[\operatorname{dist}(z^k,Z^\star)\to0,\qquad R(z^k)\to0,\qquad R(\bar z^K)\le r(K),\qquad C_\varepsilon\le\inf\{C_K:R(\bar z^K)\le\varepsilon\},\] or a perturbation bound \(\sup_k\operatorname{dist}(z^k,Z^\star)\le\Phi(\text{initial error},\text{noise})\). A complete guarantee identifies whether iterates are last or ergodic, whether the claim is deterministic or probabilistic, and what network communication unit is counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed primal-dual guarantee is a fully quantified statement connecting problem, graph, and algorithm assumptions to a measurable conclusion. The conclusion may concern convergence to the saddle set, decay of a residual or gap, stability under errors, or the communication required to reach a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The guarantee object is the explicit implication from problem, network, and algorithm hypotheses to a convergence, certificate, stability, rate, or communication-complexity assertion.
special_cases_latex: An ergodic rate guarantee has the form \(R(\bar z^K)\le c/(K+1)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A rate bound determines an iteration complexity only after the residual and cost unit are fixed.
boundary_notes: Empirical performance without quantified hypotheses is not a mathematical guarantee.
Iteration complexity and communication complexity may differ when an iteration uses multiple message rounds.

notation.meaning: Specified cumulative communication cost through iteration K.

children.title: Primal-Dual Convergence under Graph Connectivity
children.top_down_role: Convergence regimes coupling network propagation and saddle stability.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Convergence under Graph Connectivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a connected graph, incidence-based agreement is exact. If a finite-dimensional distributed primal-dual update is averaged and its fixed points are exactly KKT points, every iterate sequence converges to a consensual primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph, let \(\mathcal X\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, and let \(K\) be an oriented incidence operator lifted to \(\mathcal X^{|V|}\), so that \[\ker K=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_{|V|}):x_1=\cdots=x_{|V|}\}.\] Suppose a distributed primal-dual splitting on a finite-dimensional product space \(\mathcal H\) is represented by \[w^{k+1}=Tw^k,\] where \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) is averaged in an inner product induced by a positive-definite operator and \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)\ne\varnothing\). Suppose a decoding map \(D\) maps the fixed-point equations exactly to the KKT system of the network saddle problem, including \(Kx=0\). Then, for every \(w^0\in\mathcal H\), the sequence \((w^k)\) converges to some \(w^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\); the decoded primal component reaches agreement, and \(D(w^\star)\) satisfies the network saddle conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, connected, and undirected.
\(\mathcal H\) is finite-dimensional.
\(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) is averaged in a positive-definite metric and \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)\ne\varnothing\).
The decoding map \(D\) identifies the fixed-point system of \(T\) with the network KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w^k\to w^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\), the decoded primal component satisfies \(Kx^\star=0\), and \(D(w^\star)\) is a primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convergence of an averaged network primal-dual map on a connected graph.

notation.meaning: Oriented graph-incidence operator lifted to the decision space.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Primal-Dual Stepsize Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive local primal and dual stepsizes satisfy the stated stability condition when the norm of the diagonally scaled network-coupling operator is strictly below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal Y\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces and consider the convex saddle problem \[\min_{x\in\mathcal X}\max_{y\in\mathcal Y}\; f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y),\] where \(K:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) is linear. Let the primal and dual stepsize operators be \(T=\operatorname{diag}(\tau_i I)\succ0\) and \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_e I)\succ0\). A sufficient preconditioned primal-dual stability condition is \[\bigl\lVert\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\bigr\rVert<1.\] This condition is equivalent to \[T^{-1}-K^*\Sigma K\succ0.\] When \(K\) is a graph-incidence or other sparse coupling operator, the condition couples the local primal stepsizes \(\tau_i\) and dual stepsizes \(\sigma_e\) to the graph and coupling weights.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal Y\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
\(f\) and \(g^*\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(K:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) is linear.
\(T\) and \(\Sigma\) are block-diagonal and strongly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\) if and only if \(T^{-1}-K^*\Sigma K\succ0\), yielding a positive primal-dual metric for the splitting.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal primal-dual stability condition coupling local stepsizes to the network operator norm.

notation.meaning: Sparse network or saddle coupling operator.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^m X_i\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(K:X\to Y\) be the linear coupling operator induced by local constraints and the communication graph, and let \(T=\operatorname{diag}(\tau_1I,\ldots,\tau_mI)\succ0\) and \(\Sigma\succ0\) be primal and dual stepsize operators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic convex primal-dual splitting with scalar local primal steps and a positive-definite dual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The distributed primal-dual stepsizes \((T,\Sigma)\) are admissible when \(T\succ0\), \(\Sigma\succ0\), and \(\|\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\|<1\). Equivalently, the block metric \(M=\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-K^*\\-K&\Sigma^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\) is positive definite. The admissible region is \(\mathcal S(K)=\{(T,\Sigma):T\succ0,\Sigma\succ0,\ \|\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\|<1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a distributed convex saddle formulation with coupling operator \(K\), a primal metric \(T\), and a dual metric \(\Sigma\), the stepsizes are admissible exactly when both metrics are positive definite and the scaled coupling has norm strictly below one. This condition defines the stability region \(\mathcal S(K)\) and is equivalent to positive definiteness of the associated primal-dual block metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((T,\Sigma)\in\mathcal S(K)\iff T\succ0,\ \Sigma\succ0,\ \|\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\|<1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-K^*\\-K&\Sigma^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\succ0\).
\(T^{-1}-K^*\Sigma K\succ0\), equivalently \(\Sigma^{-1}-KTK^*\succ0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(T=\tau I\) and \(\Sigma=\sigma I\), admissibility is \(\tau\sigma\|K\|^2<1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The admissible region depends jointly on operator geometry and network-induced coupling through \(K\).
Replacing the strict inequality by a verified margin \(\|\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\|\leq1-\delta\), \(\delta>0\), yields a uniformly positive-definite metric.
boundary_notes: This definition does not cover method-specific relaxations that permit equality at the boundary.
Additional smooth forward terms can impose a separate cocoercivity or Lipschitz restriction on \(T\).

children.title: Distributed Feasibility and Agreement Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate families for coupling feasibility and network agreement.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a connected graph have incidence matrix \(B\), let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in(\mathbb R^d)^m\), let \(\mathcal X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed local feasible sets, and let \(A_ix_i=b_i\) represent local affine constraints. Write \(\mathbf B=B\otimes I_d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-agent consensus optimization with closed local sets and optional affine constraints; the certificate measures feasibility and agreement separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasibility-agreement certificate is a pair \(C(x)=(r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x),r_{\mathrm{agr}}(x))\in\mathbb R_+^2\), where \(r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)=\big(\sum_{i=1}^m\operatorname{dist}(x_i,\mathcal X_i)^2+\sum_{i=1}^m\|A_ix_i-b_i\|^2\big)^{1/2}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{agr}}(x)=\|\mathbf Bx\|\). An \((\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_a)\)-certificate satisfies \(r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)\leq\varepsilon_f\) and \(r_{\mathrm{agr}}(x)\leq\varepsilon_a\). It is exact when both residuals vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate assigns to the stacked agent state two nonnegative residuals: one aggregates violations of local set and affine constraints, and the other measures disagreement across graph edges. The state is certified to tolerances \((\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_a)\) when the corresponding residuals do not exceed those tolerances; zero residuals certify exact local feasibility and network agreement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(x)\leq(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_a)\iff r_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)\leq\varepsilon_f\ \text{and}\ r_{\mathrm{agr}}(x)\leq\varepsilon_a.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For connected \(G\), \(r_{\mathrm{agr}}(x)=0\iff x_1=\cdots=x_m\).
\(C(x)=(0,0)\iff x_i\in\mathcal X_i,\ A_ix_i=b_i\ \forall i,\ \text{and}\ x_1=\cdots=x_m\).
special_cases_latex: Without affine constraints, omit \(\sum_i\|A_ix_i-b_i\|^2\).
For unconstrained consensus, \(C(x)=(0,\|\mathbf Bx\|)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The two tolerances prevent a small aggregate merit value from concealing either infeasibility or disagreement.
Any norm-equivalent edge residual can replace \(\|\mathbf Bx\|\) if the chosen norm is stated.
boundary_notes: Objective suboptimality and saddle residuals are not components of this certificate.
For disconnected graphs, zero edge disagreement guarantees agreement only within connected components.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from z to S.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint feasibility-agreement certificate
Primal–Dual Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal pair, a multiplier, and matching local subgradients certify optimality when the primal and stationarity residuals all vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\), \(\mathcal Z\), and \(\mathcal Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(A:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) and \(B:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y\) be bounded linear operators, and consider \[\min_{x\in\mathcal X,\,z\in\mathcal Z} f(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c.\] A tuple \((x,z,y,s_x,s_z)\) is an exact primal-dual feasibility certificate when \[s_x\in\partial f(x),\qquad s_z\in\partial g(z),\qquad Ax+Bz-c=0,\] and \[s_x+A^*y=0,\qquad s_z+B^*y=0.\] These relations are the KKT conditions. Under the stated convexity and strong-duality assumptions, they certify that \((x,z)\) is primal optimal and \(y\) is dual optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\), \(\mathcal Z\), and \(\mathcal Y\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(f:\mathcal X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:\mathcal Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(A:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) and \(B:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y\) are bounded and linear.
Strong duality holds for the linear constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed zero residuals certify primal feasibility, dual optimality, primal optimality, and equality of the primal and dual optimal values.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact KKT residual certificate for a convex linearly constrained distributed problem.

notation.meaning: Objective subgradients at the candidate primal variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edgewise endpoint differences form a directly verifiable residual. On a connected graph, its vanishing is equivalent to every agent holding the same decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph with an arbitrary orientation, let \(D\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times|V|}\) be its oriented edge-node incidence matrix, and let \(x=(x_i)_{i\in V}\in(\mathbb R^d)^{|V|}\) be the stacked local decisions. Define the consensus residual \[r_{\mathrm{con}}=(D\otimes I_d)x.\] Each edge can compute its oriented endpoint difference, and the assembled residual vanishes exactly when all adjacent decisions agree. Connectivity gives \[\ker(D\otimes I_d)=\{\mathbf 1\otimes v:v\in\mathbb R^d\},\] so \(r_{\mathrm{con}}=0\) certifies global agreement.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite, connected, and undirected.
\(D\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times|V|}\) is an oriented edge-node incidence matrix of \(G\).
Every local decision belongs to \(\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{con}}=0\) if and only if there exists \(v\in\mathbb R^d\) such that \(x=\mathbf 1\otimes v\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence-residual certificate for exact agreement on a connected undirected graph.

notation.meaning: Stacked vector with common value v at every node.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Feasibility–Agreement Residuals
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The joint residual combines affine-feasibility violation and network disagreement, and it vanishes exactly when the affine constraints and componentwise consensus both hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,d,p\in\mathbb N\), let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected communication graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(B\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times m}\) be an oriented incidence matrix of \(G\). For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathbb R^{md}\), where \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times md}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(C=B\otimes I_d\). Define \[r_{\mathrm{joint}}(x):=\bigl(\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\|Cx\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.\] Then \(r_{\mathrm{joint}}(x)\ge0\), and \(r_{\mathrm{joint}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(Ax=b\) and \(x_i=x_j\) for every pair \(i,j\) in the same connected component of \(G\).
assumptions_latex: \(m,d,p\in\mathbb N\).
\(G=(V,E)\) is undirected and \(B\) is an oriented incidence matrix of \(G\).
\(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times md}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers that annihilate the two constraint operators and pair to one with the affine right-hand side certify incompatibility; conversely, every inconsistent finite-dimensional joint affine system admits such normalized multipliers.

children.title: Convergence with Compressed Communication
children.top_down_role: Guarantee and failure families for optimization under lossy communication.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\) agents hold states \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) and minimize \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Let \(Q_{ij}^k\) denote the possibly randomized compression map applied to the message sent from agent \(j\) to agent \(i\), and set \(\bar x^k=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A property of a specified distributed algorithm-compressor pair; the definition separates optimization and consensus requirements and is not itself a rate theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compressed distributed algorithm is convergent to a solution \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\) if its iterates, generated using messages \(Q_{ij}^k(m_{ij}^k)\), satisfy both optimization convergence and network agreement. Almost-sure convergence means \(\bar x^k\to x^\star\) and \(\max_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|\to0\) almost surely. Mean-square convergence replaces these limits by \(\mathbb E\|\bar x^k-x^\star\|^2\to0\) and \(\mathbb E[n^{-1}\sum_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|^2]\to0\). Convergence to an error neighborhood of radius \(r\) means the corresponding limsup is at most \(r^2\), rather than zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compressed distributed convergence means that an algorithm using compressed messages simultaneously approaches a minimizer of the aggregate objective and reaches agreement among agents. The mode of convergence must be stated explicitly, such as almost sure or mean square. If the limiting error is nonzero, the property is convergence to a neighborhood rather than exact convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x^k\to x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\quad\text{and}\quad\max_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|\to0\) in the declared convergence mode.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In mean square, agreement can be written as \(n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb E\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|^2\to0\).
special_cases_latex: Exact communication is the special case \(Q_{ij}^k(v)=v\).
Neighborhood convergence permits \(\limsup_k\mathbb E\|\bar x^k-x^\star\|^2\le r^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact optimization convergence plus agreement implies \(x_i^k\to x^\star\) for every agent in the same mode.
boundary_notes: Objective-value convergence alone does not define agent agreement.
The compressor assumptions and algorithmic update must be specified before this property can become a guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Convex Rate under Independent Unbiased Compression
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent unbiased compression preserves the inverse-square-root convex rate, inflating its constant by the square root of the averaged compressor-variance factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Subgradient Bound, suppose \(\|x_0-x^*\|\le D\) and choose \[\alpha_k=\frac{D}{G\sqrt{(1+\omega/n)K}},\qquad 0\le k<K.\] Then \(\bar x_K=K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}x_k\) and \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f(x^*)]\le\frac{DG\sqrt{1+\omega/n}}{\sqrt K}.\] Consequently, expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\) is guaranteed when \[K\ge\frac{D^2G^2(1+\omega/n)}{\varepsilon^2}.\]
assumptions_latex: All assumptions of Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Subgradient Bound hold.
The horizon \(K\) is fixed when the constant stepsize is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f(x^*)]\le DG\sqrt{1+\omega/n}/\sqrt K.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Subgradient Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronized distributed projected subgradient descent retains its convex ergodic bound, with independent unbiased compression adding averaged variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf_i on a closed convex set C, let x^*\in\arg\min_C f, and choose g_{i,k}\in\partial f_i(x_k) with \|g_{i,k}\|\le G. Suppose q_{i,k}=Q_{i,k}(g_{i,k}) are conditionally independent across workers and satisfy \mathbb E_kq_{i,k}=g_{i,k} and \mathbb E_k\|q_{i,k}-g_{i,k}\|^2\le\omega\|g_{i,k}\|^2. For \[x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k\bar q_k),\quad \bar q_k=n^{-1}\sum_iq_{i,k},\quad \bar x_K=\frac{\sum_{k<K}\alpha_kx_k}{\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k},\] \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f(x^*)]\le\frac{\|x_0-x^*\|^2+G^2(1+\omega/n)\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k}.\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex with subgradients bounded by G on C.
Compressors are conditionally unbiased and conditionally independent across workers.
A minimizer exists and all workers use the common iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f(x^*)]\le[\|x_0-x^*\|^2+G^2(1+\omega/n)\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k^2]/[2\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex convergence for synchronized workers averaging independently compressed subgradients.
review_flags: Covers synchronized exact aggregation, not decentralized spectral mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Convex Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An abstract convex convergence result for unbiased compressed stochastic subgradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be convex with a minimizer \(x^\star\), and consider \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_k Q(g^k)\). Suppose \(\mathbb E[g^k\mid x^k]\in\partial F(x^k)\), \(\mathbb E[\|g^k\|^2\mid x^k]\leq G^2\), and the compressor obeys \(\mathbb E[Q(v)\mid v]=v\) and \(\mathbb E\|Q(v)-v\|^2\leq\omega\|v\|^2\). If \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}F(x^k)=F(x^\star)\) almost surely; standard bounded-iterate conditions give convergence to the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbiased compression with bounded relative variance preserves asymptotic convex subgradient convergence under square-summable but nonsummable step sizes.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex, attains its minimum, and stochastic subgradients have bounded conditional second moment
\(Q\) is conditionally unbiased with relative variance parameter \(\omega<\infty\)
\(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}F(x^k)=F(x^\star)\) almost surely.
review_flags: A compressor-specific theorem source and its precise boundedness hypotheses are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the convex-convergence leaf, but its almost-sure conclusion and the additional solution-set convergence assertion require a compressor-specific theorem with the exact stochastic measurability and boundedness hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\), assume \(X^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}F\ne\varnothing\), and let \(x_i^k\) be iterates produced using compressed communications. Write \(F^\star=\min F\) and \(\bar x^k=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex finite-dimensional objectives. The definition admits last-iterate or ergodic output and requires the output convention to be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compressed distributed method has convex convergence for an output sequence \(\widehat x^K\) if the compression-driven iterates satisfy \(F(\widehat x^K)-F^\star\to0\) and their consensus residual tends to zero in a declared deterministic or probabilistic mode. For mean convergence this is \(\mathbb E[F(\widehat x^K)-F^\star]\to0\) together with \(\mathbb E[n^{-1}\sum_i\|x_i^K-\bar x^K\|^2]\to0\). If boundedness and lower semicontinuity are part of the selected regime, solution-set convergence may instead be recorded as \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x^K,X^\star)^2]\to0\). The output may be the last average \(\bar x^K\) or a stated weighted average of iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compressed convex convergence is vanishing convex objective suboptimality together with vanishing disagreement for an explicitly defined output. The convergence mode and whether the output is the last iterate or an ergodic average are part of the definition. Distance to the solution set is an alternative criterion only in a regime that supports that implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[F(\widehat x^K)-F^\star]\to0\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbb E\!\left[\frac1n\sum_i\|x_i^K-\bar x^K\|^2\right]\to0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(F\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with unique minimizer \(x^\star\), objective convergence controls \(\mathbb E\|\widehat x^K-x^\star\|^2\) through the quadratic-growth inequality.
special_cases_latex: Ergodic convergence uses \(\widehat x^K=(\sum_{k=0}^{K}a_k\bar x^k)/(\sum_{k=0}^{K}a_k)\) for declared weights \(a_k>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If the objective gap and disagreement vanish, every agent's declared output has asymptotically optimal objective value under the continuity conditions of the chosen regime.
boundary_notes: This definition does not supply a rate.
For merely convex objectives, objective convergence need not imply convergence to a unique point.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Tuned Nonconvex Compression Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing the stepsize using the horizon removes the fixed compression-variance floor and yields an inverse-square-root squared-gradient rate; with zero compression variance the rate is inverse-linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Nonconvex Stationarity, write \(\Delta=f(x_0)-f_{\inf}\). knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Nonconvex Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected stationarity for smooth nonconvex descent with unbiased compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be bounded below and have \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient. For \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha Q(\nabla F(x^k))\), assume \(\mathbb E[Q(v)\mid v]=v\) and \(\mathbb E\|Q(v)\|^2\leq(1+\omega)\|v\|^2\). If \(0<\alpha<2/(L(1+\omega))\), then, for \(K\geq1\), \[\min_{0\leq k<K}\mathbb E\|\nabla F(x^k)\|^2\leq\frac{F(x^0)-F_{\inf}}{K\left(\alpha-\frac{L(1+\omega)\alpha^2}{2}\right)}.\] Hence the expected squared gradient norm approaches zero at order \(O(K^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth nonconvex objectives, unbiased compression slows descent through its variance factor but retains an inverse-iteration expected stationarity rate at a suitably small step size.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Disagreement Decomposition and Floor
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disagreement consists of a geometric network transient plus accumulated optimization and compression forcing; persistent forcing creates a spectral-gap-amplified floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define h_k=\alpha_k\|JG^k\|_F and c_k=\|W-I\|_2\|JE^k\|_F. Then \[\|JX^K\|_F\le\rho^K\|JX^0\|_F+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\rho^{K-1-k}(h_k+c_k).\] If h_k\le h and c_k\le c, then \[\|JX^K\|_F\le\rho^K\|JX^0\|_F+\frac{1-\rho^K}{1-\rho}(h+c).\]
assumptions_latex: The preceding one-step disagreement recursion holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|JX^K\|_F\le\rho^K\|JX^0\|_F+\sum_{k<K}\rho^{K-1-k}(h_k+c_k)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average-preserving compressed mixing leaves the average recursion unchanged while disagreement separates into network contraction, gradient heterogeneity, and reconstruction error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let W be doubly stochastic, J=I-\frac1n\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top, and \|WJ\|_2\le\rho<1. If \[X^{k+1}=WX^k-\alpha_kG^k+(W-I)E^k,\] then \[\bar x^{k+1}=\bar x^k-\alpha_k\bar g^k\] and \[\|JX^{k+1}\|_F\le\rho\|JX^k\|_F+\alpha_k\|JG^k\|_F+\|W-I\|_2\|JE^k\|_F.\]
assumptions_latex: W is doubly stochastic with disagreement norm at most \(\rho<1\).
The displayed compressed-mixing recursion holds.

knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Distributed Convergence Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A recursion-level decomposition of optimization, network, and compression errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a nonnegative distributed optimality measure \(V_k\) satisfy \(V_{k+1}\leq(1-c\alpha_k)V_k+A\alpha_k^2+B\alpha_k^2\chi^2+C\alpha_k^2\omega_k\), where \(c>0\), \(A,B,C\geq0\), \(\chi\) measures network difficulty, and \(\omega_k\) measures compression error. Then, with \(P_{s,K}=\prod_{j=s}^{K-1}(1-c\alpha_j)\), \[V_K\leq P_{0,K}V_0+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}P_{k+1,K}\alpha_k^2\bigl(A+B\chi^2+C\omega_k\bigr).\] The four terms respectively expose initial optimization error, intrinsic algorithmic error, network error, and compression error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unrolling a contractive error recursion separates initial, intrinsic optimization, network, and compression contributions to the final accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(V_k\geq0\) obeys the displayed one-step recursion
\(0\leq c\alpha_k\leq1\)
\(A,B,C,\chi,\omega_k\geq0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_K\) admits the displayed additive decomposition weighted by contraction products \(P_{s,K}\).
review_flags: The algebraic representation is exact, but a distributed-compression source is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursion unrolling is algebraically valid under the listed nonnegative-factor condition and representation is an appropriate kind, but the interpretation of its coefficients as intrinsic, network, and compression errors lacks supporting distributed-compression evidence.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a distributed method run for \(K\) iterations, let \(\mathcal E_K\ge0\) be a declared optimization error, let \(\rho\in[0,1)\) quantify network contraction, and let \(\delta_k\ge0\) quantify the communication distortion injected at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A taxonomy of nonasymptotic bounds that explicitly separates optimization, network, and compression contributions; it does not select universal functional forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compressed distributed convergence bound is decomposed when it has the form \(\mathcal E_K\le B_{\mathrm{opt}}(K)+B_{\mathrm{net}}(K;\rho)+B_{\mathrm{comp}}(K;\delta_0,\ldots,\delta_{K-1})\), where every term is nonnegative and has an operationally distinct source: \(B_{\mathrm{opt}}\) is the bound remaining under exact centralized communication, \(B_{\mathrm{net}}\) is the additional graph-mixing or disagreement contribution and vanishes in the ideal-consensus limit, and \(B_{\mathrm{comp}}\) is the additional distortion contribution and equals zero when all communication errors vanish. The error metric \(\mathcal E_K\), averaging convention, probability mode, and dependence of constants must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressed distributed convergence bound is a nonasymptotic error inequality whose right side is separated into optimization, network, and compression contributions. The network term disappears in the ideal-consensus limit, and the compression term disappears under exact messages. The error metric, expectation or probability convention, output rule, and constants are part of the bound's definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E_K\le B_{\mathrm{opt}}(K)+B_{\mathrm{net}}(K;\rho)+B_{\mathrm{comp}}(K;\delta_{0:K-1})\).
special_cases_latex: With exact communication, \(\delta_k=0\) for all \(k\) and \(B_{\mathrm{comp}}=0\).
With exact averaging at every iteration, the graph contribution is set to \(B_{\mathrm{net}}=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If all three terms tend to zero, then \(\mathcal E_K\to0\).
If the compression term has a positive limiting floor, the displayed bound alone certifies at most neighborhood accuracy.
boundary_notes: An arbitrary algebraic splitting is not operationally decomposed unless each term obeys the stated limiting interpretation.
This definition does not assert that the three effects are statistically independent.
review_flags: The decomposition is a candidate taxonomy; no inspectable source established it as a canonical definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposed compressed-distributed error bound

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(V_{k+1}\le(1-\gamma)V_k+b_k\), then \[V_K\le(1-\gamma)^KV_0+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}(1-\gamma)^{K-1-k}b_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recursion is mathematically correct but does not itself identify a distributed compressed method or derive network and compression terms.
assumptions_latex: The forced-contraction recursion is assumed.

Without an instantiated distributed method, compressor model, and graph-dependent constants, it belongs under general perturbation recurrences rather than this terminal leaf.

children.title: Federated Convergence under Client Heterogeneity
children.top_down_role: Convergence families separating sampling, drift, and objective mismatch.

knowledge_statements.title: Federated Convergence under Client Heterogeneity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average stationarity error is bounded by optimization progress, squared heterogeneity-induced bias, client-sampling variance, and local stochastic variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-smooth and bounded below by \(F_*\). Consider \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta g_t\), where \(0<\eta\le(4L)^{-1}\), \(\mathbb E[g_t\mid x_t]=\nabla F(x_t)+b_t\), and \(\mathbb E[\lVert g_t-\mathbb E[g_t\mid x_t]\rVert^2\mid x_t]\le V_t^{\mathrm{samp}}+V_t^{\mathrm{loc}}\). Then
\[\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb E\lVert\nabla F(x_t)\rVert^2\le\frac{4(F(x_0)-F_*)}{\eta T}+4\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb E\lVert b_t\rVert^2+2L\eta\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb E\bigl[V_t^{\mathrm{samp}}+V_t^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr].\]
Here \(b_t\) can collect objective mismatch and uncorrected client drift.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable, \(L\)-smooth, and bounded below by \(F_*\).
The displayed conditional mean and variance bounds hold for \(g_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed average-gradient bound separates persistent bias from sampling and local stochastic variance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonconvex smooth descent bound separating estimator bias, sampling variance, and local stochastic variance.

notation.meaning: conditional estimator bias from drift or objective mismatch

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic biased stochastic-gradient descent template specialized to federated error components
constants and hypotheses require source verification

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: A theorem fits this convergence container, but the exact constants and sufficient hypotheses in the biased stochastic-gradient bound require authoritative verification. The identification of the bias and variance terms with federated heterogeneity components is also unsourced.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_i p_iF_i(x)\), let \(x_t\) be the server iterate, and let \(\mathcal E_t\ge0\) be an optimization-error measure. Let \(V_t\), \(D_t\), and \(B_t\) quantify stochastic or participation variance, local-update drift, and objective-weight mismatch.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A definition of a convergence-bound family that explicitly separates three heterogeneity mechanisms; it is not itself a rate theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A federated convergence statement is heterogeneity-separated when it has the form \(\mathbb E[\mathcal E_T]\le A_T\mathcal E_0+\mathcal V_T(V_{0:T-1})+\mathcal D_T(D_{0:T-1})+\mathcal B_T(B_{0:T-1})\), where \(A_T\) is an optimization contraction or decay term and the three nonnegative functionals vanish, respectively, when sampling noise is absent, local iterates do not drift from their reference server iterates, and effective client weights equal target weights. Canonical pointwise quantities include \(V_t=\mathbb E\|\widehat g_t-\mathbb E_t\widehat g_t\|^2\), \(D_t=\sum_i p_i\mathbb E\|x_{t,i}-x_t\|^2\), and \(B_t=\sup_{x\in X}|\sum_i(q_{t,i}-p_i)F_i(x)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heterogeneity-separated convergence bound reports optimization decay plus distinct contributions from participation or stochastic variance, divergence of local models from the server reference, and mismatch between effective and intended client weights. Each contribution is defined to disappear when its corresponding mechanism is absent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\mathcal E_T]\le A_T\mathcal E_0+\mathcal V_T+\mathcal D_T+\mathcal B_T\), with separately identified variance, drift, and mismatch terms.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For smooth nonconvex analysis, \(\mathcal E_T\) may be an average such as \(T^{-1}\sum_{t<T}\mathbb E\|\nabla F(x_t)\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: Full deterministic participation removes client-sampling variance but not necessarily stochastic-gradient variance or local drift.
One local step can reduce drift accumulation without eliminating objective heterogeneity.
immediate_consequences_latex: A residual error floor can be attributed to a specific nonvanishing term only when the bound preserves this separation.
boundary_notes: Different analyses use inequivalent heterogeneity constants; this definition fixes roles rather than numerical constants.
No convergence rate follows without assumptions on objectives, gradients, step sizes, and sampling.
review_flags: No source was found for this exact three-way named decomposition.
standard_field_rationale: variance, local disagreement, and objective-weight mismatch are standard distinct mechanisms in federated analyses.

children.title: Bounded-Staleness Convergence
children.top_down_role: Guarantee families under uniformly controlled delays.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Staleness Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive fixed-point iteration converges despite asynchrony when delays and gaps between component updates are uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be complete under a block-maximum norm, and let \(F:X\to X\) satisfy \(\lVert F(x)-F(z)\rVert\le q\lVert x-z\rVert\) for some \(q\in[0,1)\). At event \(k\), selected components replace their values by the corresponding components of \(F\) evaluated at a mixed-time vector whose timestamps lie in \([k-\tau,k]\); unselected components are unchanged. If every component is selected at least once in every \(B\) consecutive events, then the asynchronous iterates converge to the unique fixed point \(x^*\) of \(F\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is complete and \(F\) is a contraction with modulus \(q<1\).
Every read is at most \(\tau<\infty\) events old.
Every component is updated within each window of \(B<\infty\) events.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}x^k=x^*\), where \(F(x^*)=x^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of asynchronous component updates for a contraction under bounded reads and bounded activation gaps.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x^k\in\mathbb R^d\) be the shared logical iterate of an asynchronous method. An update committed at time \(k\) may use blocks \(x_j^{s_j(k)}\), where \(s_j(k)\le k\). Let \(X^\star\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be the target solution set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional asynchronous deterministic or stochastic iterations with a uniform bound on information age; the definition does not itself assert a rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The execution has bounded staleness if there is an integer \(\tau<\infty\) such that \(k-\tau\le s_j(k)\le k\) for every logical time \(k\) and every block read by the update at \(k\). The method is convergent under bounded staleness if, for every execution satisfying this delay bound together with the method's stated activation and stepsize conditions, \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,X^\star)\to0\) as \(k\to\infty\); in a stochastic formulation the declared mode is almost sure convergence or convergence in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An execution is bounded-stale when one finite integer tau uniformly bounds the age of every block used by every update. A method has bounded-staleness convergence when every execution obeying that delay bound and the method's activation and stepsize requirements approaches the designated solution set in its declared deterministic or stochastic convergence mode.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\tau<\infty\;\forall k,j:\ 0\le k-s_j(k)\le\tau\), and admissible executions satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,X^\star)\to0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(d_j(k):=k-s_j(k)\), bounded staleness is equivalent to \(\sup_{k,j}d_j(k)<\infty\).
special_cases_latex: The synchronous regime is the special case \(\tau=0\).
A fixed delay \(d\) satisfies the definition with \(\tau=d\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every value read at logical time \(k\) was produced no earlier than \(k-\tau\).
boundary_notes: A finite delay bound alone does not guarantee convergence; activation, regularity, and stepsize hypotheses remain method-specific.
Unbounded but eventually delivered information belongs to total asynchrony, not this regime.

notation.meaning: logical time at which block j used by update k was produced

children.title: Total-Asynchrony Convergence
children.top_down_role: Guarantees under eventual-update and fairness regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Total-Asynchrony Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive asynchronous iteration converges with unbounded delays if every component updates forever and all information timestamps eventually advance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be complete under a block-maximum norm, and let \(F:X\to X\) be a contraction with modulus \(q<1\). At each event, any selected component \(i\) is replaced by \(F_i\) evaluated using timestamps \(s_{ij}(k)\le k\). Suppose every component is updated infinitely often and, along the update events of each component, \(s_{ij}(k)\to\infty\) for every required component \(j\). Then arbitrary finite but nonuniform update and communication delays are permitted, and the asynchronous iterates converge to the unique fixed point of \(F\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a contraction on a complete block-maximum-norm product space.
Each component is updated infinitely often.
Every timestamp used along relevant updates tends to infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}x^k=x^*\), where \(x^*\) is the unique solution of \(F(x^*)=x^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contractive fixed-point convergence with unbounded delays satisfying only fairness and vanishing information age.

notation.meaning: timestamp of component j used to update component i

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let agents or blocks be indexed by \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Let \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb N\) be the logical times at which block \(i\) is updated, and let \(s_{ij}(k)\le k\) denote the timestamp of block \(j\) used by agent \(i\) at \(k\in K_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical total-asynchrony model: delays need not be uniformly bounded, but updates are fair and every repeatedly used information stream becomes arbitrarily fresh.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An execution is totally asynchronous if \(K_i\) is infinite for every \(i\), and for every ordered dependency \((i,j)\), every sequence \(k_r\in K_i\) with \(k_r\to\infty\) satisfies \(s_{ij}(k_r)\to\infty\). A method converges under total asynchrony when every such admissible execution, subject to the method's remaining hypotheses, satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,X^\star)\to0\). No finite bound on \(k-s_{ij}(k)\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total asynchrony requires every block to update infinitely often and requires the timestamps of information used along late updates to tend to infinity. Information may be arbitrarily old at selected times, so long as permanently frozen information is excluded. Convergence under total asynchrony means that every execution meeting these fairness and eventual-freshness conditions approaches the target set under the method's other assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall i:\ |K_i|=\infty\), \(k_r\in K_i,\ k_r\to\infty\Rightarrow s_{ij}(k_r)\to\infty\), and admissible trajectories obey \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,X^\star)\to0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eventual freshness can be written as \(\forall q\in\mathbb N\;\exists R\;\forall r\ge R:\ s_{ij}(k_r)\ge q\).
special_cases_latex: Every bounded-staleness fair execution is totally asynchronous.
Synchronous execution is totally asynchronous when every block continues updating.
immediate_consequences_latex: No agent may stop updating permanently, and no dependency may use one fixed historical value forever.
boundary_notes: Total asynchrony permits \(\sup_{i,j,k}(k-s_{ij}(k))=\infty\).
Fairness and eventual freshness are execution conditions, not sufficient convergence conditions for an arbitrary update map.

notation.meaning: update times of block or agent i

children.title: Delay-Speedup Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between concurrency gains and stale-update penalties.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For worker count \(p\), let \(T_p(\varepsilon)\) be wall-clock time to attain error at most \(\varepsilon\), let \(N_p(\varepsilon)\) be the required committed updates, and let \(\tau_p\) quantify maximum or effective staleness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: System-level definition separating per-update algorithmic degradation from parallel wall-clock throughput; no universal functional form is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The delay–speedup tradeoff at accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\) is the pair \((S_p(\varepsilon),D_p(\varepsilon))\), where \(S_p(\varepsilon):=T_1(\varepsilon)/T_p(\varepsilon)\) is wall-clock speedup and \(D_p(\varepsilon):=N_p(\varepsilon)/N_1(\varepsilon)\) is the update-complexity inflation associated with concurrency and staleness \(\tau_p\). Linear speedup holds on an operating range \(P\) when constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), independent of \(p\in P\), satisfy \(cp\le S_p(\varepsilon)\le Cp\). A delay-limited scalability boundary is a value of \(p\) beyond which growth of \(D_p\), idle time, or communication makes \(S_p/p\) decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tradeoff records both the reduction in wall-clock time achieved with p workers and the extra algorithmic updates required because concurrency produces stale or conflicting work. Linear speedup means speedup remains proportional to worker count over a declared operating range. The delay-limited boundary begins when stale-update penalties or system overhead reduce efficiency as more workers are added.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_p(\varepsilon)=T_1(\varepsilon)/T_p(\varepsilon)\), \(D_p(\varepsilon)=N_p(\varepsilon)/N_1(\varepsilon)\), and linear speedup means \(S_p(\varepsilon)=\Theta(p)\) on the stated range.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Parallel efficiency is \(E_p(\varepsilon):=S_p(\varepsilon)/p\); linear speedup is equivalent to bounding \(E_p\) above and away from zero uniformly on \(P\).
special_cases_latex: If update cost is unchanged and \(D_p=1\), idealized speedup is \(S_p=p\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A claim of iteration speedup and a claim of wall-clock speedup are distinct unless update throughput is specified.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assume that delay is a deterministic function of worker count.
Hardware, scheduling, and communication costs must be included in \(T_p\) for an end-to-end claim.
review_flags: The hinted concurrency-tradeoff source was not inspected at statement level; this candidate therefore has no evidentiary locator.
knowledge_statements.title: Delay–speedup tradeoff profile
Delay-Dependent Convergence Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A delay bound of τ slows the worst-case contraction exponent and event complexity by a factor of at most τ+1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\to X\) be a contraction with modulus \(q\in(0,1)\) and fixed point \(x^*\). Consider
\[
x^{k+1}=F(x^{k-d_k}),\qquad 0\le d_k\le\min\{\tau,k\}.
\]
Then
\[
\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert\le q^{\lceil k/(\tau+1)\rceil}\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert.
\]
Consequently, achieving \(\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert\le\varepsilon\) is guaranteed after at most
\[
(\tau+1)\left\lceil\frac{\log(\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert/\varepsilon)}{-\log q}\right\rceil
\]
events, for \(0<\varepsilon<\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is complete and \(F\) is a \(q\)-contraction.
\(0\le d_k\le\min\{\tau,k\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated error and event-complexity bounds hold for every admissible delay sequence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case event complexity for delayed iteration of a contractive map.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Speedup Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel speedup is near-linear while delay increases the required update count by only a worker-independent constant factor relative to the zero-delay serial baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K(\tau,\varepsilon)\) be the number of update events required for accuracy \(\varepsilon\) when staleness is bounded by \(\tau\). Suppose \(p\) workers process \(p\) events per unit time with negligible overhead and that the one-worker baseline has \(\tau(1)=0\). Define
\[
T_p(\varepsilon)=\frac{K(\tau(p),\varepsilon)}{p},\qquad T_1(\varepsilon)=K(0,\varepsilon),\qquad S_p(\varepsilon)=\frac{T_1(\varepsilon)}{T_p(\varepsilon)}.
\]
A worker range is a near-linear speedup regime with constant \(C\ge1\) when
\[
K(\tau(p),\varepsilon)\le C K(0,\varepsilon)
\]
throughout that range. Then \(S_p(\varepsilon)\ge p/C\).
assumptions_latex: Workers sustain aggregate throughput \(p\) updates per unit time.
Scheduling and communication overhead are excluded from \(T_p\).
The one-worker baseline satisfies \(\tau(1)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounded-work-inflation condition implies \(S_p(\varepsilon)\ge p/C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-throughput criterion for near-linear asynchronous parallel speedup.

notation.meaning: updates required at delay bound τ and accuracy ε
speedup over the zero-delay one-worker baseline

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Update Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stale-gradient error is at most the smoothness constant times the accumulated iterate movement since the gradient was computed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) have \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and let an event use the stale gradient \(g^k=\nabla f(x^{k-d_k})\), where \(0\le d_k\le\tau\). Then
\[
\lVert g^k-\nabla f(x^k)\rVert
\le L\lVert x^{k-d_k}-x^k\rVert
\le L\sum_{t=k-d_k}^{k-1}\lVert x^{t+1}-x^t\rVert.
\]
Thus staleness contributes an error controlled by the cumulative motion during the omitted events; it vanishes whenever the sum of those intervening step lengths vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(z)\rVert\le L\lVert x-z\rVert\) for all \(x,z\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
\(0\le d_k\le\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert g^k-\nabla f(x^k)\rVert\le L\sum_{t=k-d_k}^{k-1}\lVert x^{t+1}-x^t\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz bound on gradient error caused by a delayed iterate.

notation.meaning: age of the gradient used at event k

knowledge_statements.title: Speedup Saturation Limits
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When staleness and delay-induced work both grow linearly with worker count, idealized parallel speedup remains uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_0(\varepsilon)>0\) be the serial update count and suppose an asynchronous method with \(p\) workers requires
\[
K_p(\varepsilon)\ge c\bigl(1+\tau(p)\bigr)K_0(\varepsilon)
\]
for some \(c>0\). Under ideal throughput \(p\), its speedup is \(S_p=pK_0(\varepsilon)/K_p(\varepsilon)\). If the induced staleness satisfies \(\tau(p)\ge a(p-1)\) for some \(a>0\), then
\[
S_p\le\frac{p}{c(1+a(p-1))}\le\frac{1}{c\min\{1,a\}}.
\]
Hence increasing worker count cannot produce unbounded speedup in this regime.
assumptions_latex: \(K_p(\varepsilon)\ge c(1+\tau(p))K_0(\varepsilon)\).
\(\tau(p)\ge a(p-1)\) with \(a,c>0\).
Aggregate processing capacity is at most \(p\) updates per unit time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_p\le 1/(c\min\{1,a\})\) for every integer \(p\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worker-independent speedup ceiling when delay-induced work grows linearly with concurrency.

notation.meaning: parallel update count required for accuracy ε

children.top_down_role: Cost models distinguishing computation, communication, synchronization, and total work.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathfrak A\) be a distributed algorithm, \(I\) an instance, \(\varepsilon>0\) an accuracy target, and \(\tau\) a terminating execution whose output satisfies a declared certificate \(C_I(\tau)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition treats distributed complexity as a resource vector so computation, communication, synchronization, volume, and elapsed time are not conflated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a terminating execution \(\tau\), define its resource vector \(R(\tau)=(N_{\mathrm{orc}},N_{\mathrm{rnd}},N_{\mathrm{msg}},N_{\mathrm{bit}},D_{\mathrm{sync}},T_{\mathrm{par}})\in[0,\infty]^6\). The worst-case distributed complexity of \(\mathfrak A\) on an instance class \(\mathcal I\) is the componentwise supremum of the resources required by executions that first produce an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate output. A scalar complexity is defined only after specifying a monotone cost functional \(w\), giving \(\mathcal C_w(\mathfrak A,\mathcal I,\varepsilon)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\sup_\omega w(R(\tau_{I,\omega,\varepsilon}))\), where \(\omega\) represents admissible randomness or schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed complexity is the vector of resources consumed before an accuracy certificate is reached. Its coordinates separately count local oracle work, sequential communication rounds, messages, encoded bits, synchronization depth, and parallel elapsed time. Worst-case complexity takes the supremum over the declared instance class and admissible executions. A scalar total cost is meaningful only after resource weights or a cost model are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R(\tau)=(N_{\mathrm{orc}},N_{\mathrm{rnd}},N_{\mathrm{msg}},N_{\mathrm{bit}},D_{\mathrm{sync}},T_{\mathrm{par}}),\qquad \mathcal C_w=\sup_{I,\omega}w(R(\tau_{I,\omega,\varepsilon})).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The attainable resource set \(\mathcal R_\varepsilon=\{R(\tau):C_I(\tau)\le\varepsilon\}\) retains tradeoffs that a single weighted scalar may hide.
special_cases_latex: Round complexity is obtained by \(w(R)=N_{\mathrm{rnd}}\); bit complexity uses \(w(R)=N_{\mathrm{bit}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Algorithms can be incomparable when neither resource vector componentwise dominates the other.
boundary_notes: Wall-clock time requires a hardware and latency model and cannot be inferred solely from operation counts.
Expected, high-probability, and worst-case complexities are distinct conventions.

notation.meaning: Declared monotone scalarization of resource use.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-regime execution-time characterization at the threshold \(T_1/T_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(T_\infty>0\). If \(p\ge T_1/T_\infty\), then \(T_p<2T_\infty\); more generally, \(p=\Omega(T_1/T_\infty)\) implies \(T_p=O(T_\infty)\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At or above the work-to-depth threshold, execution time is within a constant factor of unlimited-processor depth. At or below it, execution time is between one and two times the single-processor work divided by the processor count, with the corresponding asymptotic regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Oracle Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed distributed execution, local oracle complexity records either the largest per-agent query count or the total query count needed to reach the declared accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a distributed algorithm execution, an oracle class, and an accuracy criterion \(E(x)\leq\varepsilon\). Let \(q_i(t)\in\mathbb N_0\) be the number of declared local oracle calls made by agent \(i\in\{1,n\}\) through iteration \(t\). Define the execution-level worst-agent and aggregate local oracle costs by \[Q_{\max}(\varepsilon):=\inf_{t:E(x^t)\leq\varepsilon}\max_{1\leq i\leq n}q_i(t),\qquad Q_{\Sigma}(\varepsilon):=\inf_{t:E(x^t)\leq\varepsilon}\sum_{i=1}^n q_i(t).\] If no qualifying iterate exists, the corresponding value is \(+\infty\). The first quantity measures worst-agent local work, and the second measures total network-wide oracle work. Query types with materially different costs are counted separately or combined through an explicit cost model.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm execution, error criterion \(E\), outputs \(x^t\), and target \(\varepsilon\) are specified.
The permitted oracle responses and their counting convention are fixed.
\(q_i(t)\in\mathbb N_0\) counts agent \(i\)'s oracle calls through iteration \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\max}(\varepsilon)\) and \(Q_{\Sigma}(\varepsilon)\) quantify worst-agent and aggregate execution-level local oracle costs, respectively.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-agent and aggregate counts of local information requests needed for accuracy.

notation.meaning: Number of local oracle calls made by agent i through iteration t.
