knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Agent \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) accesses its private function or constraint data only through an oracle \(\mathcal O_i\), which may return a function value, gradient, subgradient, proximal point, stochastic sample, or another declared response.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This measure counts local information queries independently of communication and local arithmetic not charged by the oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an execution \(\tau\), let \(q_i(\tau)\) be the number of calls to \(\mathcal O_i\) made before an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate certificate is produced. The aggregate local oracle cost is \(N_{\mathrm{orc}}^{\Sigma}(\tau)=\sum_{i=1}^n q_i(\tau)\), while the parallel-depth oracle cost is \(N_{\mathrm{orc}}^{\max}(\tau)=\max_i q_i(\tau)\). For algorithm \(\mathfrak A\) and instance class \(\mathcal I\), the corresponding worst-case complexity is the supremum of the selected count over all admissible instances and executions reaching the target. Different oracle response types must be counted separately or assigned declared weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local oracle complexity counts private-data queries made by agents before the required accuracy is certified. The aggregate convention sums calls over agents; the parallel-depth convention takes the maximum per-agent count. Function-value, derivative, subgradient, proximal, and stochastic calls are distinct resources unless an explicit weighting combines them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_{\mathrm{orc}}^{\Sigma}(\tau)=\sum_{i=1}^n q_i(\tau),\qquad N_{\mathrm{orc}}^{\max}(\tau)=\max_{1\le i\le n}q_i(\tau).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A typed query vector \((q_i^{\mathrm{val}},q_i^{\mathrm{grad}},q_i^{\mathrm{prox}},q_i^{\mathrm{stoch}})\) is equivalent to a scalar count only after weights are fixed.
special_cases_latex: If every synchronous iteration makes one gradient call at every agent, then after \(K\) iterations the aggregate count is \(nK\) and the per-agent depth is \(K\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Equal round complexity does not imply equal oracle complexity when agents perform multiple local steps between communications.
boundary_notes: Communication, encoding, and arbitrary local arithmetic are excluded unless the oracle model charges them.
Batch size must be declared when one stochastic call can process multiple samples.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Communication-Round Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication-round complexity is the minimum number of sequential neighbor-exchange stages needed to satisfy a declared accuracy and success criterion, regardless of intervening local computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a synchronous graph model and an accuracy predicate \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon(x)\) that incorporates the selected deterministic, expected, or high-probability success convention. One communication round permits every agent to send messages to its current neighbors and receive the corresponding messages before the next adaptive exchange. If \(x^R\) is the distributed output after \(R\in\mathbb N_0\) rounds, define \[R(\varepsilon):=\inf\left\{R\in\mathbb N_0:\mathcal A_\varepsilon(x^R)\text{ holds}\right\}.\] If the set is empty, \(R(\varepsilon):=+\infty\). Local computations between two exchanges do not increase this count, whereas \(k\) sequential consensus or gossip exchanges count as \(k\) rounds.
assumptions_latex: Communication is organized into synchronous neighbor-exchange rounds.
The graph model and accuracy predicate \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon\) are fixed.
The predicate includes the selected deterministic, expected, or high-probability success convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(\varepsilon)\) is the minimum number of sequential communication rounds after which \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon(x^R)\) holds, or \(+\infty\) if no such round exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential network-exchange rounds required to attain a declared accuracy.

notation.meaning: Distributed output after R communication rounds.
Accuracy predicate including the chosen success convention.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let communication occur on an admissible graph or time-varying graph sequence. In one round, each agent may form messages from its current local information, transmit them over simultaneously available edges, receive that round's messages, and update its state.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The measure counts causal network depth, not message volume, bit length, local computation, or physical elapsed time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A communication round is one synchronous causal layer of neighbor-to-neighbor message exchange. For execution \(\tau\), let \(N_{\mathrm{rnd}}(\tau)\) be the number of such layers before the first output satisfying the declared \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy certificate. The communication-round complexity of algorithm \(\mathfrak A\) over \(\mathcal I\) is \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rnd}}(\mathfrak A,\mathcal I,\varepsilon)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\sup_\omega N_{\mathrm{rnd}}(\tau_{I,\omega,\varepsilon})\). For asynchronous executions, a round surrogate must be defined explicitly, for example as communication depth in the event-dependency directed acyclic graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication-round complexity is the worst-case number of sequential network-exchange layers required before the accuracy target is reached. Transmissions within the same causal layer count as one round even if many messages are sent. Asynchronous systems require an explicit causal-depth or epoch convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rnd}}(\mathfrak A,\mathcal I,\varepsilon)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\sup_\omega N_{\mathrm{rnd}}(\tau_{I,\omega,\varepsilon}).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under a synchronous model with one mixing operation per iteration, iteration count and communication-round count coincide.
Communication depth is the length of the longest chain of message-dependent exchange events in a causal execution graph.
special_cases_latex: Performing \(s\) consecutive consensus exchanges per optimization iteration costs \(sK\) rounds after \(K\) iterations.
immediate_consequences_latex: Round complexity can remain unchanged when messages are enlarged, so it does not control communication volume.
boundary_notes: A broadcast counts according to the declared network primitive; it must not silently be treated as one neighbor round.
Idle time and link latency are excluded from an abstract round count.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Message, coordinate, and bit communication costs
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a terminating distributed execution \(\tau\), let \(M(\tau)\) be its multiset of directed transmissions. Each message \(m\in M(\tau)\) has an encoded length \(\ell(m)\in\mathbb N\) bits and may contain \(d(m)\) scalar coordinates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This taxonomy concerns communication volume and keeps it distinct from sequential communication depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The message complexity is \(N_{\mathrm{msg}}(\tau)=|M(\tau)|\). The coordinate complexity is \(N_{\mathrm{coord}}(\tau)=\sum_{m\in M(\tau)}d(m)\). The bit complexity is \(N_{\mathrm{bit}}(\tau)=\sum_{m\in M(\tau)}\ell(m)\), including declared headers or metadata when the model charges them. For a class of instances and executions, each worst-case complexity is the supremum of the corresponding count before an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate certificate is reached. Equivalence between coordinate and bit counts requires a fixed encoding precision; without it, transmitting one real coordinate has no finite intrinsic bit cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Message complexity counts transmissions, coordinate complexity sums transmitted scalar entries, and bit complexity sums encoded lengths. These are different measures: a single message may contain many coordinates, and a coordinate may require a variable number of bits. Worst-case costs are measured up to the first certified accurate output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_{\mathrm{msg}}=|M|,\qquad N_{\mathrm{coord}}=\sum_{m\in M}d(m),\qquad N_{\mathrm{bit}}=\sum_{m\in M}\ell(m).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If every coordinate is encoded using exactly \(b\) bits and headers are excluded, then \(N_{\mathrm{bit}}=bN_{\mathrm{coord}}\).
special_cases_latex: Sending one dense vector in \(\mathbb R^d\) on every directed edge in every round gives coordinate cost \(d\) times the number of directed edge transmissions.
immediate_consequences_latex: A round-efficient algorithm need not be bit-efficient, and compression can lower bit cost without lowering round count.
boundary_notes: Infinite-precision real messages do not define finite bit complexity.
Broadcast accounting must state whether one physical broadcast or one transmission per recipient is charged.

notation.meaning: Multiset of directed messages transmitted during execution \(\tau\).
Number of scalar coordinates in message \(m\).

Message-Count Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Message-count complexity is the worst-case number of completed edgewise message transmissions over all declared instances and admissible executions before an accuracy-qualified output is produced; an unsuccessful execution has infinite count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an admissible execution transcript \(\tau\), define \[M(\tau)=\sum_{e\in\tau}\mathbf{1}\{e\text{ is a completed message transmission}\}.\] For a distributed algorithm \(A\), instance class \(\mathcal I\), accuracy predicate \(P_\varepsilon(x;I)\), and admissible-execution set \(\Omega_A(I)\), define \[M_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I,\,\omega\in\Omega_A(I)}M(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega)).\] Here \(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega)\) ends when an output satisfying \(P_\varepsilon\) is first produced. Its message count is \(+\infty\) if no such output is produced. Each multicast is counted once per receiving edge, and retransmissions are counted separately.

\(\mathcal I\) is the declared instance class, and \(\Omega_A(I)\) is the declared class of admissible executions on \(I\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bit-Communication Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bit-communication complexity is the worst-case total charged binary length over all declared instances and admissible executions before an accuracy-qualified output is produced; an unsuccessful execution has infinite cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell(e)\in\mathbb N_0\) be the complete encoded length, in bits, of communication event \(e\), including every header charged by the declared model. For a transcript \(\tau\), define \[B(\tau)=\sum_{e\in\tau}\ell(e).\] For algorithm \(A\), instance class \(\mathcal I\), and admissible-execution set \(\Omega_A(I)\), define \[B_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I,\,\omega\in\Omega_A(I)}B(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega)).\] The transcript ends when an output satisfying the declared \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy predicate is first produced, and an execution that produces no such output has value \(+\infty\). Preshared random seeds cost zero only when the declared model makes them free; otherwise their communicated descriptions contribute to \(B\).
assumptions_latex: \(\ell(e)\) is fixed by a declared binary encoding and accounting convention.
\(\mathcal I\) and each admissible-execution set \(\Omega_A(I)\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I,\,\omega\in\Omega_A(I)}\sum_{e\in\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega)}\ell(e)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts encoded payload and protocol bits transmitted before attaining accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Transmission Volume
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate volume is the worst-case total number of scalar entries carried across receiving edges, irrespective of their encoding precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each communication event \(e\) carries an encoded vector whose decoded payload exposes a set \(S_e\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d_e\}\) of transmitted scalar coordinates. Define the coordinate-transmission volume of transcript \(\tau\) by \[V_{\mathrm{coord}}(\tau)=\sum_{e\in\tau}|S_e|.\] The worst-case volume for algorithm \(A\) is \[V_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}V_{\mathrm{coord}}(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon)).\] A coordinate sent to several neighbors is charged once per receiving edge; metadata and coordinate precision are excluded and must instead be charged by a bit measure.
assumptions_latex: Each message has a declared decoded coordinate support \(S_e\).
A multicast payload is represented by one event for each receiving edge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\sum_{e\in\tau_A(I,\varepsilon)}|S_e|\).

knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Precision Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precision is fixed, accuracy-dependent finite, or ideal exact-real according to whether the maximum encoded payload length stays bounded as accuracy tightens.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a family of encoders \(Q_\varepsilon\), let \(b(\varepsilon)=\sup_z\ell(Q_\varepsilon(z))\) over admissible payloads \(z\). The family has fixed precision if \(\sup_{0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0}b(\varepsilon)<\infty\); it has accuracy-dependent finite precision if every \(b(\varepsilon)<\infty\) but \(\sup_{0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0}b(\varepsilon)=\infty\); and it is an exact-real regime if payloads are ideal real words whose charged length is not represented by finite \(b(\varepsilon)\). Bit-complexity comparisons are meaningful only within the same regime and encoding convention.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_\varepsilon\) and its binary length function \(\ell\) are specified for every target \(0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0}b(\varepsilon)<\infty\) characterizes the fixed-precision regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies communication models by how message precision may depend on target accuracy.

notation.meaning: Encoder used at target accuracy epsilon.

children.title: Distributed Wall-Clock and Parallel-Time Complexity
children.top_down_role: Latency-aware cost incorporating concurrency and synchronization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Represent an execution \(\tau\) by a directed acyclic event graph \(H_\tau=(V_\tau,A_\tau)\). Vertices are local computations, transmissions, receptions, or synchronization events; arcs encode causal precedence. Each event \(v\) has duration \(c(v)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This model captures concurrency, heterogeneous communication delays, and synchronization; it is distinct from aggregate work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The latency-aware parallel time of execution \(\tau\) is its weighted critical-path length \(T_{\mathrm{par}}(\tau)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P(H_\tau)}\sum_{v\in P}c(v)\), where \(\mathcal P(H_\tau)\) is the set of directed causal paths ending at the first event that exposes an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate output. Its worst-case complexity is the supremum over the declared instance, schedule, delay, and randomness class. For a bulk-synchronous model with round latency \(L_k\) and between-round critical local work \(W_k\), this specializes to \(T_{\mathrm{par}}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}(L_k+W_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Latency-aware parallel-time complexity is the duration of the longest causal chain leading to an accurate output. Independent work runs concurrently and therefore contributes through a maximum rather than a sum. A synchronous specialization adds per-round communication latency and the critical local work between barriers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T_{\mathrm{par}}(\tau)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P(H_\tau)}\sum_{v\in P}c(v).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With unlimited processors and deterministic event durations, the weighted critical path is the earliest completion time permitted by the precedence constraints.
special_cases_latex: For constant round latency \(L\), constant critical work \(W\), and \(K\) barriers, \(T_{\mathrm{par}}=K(L+W)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Reducing total work need not reduce parallel time if the critical path is unchanged.
boundary_notes: Contention, queueing, failures, and bandwidth limits are included only when represented in event durations or precedence constraints.
This is a model-based time, not a machine-independent operation count.

Wall-Clock Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wall-clock complexity is the worst-case modeled elapsed time over all declared instances and admissible executions until an accuracy-qualified output first becomes available; a nonterminating execution has infinite time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an admissible timed execution \(\tau_A(I,psilon;\omega)\), let \(t_0(I,\omega)\) be its start time and \(t_{\mathrm{out}}(I,\omega)\) the first time an admissible processor produces an output satisfying the declared \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy predicate. Define \[T_{\mathrm{wall}}(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega))=t_{\mathrm{out}}(I,\omega)-t_0(I,\omega),\] and \[T_A^{\mathrm{wall}}(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I,\,\omega\in\Omega_A(I)}T_{\mathrm{wall}}(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega)).\] Computation, queueing, transmission, latency, waiting, and synchronization contribute according to their actual overlap in the declared machine and scheduler model. If no qualifying output is produced, the execution time is \(+\infty\).
assumptions_latex: The machine, network, scheduler, and event-duration model are fixed.
\(\Omega_A(I)\) specifies all admissible executions of \(A\) on \(I\).
The first qualifying output time \(t_{\mathrm{out}}\) is observable under the declared termination rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_A^{\mathrm{wall}}(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I,\,\omega\in\Omega_A(I)}(t_{\mathrm{out}}(I,\omega)-t_0(I,\omega))\).

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel-Time Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel-time complexity is the worst-case weighted critical-path length of the execution, assuming causally independent operations can run concurrently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent an execution by a directed acyclic graph \(D_\tau=(V_\tau,E_\tau)\), where vertices are primitive computation or communication operations, edges encode causal precedence, and \(w(v)\geq0\) is the charged duration of operation \(v\). Its parallel time is the weighted span \[T_\infty(\tau)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P(D_\tau)}\sum_{v\in P}w(v).\] For algorithm \(A\), define \[T_A^\infty(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}T_\infty(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon)).\] With unit operation weights this equals the maximum number of causally sequential operations, not total work.
assumptions_latex: \(D_\tau\) is acyclic and contains every charged operation preceding the output.
Each operation has a nonnegative model weight \(w(v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_A^\infty(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\max_{P\in\mathcal P(D_\tau)}\sum_{v\in P}w(v)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Latency Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every valid-output causal path contains an unavoidable communication chain, elapsed time is at least the smallest accumulated duration lower bound among those chains; in particular, R sequential communications of latency at least lambda_min require at least R times lambda_min.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_\tau\) be the causal graph of a timed execution \(\tau\), and let \(\lambda(v)\geq0\) be a lower bound on the actual elapsed duration of each communication operation \(v\). Let \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\) be a family of directed communication chains such that every causal path producing an \(\varepsilon\)-valid output contains at least one \(C\in\mathcal C_\varepsilon\). Because causally ordered operations cannot overlap, \[T_{\mathrm{wall}}(\tau)\geq\min_{C\in\mathcal C_\varepsilon}\sum_{v\in C}\lambda(v).\] In particular, if every such chain contains at least \(R_\varepsilon\) causally sequential communication operations and \(\lambda(v)\geq\lambda_{\min}\) for each of them, then \[T_{\mathrm{wall}}(\tau)\geq R_\varepsilon\lambda_{\min}.\] Concurrent local computation cannot reduce this causal latency term.
assumptions_latex: Every causal path leading to a valid output contains at least one chain \(C\in\mathcal C_\varepsilon\).
For every communication operation \(v\), its actual elapsed duration is at least \(\lambda(v)\geq0\).
Operations on a directed causal chain cannot overlap in time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{wall}}(\tau)\geq\min_{C\in\mathcal C_\varepsilon}\sum_{v\in C}\lambda(v)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bounds completion time using unavoidable causal communication chains.

notation.meaning: Family of communication chains such that every valid-output causal path contains at least one member.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Overhead
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronization overhead may be measured either as total worker waiting plus separately charged barrier service or as the sum of maximum individual waiting at each barrier; neither convention alone determines global critical-path overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider barriers \(k=1,\ldots,K\) with finite participant sets \(W_k\). Let \(a_{ik}\) be worker \(i\)'s arrival time, let \(r_k\geq\max_{i\in W_k}a_{ik}\) be the release time, and let \(s_k\geq0\) be a separately charged service cost not already included in the waiting intervals. Define aggregate worker-time synchronization overhead by \[H_{\mathrm{sync}}^{\mathrm{agg}}(\tau)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(\sum_{i\in W_k}(r_k-a_{ik})+s_k\right).\] A distinct per-barrier maximum-wait measure is \[H_{\mathrm{sync}}^{\max}(\tau)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(\max_{i\in W_k}(r_k-a_{ik})+s_k\right).\] Neither quantity is, without additional execution-path assumptions, identical to the synchronization contribution on the global critical path. The selected convention must accompany every reported value.
assumptions_latex: Each barrier \(k\) has a finite participant set \(W_k\).
Arrival and release times satisfy \(r_k\geq a_{ik}\) for every \(i\in W_k\).
The service charge \(s_k\geq0\) is not already included in \(r_k-a_{ik}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{\mathrm{sync}}^{\mathrm{agg}}(\tau)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(\sum_{i\in W_k}(r_k-a_{ik})+s_k\right)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies barrier-induced waiting and separately charged barrier service under an explicit accounting convention.

notation.meaning: Arrival time of worker i at barrier k.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal I\) be a distributed problem class, \(\mathfrak M\) an information and communication model, and \(R_j(\mathfrak A,I,\varepsilon)\) the cost of algorithm \(\mathfrak A\) in resource coordinate \(j\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the minimax resource complexity \(L_j(\mathcal I,\mathfrak M,\varepsilon)=\inf_{\mathfrak A\in\mathfrak M}\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}R_j(\mathfrak A,I,\varepsilon)\). knowledge_statements.title: Joint Oracle–Network Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a common hard family, worst-case local-oracle work and communication depth must simultaneously dominate their respective lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_A(I)\) be the maximum number of local oracle calls made by any processor and \(R_A(I)\) the number of sequential communication rounds. Suppose a common hard family \(\mathcal H\) satisfies: every algorithm producing an \(\varepsilon\)-valid output on all \(I\in\mathcal H\) has some instance \(I_q\) with \(q_A(I_q)\geq Q_\varepsilon\), and some possibly different instance \(I_R\) with \(R_A(I_R)\geq R_\varepsilon\). Then its worst-case resource vector obeys \[\left(\sup_{I\in\mathcal H}q_A(I),\sup_{I\in\mathcal H}R_A(I)\right)\succeq(Q_\varepsilon,R_\varepsilon).\] A scalar time lower bound additionally requires explicit oracle and network timing rules.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a common hard instance family for both resource arguments.
Every admissible algorithm must return an \(\varepsilon\)-valid output on every \(I\in\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\sup_{I\in\mathcal H}q_A(I),\sup_{I\in\mathcal H}R_A(I)\bigr)\succeq(Q_\varepsilon,R_\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract joint lower bound for local oracle calls and sequential network rounds.

notation.meaning: Maximum local-oracle calls at any processor on instance I.
Sequential communication rounds on instance I.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A joint oracle–network lower bound is a set \(\mathcal L_\varepsilon\subseteq[0,\infty]^2\) such that every admissible algorithm \(\mathfrak A\) has some instance \(I\in\mathcal I\) and graph \(G\in\mathcal G\) for which its cost pair \((Q,R)\) lies in \(\mathcal L_\varepsilon\) before it can satisfy the \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy criterion. Equivalently, an upward-closed feasible-cost region \(\mathcal F_\varepsilon\) may be lower-bounded by inequalities \(\Phi_a(Q,R;I,G,\varepsilon)\ge1\). A genuinely joint bound cannot be represented solely by the conjunction \(Q\ge q_0\) and \(R\ge r_0\) when a nontrivial tradeoff between the resources is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint oracle–network lower bound describes cost pairs that no distributed algorithm can beat: limited local oracle access and limited communication are considered simultaneously. The result may be a forbidden low-cost region or a family of tradeoff inequalities. It is stronger in structure than merely listing independent lower bounds for queries and rounds.

equivalent_formulations_latex: The Pareto frontier of the upward-closed feasible-cost region gives the minimal communication attainable at each allowed oracle budget, and conversely.
special_cases_latex: An additive tradeoff \(Q/q_0+R/r_0\ge1\) is joint because additional use of one resource can compensate for the other within the stated model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Marginalizing the joint region yields valid but potentially weaker separate oracle and network lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Round Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If radius-R information cannot distinguish two instances requiring incompatible outputs, every correct deterministic algorithm needs more than R communication rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a synchronous graph \(G=(V,E)\), after \(R\) neighbor-to-neighbor communication rounds, the state of node \(v\) depends only on initial data and oracle responses within the closed radius-\(R\) neighborhood \(N_R[v]\). Hence, if two admissible instances \(I_0,I_1\) agree on \(N_R[v]\) but their sets of \(\varepsilon\)-valid outputs at \(v\), denoted \(S_\varepsilon(I_0,v)\) and \(S_\varepsilon(I_1,v)\), are disjoint, no deterministic algorithm terminating at \(v\) within \(R\) rounds is correct on both. Consequently its worst-case round complexity exceeds \(R\).
assumptions_latex: Communication in each synchronous round traverses at most one edge.
\(I_0\) and \(I_1\) induce identical observations within \(N_R[v]\).
\(S_\varepsilon(I_0,v)\cap S_\varepsilon(I_1,v)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locality-based lower bound on sequential synchronous communication depth.

notation.meaning: Closed graph neighborhood of radius R around node v.
Set of epsilon-valid outputs permitted at node v for instance I.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix an instance class \(\mathcal I\), graph class \(\mathcal G\), distributed information model \(\mathfrak M\), accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\), and success level \(1-\delta\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A communication-round lower bound states that every algorithm allowed by the model fails on some admissible problem and network if it uses fewer than the specified number of sequential communication layers. knowledge_statements.title: Bit-Communication Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinguishing M instances with incompatible valid outputs requires enough communicated bits to encode at least M distinct transcripts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_M\) be admissible instances whose required \(\varepsilon\)-valid decision outputs are pairwise disjoint. Consider a deterministic distributed protocol whose decision is a function of a binary communication transcript and which is correct on every \(I_j\). The transcripts produced by these instances must be pairwise distinct. If every transcript has length at most \(B\), at most \(2^{B+1}-1\) variable-length binary transcripts are available; therefore \[B\geq\left\lceil\log_2(M+1)\right\rceil-1.\] Under a fixed-length transcript convention the sharper bound is \(B\geq\lceil\log_2 M\rceil\).
assumptions_latex: The protocol is deterministic and correct on each \(I_j\).
The \(\varepsilon\)-valid decision-output sets of \(I_1,\ldots,I_M\) are pairwise disjoint.
Communication transcripts are binary strings of maximum length \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\geq\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil-1\), with \(B\geq\lceil\log_2M\rceil\) for fixed-length transcripts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript-counting lower bound for deterministic finite-bit protocols.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The variable-length transcript counting calculation is internally consistent for deterministic binary transcripts, and the fixed-length specialization is correctly distinguished. However, no communication-complexity source is supplied, so the transcript model and lower bound lack required evidence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix a distributed problem class \(\mathcal I\), communication network class \(\mathcal G\), finite-alphabet encoding model \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bit}}\), accuracy \(\varepsilon\), and failure probability \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition applies to finite encoded transcripts and charges the total number of transmitted bits, independently of how they are partitioned into messages or rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(L_{\mathrm{bit}}(\mathcal I,\mathcal G,\varepsilon,\delta)\) is a bit-communication lower bound if every protocol \(\Pi\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bit}}\) has some admissible instance and network on which achieving the declared \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy criterion with probability at least \(1-\delta\) requires a transcript whose total encoded length is at least \(L_{\mathrm{bit}}\). Equivalently, the minimax worst-case bit cost is at least \(L_{\mathrm{bit}}\). Public randomness, private randomness, variable-length coding, headers, and expected versus worst-case transcript length must be fixed by the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bit-communication lower bound is the minimum encoded information volume that every admissible distributed protocol must transmit on some problem and network before it can meet the accuracy and success requirements. The encoding and randomness conventions are part of the statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{\Pi\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bit}}}\sup_{I\in\mathcal I,\,G\in\mathcal G}N_{\mathrm{bit}}(\Pi,I,G,\varepsilon,\delta)\ge L_{\mathrm{bit}}(\mathcal I,\mathcal G,\varepsilon,\delta).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed-length \(b\)-bit messages, a lower bound of \(M\) messages implies \(bM\) transmitted bits under the same charging convention.
special_cases_latex: A per-edge lower bound sums only when the hard-instance argument establishes simultaneous traffic requirements on those edges.
immediate_consequences_latex: A bit lower bound can distinguish protocols having identical communication-round complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Dependent Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When distant data changes the required output, information propagation forces at least the corresponding graph distance in communication rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) contain nodes \(u,v\) at graph distance \(D\). Suppose two admissible instances differ only in data held at \(u\), while their \(\varepsilon\)-valid output sets at \(v\) are disjoint. In the synchronous neighbor-communication model, the state of \(v\) is identical on the two instances for every round \(R<D\), because information from \(u\) cannot yet reach \(v\). Thus no deterministic algorithm required to output correctly at \(v\) can terminate in fewer than \(D\) rounds on both instances, and its worst-case communication-round complexity satisfies \[R_A(\varepsilon;G)\geq D.\]
assumptions_latex: Each synchronous communication round moves information across at most one edge of \(G\).
The two instances differ only at node \(u\).
Their \(\varepsilon\)-valid output sets at node \(v\) are disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_A(\varepsilon;G)\geq\operatorname{dist}_G(u,v)=D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diameter-form information-propagation lower bound on a fixed communication graph.

notation.meaning: Graph distance between the data node u and decision node v.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G\) be a connected communication graph and \(\vartheta(G)\) a declared topology parameter, such as diameter \(D(G)\), conductance, spectral gap \(1-\lambda_2(W)\), or condition number of a graph operator.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A topology-dependent lower bound is a function \(L(\vartheta(G),\varepsilon,\mathcal P)\) such that, for every admissible algorithm, there exists a problem instance compatible with \(G\) for which the selected resource cost before \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy is at least \(L(\vartheta(G),\varepsilon,\mathcal P)\), where \(\mathcal P\) contains the remaining objective and oracle parameters. The dependence is substantive when varying graphs while holding \(\mathcal P\) fixed changes the lower-bound order or constant. For a graph class, the worst-case bound takes the supremum over its topology parameter values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A topology-dependent lower bound makes distributed hardness an explicit function of the communication graph, commonly through diameter or spectral conditioning. Every admissible algorithm must incur that cost on some compatible objective instance. The graph parameter and resource being bounded must be declared.

special_cases_latex: Finite-speed information propagation commonly yields diameter-indexed communication-depth bounds under neighbor-only communication.
immediate_consequences_latex: A graph-independent upper bound cannot match a topology-dependent lower bound uniformly unless it dominates the worst topology in the class.
boundary_notes: Diameter, spectral gap, and conductance are not interchangeable without graph-class assumptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Family attaining distributed minimax resource bounds
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For parameter vector \(\alpha\), let \(\mathcal I_\alpha\) be a distributed instance class under model \(\mathfrak M_\alpha\). Let \(L_j(\alpha,\varepsilon)\) be a valid minimax lower bound for each declared resource coordinate \(j\).

Lower-Bound-Matching Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method is lower-bound matching when its oracle calls and communication rounds attain their respective lower bounds, up to stated constants and polylogarithmic factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed algorithm family is lower-bound matching on \((\mathcal P,\mathcal M)\) when there are constants \(c,C>0\), independent of the instance and target accuracy, such that every \(P\in\mathcal P\) and admissible \(\varepsilon\) satisfy \[cL_{\rm or}(P,\varepsilon)\le Q_{\rm or}(P,\varepsilon)\le C L_{\rm or}(P,\varepsilon)\,\ell_{\rm or}(P,\varepsilon),\qquad cL_{\rm com}(P,\varepsilon)\le Q_{\rm com}(P,\varepsilon)\le C L_{\rm com}(P,\varepsilon)\,\ell_{\rm com}(P,\varepsilon),\] where \(\ell_{\rm or}\) and \(\ell_{\rm com}\) are the explicitly permitted polylogarithmic factors. Matching only one resource does not establish simultaneous lower-bound matching.
assumptions_latex: A distributed problem class \(\mathcal P\) and a communication-oracle model \(\mathcal M\) are fixed.
For every instance \(P\in\mathcal P\) and accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\), valid lower bounds \(L_{m or}(P,\varepsilon)\) and \(L_{m com}(P,\varepsilon)\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{m or}=\widetilde\Theta(L_{m or})\) and \(Q_{m com}=\widetilde\Theta(L_{m com})\) uniformly over \(\mathcal P\).

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Distributed Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal accelerated schemes require order square-root objective conditioning in local gradients and square-root combined objective–network conditioning in communication rounds, up to logarithmic accuracy factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x)\), where each agent initially knows only \(f_i\). For any \(\varepsilon\in(0,F(x^0)-F^*)\), accelerated distributed first-order methods combining objective acceleration with polynomially accelerated gossip can produce local iterates whose average \(\bar x\) satisfies \(F(\bar x)-F^*\leq\varepsilon\) using \(O(\sqrt{\kappa}\log((F(x^0)-F^*)/\varepsilon))\) local gradient evaluations per agent and \(O(\sqrt{\kappa\chi}\log((F(x^0)-F^*)/\varepsilon))\) communication rounds. Here one multiplication by the network mixing operator counts as one communication round.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and \(L\)-smooth, while \(F\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(0<\mu\leq L\).
The communication graph is fixed, connected, and undirected, with symmetric positive-semidefinite gossip Laplacian \(W\).
Exact local gradients and synchronous communication rounds are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_{\mathrm{grad}}=O\!\left(\sqrt{\kappa}\log\frac{F(x^0)-F^*}{\varepsilon}\right),\qquad N_{\mathrm{comm}}=O\!\left(\sqrt{\kappa\chi}\log\frac{F(x^0)-F^*}{\varepsilon}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly convex smooth decentralized optimization over a fixed connected undirected network.

notation.meaning: Network condition number using the smallest positive Laplacian eigenvalue.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle–Network Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle-network tradeoffs are the Pareto boundary of attainable pairs of local-oracle calls and communication rounds at a fixed accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each admissible algorithm \(A\), let \(Q_{\rm or}(A,\varepsilon)\) count local-oracle calls and let \(Q_{\rm com}(A,\varepsilon)\) count communication rounds needed to meet the prescribed accuracy. The attainable region is \[\mathcal F_\varepsilon=\bigl\{(q,c)\in\mathbb N^2:\exists A,\ Q_{\rm or}(A,\varepsilon)\le q,\ Q_{\rm com}(A,\varepsilon)\le c\bigr\}.\] It is upward closed. Its Pareto-minimal elements constitute the oracle-network tradeoff: improving one coordinate without worsening the other is impossible within the model. A lower-bound region \(\mathcal L_\varepsilon\) is matched when the attainable Pareto boundary agrees with its boundary up to the declared approximation factors.
assumptions_latex: A distributed problem class, local-oracle model, communication model, and accuracy criterion are fixed.
Worst-case oracle and communication counts are finite for at least one admissible algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_\varepsilon=\{(q,c):\exists A,\ (Q_{\rm or}(A),Q_{\rm com}(A))\preceq(q,c)\}\), with the tradeoff given by its Pareto-minimal boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-independent Pareto representation; numerical tradeoff curves require a specified function class and network oracle.

notation.meaning: Worst-case local-oracle and communication complexities of algorithm A
Upward-closed attainable resource region at accuracy epsilon

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto-region representation is mathematically coherent and its content kind fits the terminal container, but no source supports the selected oracle-network model or the asserted comparison with a lower-bound region.

knowledge_statements.title: Regime-Specific Optimality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regime-specific optimality requires uniform lower-bound matching within every declared parameter regime and for every counted resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\{A_k\}_{k=1}^K\) is regime-specifically optimal for the partition \(\Theta=\bigcup_{k=1}^K\Theta_k\) if, for every counted resource \(r\in\mathcal R\), there are constants \(C_{k,r}>0\) and declared polylogarithmic factors \(\ell_{k,r}\) such that \[Q_{k,r}(\theta,\varepsilon)\le C_{k,r}L_{k,r}(\theta,\varepsilon)\ell_{k,r}(\theta,\varepsilon)\qquad\text{for all }\theta\in\Theta_k.\] The quantifier is uniform within each regime. Consequently, pointwise tuning at one parameter value, or matching only the dominant resource while violating another resource lower bound, is insufficient for regime-specific optimality.
assumptions_latex: The parameter space \(\Theta\) is partitioned into regimes \(\Theta_1,\ldots,\Theta_K\).
Each regime has resource lower bounds \(L_{k,r}(\theta,\varepsilon)\) for resources \(r\) in a fixed finite set \(\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_k}Q_{k,r}(\theta,\varepsilon)/L_{k,r}(\theta,\varepsilon)\le C_{k,r}\ell_{k,r}(\theta,\varepsilon)\) for every \(k\) and \(r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal uniformity condition for claims whose optimal algorithm or dominant resource changes across parameter ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Primal-Dual Communication Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under this synchronous protocol, every edge contributes two directed vector messages per round, giving exactly two messages and at most twice the encoded vector payload per edge-round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a fixed undirected graph and let \(T,d,q\in\mathbb N\). Consider a synchronous distributed primal-dual execution lasting \(T\) communication rounds. Suppose that in every round each endpoint of every edge sends one \(d\)-coordinate vector to the other endpoint, with each coordinate encoded using at most \(q\) bits. Then the execution uses exactly \(T\) rounds and exactly \(2|E|T\) directed messages, and it transmits at most \(2|E|Tdq\) payload bits. If accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\) is guaranteed after \(T(\varepsilon)\) rounds, these counts hold with \(T=T(\varepsilon)\). Headers, synchronization traffic, and retransmissions are excluded.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a fixed undirected communication graph.
\(T,d,q\in\mathbb N\).
Every coordinate uses at most \(q\) bits.
Protocol overhead and retransmissions are excluded.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Communication complexity of a distributed primal-dual method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a communication graph. A distributed primal-dual algorithm \(\mathcal A\) generates iterates and, during round \(t\), transmits messages \(m_{e,t}\) over directed edge uses \(e\). Let \(C(z)\) be a prescribed accuracy certificate and \(\varepsilon\) its target.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous or explicitly round-indexed distributed methods; rounds, messages, scalars, and bits are distinguished cost measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The communication stopping time is \(T_\varepsilon=\inf\{t\in\mathbb N:C(z^t)\leq\varepsilon\}\). The round complexity is \(R_\varepsilon=T_\varepsilon\); the message complexity is \(M_\varepsilon=\sum_{t=1}^{T_\varepsilon}\sum_e\mathbf1\{m_{e,t}\text{ is sent}\}\); the scalar complexity is \(S_\varepsilon=\sum_{t=1}^{T_\varepsilon}\sum_e\dim(m_{e,t})\); and, under an encoding with length \(\ell(m)\), the bit complexity is \(B_\varepsilon=\sum_{t=1}^{T_\varepsilon}\sum_e\ell(m_{e,t})\). These quantities form the communication-complexity profile \(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon(\mathcal A,G)=(R_\varepsilon,M_\varepsilon,S_\varepsilon,B_\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication complexity is the cost incurred before the first iterate satisfying the declared accuracy certificate. Its profile records four noninterchangeable quantities: elapsed communication rounds, transmitted messages, transmitted scalar coordinates, and encoded bits. The graph, scheduling convention, message dimension, encoding, and certificate are part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon(\mathcal A,G)=(R_\varepsilon,M_\varepsilon,S_\varepsilon,B_\varepsilon)\) with every component accumulated through \(T_\varepsilon\).
special_cases_latex: If every active directed edge sends one \(d\)-vector per round, then \(S_\varepsilon=dM_\varepsilon\).
If all \(|E|\) undirected edges are used in both directions every round, then \(M_\varepsilon=2|E|R_\varepsilon\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Round complexity alone does not determine bit complexity without a communication and encoding model.
Local computation and oracle calls are excluded unless incorporated as separate coordinates of a broader cost profile.
boundary_notes: For asynchronous algorithms, a round must be defined through epochs, causal depth, or another explicit convention.
Infinite-precision real messages have no finite bit cost without a quantization model.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Quantization Accuracy–Bit Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform coordinate quantization has logarithmic payload cost in inverse distortion and Euclidean distortion proportional to the square root of dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For v\in[-R,R]^d, choose N=\lceil2R/\Delta\rceil+1 equally spaced scalar levels on [-R,R] and quantize each coordinate to a nearest level. Then the spacing is at most \Delta and \[\|Q(v)-v\|_2\le\frac{\sqrt d\,\Delta}{2}.\] A fixed-length coordinate index uses \[b_{\rm pay}=d\lceil\log_2N\rceil\] bits. For M_T such messages and h charged overhead bits per message, \[B_T=M_T\bigl(d\lceil\log_2N\rceil+h\bigr).\]
assumptions_latex: Every coordinate lies in \([-R,R]\).
The declared N-level nearest-neighbor uniform quantizer is used.
Fixed-length indices and h overhead bits per message are charged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Q(v)-v\|_2\le\sqrt d\Delta/2\) and \(B_T=M_T(d\lceil\log_2N\rceil+h)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete dimension, distortion, and fixed-length payload accounting.
review_flags: Corrected the builder's level-count bound, which was not valid for an arbitrary grid of spacing merely at most Delta.

knowledge_statements.title: Compression Bit Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total transmitted-bit accounting for achieving a prescribed optimization accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose round \(k\) transmits \(m_k\) compressed vectors and the \(j\)-th transmitted vector in that round has code length \(b_{k,j}\) bits. If an algorithm guarantees an error measure \(E_K\leq\varepsilon\) after \(K(\varepsilon)\) rounds, then its total payload-bit complexity is \[B(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_k}b_{k,j}.\] If \(m_k=m\), every code length satisfies \(b_{k,j}\leq b\), and \(K(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{-p}\), then \(B(\varepsilon)\leq mbC\varepsilon^{-p}\). Protocol overhead must either be included in the code lengths or reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bit complexity sums the actual lengths of all transmitted codes until the target accuracy is reached. Uniform upper bounds multiply vectors per round, bits per vector, and round complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(E_{K(\varepsilon)}\leq\varepsilon\)
Round \(k\) transmits \(m_k\) vectors with code lengths \(b_{k,j}\)
Protocol overhead is either included in \(b_{k,j}\) or explicitly excluded
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_k}b_{k,j}\), and under the uniform bounds \(B(\varepsilon)\leq mbC\varepsilon^{-p}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Federated-Averaging Communication Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a convergence round bound, total messages scale with participating clients per round, while total local oracle calls also scale with each client's local-step count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(\varepsilon)=\min\{R:\mathcal{E}(x^R)\le\varepsilon\}\). Under the stated message model, reaching accuracy \(\varepsilon\) uses \(R(\varepsilon)\) synchronization rounds, \[M(\varepsilon)=2\sum_{t=0}^{R(\varepsilon)-1}m_t\] client messages, equivalently \(dM(\varepsilon)\) transmitted scalar coordinates, and \[N(\varepsilon)=\sum_{t=0}^{R(\varepsilon)-1}\sum_{i\in S_t}K_{i,t}\] local oracle calls. A convergence theorem supplies \(R(\varepsilon)\); these identities expose the tradeoff between local work, participation, and communication.
assumptions_latex: One communication round broadcasts one \(d\)-dimensional server model and receives one \(d\)-dimensional response from each of \(m_t\) participating clients.
An accuracy criterion \(\mathcal{E}(x)\le\varepsilon\) and a convergence guarantee determining \(R(\varepsilon)\) are fixed.
Client \(i\) performs \(K_{i,t}\) local oracle calls in round \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The round complexity is \(R(\varepsilon)\), the client-message complexity is \(2\sum_{t<R(\varepsilon)}m_t\), and the local-oracle complexity is \(\sum_{t<R(\varepsilon)}\sum_{i\in S_t}K_{i,t}\).

children.title: Compression Operators
children.top_down_role: Lossy communication families used to encode distributed updates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) carry compressor randomness and let \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) encode and decode a vector into a communicated representation. Expectations are over this internal randomness conditional on the input.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector compressors used for distributed states, gradients, residuals, or tracking variables; exact bit encoding is a separate cost specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compression-operator family is a collection \(\mathcal Q\) of measurable maps \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) with declared communication cost and an explicit distortion contract. Two canonical contracts are: unbiased bounded variance, \(\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x\) and \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|^2\le\omega\|x\|^2\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^d\); and contractive compression, \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|^2\le(1-\alpha)\|x\|^2\) for all \(x\), where \(\omega\ge0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1]\). Membership in the family records which contract and constants hold; neither property is implicit from the word compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compression operator maps a vector to a possibly randomized lossy reconstruction that can be communicated more cheaply under a declared coding model. The operator family is mathematically specified by a distortion condition, commonly unbiased relative variance or mean-square contraction, together with its constants. Unbiased and contractive compressors are distinct families and must not be conflated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(Q\in\mathcal Q\) is classified by a stated all-input distortion inequality and, when applicable, the equality \(\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an unbiased compressor, \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|^2\) is equivalent to the variance bound.
A deterministic compressor is represented by a degenerate randomness space.
special_cases_latex: Identity compression has \(\omega=0\) and \(\alpha=1\).
Random sparsification, quantization, and low-rank sketches may satisfy different contracts with method-dependent constants.
immediate_consequences_latex: A contractive compressor may be biased.
An unbiased compressor with large \(\omega\) can introduce substantial update variance.
boundary_notes: The distortion contract does not itself establish a bit count or convergence rate.
Absolute-error compressors require a different inequality and are not covered by the displayed relative contracts.

notation.meaning: Relative mean-square variance parameter for an unbiased compressor.

review_flags: The supplied locator hints were not verified to contain these modern compressor contracts.
A precise compression-operator source locator is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized lossy compression operators

children.title: Quantization Methods
children.top_down_role: Reduced-precision encoding of states, gradients, or trackers.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Rounding
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly selecting an adjacent grid point removes rounding bias while retaining bounded mean-square error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in[k\Delta,(k+1)\Delta]\), output \(k\Delta\) with probability \(((k+1)\Delta-x)/\Delta\) and \((k+1)\Delta\) otherwise. Then \(\mathbb E[Q_\Delta(x)\mid x]=x\) and \(\mathbb E[(Q_\Delta(x)-x)^2\mid x]\le\Delta^2/4\). Coordinatewise application gives \(\mathbb E[\|Q_\Delta(x)-x\|_2^2\mid x]\le d\Delta^2/4\).
assumptions_latex: Each coordinate lies between two finite adjacent grid points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Q_\Delta(x)\mid x]=x\),\quad \(\mathbb E[\|Q_\Delta(x)-x\|_2^2\mid x]\le d\Delta^2/4\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased scalar quantization between adjacent grid points.

notation.meaning: index of the lower adjacent grid point

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Scalar Quantization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding coordinates to a uniform grid gives a deterministic absolute-error bound when no value is clipped.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For spacing \(\Delta>0\), define \(Q_\Delta(x)_j=\Delta\operatorname{round}(x_j/\Delta)\). If no coordinate is clipped, then \(|Q_\Delta(x)_j-x_j|\le\Delta/2\), and therefore \(\|Q_\Delta(x)-x\|_2\le\Delta\sqrt d/2\).
assumptions_latex: Ties use a fixed rounding convention.
No coordinate is saturated or clipped.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Q_\Delta(x)-x\|_2\le\Delta\sqrt d/2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise deterministic reduced-precision encoding on an unclipped grid.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Range Saturation Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite reconstruction range produces unbounded absolute error on unbounded inputs unless scaling or overflow handling is added.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a scalar quantizer has reconstruction set \(\mathcal C\subset[-M,M]\), then for every \(|x|>M\), \(|Q(x)-x|\ge |x|-M\). Consequently, no such finite-range quantizer has a finite global input-independent absolute-error bound without a scaling or overflow mechanism.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)\in\mathcal C\subset[-M,M]\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform absolute-error guarantees outside a finite reconstruction range.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantization Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-alphabet compression of vectors used in distributed optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be an input domain and let \(\mathcal{C}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be a finite codebook. A possibly randomized vector quantizer is a map \(Q:\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}\). It is unbiased on \(\mathcal{D}\) when \(\mathbb{E}[Q(x)\mid x]=x\) for every \(x\in\mathcal{D}\). It has relative second-moment parameter \(\omega\ge0\) on \(\mathcal{D}\) when \[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\mid x\right]\le\omega\|x\|_2^2\] for every \(x\in\mathcal{D}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-alphabet quantization replaces an input vector by a codebook element; unbiasedness and relative mean-square distortion may be imposed on a specified input domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(\mathcal{C}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is finite.
The norm is the Euclidean norm on \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Using a fixed-length codebook index, \(Q(x)\) can be represented using \(\lceil\log_2|\mathcal{C}|\rceil\) bits, excluding metadata.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-codebook quantizer with unbiasedness and relative variance properties

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be the input domain, \(\mathcal C\) a finite or countable code alphabet, \(E:X\times\Omega\to\mathcal C\) an encoder, and \(D:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R^d\) a decoder.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-precision encoding of distributed vectors; deterministic and randomized scalar or vector quantizers are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quantization method is an encoder--decoder pair whose reconstruction operator is \(Q(x;\xi)=D(E(x;\xi))\) and whose communicated symbol belongs to the declared discrete alphabet \(\mathcal C\). Its specification includes the representable set \(D(\mathcal C)\), code length or alphabet size, treatment of overflow, and a pointwise or stochastic distortion condition. A randomized unbiased quantizer additionally satisfies \(\mathbb E_
\xi[Q(x;\xi)]=x\) for every \(x\in X\); a deterministic uniform scalar quantizer with step \(\Delta>0\) maps each coordinate to a declared grid and, absent clipping, satisfies \(\|Q(x)-x\|_
\infty\le\Delta/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quantization encodes a real vector using a discrete symbol and reconstructs it from a finite- or countable-precision representation. A complete definition states the code alphabet, reconstruction points, bit or symbol cost, overflow behavior, and distortion guarantee. Randomized rounding may preserve the input in expectation, while deterministic uniform rounding provides a coordinatewise absolute-error bound when clipping does not occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=D\circ E\) has discrete communicated output \(E(x;\xi)\in\mathcal C\) and satisfies its declared distortion and, if claimed, unbiasedness conditions for every \(x\in X\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A codebook quantizer can be specified by decision regions \((R_c)_{c\in\mathcal C}\) and reconstruction points \(y_c\), with \(Q(x)=y_c\) for \(x\in R_c\).
special_cases_latex: Coordinatewise uniform quantization uses a regular scalar grid of spacing \(\Delta\).
Stochastic rounding selects adjacent grid points with probabilities chosen so their mean equals the input coordinate.
Sign quantization communicates a scale together with coordinate signs.
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite alphabet on an unbounded input domain requires clipping, adaptive scaling, or unbounded distortion.
Quantization is a compression family distinguished by a discrete reconstruction representation.
boundary_notes: The displayed \(\Delta/2\) bound excludes clipping and assumes nearest-grid rounding.
A countable alphabet does not by itself give a fixed finite bit budget.
review_flags: No supplied source locator was verified to support the exact encoder-decoder and distortion formulation.
A precise quantization source is required before review.

children.title: Sparsification Methods
children.top_down_role: Coordinate selection and sparse update communication.

knowledge_statements.title: Top-k Sparsification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Top-k keeps the largest coordinates, is a best Euclidean k-sparse approximation, and satisfies the sharp uniform contraction bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x\in\mathbb R^d and 1\le k\le d, let J_k(x) contain indices of k largest values of |x_j|, using a fixed tie rule, and define (T_k(x))_j=x_j\mathbf 1_{\{j\in J_k(x)\}}. Then \|x-T_k(x)\|_2=\min_{\|z\|_0\le k}\|x-z\|_2 and \|x-T_k(x)\|_2^2\le(1-k/d)\|x\|_2^2.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R^d.
1\le k\le d.
Ties are resolved by a fixed rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic retention of the largest-magnitude coordinates.

notation.meaning: number of nonzero coordinates of z

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsification Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-support compression with sparse transmitted values and indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparsifier is a possibly randomized map \(S:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) such that \(\|S(x)\|_0\le k\) almost surely for every input \(x\), where \(1\le k\le d\). Uniform random-\(k\) sparsification selects a uniformly random subset \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) of size \(k\) and sets \[S(x)_j=\frac{d}{k}x_j\mathbf{1}_{\{j\in I\}}.\] It satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[S(x)\mid x]=x\) and \(\mathbb{E}[\|S(x)-x\|_2^2\mid x]=(d/k-1)\|x\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparsification communicates at most k coordinates; scaled uniform random selection is unbiased with an explicit mean-square distortion.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(1\le k\le d\).
The subset \(I\) is sampled uniformly without replacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transmitted update uses at most \(k\) values and indices while preserving the input in conditional expectation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(d\in\mathbb N\), let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) carry any compressor randomness, and equip \(\mathbb R^d\) with the Euclidean norm. For \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), write \(\operatorname{supp}(x)=\{j:x_j\ne0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic or randomized coordinate sparsification; quantization of retained values and low-rank matrix sketches are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A map \(S:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) is a \(k\)-coordinate sparsifier if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), there is a measurable index set \(I(x,\xi)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(|I(x,\xi)|\le k\) almost surely and measurable coefficients \(a_j(x,\xi)\) such that \([S(x,\xi)]_j=a_j(x,\xi)x_j\) for \(j\in I(x,\xi)\) and \([S(x,\xi)]_j=0\) otherwise. Thus \(|\operatorname{supp}(S(x,\xi))|\le k\) almost surely. A sparsification method communicates the selected indices and retained scaled values and reconstructs exactly this sparse vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate-sparsification compressor on \(\mathbb R^d\) selects at most \(k\) coordinates, possibly as a random or input-dependent function, scales retained entries, and sets every unselected coordinate to zero. Its defining property is the almost-sure support bound \(|\operatorname{supp}(S(x,\xi))|\le k\) for every input \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\text{ is a }k\text{-coordinate sparsifier}\iff \forall x,\ \exists I(x,\xi),\ |I(x,\xi)|\le k\text{ a.s.},\ [S(x,\xi)]_j=a_j(x,\xi)x_j\mathbf 1_{\{j\in I(x,\xi)\}}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The support condition is equivalently \(\|S(x,\xi)\|_0\le k\) almost surely for every \(x\), together with coordinatewise retention and scaling.
special_cases_latex: Top-\(k\) sparsification takes \(I(x)\) to be indices of the \(k\) largest values of \(|x_j|\) and uses \(a_j=1\).
Uniform random-\(k\) sparsification samples a size-\(k\) subset and may use \(a_j=d/k\), yielding \(\mathbb E[S(x,\xi)]=x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: At most \(k\) numerical values and their indices need be transmitted per input.
When \(k=d\) and \(a_j=1\), the operator is the identity.
boundary_notes: The support bound alone does not imply unbiasedness, contraction, or an absolute-error guarantee.
Block sparsification requires replacing scalar coordinates by a specified block decomposition.
review_flags: No supplied source locator was verified to state this exact coordinate-sparsifier definition.

children.top_down_role: Structured low-dimensional representations of updates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Low-Rank Sketch Compressor for Matrix Updates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m,n,r\in\mathbb N\) with \(r<\min\{m,n\}\). Matrix updates lie in \(\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), equipped with the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-valued communication represented by rank-constrained factors or sketches; coordinate sparsity is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank-\(r\) sketch compressor is an encoder-decoder pair \(E:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\times\Omega\to\mathcal Z\) and \(D:\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) whose reconstruction \(C(X,\xi)=D(E(X,\xi))\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(C(X,\xi))\le r\) almost surely for every \(X\). In a factor-sketch realization, the message contains \(U(X,\xi)\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) and \(V(X,\xi)\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(C(X,\xi)=U(X,\xi)V(X,\xi)^{\mathsf T}\). A projection-sketch realization may instead communicate products such as \(X\Omega\) and auxiliary information sufficient to reconstruct a rank-at-most-\(r\) approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank sketch compressor maps every matrix update \(X\) to a message whose decoded matrix has rank at most \(r\). A canonical factor form transmits matrices \(U\) and \(V\) and reconstructs \(UV^{\mathsf T}\), replacing \(mn\) entries by structured information of order \(r(m+n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\text{ is rank-}r\text{ sketch compression}\iff C=D\circ E\text{ and }\operatorname{rank}(C(X,\xi))\le r\text{ a.s. for every }X.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Every reconstructed matrix admits factors \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) and \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfying \(C(X,\xi)=UV^{\mathsf T}\).
special_cases_latex: Truncated singular-value compression uses \(C(X)=\sum_{j=1}^r\sigma_j u_jv_j^{\mathsf T}\).
For \(r=1\), each reconstruction is an outer product \(uv^{\mathsf T}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A factor message contains \(r(m+n)\) scalars before metadata, compared with \(mn\) scalars for a dense matrix.
If \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\) and the encoder is exact on rank-\(r\) inputs, then \(C(X)=X\).
boundary_notes: A random linear sketch without a specified decoder and rank-constrained reconstruction is not, by this definition, a low-rank compressor.
The rank constraint alone supplies no approximation-error, unbiasedness, or convergence guarantee.
review_flags: No inspected supplied locator supports the exact encoder-decoder and rank-factor formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Sketch Compressor for Matrix Updates
Spectral Error and Exactness of Truncated-Rank Compression
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral error is the first discarded singular value, and truncated-rank compression is lossless exactly when the update rank fits the budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with ordered singular values and rank-\(r\) truncation \(X_r\), \(\|X-X_r\|_2=\sigma_{r+1}(X)\), where \(\sigma_{p+1}(X)=0\) and \(p=\min\{m,n\}\). Consequently, \(X_r=X\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\).
assumptions_latex: \(0\le r\le p=\min\{m,n\}\).
Singular values are ordered nonincreasingly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|X-X_r\|_2=\sigma_{r+1}(X)\), and \(X_r=X\iff\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-norm error and the lossless boundary for truncated-SVD update compression.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Update Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated-SVD compression of a matrix-valued optimization update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), let \(s=\min\{p,q\}\), and write a thin singular value decomposition \(X=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_s)V^\top\), where \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times s}\), \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times s}\), and \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_s\ge0\). For an integer \(r\) with \(0\le r\le s\), define \[X_r=U_{[:,1:r]}\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)V_{[:,1:r]}^\top.\] Then \(X_r\) minimizes \(\|X-Y\|_F\) over matrices \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le r\), and \(\|X-X_r\|_F^2=\sum_{j=r+1}^s\sigma_j^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncating a thin singular value decomposition produces a matrix of rank at most r with the best Frobenius-norm reconstruction error among all such matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), \(p,q\in\mathbb{N}\), and \(r\in\{0,\ldots,\min\{p,q\}\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained singular-vector factors define a rank-at-most-\(r\) message with optimal Frobenius reconstruction error.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Range-Sketch Compression
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random test matrix samples the update's range, and projection onto that range gives a rank-limited reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), draw \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times\ell}\), form \(Y=X\Omega\), and let \(Q\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\operatorname{range}(Y)\). Reconstruct \(\widehat X=QQ^\top X\), equivalently from transmitted factors \((Q,Q^\top X)\). For every realization, \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\le\ell\) and \(X-\widehat X=(I-QQ^\top)X\).
assumptions_latex: \(1\le\ell\le\min\{m,n\}\).
The factor-transmission convention is known to encoder and decoder.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\le\ell\) and \(X-\widehat X=(I-QQ^\top)X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided randomized range finding for a matrix-valued update.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis for the sampled range

knowledge_statements.title: Random Sketch Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear sketch transmission with decoder-based approximate reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times s}\) be a random sketching matrix with \(1\le s<q\), and suppose the realization of \(S\) is determined by randomness shared by the encoder and decoder. The encoder transmits \(Y=XS\), and a decoder \(D_S:\mathbb{R}^{p\times s}\to\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\) produces \(\widehat X=D_S(Y)\). Given \(\epsilon\ge0\), \(\delta\in[0,1]\), and a class \(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), the pair is an \((\epsilon,\delta)\) Frobenius reconstruction compressor on \(\mathcal{X}\) when \[\Pr_S\!\left(\|D_S(XS)-X\|_F\le\epsilon\|X\|_F\right)\ge1-\delta\] for every \(X\in\mathcal{X}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random linear sketch is transmitted instead of the full matrix, and a decoder reconstructs it with a specified probabilistic relative-error guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(p,q,s\in\mathbb{N}\), \(1\le s<q\), \(\epsilon\ge0\), and \(\delta\in[0,1]\).
The sketch randomness is shared by the encoder and decoder, \(D_S\) is measurable, and the probability is over that randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sketch payload contains \(ps\) scalar values; seed, metadata, and scalar-encoding costs are excluded from this count.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic encoder-decoder definition for random linear sketch compression

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Rank–Accuracy Frontier
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarded singular-value energy decreases with rank, so the first rank meeting the tolerance is cheapest under any monotone rank-cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E_r^2=\sum_{j=r+1}^{p}\sigma_j^2\) and \(r_\varepsilon=\min\{r\in\{0,\ldots,p\}:E_r\le\varepsilon\}\). Then \(E_{r+1}\le E_r\), and \(r_\varepsilon\) is the smallest truncated-SVD rank meeting tolerance \(\varepsilon\). Under any message-cost function nondecreasing in \(r\), it has minimum cost among tolerance-feasible truncated-SVD ranks.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The declared message cost is nondecreasing in rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\varepsilon=\min\{r:E_r\le\varepsilon\}\) minimizes the declared monotone cost over tolerance-feasible ranks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum rank meeting a Frobenius reconstruction tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Budget Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication-beneficial ranks for factored matrix-update transmission.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dense update \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), direct transmission costs \(pq\) scalar values. Transmitting a rank-\(r\) factorization \(X_r=AB^\top\), with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times r}\) and \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times r}\), costs \(r(p+q)\) scalar values before metadata and quantization. The factorization reduces this scalar budget exactly when \[r(p+q)<pq,\quad\text{equivalently}\quad r<\frac{pq}{p+q}.\] Under a budget of at most \(B_0\) scalar values, the feasible ranks satisfy \(r\le\lfloor B_0/(p+q)\rfloor\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low-rank factors save scalar communication only below a dimension-dependent rank threshold; a fixed budget directly limits the feasible rank.
assumptions_latex: \(p,q\in\mathbb{N}\), \(0\le r\le\min\{p,q\}\), and both factors are transmitted densely.
Each transmitted scalar has equal cost, while metadata and numerical precision overhead are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The communication-beneficial regime is \(0\le r<pq/(p+q)\), further restricted by \(r\le\lfloor B_0/(p+q)\rfloor\) when a budget \(B_0\) is imposed.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct parameter counting for dense low-rank factors
bit-level costs require a specified encoding model
