knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Injectivity Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured class is exactly recoverable precisely when no nonzero difference of two admissible matrices lies in the sketch nullspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(\mathcal S(X)=S\operatorname{vec}(X)\). A decoder satisfying \(D(\mathcal S(X))=X\) for every \(X\in\mathcal X\) exists if and only if \(\ker S\cap\operatorname{vec}(\mathcal X-\mathcal X)=\{0\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is linear.
The decoder may be defined arbitrarily outside \(\mathcal S(\mathcal X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\circ\mathcal S=I_{\mathcal X}\iff\ker S\cap\operatorname{vec}(\mathcal X-\mathcal X)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-recovery boundary for a structured matrix class under a fixed linear sketch.

knowledge_statements.title: Stable-Reconstruction Gain Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Injectivity alone does not ensure stable reconstruction; admissible differences must have uniformly positive sketch gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}=\inf_{X\ne X',\,X,X'\in\mathcal X}\|S\operatorname{vec}(X-X')\|_2/\|X-X'\|_F\). If an \(L\)-Lipschitz decoder on \(\mathcal S(\mathcal X)\) exactly recovers every \(X\in\mathcal X\), then \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}\ge1/L\). Hence \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}=0\) precludes uniformly Lipschitz-stable exact recovery, even if the sketch is injective on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions_latex: \(D(S\operatorname{vec}(X))=X\) for every \(X\in\mathcal X\).
\(D\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathcal S(\mathcal X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}\ge L^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary conditioning for Lipschitz recovery on a structured class.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch Reconstruction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and stable recovery of rank-bounded matrices from linear sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R^s\) be linear and let \(\mathcal M_r=\{X:\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\}\). Every \(X\in\mathcal M_r\) is uniquely determined by \(\mathcal A(X)\) if and only if \(\ker(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal M_{2r}=\{0\}\). Define \(\alpha_{2r}=\inf\{\|\mathcal A(H)\|_2:\operatorname{rank}(H)\le2r,\ \|H\|_F=1\}\). Stable reconstruction on \(\mathcal M_r\) requires \(\alpha_{2r}>0\), yielding \(\|X-Y\|_F\le\alpha_{2r}^{-1}\|\mathcal A(X)-\mathcal A(Y)\|_2\). A nonzero rank-at-most-\(2r\) null-space element therefore prevents unique recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sketch recovers every rank-r matrix exactly only when its null space contains no nonzero matrix of rank at most 2r; positive restricted gain gives stability.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n,r,s\in\mathbb N\) with \(r\le\min\{m,n\}\).
\(\mathcal A\) is a linear sketching operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A|_{\mathcal M_r}\text{ is injective}\iff\ker(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal M_{2r}=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Matrices of rank at most r.
Minimum sketch gain over unit Frobenius-norm matrices of rank at most 2r.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard null-space characterization for low-rank linear inverse problems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The null-space characterization and restricted-gain stability statement are mathematically coherent and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports these nontrivial low-rank recovery claims.

children.title: Reference-State Predictive Compression Family
children.top_down_role: Encoding innovations relative to stored or predicted states.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_t\in\mathbb R^d\) be a sequence held by a sender. Before round \(t\), sender and receiver possess a synchronized reference \(h_t\in\mathbb R^d\). Let \(Q_t:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be an innovation compressor.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stateful predictive compression with synchronized encoder-decoder references in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reference-state predictive compressor encodes the innovation \(\delta_t=x_t-h_t\), transmits a representation of \(q_t=Q_t(\delta_t,\xi_t)\), and reconstructs \(\widehat x_t=h_t+q_t\). Its reference update is a shared measurable rule \(h_{t+1}=H_t(h_t,q_t,\widehat x_t)\), evaluated identically by sender and receiver, so their references remain equal whenever initialized equally and supplied the same message. The defining distinction is that the compressed argument is the innovation relative to a reproducible reference, not the full state \(x_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reference-state predictive compression maintains the same reference \(h_t\) at the sender and receiver, compresses only the innovation \(x_t-h_t\), reconstructs \(h_t+Q_t(x_t-h_t)\), and advances both copies of the reference by the same update rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_t=x_t-h_t,\quad q_t=Q_t(\delta_t,\xi_t),\quad \widehat x_t=h_t+q_t,\quad h_{t+1}=H_t(h_t,q_t,\widehat x_t).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The reconstruction error equals the innovation-compression error: \(\widehat x_t-x_t=Q_t(x_t-h_t,\xi_t)-(x_t-h_t)\).
special_cases_latex: With \(h_{t+1}=\widehat x_t\), the decoded state becomes the next prediction reference.
With \(h_t=0\) for all \(t\), the construction reduces to memoryless compression of \(x_t\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Equal initial references and identical received messages imply equal sender and receiver references at every subsequent round.
If \(Q_t(0,\xi)=0\), an input equal to its reference is reconstructed without innovation error.
boundary_notes: Desynchronization caused by packet loss requires an additional recovery or acknowledgment protocol.
No accuracy benefit follows unless the innovations or their compressed errors are controlled.
review_flags: The supplied source hints do not provide a verified locator for this stateful predictive-compression definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Reference-State Predictive Compressor
Variation-Controlled Difference Magnitude
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the previous state as reference, the encoded value is exactly the state increment, so its magnitude is governed by temporal variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the shared reference is the preceding state, \(h_t=x_{t-1}\), then \(\Delta_t=x_t-x_{t-1}\). Hence \(\|\Delta_t\|=\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|\) and \(\sum_{t=1}^T\|\Delta_t\|=\sum_{t=1}^T\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|\). A bound on one-step state variation is therefore exactly a bound on the compressor input magnitude.
assumptions_latex: Sender and receiver share the exact preceding state as reference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_t=x_t-x_{t-1}\), and \(\|\Delta_t\|\le v_t\iff\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|\le v_t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relation between consecutive-state variation and the encoded innovation.

knowledge_statements.title: Difference Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding an update relative to a shared reference state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a source vector \(x_t\in\mathbb R^d\) and a reference \(s_t\in\mathbb R^d\) known to both endpoints, the encoder forms \(\Delta_t=x_t-s_t\) and transmits \(q_t=Q(\Delta_t)\). The decoder reconstructs \(\widehat x_t=s_t+q_t\). Consequently, \(\widehat x_t-x_t=Q(\Delta_t)-\Delta_t\); thus the reconstruction error is exactly the compression error of the difference rather than that of the full state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transmit a compressed difference from a shared reference and add it back at the decoder; reconstruction error equals the difference-compression error.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t,s_t\in\mathbb R^d\).
\(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is a possibly randomized compressor.
Encoder and decoder use the same \(s_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_t=s_t+Q(x_t-s_t),\qquad \widehat x_t-x_t=Q(\Delta_t)-\Delta_t\).

notation.meaning: Difference between the source and reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The differential encoding identities are correct and representation is the appropriate kind, but the record supplies no inspectable compression-specific citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Reconstruction Error Identity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction error is exactly compression error on the prediction residual, so a smaller residual proportionally reduces distortion under a relative-error compressor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r_t=x_t-h_t, q_t=Q_t(r_t), and \widehat x_t=h_t+q_t. Then \widehat x_t-x_t=Q_t(r_t)-r_t. If \mathbb E[\|Q_t(r)-r\|_2^2\mid r]\le\omega_t\|r\|_2^2 for every r, then \mathbb E[\|\widehat x_t-x_t\|_2^2\mid x_t,h_t]\le\omega_t\|x_t-h_t\|_2^2.
assumptions_latex: x_t,h_t\in\mathbb R^d.
Q_t satisfies the stated conditional relative mean-square error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x_t-x_t=Q_t(x_t-h_t)-(x_t-h_t),\qquad \mathbb E[\|\widehat x_t-x_t\|_2^2\mid x_t,h_t]\le\omega_t\|x_t-h_t\|_2^2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact distortion transfer when a state is compressed relative to its prediction.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictive State Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State transmission by compressing residuals from synchronized predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize identical predictor states \(p_0^E=p_0^D\). At round \(t\), the encoder observes \(x_t\), computes \(r_t=x_t-p_t^E\), and sends \(q_t=Q(r_t)\). The decoder outputs \(\widehat x_t=p_t^D+q_t\). Both endpoints then apply the same deterministic transition \(p_{t+1}^E=\Phi(p_t^E,\widehat x_t,q_t)\) and \(p_{t+1}^D=\Phi(p_t^D,\widehat x_t,q_t)\). The procedure stops under the enclosing optimization algorithm's rule and returns the decoded state sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both endpoints predict the next state, communicate a compressed prediction residual, reconstruct the state, and update identical predictors from common information.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t,p_t^E,p_t^D\in\mathbb R^d\).
\(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is a compressor.
\(\Phi\) is deterministic and identically implemented at both endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_t^E=p_t^D\Longrightarrow\widehat x_t-x_t=Q(x_t-p_t^E)-(x_t-p_t^E)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical predictive residual coding recursion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The synchronized predictive-residual recursion is internally consistent and algorithm fits the container, but no source establishes this as a recognized distributed predictive-compression procedure.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference-State Synchronization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal initialization, identical received messages, and identical deterministic updates keep sender and receiver references synchronized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let sender and receiver references be \(h_t^{\mathrm{s}},h_t^{\mathrm{r}}\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Synchronization holds if \(h_0^{\mathrm{s}}=h_0^{\mathrm{r}}\), both endpoints receive the same message \(q_t\), and both update by one deterministic map \(U_t\): \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm{s}}=U_t(h_t^{\mathrm{s}},q_t)\) and \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm{r}}=U_t(h_t^{\mathrm{r}},q_t)\). These conditions preserve equality of the references at every round.
assumptions_latex: \(h_0^{\mathrm{s}}=h_0^{\mathrm{r}}\).
Both endpoints apply the same deterministic \(U_t\) to the same \(q_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_t^{\mathrm{s}}=h_t^{\mathrm{r}}\) for every \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant ensuring identical predictive references at sender and receiver.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Reference-State Synchronization, and the equality invariant follows from the stated common initialization, messages, and deterministic updates. No citation with a specific locator is supplied for this synchronization condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Predictor Amplifies Reference Mismatch
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unstable predictor can geometrically amplify a small initial disagreement between encoder and decoder references.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm s}=a h_t^{\mathrm s}\) and \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm r}=a h_t^{\mathrm r}\), with \(|a|>1\) and no resynchronization. If \(h_0^{\mathrm r}-h_0^{\mathrm s}=\delta\ne0\), then \(h_t^{\mathrm r}-h_t^{\mathrm s}=a^t\delta\). Thus an initial reference discrepancy grows geometrically even without additional quantization error.
assumptions_latex: No synchronization correction is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|h_t^{\mathrm r}-h_t^{\mathrm s}|=|a|^t|\delta|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar counterexample showing geometric amplification of unsynchronized predictor states.

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Mismatch Propagation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonexpansive predictor prevents one-step mismatch growth; an expansive Lipschitz bound permits geometric amplification unless synchronization corrects it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If sender and receiver apply the same \(L\)-Lipschitz predictor \(P\), then \(\|P(h_t^{\mathrm r})-P(h_t^{\mathrm s})\|\le L\|h_t^{\mathrm r}-h_t^{\mathrm s}\|\). Therefore \(L\le1\) guarantees nonexpansion in the absence of other errors, whereas an assumption with \(L>1\) permits geometric amplification and supplies no nonexpansion guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
Sender and receiver apply the same predictor.
No synchronization correction or additional mismatch input is applied in this step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|e_{t+1}\|\le L\|e_t\|\), where \(e_t=h_t^{\mathrm r}-h_t^{\mathrm s}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step reference-desynchronization bound for a common predictor map.
review_flags: Corrected the builder's overly strong claim that nonexpansion is possible only when the declared Lipschitz constant is at most one.

knowledge_statements.title: Prediction-Mismatch Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstruction bias caused by unequal encoder and decoder predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the encoder predicts with \(a_t\), sends \(q_t=Q(x_t-a_t)\), and the decoder predicts with \(b_t\), producing \(\widehat x_t=b_t+q_t\). Then \(\widehat x_t-x_t=(b_t-a_t)+Q(x_t-a_t)-(x_t-a_t)\). Hence prediction mismatch adds directly to compression error. In particular, for the identity compressor \(Q(z)=z\), reconstruction still fails whenever \(a_t\ne b_t\), because \(\widehat x_t-x_t=b_t-a_t\); compressor accuracy alone cannot correct unsynchronized references.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unequal predictions add their mismatch directly to reconstruction error; even lossless residual transmission cannot repair an unsynchronized reference.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t,a_t,b_t\in\mathbb R^d\).
The encoder uses \(a_t\) while the decoder uses \(b_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_t-x_t=(b_t-a_t)+\bigl(Q(x_t-a_t)-(x_t-a_t)\bigr)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact algebraic decomposition of predictive decoding error

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mismatch-error decomposition is algebraically correct and failure_boundary is the correct role, but no predictive-coding source is cited for the modeled failure phenomenon.

children.title: Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Compressor classes supporting different stability and convergence mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be measurable, and let expectations be conditional on the input \(x\). Fix \(b\ge0\), \(\omega\ge0\), and \(\sigma\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general finite-dimensional second-moment condition that records bias, relative distortion, and absolute distortion without requiring any one specialized compressor class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The compressor \(C\) satisfies the \((b,\omega,\sigma)\) moment condition if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), \(\|\mathbb E[C(x,\xi)]-x\|\le b\|x\|\) and \(\mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)-x\|^2\le\omega\|x\|^2+\sigma^2\). The first inequality controls systematic bias; the second permits both input-relative and magnitude-independent reconstruction error. Deterministic compressors are included by treating \(\Omega\) as a singleton. Specialized conditions arise by fixing parameters or replacing these bounds with stronger contraction or pathwise requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressor satisfies a general moment condition when its mean bias is at most \(b\|x\|\) and its mean-square reconstruction error is at most \(\omega\|x\|^2+\sigma^2\) for every input. The parameters separately expose bias, relative error, and absolute error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x\in\mathbb R^d:\quad \|\mathbb E C(x)-x\|\le b\|x\|,\qquad \mathbb E\|C(x)-x\|^2\le\omega\|x\|^2+\sigma^2.\)
special_cases_latex: Setting \(b=0\) imposes mean preservation when the first bound is attained as equality zero.
Setting \(\sigma=0\) gives a purely relative mean-square error bound; setting \(\omega=0\) gives a uniform absolute mean-square bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: At \(x=0\), the second condition gives \(\mathbb E\|C(0,\xi)\|^2\le\sigma^2\).
If \(\sigma=0\), then \(C(0,\xi)=0\) almost surely.
boundary_notes: These conditions do not specify message length, sparsity, quantization levels, or decoder structure.
Different convergence analyses may require only one inequality or a stronger conditional version relative to an algorithmic filtration.

notation.meaning: relative and absolute mean-square error parameters

review_flags: This unifying parameterization is mathematically plausible but no supplied locator was verified to present it as the canonical compressor condition.

children.title: Unbiased Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Random compression preserving updates in expectation.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Output Second-Moment Form
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an unbiased compressor, a relative variance bound is equivalent to an output second-moment bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \mathbb E[Q(x)]=x, then \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2=\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2-\|x\|_2^2. Therefore \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2 is equivalent to \mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|_2^2. Either form implies Q(0)=0 almost surely.
assumptions_latex: Q(x) has finite second moment for every x.
\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x for every x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2\iff\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|_2^2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent second-moment representation for an unbiased compressor.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Compressor Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation preservation with relative second-moment error control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomized map \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) is an unbiased compressor with variance parameter \(\omega\ge0\) when, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), \(\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x\) and \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2\). The expectation is over the compressor's internal randomness. Unbiasedness also gives the equivalent second-moment bound \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased compressor preserves every input in expectation and bounds its mean-square compression error proportionally to the input's squared norm.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) is measurable.
\(\omega\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x,\qquad \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb R^d\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional unbiased relative-variance compressor class

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unbiasedness and relative mean-square error conditions are standard, and the second-moment implication is correct, but no authoritative compressor-definition source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be measurable. Expectations are taken over compressor randomness conditionally on the deterministic input \(x\), and \(\|\cdot\|\) is the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random finite-dimensional compressors that preserve every input in conditional expectation and have relative second-moment distortion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\omega\ge0\), \(C\) is an unbiased compressor with variance parameter \(\omega\) if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), \(\mathbb E[C(x,\xi)]=x\) and \(\mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)-x\|^2\le\omega\|x\|^2\). Equivalently, mean preservation together with the identity \(\mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)\|^2=\|x\|^2+\mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)-x\|^2\) yields \(\mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)\|^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased bounded-variance compressor preserves each input in expectation and bounds its mean-square compression error by \(\omega\) times the squared input norm, uniformly over all inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x\in\mathbb R^d:\quad \mathbb E[C(x,\xi)]=x,\qquad \mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)-x\|^2\le\omega\|x\|^2.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under \(\mathbb E[C(x,\xi)]=x\), the variance bound is equivalent to \(\mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)\|^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: The identity compressor has \(\omega=0\).
Uniform random-\(k\) sparsification scaled by \(d/k\) has a dimension-dependent variance parameter.
immediate_consequences_latex: The conditions force \(C(0,\xi)=0\) almost surely.
If \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to a past filtration and fresh compressor randomness is conditionally independent, then \(\mathbb E[C(x_t,\xi_t)\mid x_t]=x_t\).
boundary_notes: Mean preservation alone is insufficient without the second-moment bound.
Biased contractive compressors are outside this class unless rescaling makes them satisfy both displayed conditions.
review_flags: No supplied local locator was verified to state both exact unbiasedness and variance inequalities.

children.title: Contractive Biased Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Biased compression controlled through contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero Preservation and Output-Moment Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every contractive compressor fixes zero and has a uniformly controlled output second moment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Q satisfies \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2 for 0<\delta\le1, then Q(0)=0 almost surely and \bigl(\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le\bigl(1+\sqrt{1-\delta}\bigr)\|x\|_2. For deterministic Q, both conclusions hold pointwise.
assumptions_latex: Q(x) has finite second moment for every x.
0<\delta\le1.
The mean-square contraction inequality holds for every input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q(0)=0\ \text{a.s.},\qquad \mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2\le(1+\sqrt{1-\delta})^2\|x\|_2^2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural consequences of mean-square compressor contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Biased Compressor Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-square contraction allowing nonzero compression bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A possibly randomized compressor \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) is \(\delta\)-contractive, with \(0<\delta\le1\), when \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). No condition \(\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x\) is imposed, so the class permits biased compressors. For deterministic \(Q\), the expectation is omitted and the inequality must hold pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive compressor reduces mean-square relative error by a fixed factor but need not preserve the input in expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) is measurable.
\(0<\delta\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^d\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mean-square contraction condition correctly permits biased compressors and condition fits the terminal container, but it lacks an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be measurable and let \(\delta\in(0,1]\). Expectations are conditional on the input.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Possibly biased randomized or deterministic compressors controlled by relative mean-square contraction toward the input.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The map \(C\) is a \(\delta\)-contractive compressor if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), \(\mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)-x\|^2\le(1-\delta)\|x\|^2\). No equality \(\mathbb E[C(x,\xi)]=x\) is required, so the class permits systematic bias. In the deterministic case the expectation is omitted and the same inequality holds pointwise. The parameter \(\delta\) measures retained fidelity: larger \(\delta\) imposes smaller relative reconstruction error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive biased compressor is any possibly biased map whose mean-square distance from every input is no more than \((1-\delta)\) times the squared input norm. Deterministic compression uses the same inequality without expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x\in\mathbb R^d:\quad \mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)-x\|^2\le(1-\delta)\|x\|^2,\qquad 0<\delta\le1.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\alpha=1-\delta\in[0,1)\), the condition is \(\mathbb E\|C(x,)-x\|^2\le\alpha\|x\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: The identity map is \(1\)-contractive.
Deterministic Top-\(k\) coordinate retention satisfies a dimension-dependent contraction bound in the Euclidean norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: The condition forces \(C(0,\xi)=0\) almost surely.
The root-mean-square reconstruction error is at most \(\sqrt{1-\delta}\|x\|\).
boundary_notes: Contractivity does not imply unbiasedness.
An absolute error floor independent of \(\|x\|\) is not allowed by this homogeneous condition.

children.title: Absolute-Error Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Compression with magnitude-independent error control.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Error Does Not Imply Relative Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed additive offset has uniformly bounded absolute error but cannot satisfy any global relative-error condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix b\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\} and define Q_b(x)=x+b. Then \|Q_b(x)-x\|_2^2=\|b\|_2^2 for every x, so Q_b has absolute-error parameter \sigma=\|b\|_2. No finite \omega satisfies \|Q_b(x)-x\|_2^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2 for every x, because the right side vanishes at x=0.
assumptions_latex: b\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_b\text{ satisfies a uniform absolute-error bound but no finite global relative-error bound.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of magnitude-independent and relative compressor conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Error Compressor Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform mean-square error independent of input magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A possibly randomized compressor \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) has absolute mean-square error at most \(\sigma^2\) when \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le\sigma^2\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), where \(\sigma\ge0\) does not depend on \(x\). Unlike relative-error conditions, this bound need not vanish as \(x\to0\). For deterministic compression, the expectation is removed and the same bound holds pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absolute-error compressor has a uniform mean-square distortion bound that does not scale with the magnitude of its input.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) is measurable.
\(\sigma\ge0\) is independent of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le\sigma^2\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard magnitude-independent compressor error condition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform absolute mean-square error condition matches the title and role, but no inspectable source supports the stated compressor class and terminology.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be measurable, and fix \(\sigma\ge0\). Expectations are conditional on the input.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The map \(C\) is an absolute mean-square-error compressor with radius \(\sigma\) if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), \(\mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)-x\|^2\le\sigma^2\). A deterministic absolute-error compressor satisfies the pointwise condition \(\|C(x)-x\|\le\sigma\) for all \(x\). Unlike relative compressor conditions, the permitted error does not scale with \(\|x\|\); consequently the definition allows nonzero error at the origin and becomes relatively more accurate for large inputs.

When \(\sigma=0\), the compressor equals the identity almost surely at every input.

At the origin, \(\mathbb E\|C(0,)\|^2\le\sigma^2\).

children.title: Deterministic Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Fixed lossy encodings without randomization.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Unbiasedness Is Trivial
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without internal randomness, unbiasedness forces the compressor to be the identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d be deterministic. Expectation over the compressor's internal randomness gives \mathbb E[Q(x)]=Q(x). Hence \mathbb E[Q(x)]=x for every x if and only if Q(x)=x for every x. Thus a nonidentity deterministic lossy compressor cannot be unbiased in this sense.
assumptions_latex: Q has no internal randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall x,\ \mathbb E[Q(x)]=x)\iff Q=I.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between deterministic lossy compression and compressor-randomness unbiasedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Compressor Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise distortion conditions for compressors without internal randomness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic compressor is a fixed map \(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\): repeated evaluations at the same \(x\) return the same \(Q(x)\), with no expectation over internal randomness. Any claimed distortion guarantee must therefore hold pointwise. For example, relative contractivity with parameter \(\delta\in(0,1]\) means \(\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). Determinism alone supplies no accuracy bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic compressor is a fixed map, so distortion guarantees are pointwise; absence of randomness by itself does not ensure accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is single-valued and fixed across calls.
For the displayed relative guarantee, \(0<\delta\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb R^d\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deterministic specialization of pointwise compressor conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly distinguishes determinism from accuracy and presents contractivity only as an additional pointwise condition, but no authoritative deterministic-compression source is cited.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) be a fixed map with no auxiliary random variable, and let \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed finite-dimensional lossy encodings governed by a uniform pathwise relative-error condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic relative-error compressor with factor \(\rho\) is a map \(C:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) satisfying \(\|C(x)-x\|\le\rho\|x\|\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). Its output is uniquely determined by its input and fixed encoder-decoder state; there is no expectation or probability qualifier. It is deterministically contractive when \(0\le\rho<1\). A communication implementation additionally supplies an encoder \(E\) and decoder \(D\) such that \(C=D\circ E\), but the analytic condition concerns the decoded map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic compressor is a fixed decoded map with no randomization. Under the canonical relative-error condition, every reconstruction differs from its input by at most \(\rho\) times the input norm; it is contractive when \(\rho<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x\in\mathbb R^d:\quad \|C(x)-x\|\le\rho\|x\|.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The squared form is \(\|C(x)-x\|^2\le\rho^2\|x\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: The identity map has \(\rho=0\).
A fixed Top-\(k\) rule is deterministic once its tie-breaking convention is fixed.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every finite-\(\rho\) deterministic relative-error compressor satisfies \(C(0)=0\).
The triangle inequality gives \(\|C(x)\|\le(1+\rho)\|x\|\).
boundary_notes: Determinism alone does not imply any error bound; the displayed inequality is an additional compressor condition.
Randomized encoders, even with deterministic decoders, are outside this deterministic-map definition.
review_flags: No supplied locator was verified to establish this relative-error condition as the canonical deterministic compressor condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Relative-Error Compressor

children.title: Compression Error Compensation
children.top_down_role: Memory and correction mechanisms controlling persistent compression error.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(u_t\in\mathbb R^d\) be an update to communicate, let \(s_t\in\mathcal S\) be compensation memory, and let \(C_t:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be a compressor.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General stateful compensation interfaces; residual error feedback, corrected consensus, and compressed gradient tracking are special mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compression-error compensation mechanism is a stateful encoder specified by measurable maps \(A_t:\mathbb R^d\times\mathcal S\to\mathbb R^d\) and \(B_t:\mathbb R^d\times\mathcal S\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal S\). At round \(t\), it forms a corrected input \(v_t=A_t(u_t,s_t)\), communicates \(q_t=C_t(v_t,\xi_t)\), and updates memory by \(s_{t+1}=B_t(u_t,s_t,q_t)\). The mechanism is error-compensating when \(s_{t+1}\) explicitly retains information about the untransmitted discrepancy \(v_t-q_t\) and a later corrected input depends on that memory. This distinguishes compensation from independently compressing each \(u_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compression error compensation augments a compressor with memory. It modifies the current update using stored state, compresses that corrected input, and updates the state using the new compression discrepancy so that information omitted now can influence later messages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_t=A_t(u_t,s_t),\qquad q_t=C_t(v_t,\xi_t),\qquad s_{t+1}=B_t(u_t,s_t,q_t),\quad v_{t+1}\text{ depends on retained information from }v_t-q_t.\)
special_cases_latex: Residual error feedback uses \(v_t=u_t+e_t\) and \(e_{t+1}=v_t-q_t\).
Reference-memory compensation may compress \(u_t-h_t\) and update a synchronized reference \(h_t\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(A_t(u,s)=u\) and \(B_t\) discards \(v_t-q_t\), the construction reduces to memoryless compression.
The state dimension and update rule determine which past compression discrepancies can affect future messages.
boundary_notes: The definition supplies a mechanism, not a convergence guarantee.
A state used only for random-number generation is not compensation unless it retains compression-discrepancy information.
review_flags: No supplied source locator was verified to state this general stateful compensation interface.
knowledge_statements.title: Stateful Compression-Error Compensation

children.title: Error Feedback
children.top_down_role: Residual accumulation and reinjection across communication rounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncontractive Zero-Compressor Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero compressor stores every missing update but never releases it, so the method stagnates and its residual diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q(v)=0 for every v, e_0=0, and g_t=g\ne0. Then q_t=0 and e_{t+1}=e_t+g=(t+1)g. If the optimizer moves only through q_t, its iterate remains fixed while the residual diverges linearly.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\equiv0\).
The optimizer moves only through transmitted vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_t=0\), \(e_t=tg\), and \(x_t=x_0\) for all t.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual storage cannot compensate for a compressor that never transmits.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Stepsize Weighted Feedback Identity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With varying stepsizes, feedback cancellation includes stepsize-difference terms and is not only a terminal-residual identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Since q_t=g_t+e_t-e_{t+1}, arbitrary finite scalar stepsizes satisfy \[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_tq_t=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_tg_t+\eta_0e_0+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}(\eta_t-\eta_{t-1})e_t-\eta_{T-1}e_T.\]
assumptions_latex: The scalar stepsizes are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{t<T}\eta_t(q_t-g_t)=\eta_0e_0+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}(\eta_t-\eta_{t-1})e_t-\eta_{T-1}e_T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary of the usual unweighted cumulative cancellation.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Bound for a Contractive Compressor
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive compressor bounds the feedback residual by a geometric convolution of past update magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For p_t=g_t+e_t, q_t=Q(p_t), and e_{t+1}=p_t-q_t, suppose \|Q(v)-v\|\le\delta\|v\| for all v, with 0\le\delta<1. Then \[\|e_{t+1}\|\le\delta^{t+1}\|e_0\|+\delta\sum_{s=0}^t\delta^{t-s}\|g_s\|.\] If \|g_t\|\le G, then \[\sup_t\|e_t\|\le\|e_0\|+\frac{\delta G}{1-\delta}.\]
assumptions_latex: The standard error-feedback residual recursion is used.
\(\|Q(v)-v\|\le\delta\|v\|\) with \(\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability of error-feedback memory under relative compression error.

knowledge_statements.title: Error Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual accumulation and reinjection for compressed optimization updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\) and residual \(e_0=0\). At round \(t\), obtain an update \(g_t\), form \(u_t=g_t+e_t\), transmit \(q_t=Q(u_t)\), set \(e_{t+1}=u_t-q_t\), and update \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tq_t\). Stop according to the enclosing optimization method and output its designated iterate. The residual recursion gives \(q_t=g_t+e_t-e_{t+1}\), hence \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}q_t=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}g_t+e_0-e_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Error feedback stores each compression residual and adds it to the next update, making cumulative transmitted updates differ only by boundary residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(g_t,e_t,x_t\in\mathbb R^d\).
\(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is a possibly randomized compressor.
\(\eta_t>0\) is the enclosing method's step size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}q_t=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}g_t-e_T\quad\text{when }e_0=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical error-feedback recursion and telescoping identity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual recursion and telescoping identity are correct and algorithm is appropriate for Error Feedback, but the canonical algorithm requires an authoritative source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(u_t\in\mathbb R^d\) be a sequence of intended updates, let \(C_t:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be compressors, and initialize a residual \(e_0\in\mathbb R^d\), commonly \(e_0=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive residual accumulation and reinjection across discrete communication rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Error feedback forms \(v_t=u_t+e_t\), transmits \(q_t=C_t(v_t,\xi_t)\), and stores the untransmitted residual \(e_{t+1}=v_t-q_t=u_t+e_t-q_t\). An optimizer using update \(u_t\) applies the communicated vector \(q_t\) while carrying \(e_{t+1}\) into the next compressed input. The recursion is defined independently of whether \(C_t\) is biased or randomized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Error feedback adds the previously untransmitted residual to the current intended update, compresses the sum, and stores the difference between that sum and the transmitted vector for reinjection at the next round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_t=u_t+e_t,\qquad q_t=C_t(v_t,\xi_t),\qquad e_{t+1}=u_t+e_t-q_t.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The recursion has the exact accounting identity \(q_t=u_t+e_t-e_{t+1}\).
For every \(T\ge1\), the defining recursion implies the cumulative identity \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}q_t=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}u_t+e_0-e_T\).
special_cases_latex: With \(e_0=0\) and the identity compressor, \(e_t=0\) and \(q_t=u_t\) for every \(t\).
A deterministic biased sparsifier can be used without changing the residual recursion.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the terminal residual \(e_T\) is small, cumulative transmitted updates closely match cumulative intended updates.
The memoryless method is recovered by forcibly resetting \(e_t=0\) before every compression.
boundary_notes: Bounded residuals and optimizer convergence require additional compressor and stepsize assumptions.
Delayed, lossy, or reordered messages require a separately specified network-state model.
review_flags: No supplied source locator was verified to contain this exact error-feedback recursion.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Error-Feedback Recursion

children.title: Error-Compensated Consensus
children.top_down_role: Compression correction applied to network averaging states.

knowledge_statements.title: Average-Preservation Boundary for Compensated Consensus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Error compensation does not itself preserve the network average; the mixing matrix must preserve sums, and row stochasticity alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\gamma((W-I_n)\otimes I_d)h^{k+1}\) with \(\gamma\ne0\), the identity \((\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_d)x^{k+1}=(\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_d)x^k\) holds for every \(h^{k+1}\) if and only if \(\mathbf 1^\top W=\mathbf 1^\top\). Thus \(W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\) alone does not ensure preservation of the arithmetic average.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
\(\gamma\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_d)x^{k+1}=(\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_d)x^k\ \forall h^{k+1}\iff \mathbf 1^\top W=\mathbf 1^\top.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sum-conservation condition for consensus corrections driven by reconstructed messages.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Compensated Consensus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A memory-based compressed consensus step for a fixed mixing matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each agent initialize arbitrary states \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and shared reconstruction memories \(h_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) sends \(q_i^k=Q(x_i^k-h_i^k)\). Every recipient reconstructs \(\widehat x_i^k=h_i^k+q_i^k\), and the memory is updated by \(h_i^{k+1}=h_i^k+\beta q_i^k\), where \(0<\beta\leq1\). The consensus state update is \[x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k+\gamma\sum_{j=1}^n W_{ij}(\widehat x_j^k-\widehat x_i^k).\] The output after stopping is \((x_1^k,\ldots,x_n^k)\); the accumulated reconstruction memory compensates innovations omitted by compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents compress deviations from shared memories, update those memories, and mix reconstructed neighbor states; retained reconstruction discrepancies compensate information lost in earlier messages.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic.
\(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is a specified compressor.
\(\beta,\gamma\) are chosen so the resulting consensus iteration is stable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_i^k+Q(x_i^k-h_i^k)\) is the communicated reconstruction used in the consensus update.

notation.meaning: Shared reconstruction memory for agent i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the particular memory recursion, reconstruction protocol, and compensation interpretation require a source specific to this compressed-consensus variant.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\) agents hold \(x_i^t\in\mathbb R^d\). Let \(W=[w_{ij}]\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a mixing matrix respecting the communication graph. Each agent and its receivers maintain synchronized reconstructions \(h_i^t\in\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous consensus with compressed innovations and reconstructed neighbor states; optimization-gradient terms are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An error-compensated compressed-consensus step encodes each innovation \(x_i^t-h_i^t\) as \(q_i^t=C_i^t(x_i^t-h_i^t,\xi_i^t)\), updates the shared reconstruction by \(h_i^{t+1}=h_i^t+q_i^t\), and mixes reconstructed states according to \(x_i^{t+1}=x_i^t+\gamma\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}(h_j^{t+1}-h_i^{t+1})\), where \(\gamma>0\). The stored \(h_i^t\) compensates persistent compression error by making future messages innovations relative to the previously reconstructed state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Error-compensated consensus maintains a reconstructed copy of each agent state, communicates a compressed difference from that copy, updates all synchronized copies with the decoded innovation, and performs network averaging using the reconstructed states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_i^t=C_i^t(x_i^t-h_i^t,\xi_i^t),\quad h_i^{t+1}=h_i^t+q_i^t,\quad x_i^{t+1}=x_i^t+\gamma\sum_jw_{ij}(h_j^{t+1}-h_i^{t+1}).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: In stacked notation, \(H^{t+1}=H^t+Q^t\) and \(X^{t+1}=X^t+\gamma(W-I)H^{t+1}\), subject to the chosen row/column stacking convention.
special_cases_latex: If \(C_i^t\) is the identity, then \(h_i^{t+1}=x_i^t\) and the step reduces to ordinary linear consensus.
If \(x_i^t=h_i^t\), a zero-preserving compressor sends \(q_i^t=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Only innovations \(q_i^t\), rather than full states, need be communicated.
Synchronized initialization and identical decoded messages preserve consistent neighbor reconstructions.
boundary_notes: Average preservation depends on properties of \(W\) and is not part of this mechanism definition.
Packet loss, directed push-sum normalization, and gradient terms require modified recursions.
review_flags: No supplied source locator was verified to support this particular compensated-consensus recursion.
knowledge_statements.title: Innovation-Compensated Compressed Consensus

children.title: Compressed Gradient Tracking
children.top_down_role: Compression and correction of primal and tracking variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Incrementally Reconstructed Compressed Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents incrementally reconstruct compressed primal and tracker innovations and apply average-preserving corrections in both recursions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let W be doubly stochastic. Agents maintain X^k,Y^k and sender-receiver-consistent reconstructions \widehat X^k,\widehat Y^k. They transmit \[Q_x(X^k-\widehat X^k),\qquad Q_y(Y^k-\widehat Y^k),\] add these messages to the corresponding reconstructions, and update \[X^{k+1}=X^k+(W-I)\widehat X^{k+1}-\alpha Y^k,\] \[Y^{k+1}=Y^k+(W-I)\widehat Y^{k+1}+
abla F(X^{k+1})-
abla F(X^k),\] with Y^0=
abla F(X^0).
assumptions_latex: W is doubly stochastic and graph compatible.
Local objectives are differentiable.
Sender and receivers initialize and update each reconstruction consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration compresses both primal and gradient-tracker communication while retaining uncompressed local states.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compression of primal and tracker innovations with average-preserving corrections.

notation.meaning: reconstructed communicated primal and tracker states

review_flags: Abstract reconstruction template; no attribution to a specific named published method.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Compressed-Tracking Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero composite residual certifies primal consensus, aggregate stationarity, tracker consensus and mass consistency, and exact reconstruction of both communicated states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J=I_n-\frac1n\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), let \(X,Y\) be the stacked primal and tracker states, and let \(\widehat X,\widehat Y\) be their communicated reconstructions. Define
\[r_{\rm cmp}^2=\|JX\|_F^2+\left\|\frac1n\mathbf1^\top\nabla F(X)\right\|_2^2+\|JY\|_F^2+\left\|\mathbf1^\top\bigl(Y-\nabla F(X)\bigr)\right\|_2^2+\|X-\widehat X\|_F^2+\|Y-\widehat Y\|_F^2.\]
Then \(r_{\rm cmp}=0\) exactly certifies primal consensus, zero aggregate gradient, tracker consensus, the tracker-sum identity, and exact primal and tracker reconstruction. For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), primal consensus and the zero aggregate-gradient term certify stationarity of \(f\) at the common primal state.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
All stacked states and reconstructions are evaluated at the same logical iteration.
The aggregate objective is \(f=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\) for the stationarity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\rm cmp}=0\Longrightarrow X=\mathbf1x^\top,\quad \nabla f(x)=0,\quad JY=0,\quad \mathbf1^\top Y=\mathbf1^\top\nabla F(X),\quad X=\widehat X,\quad Y=\widehat Y.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori consistency and stationarity test for incrementally reconstructed compressed gradient tracking.

notation.meaning: Communicated reconstructions of primal and tracker states.

review_flags: Revised from the builder proposal to include the tracker-sum defect; tracker consensus alone does not certify consistency with the aggregate gradient.
Zero residual certifies the displayed terminal conditions but does not establish that a recursion reaches them.
Evaluating this global residual may require a separate aggregation operation.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Information Compression Destroys Consensus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressor transmitting no information can make the trackers vanish while agents converge to distinct local minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two scalar agents, let f_1(x)=\tfrac12(x-1)^2, f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x+1)^2, X^0=(0,0)^{\mathsf T}, Y^0=(-1,1)^{\mathsf T}, and let Q_x=Q_y\equiv0 with zero reconstructions. In the accepted incrementally reconstructed recursion, for 0<\alpha<2, Y^{k+1}=(1-\alpha)Y^k and X^k=\bigl(1-(1-\alpha)^k\bigr)(1,-1)^{\mathsf T}. Hence Y^k\to0 while X^k\to(1,-1)^{\mathsf T}.
assumptions_latex: The accepted incrementally reconstructed recursion is used.
Q_x=Q_y\equiv0.
0<\alpha<2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y^k\to0,\qquad X^k\to(1,-1)^{\mathsf T}\notin\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compressor-quality boundary for primal-and-tracker reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Tracker-Sum Invariant
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average-preserving correction keeps the sum of trackers equal to the sum of current local gradients despite compressed tracker messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the preceding recursion, \mathbf1^	op(W-I)=0 gives \[\mathbf1^	op Y^{k+1}=\mathbf1^	op Y^k+\mathbf1^	op(
abla F(X^{k+1})-
abla F(X^k)).\] If \mathbf1^	op Y^0=\mathbf1^	op
abla F(X^0), then \[\mathbf1^	op Y^k=\mathbf1^	op
abla F(X^k)\quad	ext{for every }k.\]
assumptions_latex: The preceding tracker recursion is used.
\(\mathbf1^\top W=\mathbf1^\top\).
The tracker is initialized with the correct aggregate gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf1^\top Y^k=\mathbf1^\top\nabla F(X^k)\) for all k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact aggregate tracking despite reconstruction error in tracker messages.

knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error-feedback compression applied separately to primal and gradient-tracking messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For differentiable local objectives \(f_i:\mathbb R^d	o\mathbb R\), initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\), \(y_i^0=
abla f_i(x_i^0)\), and residuals \(e_{x,i}^0=e_{y,i}^0=0\). At iteration \(k\), form \(\widetilde x_i^k=Q(x_i^k+e_{x,i}^k)\), \(\widetilde y_i^k=Q(y_i^k+e_{y,i}^k)\), and set \(e_{x,i}^{k+1}=x_i^k+e_{x,i}^k-\widetilde x_i^k\), \(e_{y,i}^{k+1}=y_i^k+e_{y,i}^k-\widetilde y_i^k\). Then update \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jW_{ij}\widetilde x_j^k-\alpha_k y_i^k,\qquad y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jW_{ij}\widetilde y_j^k+
abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x_i^k).\] Return the terminal primal states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent error-feedback-compresses both its primal and tracking messages, mixes received reconstructions, and corrects the tracker by its local gradient change.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is a prescribed mixing matrix compatible with the communication graph.
\(Q\) and \((\alpha_k)\) are chosen so the compressed recursion is well defined.
\(f_i\) is differentiable for every agent \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual recursions retain both primal and tracking information discarded by compression.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but this exact joint primal/tracker error-feedback recursion is specialized and cannot be validated without a supporting source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\) agents minimize \(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x)\), with differentiable \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\). Let \(W=[w_{ij}]\) be a mixing matrix. Agent \(i\) stores a primal state \(x_i^t\), tracker \(y_i^t\), and synchronized reconstructions \(h_{x,i}^t,h_{y,i}^t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous decentralized gradient tracking with compressed primal and tracker innovations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compressed gradient-tracking method communicates \(q_{x,i}^t=C_{x,i}^t(x_i^t-h_{x,i}^t)\) and \(q_{y,i}^t=C_{y,i}^t(y_i^t-h_{y,i}^t)\), then sets \(h_{x,i}^{t+1}=h_{x,i}^t+q_{x,i}^t\) and \(h_{y,i}^{t+1}=h_{y,i}^t+q_{y,i}^t\). A canonical decoded-state recursion is \(x_i^{t+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}h_{x,j}^{t+1}-\alpha y_i^t\) and \(y_i^{t+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}h_{y,j}^{t+1}+\nabla f_i(x_i^{t+1})-\nabla f_i(x_i^t)\), with \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compressed gradient tracking maintains primal and gradient-tracker variables, compresses innovations of both relative to synchronized reconstructions, mixes the decoded primal and tracker states, and adds the local gradient difference to the tracker update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{x,i}^t=C_{x,i}^t(x_i^t-h_{x,i}^t),\ q_{y,i}^t=C_{y,i}^t(y_i^t-h_{y,i}^t),\ x_i^{t+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}h_{x,j}^{t+1}-\alpha y_i^t,\ y_i^{t+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}h_{y,j}^{t+1}+\nabla f_i(x_i^{t+1})-\nabla f_i(x_i^t).\)
special_cases_latex: Identity compressors with reconstructions equal to current states recover an uncompressed gradient-tracking recursion.
Compressing only \(x_i^t\) is obtained by taking \(C_{y,i}^t\) to be the identity.
immediate_consequences_latex: Both communicated streams are innovations rather than necessarily dense full states.
When \(W\) is doubly stochastic and trackers are initialized by local gradients, the uncompressed tracker recursion has the standard aggregate-gradient accounting relation.
boundary_notes: The displayed equations define a representative family; exact mixing order varies across compressed gradient-tracking algorithms.
Convergence requires graph, smoothness, compressor, initialization, and stepsize conditions not asserted here.

notation.meaning: shared decoded primal and tracker references

children.title: Communication-Frequency Reduction Methods
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms reducing how often network information is exchanged.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(t\in\mathbb N_0\) index local computation steps on a graph \(G=(V,E)\). For each directed edge \((i,j)\), let \(a_{ij}^t\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether a message is sent at step \(t\), and let \(\widehat z_{i\to j}^t\) be the receiver's stored value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time mechanisms that omit some network exchanges while retaining local computation or stored neighbor information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed iteration uses communication-frequency reduction when its communication schedule \(A_t=\{(i,j)\in E:a_{ij}^t=1\}\) is a proper subset of \(E\) for at least some computation steps and every inactive edge uses a specified no-message rule. Canonically, \(\widehat z_{i\to j}^{t+1}=z_i^t\) when \(a_{ij}^t=1\), while \(\widehat z_{i\to j}^{t+1}=\widehat z_{i\to j}^t\) when \(a_{ij}^t=0\). Its frequency through horizon \(T\) is \(F_T=(T|E|)^{-1}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}|A_t|\); reduction relative to all-edge communication means \(F_T<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication-frequency reduction specifies which edges transmit at each computation step and what receivers use when no message arrives. Under zero-order holding, receivers retain the last transmitted state. The normalized number of active edge-rounds is below that of communicating on every edge at every step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_t\subseteq E,\quad \widehat z_{i\to j}^{t+1}=a_{ij}^tz_i^t+(1-a_{ij}^t)\widehat z_{i\to j}^t,\quad F_T=\frac{1}{T|E|}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}|A_t|<1.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The number of suppressed edge transmissions through \(T\) is \(T|E|(1-F_T)\).
special_cases_latex: Periodic communication uses \(A_t=E\) only when \(t\) is a multiple of a fixed period.
Event-triggered communication chooses \(A_t\) from locally observed state discrepancies.
immediate_consequences_latex: When \(A_t=\varnothing\), the step performs no network transmission and all receiver caches are held fixed.
When \(A_t=E\) for every \(t\), \(F_T=1\) and there is no frequency reduction.
boundary_notes: Smaller messages at every round constitute compression, not frequency reduction, unless some transmissions are also omitted.
A low value of \(F_T\) alone gives no convergence or wall-clock guarantee.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a consensus matrix with \(P\mathbf1=\mathbf1\). At outer optimization epoch \(k\), stack agent inputs as \(Z^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) and choose an inner communication count \(s_k\in\mathbb N_0\). Let \(J=n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested distributed schemes whose amount of consensus work or target consensus tolerance varies by outer epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable-accuracy consensus family replaces exact averaging \(JZ^k\) by \(\widetilde Z^k=P^{s_k}Z^k\), where the schedule \((s_k)\) is not required to be constant. Its achieved consensus error is \(E_k=\|(P^{s_k}-J)Z^k\|\). Equivalently, the inner solver may be specified by tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\) and stopped at an \(s_k\) satisfying \(E_k\le\varepsilon_k\). The sequence \((s_k)\) or \((\varepsilon_k)\) is part of the algorithm definition and controls communication accuracy across optimization epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-accuracy consensus performs a nonconstant number of mixing rounds at each outer optimization epoch, or equivalently enforces an epoch-dependent consensus tolerance. The approximate average is \(P^{s_k}Z^k\), and its deviation from exact averaging is explicitly controlled by \(s_k\) or \(\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde Z^k=P^{s_k}Z^k,\qquad E_k=\|(P^{s_k}-J)Z^k\|\le\varepsilon_k,\qquad s_k\text{ may vary with }k.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: An iteration-count schedule \((s_k)\) and a tolerance schedule \((\varepsilon_k)\) are interchangeable whenever a known mixing bound maps \(s_k\) to an upper bound on \(E_k\).
special_cases_latex: Constant \(s_k=s\) gives fixed-accuracy multi-consensus.
Increasing \(s_k\) can produce decreasing tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The communication cost through epoch \(K\) is proportional to \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}s_k\) synchronous mixing rounds.
Taking \(s_k=0\) yields \(\widetilde Z^k=Z^k\), meaning no inner communication at epoch \(k\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe how fast \(\varepsilon_k\) must decrease.
Time-varying or directed networks require products of mixing matrices rather than a single power \(P^{s_k}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated symmetric mixing preserves the average and raises each disagreement eigenvalue to the number of rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) be doubly stochastic with eigenpairs \((\lambda_i,u_i)\), \(\lambda_1=1\), and \(u_1=\mathbf1/\sqrt n\). If \(Z=JZ+\sum_{i=2}^n u_i a_i^{\mathsf T}\), then \[W^sZ=JZ+\sum_{i=2}^n\lambda_i^s u_i a_i^{\mathsf T},\qquad \|(I-J)W^s\|_2=\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i|^s.\] Repetition converges to exact averaging exactly when \(\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i|<1\).
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) is doubly stochastic.
The consensus eigenvector is \(\mathbf1/\sqrt n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Round Consensus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer optimization step is preceded by a chosen number of repeated neighbor-averaging rounds, yielding the effective mixing operator W raised to that number.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a mixing matrix, let \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\), and let \(Z^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) stack the agents' vectors at outer iteration \(k\). Choose an integer \(s_k\geq1\), initialize \(Z^{k,0}=Z^k\), and compute \(Z^{k,\ell+1}=WZ^{k,\ell}\) for \(\ell=0,\ldots,s_k-1\). Supply \(\widetilde Z^k=Z^{k,s_k}=W^{s_k}Z^k\) to the prescribed outer optimization update. Stop when the outer method's criterion is met; the communication cost through iteration \(K\) is \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}s_k\) mixing rounds.
assumptions_latex: \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}W=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\).
In the specified matrix norm, there is a \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \(\|(I-J)WZ\|\leq\rho\|(I-J)Z\|\) for every \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\).
Each integer \(s_k\geq1\) is selected before its inner loop.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde Z^k=W^{s_k}Z^k\) and \(\|(I-J)\widetilde Z^k\|\leq\rho^{s_k}\|(I-J)Z^k\|\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bias–Disagreement Decomposition of Inexact Consensus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact-consensus error consists of average drift plus residual disagreement; disagreement alone is insufficient when the operation changes the average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\), \[\widetilde Z-JZ=J(\widetilde Z-Z)+(I-J)\widetilde Z.\] Under the Frobenius norm these terms are orthogonal, so \[\|\widetilde Z-JZ\|_F^2=\|J(\widetilde Z-Z)\|_F^2+\|(I-J)\widetilde Z\|_F^2.\]
assumptions_latex: \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\).
The squared identity uses the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde Z-JZ\|_F^2=\|J(\widetilde Z-Z)\|_F^2+\|(I-J)\widetilde Z\|_F^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal decomposition distinguishing average drift from residual disagreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Consensus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact consensus returns states within a prescribed tolerance of exact averaging, optionally with exact preservation of the original network average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stacked states \(Z^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\), define the exact averaging projector \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\). A consensus output \(\widetilde Z^k\) is \(\varepsilon_k\)-inexact, in a specified matrix norm, when \(J\widetilde Z^k=JZ^k\) and \(\|(I-J)\widetilde Z^k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\). More generally, if the inner operation need not preserve the average, require \(\|\widetilde Z^k-JZ^k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\). The nonnegative sequence \((\varepsilon_k)\) is part of the outer algorithm's accuracy specification.
assumptions_latex: All agent states have the same dimension \(d\).
A matrix norm and nonnegative tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inner consensus error at outer iteration \(k\) is bounded by \(\varepsilon_k\) under the selected formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite inner communication is modeled by a bounded deviation from exact network averaging.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Budgets for Standard Accuracy Schedules
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric mixing costs linear cumulative rounds for fixed accuracy, order K log K for polynomial tightening, and order K squared for geometric tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(D_k\le D\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and choose the smallest \(s_k\ge0\) satisfying \(\rho^{s_k}D\le\varepsilon_k\). A fixed positive tolerance gives \(S_K=O(K)\). If \(\varepsilon_k=c(k+1)^{-p}\), with \(c,p>0\), then \(s_k=O(\log(k+1))\) and \(S_K=O(K\log K)\). If \(\varepsilon_k=cq^k\), with \(q\in(0,1)\), then \(s_k=O(k)\) and \(S_K=O(K^2)\).
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\le D<\infty\).
One-round disagreement contracts by \(\rho\in(0,1)\).
Budgets use the accepted seed's minimal geometric-contraction rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_K=O(K)\), \(O(K\log K)\), or \(O(K^2)\) for fixed, polynomial, or geometric tolerance schedules, respectively.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication cost induced by standard tolerance schedules under geometric mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Consensus Budgeting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose enough inner mixing rounds that geometric disagreement contraction reaches the required tolerance; total communication is the sum of these round budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one mixing round contracts disagreement by \(\rho\in(0,1)\): \(\|(I-J)WZ\|\leq\rho\|(I-J)Z\|\). If the pre-consensus disagreement at outer iteration \(k\) is bounded by \(D_k\), then any integer \(s_k\) satisfying \(\rho^{s_k}D_k\leq\varepsilon_k\) guarantees the requested consensus accuracy. For \(D_k>\varepsilon_k>0\), the smallest sufficient budget is \(s_k=\left\lceil\log(D_k/\varepsilon_k)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil\); take \(s_k=0\) when \(D_k\leq\varepsilon_k\). The cumulative communication budget through \(K\) outer iterations is \(S_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}s_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\) and \(WJ=JW=J\).
A uniform contraction factor \(\rho\in(0,1)\) is known.
Bounds \(D_k\geq0\) and targets \(\varepsilon_k>0\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|(I-J)W^{s_k}Z^k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\) and \(S_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}s_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus rounds are selected to meet prescribed outer-iteration error tolerances.

notation.meaning: bound on disagreement before inner consensus

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial and Geometric Accuracy Schedules
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial tolerances vanish for positive exponents but are summable only above exponent one; geometric tolerances are summable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c>0\), \(\varepsilon_k=c(k+1)^{-p}\) vanishes exactly when \(p>0\) and is summable exactly when \(p>1\). For \(q\in(0,1)\), \(\varepsilon_k=cq^k\) is summable and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k=c/(1-q)\).
assumptions_latex: For the geometric schedule, \(q\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k c(k+1)^{-p}<\infty\iff p>1\), while \(\sum_k cq^k=c/(1-q)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical schedules separating vanishing, summable, and nonsummable consensus-error regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus-Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three error schedules distinguished by their asymptotic accumulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\varepsilon_k)_{k\geq0}\) bound the consensus error injected at outer iterations. The fixed-accuracy regime has \(\sup_k\varepsilon_k\leq\bar\varepsilon\) for some \(\bar\varepsilon>0\) and generally permits a persistent error floor. The vanishing regime has \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), eliminating persistent pointwise consensus error but not necessarily its cumulative effect. The summable regime has \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), hence is vanishing and has finite cumulative consensus error. These implications concern the error schedule alone; convergence of a surrounding optimization method requires its own stability hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed tolerances can leave an error floor; vanishing tolerances remove pointwise error; summable tolerances additionally bound cumulative error and always vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\Rightarrow\varepsilon_k\to0\), while bounded fixed accuracy does not imply vanishing error.

notation.meaning: Consensus-error bound at outer iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Event-Triggered Communication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent communicates only when its current state differs sufficiently from its last transmitted state; otherwise neighbors reuse the stored value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Agent \(i\) stores its last transmitted state \(\hat x_i^k\) and observes \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\). Given thresholds \(\tau_i^k\geq0\), define \(a_i^k=1\) if \(\|x_i^k-\hat x_i^k\|>\tau_i^k\), and \(a_i^k=0\) otherwise. If \(a_i^k=1\), transmit \(x_i^k\) and set \(\hat x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\); otherwise transmit nothing and set \(\hat x_i^{k+1}=\hat x_i^k\). The prescribed distributed update uses neighbors' stored values \(\hat x_j^{k+1}\). Stop under the optimization criterion and output the terminal local states.
assumptions_latex: Each agent can evaluate its local innovation norm.
Neighbors retain the most recently received state.
The threshold schedule \((\tau_i^k)\) is prescribed or locally computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When communication is suppressed, \(\|x_i^k-\hat x_i^k\|\leq\tau_i^k\), so the induced stale-state error is locally bounded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agents transmit only when a locally measurable innovation exceeds a scheduled threshold.

notation.meaning: last transmitted state of agent i

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At step \(t\), agent \(i\) holds \(z_i^t\in\mathbb R^d\) and the last value it transmitted, \(\widehat z_i^t\). Let \(\phi_i^t\) be a locally computable trigger function and let \(\tau_i^t\ge0\) be a threshold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time communication decisions based only on locally available state, memory, time, and prescribed thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Communication by agent \(i\) is event-triggered when its transmission indicator is \(a_i^t=\mathbf1_{\{\phi_i^t(z_i^t,\widehat z_i^t,\mathcal I_i^t)\ge\tau_i^t\}}\), where \(\mathcal I_i^t\) contains only information available locally before the decision. If \(a_i^t=1\), the agent sends a message representing \(z_i^t\) and sets \(\widehat z_i^{t+1}=z_i^t\); otherwise it sends nothing and sets \(\widehat z_i^{t+1}=\widehat z_i^t\). A canonical discrepancy trigger uses \(\phi_i^t=\|z_i^t-\widehat z_i^t\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Event-triggered communication sends only when a locally observable trigger reaches a threshold. With the standard discrepancy trigger, an agent compares its current state with its last transmitted state; if the test fails, it sends nothing and keeps the old transmitted-state cache.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i^t=\mathbf1_{\{\phi_i^t\ge\tau_i^t\}},\qquad \widehat z_i^{t+1}=a_i^tz_i^t+(1-a_i^t)\widehat z_i^t.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The transmission times are the stopping indices \(\mathcal T_i=\{t\in\mathbb N_0:\phi_i^t\ge\tau_i^t\}\).
special_cases_latex: A state-difference trigger transmits when \(\|z_i^t-\widehat z_i^t\|\ge\tau_i^t\).
A relative trigger uses \(\|z_i^t-\widehat z_i^t\|\ge c_i^t\|z_i^t\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: No communication occurs at steps outside \(\mathcal T_i\).
A zero threshold with a nonnegative trigger generally recovers always-active communication, subject to the chosen strict or non-strict inequality.
boundary_notes: Continuous-time triggers require a separate definition and may require a non-Zeno condition.
A trigger depending on unavailable global information is not locally event-triggered under this definition.

children.title: Redundancy-Suppressed Communication Family
children.top_down_role: Suppression of exchanges judged redundant or low impact.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a directed link \((i,j)\), let \(m_{ij}^t\in\mathcal M\) be the candidate message, let \(r_{ij}^t\in\mathcal M\) be the receiver-reconstructible surrogate known consistently at both endpoints, and let \(d_{ij}:\mathcal M\times\mathcal M\to[0,\infty)\) be an impact measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message suppression based on predicted receiver knowledge or bounded incremental impact, distinct from merely quantizing every message.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A redundancy-suppressed communication rule chooses \(a_{ij}^t=\mathbf1_{\{d_{ij}(m_{ij}^t,r_{ij}^t)>\eta_{ij}^t\}}\) for a threshold \(\eta_{ij}^t\ge0\). If \(a_{ij}^t=1\), message \(m_{ij}^t\) is sent and the receiver uses it; if \(a_{ij}^t=0\), no payload is sent and the receiver substitutes the reproducible surrogate \(r_{ij}^t\). The suppressed candidate is declared redundant precisely because replacing it by \(r_{ij}^t\) has measured impact at most \(\eta_{ij}^t\). Both endpoints update any predictor state by an agreed rule so future surrogates remain reproducible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundancy-suppressed communication predicts what the receiver can already reconstruct and sends a candidate message only when its difference or estimated impact exceeds a threshold. Otherwise the receiver uses the shared surrogate without receiving a payload.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_{ij}^t=\mathbf1_{\{d_{ij}(m_{ij}^t,r_{ij}^t)>\eta_{ij}^t\}},\qquad \widetilde m_{ij}^t=a_{ij}^tm_{ij}^t+(1-a_{ij}^t)r_{ij}^t.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Suppression occurs exactly on \(\{t:d_{ij}(m_{ij}^t,r_{ij}^t)\le\eta_{ij}^t\}\).
special_cases_latex: Duplicate suppression takes \(d_{ij}(m,r)=\mathbf1_{\{m\ne r\}}\) and omits messages identical to the receiver cache.
A predictive rule uses \(r_{ij}^t\) generated from a shared state model and suppresses sufficiently small innovations.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every suppressed message incurs surrogate discrepancy at most \(\eta_{ij}^t\) in the chosen impact measure.
With \(\eta_{ij}^t=0\), only exactly or metrically indistinguishable messages are suppressed when \(d_{ij}\) is a metric.
boundary_notes: The impact measure must be specified; different choices define different redundancy notions.
If the receiver cannot reproduce \(r_{ij}^t\), suppression requires an additional synchronization protocol.
This mechanism does not itself bound accumulated algorithmic error or guarantee convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worker skips transmission when its new message is close to its cached message, and the algorithm reuses the cached value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Worker \(i\) computes a candidate message \(m_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) and retains its last transmitted message \(\hat m_i^{k-1}\). Given a nonnegative threshold \(\tau_i^k\), transmit and set \(\hat m_i^k=m_i^k\) when \(\|m_i^k-\hat m_i^{k-1}\|>\tau_i^k\); otherwise set \(\hat m_i^k=\hat m_i^{k-1}\) without communication. The coordinator or neighbors execute the prescribed optimization update using \(\hat m_i^k\) in place of \(m_i^k\). Terminate under the outer stopping rule and output the resulting iterate.

Recipients cache the last transmitted message.
Thresholds \(\tau_i^k\geq0\) are prescribed.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Gap Scheduled-Mixing Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximum communication gap of B slows the iteration-indexed contraction exponent by at most B; the active-round requirement is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every block of B\ge1 consecutive iterations contains an active round, then C_K\ge\lfloor K/B\rfloor and \[\|JZ^K\|_F\le\rho^{\lfloor K/B\rfloor}\|JZ^0\|_F.\] For 0<\varepsilon<\|JZ^0\|_F, it suffices that \[K\ge B\left\lceil\frac{\log(\|JZ^0\|_F/\varepsilon)}{-\log\rho}\right\rceil.\]
assumptions_latex: Every B-iteration window contains an active round.
The active-round mixing-product assumptions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|JZ^K\|_F\le\rho^{\lfloor K/B\rfloor}\|JZ^0\|_F\).
