knowledge_statements.title: Permanent-Skipping Consensus Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every communication round is skipped and local computation does not couple agents, unequal initial states remain unequal forever.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two agents with scalar state \(z^k=(z_1^k,z_2^k)\), identity local computation, and communication indicator \(a_k\). If skipped rounds apply identity mixing, \(a_k=0\) for every \(k\), and \(z_1^0\neq z_2^0\), then \(z^{k+1}=z^k\) for every \(k\). Hence the initial disagreement persists and consensus is never attained.
assumptions_latex: Skipped rounds apply identity mixing.
\(a_k=0\) for every \(k\).
Local computation is the identity map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_1^k-z_2^k=z_1^0-z_2^0\neq0\quad\text{for all }k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when a scheduled communication process suppresses every round.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Round Mixing Product
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed mixing, identity skips disappear from the product, so disagreement contracts according to the number of active rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let J=I-\frac1n\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top, let W be doubly stochastic with \|JW\|_2\le\rho<1, and set W_k=a_kW+(1-a_k)I for a_k\in\{0,1\}. For Z^{k+1}=W_kZ^k and C_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}a_k, \[Z^K=W^{C_K}Z^0,\qquad \|JZ^K\|_F\le\rho^{C_K}\|JZ^0\|_F.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Skipped-Round Communication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A masked communication schedule with cache reuse during inactive rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix binary activation indicators \(a_i^k\in\{0,1\}\). Agent \(i\) initializes a message cache \(z_i^0=m_i^0\). At round \(k\), it computes \(m_i^k\); if \(a_i^k=1\), it broadcasts and sets \(z_i^{k+1}=m_i^k\), while if \(a_i^k=0\), it skips communication and sets \(z_i^{k+1}=z_i^k\). The distributed optimization update uses the newest available caches. A bounded-gap schedule satisfies \(\sum_{t=k}^{k+B-1}a_i^t\geq1\) for every \(i,k\), ensuring that no agent skips more than \(B-1\) consecutive rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary schedule suppresses selected communication rounds while cached messages remain active; a bounded-gap rule prevents indefinitely silent agents.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i^k\in\{0,1\}\) is known to agent \(i\) at round \(k\).
\(B\geq1\) is an integer when bounded communication gaps are required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i^k=0\Rightarrow z_i^{k+1}=z_i^k\), and the bounded-gap condition guarantees at least one transmission per \(B\) rounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two agents with stacked scalar state \(z^k=(z_1^k,z_2^k)\), averaging matrix \(W=\tfrac12\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), and identity local computation. If the communication indicators satisfy \(a_k=0\) for every \(k\) and \(z_1^0\neq z_2^0\), then the effective mixing operator is always \(I\), so \(z^k=z^0\) and consensus is never attained. More generally, finitely many active rounds cannot guarantee consensus for every nonexact finite-round mixing operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If communication is skipped forever, unequal agents remain unequal; finite communication is generally insufficient for exact consensus.
assumptions_latex: Skipped rounds apply identity mixing.
Local computation is the identity map.
The initial agent states disagree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_1^k-z_2^k=z_1^0-z_2^0\neq0\) for all \(k\) when \(a_k\equiv0\).

notation.meaning: indicator that communication occurs at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disagreement contraction under identity operators on skipped rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J=I-\frac1n\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), let \(W\) be doubly stochastic with \(\|JW\|_2\le\rho<1\), and set \(W_k=a_kW+(1-a_k)I\), where \(a_k\in\{0,1\}\). For the communication-only recursion \(Z^{k+1}=W_kZ^k\) and \(C_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}a_k\), \[Z^K=\left(\prod_{k=0}^{K-1}W_k\right)Z^0=W^{C_K}Z^0,\qquad \|JZ^K\|_F\le\rho^{C_K}\|JZ^0\|_F.\] Thus skipped rounds neither contract nor enlarge disagreement; contraction is determined by the number of active rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed mixing matrix, identity skips disappear from the ordered product, so disagreement contracts according to the number of active communication rounds.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(\|JW\|_2\le\rho<1\).
\(a_k\in\{0,1\}\) and skipped rounds use \(I\).
The displayed recursion contains no intervening local perturbation.

notation.meaning: number of active rounds before K

Lipschitz Downstream-Impact Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid Lipschitz sensitivity bound converts the tested message-substitution error into a certified per-event downstream-impact bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the recipient uses \(H_i^k\) satisfying \[\|H_i^k(u)-H_i^k(v)\|\le L_i^k\|u-v\|\] on the relevant region. If transmission is suppressed only when \(\|m_i^k-q_i^k\|\le\tau_i^k\), then \[\|H_i^k(m_i^k)-H_i^k(q_i^k)\|\le L_i^k\tau_i^k.\]
assumptions_latex: The displayed Lipschitz inequality holds on the relevant message region.
Recipients use the same substitute \(q_i^k\) appearing in the test.
The test and sensitivity bound use compatible norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|H_i^k(m_i^k)-H_i^k(q_i^k)\|\le L_i^k\tau_i^k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a message-substitution threshold into a per-event bound on the omitted update contribution.
review_flags: This is a per-event certificate; accumulation belongs to the Suppression-Error Accumulation sibling.

knowledge_statements.title: Small Local Novelty Can Have Large Downstream Impact
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A message can appear locally redundant yet have arbitrarily large downstream effect when the recipient amplifies small differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar messages let \(H_c(m)=cm\). Given any novelty threshold \(\tau>0\) and desired impact \(M>0\), choose \(m-q=\tau/2\) and \(c>2M/\tau\). Then \[|m-q|\le\tau\quad\text{but}\quad|H_c(m)-H_c(q)|>M.\] Hence an unscaled message-difference score cannot uniformly control downstream error when sensitivity is unbounded.
assumptions_latex: No uniform upper bound on downstream sensitivity is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |m-q|\le\tau\not\Rightarrow|H(m)-H(q)|\le M\text{ uniformly over }H.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calibration failure when message-space novelty is not matched to downstream sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Score and Suppression Action
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A redundancy rule suppresses a message when a local score is below threshold and uses the explicitly declared cached or predicted substitute.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_i^k\) be a candidate message and \(q_i^k\) the value that recipients can use without receiving it, such as a cached message or a jointly reconstructible prediction. Let \(R_i^k=R(m_i^k,q_i^k,\zeta_i^k)\ge0\) be a locally computable redundancy score. For \(\tau_i^k\ge0\), suppress transmission exactly when \(R_i^k\le\tau_i^k\); on suppression, recipients substitute \(q_i^k\) for \(m_i^k\).
assumptions_latex: The sender can compute the score from locally available information.
Recipients possess or can reconstruct the declared substitute \(q_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_i^k\le\tau_i^k\Longrightarrow m_i^k\text{ is not sent and recipients use }q_i^k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic local definition tying a redundancy score to the exact substitute used when communication is omitted.

notation.meaning: receiver-available substitute for the omitted message
local side information used by the score

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Redundancy-Score Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundancy may be measured against a cached message, a shared prediction, or the induced downstream contribution, provided the tested value is the value actually substituted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate message \(m_i^k\), cached value \(\widehat m_i\), receiver-reconstructible prediction \(\widetilde m_i^k\), and downstream contribution map \(H_i^k\), canonical choices are \[R_{\rm cache}=\|m_i^k-\widehat m_i\|,\qquad R_{\rm pred}=\|m_i^k-\widetilde m_i^k\|,\qquad R_{\rm imp}(q)=\|H_i^k(m_i^k)-H_i^k(q)\|.\] The first authorizes substitution by \(\widehat m_i\), the second by \(\widetilde m_i^k\), and the third directly scores the effect of its declared substitute \(q\). Their thresholds are not interchangeable without comparison bounds.
assumptions_latex: The prediction variant requires sender and receiver to reconstruct the same \(\widetilde m_i^k\).
The impact variant requires the relevant downstream map to be evaluable or soundly bounded.
Each score is paired with the substitute appearing in that score.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{\rm cache},R_{\rm pred},R_{\rm imp}\text{ control distinct substitution quantities}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message-novelty, prediction-error, and downstream-impact scores using the actual suppression substitute.

notation.meaning: shared prediction of the current message

review_flags: A prediction-error score is unsound for cached-message reuse unless the cache and prediction are linked by an additional bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy-Based Suppression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Suppression determined by the innovation relative to a reconstructible cached message.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_i^k\) be agent \(i\)'s current message and let \(z_i^k\) be a cached message already available to every intended recipient. For a threshold \(\tau_i^k\geq0\), the message is declared redundant and suppressed exactly when \[\lVert m_i^k-z_i^k\rVert\leq\tau_i^k.\] Recipients then use \(z_i^k\), producing a substitution error \(r_i^k=m_i^k-z_i^k\) satisfying \(\lVert r_i^k\rVert\leq\tau_i^k\). If the inequality fails, the current message is transmitted and becomes the new common cache.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A message is suppressed when it is close enough to a recipient-reconstructible cache, with the suppression threshold directly bounding the substitution error.
assumptions_latex: \(m_i^k,z_i^k\) lie in a common normed vector space.
\(z_i^k\) is available to every intended recipient.
\(\tau_i^k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Suppression certifies \(\lVert m_i^k-z_i^k\rVert\leq\tau_i^k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but the threshold criterion and common-cache protocol are a particular redundancy-suppression model requiring source support.

knowledge_statements.title: Skipped-Innovation Accumulation Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stale-message error is the sum of innovations since the last transmission, so bounded refresh age or bounded skipped-interval variation controls accumulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t(k)\le k\) be the last transmission time and \(\hat m^k=m^{t(k)}\). Then \[m^k-\hat m^k=\sum_{j=t(k)+1}^{k}(m^j-m^{j-1}),\qquad \|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le\sum_{j=t(k)+1}^{k}\|m^j-m^{j-1}\|.\] If \(k-t(k)\le H\) and every one-step innovation is at most \(\delta\), then \(\|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le H\delta\).
assumptions_latex: \(m^k\) lies in a normed vector space.
\(\hat m^k=m^{t(k)}\), where \(t(k)\) is the last transmission time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le\sum_{j=t(k)+1}^{k}\|m^j-m^{j-1}\|\); bounded age and increments imply \(\|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le H\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact accounting of staleness accumulated since the last transmitted message.

notation.meaning: last transmission time by iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Suppression-Error Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic perturbation boundary for communication-suppressed distributed iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the communicated state satisfy \(x^{k+1}=T_k(x^k)+e^k\), and let the unsuppressed reference satisfy \(y^{k+1}=T_k(y^k)\) with \(x^0=y^0\). If every \(T_k\) is nonexpansive, then \(\|x^K-y^K\|\leq\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|e^k\|\). Thus summable suppression errors give uniformly bounded accumulated deviation. Without cancellation or contraction, a persistent error need not vanish: for \(T_k(z)=z\) and \(e^k=e\neq0\), one has \(x^K-y^K=Ke\), so suppression error grows linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonexpansive iterations accumulate suppression errors by at most their norm sum; a constant uncancelled error can instead produce deviation growing linearly with the number of rounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x^K-y^K\|\leq\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|e^k\|\), while constant nonzero errors can yield \(\|x^K-y^K\|=K\|e\|\).

notation.meaning: round-k perturbation caused by suppressed communication

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Communication Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method converts a progress-dependent accuracy target into the minimum geometric-mixing budget needed at each optimization iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), select a target communication error \(\varepsilon_k>0\) from locally or globally available progress information. Given a disagreement bound \(D_k\) and mixing contraction \(\rho\in(0,1)\), choose \(s_k=\max\{0,\lceil\log(D_k/\varepsilon_k)/\log(1/\rho)\rceil\}\), interpreting the logarithmic term as zero when \(D_k\leq\varepsilon_k\). Apply \(s_k\) consensus rounds, producing \(\widetilde Z^k=W^{s_k}Z^k\), and then execute the prescribed optimization update. Stop under the outer criterion and report both the terminal iterate and cumulative communication \(\sum_{t< K}s_t\).
assumptions_latex: One mixing round contracts disagreement by a known \(\rho\in(0,1)\).
A valid bound \(D_k\) on current disagreement is available.
The target sequence \((\varepsilon_k)\) is generated by a prescribed adaptation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected budget guarantees \(\|(I-J)\widetilde Z^k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\) whenever \(\|(I-J)Z^k\|\leq D_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication effort increases or decreases according to an outer-iteration accuracy target.
review_flags: The mixing basis is provisionally sourced, but a dedicated source is needed for the adaptive target-selection rule.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The mixing-budget formula is valid under the stated contraction assumptions, but the adaptive target-selection rule—the defining content of this leaf—is left unspecified. The cited mixing-matrix section does not by itself support a progress-dependent adaptation mechanism.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let agents communicate vectors in \(\mathbb R^d\) at optimization iterations \(k\in\mathbb N\). Let \(Q_k:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be the possibly randomized encoder-decoder map used at iteration \(k\), and let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain the history before that communication.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional distributed optimization with iteration-dependent lossy communication; the definition covers deterministic or conditionally randomized errors but does not assert convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive communication-accuracy schedule is a sequence \((Q_k,\varepsilon_k)_{k\ge0}\) with \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), where \(Q_k\) may be selected using \(\mathcal F_k\), such that every transmitted \(v_k\in\mathbb R^d\) satisfies a prescribed conditional error criterion, for example \(\mathbb E[\|Q_k(v_k)-v_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le \varepsilon_k^2\). The schedule is vanishing if \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), summably accurate if \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), and relatively accurate if there are \(\omega_k\ge0\) such that \(\mathbb E[\|Q_k(v)-v\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\omega_k\|v\|^2\) for all admissible \(v\). Adaptivity means that the accuracy parameter or coding rule is chosen from the available history rather than fixed uniformly over all iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive communication accuracy is an iteration-indexed, history-measurable choice of coding rule and error tolerance. Every communicated vector must obey the stated conditional error bound. Accuracy is vanishing when the absolute tolerances tend to zero, summably accurate when they are summable, and relatively accurate when error is bounded by an iteration-dependent multiple of the input norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\|Q_k(v_k)-v_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\varepsilon_k^2\), with \((Q_k,\varepsilon_k)\) selectable from \(\mathcal F_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For deterministic communication, the conditional criterion reduces to \(\|Q_k(v_k)-v_k\|\le\varepsilon_k\).
special_cases_latex: A fixed-accuracy compressor has \(Q_k=Q\) and \(\varepsilon_k=\varepsilon\) for every \(k\).
A progressively refined quantizer is represented by \(\varepsilon_{k+1}\le\varepsilon_k\) and \(\varepsilon_k\to0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\), then the sequence of absolute communication-error budgets is summable.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe how rapidly accuracy must increase or establish that any optimization method converges.
Bit rate and error tolerance are different objects unless an explicit rate-distortion relation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the agents. A global event counter \(k\in\mathbb N\) is used only for analysis. Let \(A(k)\subseteq V\) be the agents updating at event \(k\), and let \(\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\) be the timestamp of agent \(j\)'s value used by agent \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract execution semantics for computation and message use, independent of a particular optimization update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A synchronization model is a class \(\mathfrak S\) of admissible schedules \(s=((A(k)),(\tau_{ij}(k)))_{k\ge0}\) satisfying declared timing, activation, and information-age constraints. Synchronous execution imposes \(A(k)=V\) and \(\tau_{ij}(k)=k\) at every round. Bounded-delay asynchrony permits irregular activations but requires a finite \(B\) such that \(0\le k-\tau_{ij}(k)\le B\) whenever a stored value is used, together with a declared fairness condition. Total asynchrony removes a uniform finite delay bound but requires every agent to update infinitely often and timestamps used along an infinite update sequence to tend to infinity. Partial barriers impose progress after a declared subset, quorum, or deadline condition is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronization model is a set of admissible activation and message-timestamp schedules. It states which agents update, how old each value may be, and what fairness or barrier rules apply. Synchronous, bounded-delay asynchronous, totally asynchronous, and partial-barrier models are distinguished by different constraints on these schedules, not by the optimization formula itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak S\subseteq\{((A(k)),(\tau_{ij}(k)))_{k\ge0}:A(k)\subseteq V,\ \tau_{ij}(k)\le k\}\) is specified by explicit activation, age, and fairness constraints.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Information age may be represented by \(d_{ij}(k)=k-\tau_{ij}(k)\ge0\).
special_cases_latex: Lockstep rounds correspond to \(A(k)=V\) and zero information age.
Serial coordinate execution corresponds to \(|A(k)|=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any convergence assertion under a synchronization model quantifies only over schedules in its admissible class.
boundary_notes: A global event counter used for analysis does not imply a globally available clock.
Packet loss and topology variation require additional schedule components unless encoded through admissibility.

Timestamp of the value from j used by i.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Execution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All required workers use the same round state, and the next state is committed only after the full barrier completes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For workers \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), synchronous execution consists of rounds \(k=0,1,\ldots\). At the start of round \(k\), every worker receives the same committed state \(x^k\), computes \(u_i^k\), and returns it before the next state is committed. The coordinator waits for every required worker and applies \[x^{k+1}=\Phi_k\!\left(x^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k\right).\] No worker begins computation for round \(k+1\) using an uncommitted state, and no update tagged with a different round enters this aggregation.
assumptions_latex: The required worker set \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is fixed for each round.
Each returned update carries its round index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle x^{k+1}=\Phi_k(x^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k)\) uses only updates computed from \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-based execution with a full coordination barrier.

notation.meaning: globally committed state for round k

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the agents, and let \(x_i^k\) be agent \(i\)'s state at the beginning of global round \(k\). Let \(m_{ji}^k\) denote the message produced by \(j\) for \(i\) during that round.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lockstep, barrier-separated execution with coordinated rounds; computation times may differ physically, but logical progress waits for the round condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An execution is synchronous if there is a sequence of global rounds \(k=0,1,\ldots\) such that every participating agent computes round-\(k\) messages from round-\(k\) states, every message admitted to the round-\(k\) update is labeled \(k\), and no agent begins its logical round-\(k+1\) update before the prescribed round-\(k\) barrier is satisfied. In the full-participation, reliable-message model, \(A(k)=V\) and the update has the form \(x_i^{k+1}=\Phi_i^k(x_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i})\). Thus the information timestamp used at round \(k\) is \(\tau_{ij}(k)=k\), unless a separately specified delayed synchronous model is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous execution consists of globally indexed rounds separated by barriers. All participating agents form round-k messages from round-k states, and admitted messages have that round's label. No agent logically advances to the next round until the specified barrier is met. In the full-participation model every agent updates once per round using current-round neighbor information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(k)=V,\quad \tau_{ij}(k)=k,\quad x_i^{k+1}=\Phi_i^k(x_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i})\) for every round \(k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Logical synchrony is equivalently a barrier ordering in which all required round-\(k\) operations precede every round-\(k+1\) state update.
special_cases_latex: A centralized parameter-server round is synchronous when the server waits for all prescribed worker messages before broadcasting the next state.
immediate_consequences_latex: No iterate mixes messages bearing different logical round indices in the full lockstep model.
boundary_notes: Simultaneous wall-clock execution is unnecessary; logical barrier ordering is the defining feature.
Waiting for only a quorum is partial-barrier rather than full synchronous execution.
review_flags: The supplied book hint was not inspectable, so the precise synchronous-execution definition lacks verified evidence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). During logical round \(k\), let \(R_k(t)\subseteq V\) be the workers whose valid round-\(k\) responses have arrived by elapsed time \(t\), let \(q_k\in\{1,cldots,n\}\) be a quorum, and let \(D_k>0\) be a deadline.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-indexed execution that bounds waiting but does not require all agents at every barrier; treatment of late messages must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial-barrier deadline regime releases round \(k\) at stopping time \(T_k=\inf\{t\ge0:|R_k(t)|\ge q_k\}\wedge D_k\). The participating set is \(A(k)=R_k(T_k)\), and the next logical state is computed using only the messages admitted by a declared late-message policy. The regime is a strict partial barrier when \(q_k<n\) is permitted. A valid specification states whether messages arriving after \(T_k\) are discarded, carried into a later round with timestamps, or used by an asynchronous correction; without that rule, the execution semantics are incomplete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-barrier deadline execution advances when either a required quorum of responses has arrived or a deadline expires. The agents whose responses are admitted form that round's participating set. Because the quorum may be smaller than the full network, progress need not wait for every agent. The model must state how late messages are treated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_k=\inf\{t\ge0:|R_k(t)|\ge q_k\}\wedge D_k,\qquad A(k)=R_k(T_k).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: A fixed-fraction barrier uses \(q_k=\lceil\alpha n\rceil\) for some \(\alpha\in(0,1]\).
special_cases_latex: If \(q_k=n\) and \(D_k=+\infty\), the rule reduces to a full barrier.
If the quorum is never reached before \(D_k\), release occurs exactly at the deadline.
immediate_consequences_latex: The waiting time satisfies \(T_k\le D_k\).
The number of admitted responses can be smaller than \(q_k\) when the deadline fires first.
boundary_notes: A deadline bounds waiting time, not necessarily the age of every model value.
Fair long-run participation requires a separate sampling or scheduling condition.

notation.meaning: Responses received by elapsed time t in round k.

Semi-Synchronous Execution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers may advance in unequal cohorts, but the difference between the fastest and slowest progress counters remains uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_i(t)\in\mathbb{N}\) denote the number of updates completed by worker \(i\) by time \(t\). Execution is semi-synchronous with skew bound \(\Delta\in\mathbb{N}\) if workers may progress without a full barrier but the scheduler enforces \[\max_i s_i(t)-\min_i s_i(t)\le\Delta\quad\text{for every }t.\] Aggregations may use proper subsets of workers, but a worker whose progress would violate the bound is paused until lagging workers advance. The case \(\Delta=0\) reduces to lockstep progress; positive \(\Delta\) permits controlled overlap between computation rounds.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many workers.
Each completed update increments exactly one progress counter.
\(\Delta\) is a fixed nonnegative integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sup_t\bigl(\max_i s_i(t)-\min_i s_i(t)\bigr)\le\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cohort-based execution with bounded progress skew.

notation.meaning: completed-update counter of worker i at time t

knowledge_statements.title: Deadline-Based Execution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each round closes at a fixed time; only on-time responses enter its aggregation unless a stale-update rule is declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given initial state \(x^0\), deadline \(D>0\), and aggregation maps \(\Phi_k\), round \(k\) starts at time \(t_k\) by broadcasting \(x^k\). Define \[A_k=\{i:\text{worker }i\text{ returns }u_i^k\text{ by }t_k+D\}.\] At time \(t_k+D\), commit \[x^{k+1}=\Phi_k\!\left(x^k,\{u_i^k:i\in A_k\}\right).\] Responses tagged with round \(k\) that arrive later are discarded or retained only under an explicitly specified stale-update rule. Stop after a prescribed number of commits or when a stated termination test holds, and output the last committed state.
assumptions_latex: \(D>0\) is fixed or specified before each round.
Every response contains worker and round identifiers.
\(\Phi_k\) is defined for every admissible response subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle x^{k+1}=\Phi_k(x^k,\{u_i^k:i\in A_k\})\) is committed at \(t_k+D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round aggregation using responses received before a fixed deadline.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Barrier Policies
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A round commits after a response quorum arrives or a deadline expires, whichever occurs first.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a quorum \(q\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), an optional deadline \(D>0\), and initial state \(x^0\). In round \(k\), broadcast \(x^k\) at time \(t_k\) and let \(n_k(t)\) count distinct valid responses received by time \(t\). Close the barrier at \[\tau_k=\min\!\left\{\inf\{t\ge t_k:n_k(t)\ge q\},\ t_k+D\right\}.\] With \(A_k\) the responders available at \(\tau_k\), commit \(x^{k+1}=\Phi_k(x^k,\{u_i^k:i\in A_k\})\). Without a deadline, omit the second argument of the minimum. Output the last committed state at termination.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le q\le m\).
Responses are deduplicated by worker and tagged by round.
The aggregation map accepts the subset available when the barrier closes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \tau_k=\min\{\text{quorum-arrival time},\ t_k+D\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation triggered by a response quorum or deadline.

notation.meaning: number of distinct valid round-k responses by time t

knowledge_statements.title: Deadline-Induced Selection Bias
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If timely responses correlate with worker identity or data, averaging only on-time gradients can be biased even when the full gradient is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two equally weighted workers with deterministic local gradients \(g_1=1\) and \(g_2=-1\), so the full gradient is \((g_1+g_2)/2=0\). Suppose worker \(1\) always responds before a deadline and worker \(2\) never does. A deadline aggregator averaging available gradients therefore returns \[\widehat g=\frac{1}{|A|}\sum_{i\in A}g_i=g_1=1,\] not the full gradient. More generally, if response inclusion depends on worker identity, data, or gradient magnitude, then conditioning on timely response changes the sampling distribution and need not preserve unbiasedness.
assumptions_latex: Workers have equal objective weights.
Worker \(1\) is always included and worker \(2\) is always excluded by the deadline.
The aggregator averages only received gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \widehat g=1\ne0=(g_1+g_2)/2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Response-time dependence can bias the aggregated gradient.

notation.meaning: set of workers meeting the deadline

children.top_down_role: Irregular execution with controlled information age.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Bounded-Staleness Read Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded delay can constrain each component's age while allowing an inconsistent snapshot assembled from several recent versions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x^0,x^1,\ldots denote committed shared states. A read used at update k may be represented by \widehat x_j^k=x_j^{\tau_j(k)}, where k-B\le\tau_j(k)\le k for every read component. The timestamps need not coincide, so \widehat x^k need not equal any single committed state x^s even though every component is at most B updates old.
assumptions_latex: Committed states admit a global logical index.
B<\infty.
Every read component has a timestamp in the stated window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x_j^k=x_j^{\tau_j(k)},\quad 0\le k-\tau_j(k)\le B,\quad \text{without necessarily having }\widehat x^k=x^s\text{ for one }s.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay reads that may combine components from different committed states.

notation.meaning: possibly inconsistent state read at update k

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Delay Asynchrony
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform bounds on information age and activation gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite agent set and consider logical events \(k\in\mathbb N\). Let \(R_k\subseteq I\times I\) contain the ordered pairs \((i,j)\) for which agent \(i\) uses agent \(j\)'s state at event \(k\), and let \(\tau_{ij}(k)\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\) be that state's timestamp. The execution has bounded-delay asynchrony if there is a finite integer \(B\ge0\) such that \[k-B\le\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\qquad\text{for every }(i,j)\in R_k,\] and every agent is activated at least once in each window \(\{k,k+1,\ldots,k+B\}\). Thus communication staleness and inter-activation time are uniformly bounded, although updates and reads may otherwise be irregular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded-delay asynchrony permits irregular execution while imposing a finite uniform bound on the age of every state actually read and on how long any agent remains inactive.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
\(\tau_{ij}(k)\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\) for every \((i,j)\in R_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every used read has age at most \(B\), and every agent is activated in every event window of length \(B+1\).

notation.meaning: ordered agent pairs corresponding to reads used at event k
timestamp read by agent i for agent j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irregular distributed execution with a uniform finite information-age and activation-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A schedule has bounded-delay asynchrony if there exists an integer \(B\ge1\) such that, for every event \(k\), active agent \(i\), and value from agent \(j\) used in that update, \(0\le k-\tau_{ij}(k)\le B\); moreover every agent is activated at least once in each block \(\{k,k+1,\ldots,k+B-1\}\). If communication links rather than nodes are the scheduled units, the same requirement is imposed on every required link. The bound \(B\) is uniform over time and schedules in the declared model class. Updates need not share round boundaries or use mutually consistent snapshots.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded-delay asynchrony permits irregular and uncoordinated updates but imposes a uniform finite bound on information age. It also imposes bounded activation gaps: every agent updates at least once in every block of a fixed length. Agents need not read a common snapshot and there is no full barrier.

immediate_consequences_latex: Every agent is activated infinitely often.
No value used by an update is more than \(B\) analysis events old.

children.title: Total Asynchrony
children.top_down_role: Execution without uniform delay bounds but with eventual information use.

knowledge_statements.title: Total Asynchrony
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every worker and information stream progresses eventually, but neither staleness nor activation gaps need have a uniform finite bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k_1^i<k_2^i<\cdots\) be the committed updates performed by worker \(i\), and let \(\tau_{ij}(k_r^i)\le k_r^i\) denote the version of component \(j\) read at its \(r\)-th activation. Execution is totally asynchronous when every worker is activated infinitely often and \[\lim_{r\to\infty}\tau_{ij}(k_r^i)=\infty\quad\text{for every }i,j.\] Thus every worker eventually uses information newer than any fixed cutoff, although no finite constant need bound \(k_r^i-\tau_{ij}(k_r^i)\) or the gaps \(k_{r+1}^i-k_r^i\).
assumptions_latex: Committed updates admit a global indexing.
Each worker-component read has an identifiable version index.
The worker set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle k_r^i\to\infty\quad\text{and}\quad\tau_{ij}(k_r^i)\to\infty\) for all \(i,j\), without uniform delay bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual activation and information refresh without uniform delay bounds.

notation.meaning: global index of worker i's r-th committed update
component-j version read at that activation

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A(k)\subseteq V\) be the agents activated at analysis event \(k\), and let \(\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\) be the timestamp of the value from \(j\) used by active agent \(i\). No finite uniform bound on \(k-\tau_{ij}(k)\) is assumed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchrony with unbounded finite delays, persistent activation, and eventual use of increasingly recent information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A schedule is totally asynchronous if every agent is activated infinitely often and information does not remain permanently frozen: for every required ordered pair \((j,i)\) and every infinite sequence \((k_m)\) of events at which agent \(i\) uses agent \(j\)'s value, \(\tau_{ij}(k_m)\to\infty\). Equivalently, for every finite timestamp threshold \(T\), only finitely many such uses have \(\tau_{ij}(k)\le T\). Individual delays \(k-\tau_{ij}(k)\) may be arbitrarily large, and activation gaps may be unbounded, provided the two eventuality conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total asynchrony allows arbitrarily large message delays and activation gaps. Nevertheless, every agent must update infinitely often, and values used repeatedly from any required source must have timestamps tending to infinity. Thus old information may persist for a long time but cannot remain permanently frozen along an infinite execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\{k:i\in A(k)\}|=\infty\ \text{for every }i,\qquad \tau_{ij}(k_m)\to\infty\ \text{along every infinite required-use sequence}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Timestamp divergence is equivalent to: for every \(T\in\mathbb N\), only finitely many required reads use a timestamp at most \(T\).
special_cases_latex: Every bounded-delay asynchronous schedule satisfying persistent activation is totally asynchronous.
immediate_consequences_latex: Total asynchrony excludes permanent agent failure when every agent is required to activate infinitely often.
It permits \(\sup_k(k-\tau_{ij}(k))=+\infty\).
boundary_notes: Mere infinite activation is insufficient if an agent forever reuses one stale value.
The definition supplies execution fairness, not convergence of an optimization algorithm.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X^k=(x_1^k,cldots,x_n^k)\) be the network state after event \(k\), let \(A(k)\subseteq V\) be active agents, and let \(X^{\tau_i(k)}=(x_1^{\tau_{i1}(k)},cldots,x_n^{\tau_{in}(k)})\) be the componentwise stale view read by agent \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal representation of delayed and partial distributed updates; it defines the state transition and residual bookkeeping but does not itself provide convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An asynchronous distributed optimization calculus represents execution by component updates \(x_i^{k+1}=\Phi_i^k(X^{\tau_i(k)},\xi_i^k)\) for \(i\in A(k)\) and \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\) for \(i\notin A(k)\), where \(\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\) and \(\xi_i^k\) contains local randomness or sampled data. Its delay vector is \(d_i^k=(k-ctau_{i1}(k),cldots,k-ctau_{in}(k))\), and its update increment is \(\Delta_i^k=x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k\). A complete calculus specifies the admissible schedule class, filtration, conditional law of activations and samples, and the optimization residual evaluated from \(X^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The asynchronous optimization calculus is an event-indexed state-transition representation. Active agents update from componentwise stale views and local randomness; inactive agents retain their states. Delays and update increments are explicit variables. A complete specification also states admissible schedules, the information filtration, random activation laws, and the optimization residual being analyzed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}\Phi_i^k(X^{\tau_i(k)},\xi_i^k),&i\in A(k),\\x_i^k,&i\notin A(k),\end{cases}\qquad \tau_{ij}(k)\le k.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using coordinate projectors \(P_{A(k)}\), the transition can be written \(X^{k+1}=X^k+P_{A(k)}(\Phi^k(X^{\tau(k)},\xi^k)-X^k)\).
special_cases_latex: Serial asynchronous execution has \(|A(k)|=1\).
Synchronous execution has \(A(k)=V\) and \(\tau_{ij}(k)=k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Inactive coordinates have zero increment: \(\Delta_i^k=0\) for \(i\notin A(k)\).
boundary_notes: The global event index is an analytical ordering device and need not be observed by agents.
Simultaneous physical events require a deterministic or probabilistic serialization convention.

notation.meaning: Agent i's componentwise stale network view.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Coordinate Fixed-Point Realization of Consensus Optimization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An asynchronous consensus optimizer can apply one block of a solution-encoding fixed-point map to delayed state information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=(T_1,\ldots,T_n):\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z\) be a fixed-point map whose fixed points encode solutions of the stated consensus problem. At event \(k\), activate \(I_k\), read \(\widehat z^k=(z_1^{s_{k1}},\ldots,z_n^{s_{kn}})\), and set \[z_{I_k}^{k+1}=z_{I_k}^k+\lambda_k\bigl(T_{I_k}(\widehat z^k)-z_{I_k}^k\bigr),\qquad z_i^{k+1}=z_i^k\quad(i\ne I_k).\] Convergence additionally requires appropriate properties of \(T\), relaxation, activation, and delays.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}T\) encodes solutions of the consensus optimization problem.
Every read timestamp satisfies \(s_{kj}\le k\).
\(\lambda_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z^{k+1}\text{ differs from }z^k\text{ only in block }I_k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic event-driven realization when a consensus optimizer is represented by a block fixed-point map.

notation.meaning: agent-i block of the solution-encoding fixed-point map

review_flags: This abstract realization does not validate the deferred uncorrected row-stochastic gradient recursion.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus and First-Order Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero incidence disagreement certifies consensus; zero aggregate gradient at consensus certifies stationarity, and optimality in the convex case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be an incidence matrix of connected \(G\), \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), and \[r_{\rm con}(X)=\|(B^\top\otimes I_d)X\|,\qquad r_{\rm stat}(X)=\left\|\sum_i\omega_i\nabla f_i(x_i)\right\|.\] Then \(r_{\rm con}(X)=0\) is equivalent to consensus. At consensus, \(r_{\rm stat}(X)=0\) is equivalent to stationarity of \(F(x)=\sum_i\omega_i f_i(x)\), and certifies global optimality when every \(f_i\) is convex.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is connected.
Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
Convexity is required for the global-optimality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\rm con}(X)=r_{\rm stat}(X)=0\Longrightarrow X=\mathbf1\otimes x\text{ and }\nabla F(x)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for the smooth unconstrained consensus model; it is not an asynchronous update rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Agent Stationary-Weight Objective Bias
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-agent row-stochastic network can target its stationary-weighted quadratic objective instead of the intended equal-weight sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let W=\begin{pmatrix}0.9&0.1\\0.2&0.8\end{pmatrix}, whose normalized stationary left vector is \pi=(2/3,1/3). Let f_1(x)=x^2/2 and f_2(x)=(x-3)^2/2, while the intended objective is F(x)=(f_1(x)+f_2(x))/2. Then \operatorname*{argmin}F=\{3/2\}, whereas \operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_i\pi_i f_i(x)=\{1\}. Consequently, an uncorrected consensus-gradient realization whose limiting descent weights are induced by W can target x=1 rather than the intended equal-weight minimizer.
assumptions_latex: W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1.
\pi^{\mathsf T}W=\pi^{\mathsf T}.
No balancing, push-sum, eigenvector learning, or equivalent objective-weight correction is used.
The realization's limiting descent weights are induced by \pi.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}F=\{3/2\}\ne\{1\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_i\pi_i f_i(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite quadratic instance demonstrating the wrong-objective boundary for uncorrected unbalanced consensus optimization.

notation.meaning: stationary left probability vector of W

review_flags: The example establishes objective bias conditional on a realization inheriting the stationary weights; it is not a convergence theorem for every asynchronous implementation.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Consensus-Optimization Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous consensus optimization solves a replicated-variable agreement problem without synchronized global rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given local functions \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) and weights \(\omega_i>0\), solve \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_n}\sum_{i=1}^n\omega_i f_i(x_i)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_i=x_j\quad(\{i,j\}\in E),\] using computation and communication events that need not form global rounds. If \(G=(V,E)\) is connected, the constraints are equivalent to \(x_1=\cdots=x_n=x\), giving \(\min_x\sum_i\omega_i f_i(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(\omega_i>0\) for all \(i\).
\(G\) is connected for equivalence to one shared decision variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i=x_j\ (\{i,j\}\in E)\Longleftrightarrow x_1=\cdots=x_n.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective and agreement model independent of a particular asynchronous recursion.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Stochastic Objective-Bias Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncorrected row-stochastic mixing generally follows stationary-distribution weights rather than the intended objective weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be primitive and row-stochastic, with \(\pi^\top W=\pi^\top\), \(\pi_i>0\), and \(\pi^\top\mathbf1=1\). Mixing preserves the \(\pi\)-weighted aggregate, not generally the prescribed \(\omega\)-weighted aggregate. Thus an uncorrected method whose descent aggregate is induced solely by \(W\) need not optimize \(\sum_i\omega_i f_i\) unless \(\pi_i=\omega_i/\sum_j\omega_j\), or balancing, push-sum, eigenvector learning, or equivalent mass correction is supplied.
assumptions_latex: \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) is primitive.
No balancing or mass-correction mechanism is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi\not\propto\omega\Longrightarrow\text{consensus preservation alone does not ensure optimization of }\sum_i\omega_i f_i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for uncorrected consensus-gradient schemes using unbalanced mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Consensus Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-agent stale-read consensus-gradient iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a graph \(G=(I,E)\), differentiable functions \(f_i:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\), stepsizes \(\alpha_k>0\), and initial states \(x_i^0\), event \(k\) activates one agent \(i_k\). It reads \(x_j^{\tau_{i_kj}(k)}\) from its neighbors, chooses nonnegative weights satisfying \(\sum_j w_{i_kj}^k=1\), and performs \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{i_kj}^k x_j^{\tau_{i_kj}(k)}-\alpha_k\nabla f_{i_k}(x_{i_k}^k),\qquad x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\ \text{for }i\ne i_k.\] The execution stops under a prescribed local residual rule or outputs the latest local states; consensus requires \(x_i-x_j\to0\) in a convergent regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each event, one agent mixes possibly stale neighbor states, takes a local gradient step, and leaves all other current states unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i\) is differentiable for every \(i\).
\(w_{i_kj}^k=0\) for unavailable nonneighbors.
Every required stale read has a defined timestamp.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The event produces \(x^{k+1}\) using no global communication round.

notation.meaning: timestamp of a stale neighbor read

knowledge_statements.title: Conservative Buffered Tracker Transport
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conservative splitting, buffering, delivery, and gradient-difference injection preserve total tracker mass despite delayed messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain held tracker masses \(y_i\), directed-channel buffers \(b_{ij}\), and gradients \(g_i=\nabla f_i(x_i)\). A send event at \(i\) chooses nonnegative fractions \(a_{ji}\) summing to one, replaces \(y_i\) by \(a_{ii}y_i^{\rm old}\), and adds \(a_{ji}y_i^{\rm old}\) to each outgoing buffer \(b_{ij}\). A receive event transfers one buffer to its receiver and zeros that buffer. When \(x_i\) changes, inject \(g_i^+-g_i^-\) into \(y_i\). Then \[\mathcal M=\sum_i y_i+\sum_{(i,j)}b_{ij}\] changes only by the injected gradient difference and equals \(\sum_i g_i\) at every event when initialized that way.
assumptions_latex: Every undelivered message is represented by a channel buffer.
Send fractions are nonnegative and sum to one, including retained mass.
Each delivered buffer is transferred exactly once.
Initially \(\mathcal M=\sum_i g_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M^k=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\quad\text{for every event }k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mass-preserving event primitive for asynchronous gradient tracking; primal descent and normalization remain separate.

notation.meaning: undelivered tracker mass sent from i to j
fraction of sender i's old tracker mass assigned to recipient j

review_flags: This transport primitive is not by itself a complete convergent gradient-tracking optimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Tracker-Mass Defect Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The defect between total augmented tracker mass and the current aggregate gradient exactly tests the tracking invariant when in-transit mass is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For augmented tracker state \(Y^k\), mass functional \(\mathcal M\), and local gradients \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\), define \[r_{\rm tr}^k=\left\|\mathcal M(Y^k)-\sum_i g_i^k\right\|.\] Then \(r_{\rm tr}^k=0\) exactly certifies the aggregate tracker-mass identity. The test is sound only when all held and in-transit tracker mass is included in \(Y^k\).
assumptions_latex: All agent-held and in-transit tracker mass is represented in \(Y^k\).
The aggregate of current local gradients is available when the certificate is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\rm tr}^k=0\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal M(Y^k)=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori test of the aggregate-gradient invariant in a buffered asynchronous tracker.
review_flags: Zero mass defect does not certify consensus, descent, or optimality.
Computing the certificate may itself require aggregation of distributed state.

knowledge_statements.title: Tracker-Mass Balance Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conservative tracker transport plus injection of the aggregate gradient change preserves the tracker-mass invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G^k=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\). If the augmented tracker state satisfies \[\mathcal M(Y^{k+1})=\mathcal M(Y^k)+G^{k+1}-G^k\] at every event and \(\mathcal M(Y^0)=G^0\), then \(\mathcal M(Y^k)=G^k\) for every \(k\).
assumptions_latex: All held and in-transit tracker mass is included in \(Y^k\).
\(\mathcal M(Y^0)=G^0\).
Every event obeys the displayed balance equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\ge0,\quad\mathcal M(Y^k)=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic condition preserving the aggregate-gradient identity across asynchronous events.

knowledge_statements.title: Naive Partial-Mixing Tracker Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Updating only one row of a doubly stochastic tracker mix generally changes total tracker mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar trackers \(y^k=(a,b)\), let only agent 1 apply the first row of \[W=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad y_1^{k+1}=\tfrac12(a+b),\quad y_2^{k+1}=b,\] with no gradient innovation. Then \[y_1^{k+1}+y_2^{k+1}=\tfrac12(a+3b)\ne a+b\] whenever \(a\ne b\), although \(W\) is doubly stochastic.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one tracker is updated.
The inactive tracker is retained.
No buffer, push, or mass-correction state is used.
There is no gradient innovation at the event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\ne b\Longrightarrow\sum_i y_i^{k+1}\ne\sum_i y_i^k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to applying one row of a synchronous balanced tracker recursion while retaining inactive trackers.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Asynchronous Tracker State
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid asynchronous tracking accounts for all held and in-transit tracker mass in an augmented event-driven state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\). An asynchronous gradient-tracking realization uses an augmented state \(Y^k\) containing agent-held tracker variables and, where applicable, undelivered buffer or channel mass. A linear mass functional \(\mathcal M\) should satisfy exactly or asymptotically \[\mathcal M(Y^k)=\sum_{i=1}^n g_i^k\quad\text{or}\quad\left\|\mathcal M(Y^k)-\sum_i g_i^k\right\|\to0,\] while only the states involved in an activated computation or communication event change.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\) is defined.
The augmented state includes tracker mass that has left a sender but has not reached a receiver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M(Y^k)\text{ is the aggregate tracker quantity to be matched to }\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-independent representation accounting for agent-held and in-transit tracker mass.

notation.meaning: total-mass functional on the augmented state

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Augmented-state push-pull tracking with delayed-message buffers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^k\) and \(y^k\) collect agent states together with delay-buffer coordinates, and set \(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\) with zero buffer mass. At event \(k\), activation and message delivery determine a row-stochastic matrix \(A^k\) and a column-stochastic matrix \(B^k\), each acting as the identity on unaffected coordinates. With \(g(x)=(\nabla f_i(x_i))_i\), perform \[x^{k+1}=A^kx^k-\alpha_k y^k,\qquad y^{k+1}=B^ky^k+g(x^{k+1})-g(x^k).\] Buffer coordinates encode undelivered messages. Stop by a prescribed consensus-and-stationarity residual, or output the latest physical-agent coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous gradient tracking mixes decisions and gradient-tracker mass through activation-dependent matrices, while a gradient-difference correction tracks changes in the aggregate gradient.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
\(A^k\) is row-stochastic and \(B^k\) is column-stochastic.
Delayed messages are represented by augmented buffer coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion defines decision and tracker updates without synchronized global rounds.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable. Agent \(i\) holds a primal state \(x_i^k\) and tracker \(y_i^k\). Let \(A(k)\) be the active set and let timestamped neighbor trackers be mixed with weights \(w_{ij}^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-indexed gradient tracking with delayed, uneven activation; the defining feature is dynamic tracking of aggregate gradient changes, not merely stale-gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An asynchronous gradient-tracking process is a distributed process with a tracker state satisfying, for each active agent, a delayed mixing-and-increment relation of the form \(y_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j}w_{ij}^k y_j^{\tau_{ij}(k)}+\nabla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-\nabla f_i(x_i^{s_i(k)})\), together with a primal update driven by \(y_i\); inactive components remain unchanged or are handled by an explicitly augmented mass-conservation state. Here \(s_i(k)\le k\) is the timestamp of the local gradient already represented in the tracker. The process is tracking-consistent when its declared aggregate invariant accounts for each gradient increment exactly once and the tracking residual relative to the network aggregate tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous gradient tracking augments each local primal variable with a tracker. An active agent mixes timestamped neighbor trackers and adds the change between its new local gradient and the local gradient already represented. A valid asynchronous specification must prevent increments from being lost or counted twice, possibly through augmented mass variables. Tracking consistency means the aggregate invariant is correct and the tracking residual vanishes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_i^{k+1}=\sum_j w_{ij}^k y_j^{\tau_{ij}(k)}+\nabla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-\nabla f_i(x_i^{s_i(k)})\quad(i\in A(k)).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: In a synchronous doubly stochastic special case with \(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\), the invariant is \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\).
special_cases_latex: Zero delays and full activation recover synchronous gradient tracking.
Uniformly bounded \(k-ctau_{ij}(k)\) gives bounded-delay asynchronous tracking.
immediate_consequences_latex: A tracker formula without a rule for delayed message mass may fail to preserve the intended aggregate invariant.
boundary_notes: The displayed local relation is a template; directed or lossy networks may require push-sum weights and virtual-node states.
Using a stale local gradient without a dynamic tracker is not gradient tracking.

notation.meaning: Timestamp of the local gradient already represented.

review_flags: No supplied source hint specifically supports asynchronous gradient tracking; the generic update template needs authoritative sourcing.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous gradient-tracking state

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-independent definition separating the tracking requirement from model-specific buffering or normalization machinery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k). An asynchronous gradient-tracking state consists of agent or augmented communication states whose decoded trackers y_i^k satisfy, exactly or asymptotically,
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n y_i^k=\sum_{i=1}^n g_i^k
\quad\text{or}\quad
\left\|\sum_i y_i^k-\sum_i g_i^k\right\|\to0,
\]
while only an activated subset of computation or communication states changes at each event. In directed or delayed implementations, in-transit message or buffer masses must be included in the conserved augmented state whenever they have left a sender but have not yet reached a receiver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous gradient tracking maintains the aggregate-gradient identity in an event-driven augmented state, including undelivered message mass when necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\) is defined at every local state.
The decoded or augmented state accounts for all tracker mass transferred between agents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Valid asynchronous tracking requires conservation of tracker mass plus injection of the current aggregate gradient change.}

children.title: Randomized Agent, Block, and Edge Activation
children.top_down_role: Network optimization driven by random node, edge, or block updates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite communication graph and \((\mathcal F_k)\) the execution filtration. At event \(k\), let \(A_k\subseteq V\), \(H_k\subseteq E\), and \(B_k\subseteq\{1,cldots,d\}\) denote active nodes, edges, and coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A classification of stochastic scheduling units and their conditional laws; it does not impose a particular optimization update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomized network-activation model is a stochastic process \((A_k,H_k,B_k)_{k\ge0}\) adapted after sampling to \((\mathcal F_{k+1})\), with conditional law \(P_k(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_k)\). It is node activation when the primitive random unit is \(A_k\); edge activation when it is \(H_k\); block activation when computation or communication is restricted to \(B_k\); and joint activation when two or more units are sampled together. The model is conditionally independent when \(P_k\) does not depend on earlier activations beyond declared exogenous state, Markovian when it depends on a current activation state, and history-dependent otherwise. Persistent excitation requires a stated positivity condition, such as \(\mathbb P(i\in A_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_i>0\) almost surely for every required node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized activation model specifies conditional distributions for active nodes, edges, and coordinate blocks at each event. It is classified by the primitive scheduling unit and by temporal dependence: conditionally independent, Markovian, or general history dependent. A positivity or persistent-excitation condition must be stated separately when every network component needs recurring opportunities to act.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A_k,H_k,B_k)\sim P_k(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_k),\qquad \mathbb P(i\in A_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_i>0\ \text{when node persistence is imposed}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Single-node sampling is represented by \(A_k=\{I_k\}\) for a random index \(I_k\).
Single-edge gossip is represented by \(H_k=\{E_k\}\) for a random edge \(E_k\).
special_cases_latex: Independent identically distributed node sampling has a time-invariant law and independent \(A_k\).
Randomized block-coordinate communication takes \(A_k=V\) while sampling only \(B_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A uniform conditional lower bound gives every required node a positive opportunity for activation at every event.
Marginal node probabilities do not determine correlations between simultaneously active nodes.
boundary_notes: Positive marginal probabilities alone do not specify independence or almost-sure bounded activation gaps.
Random topology and random activation coincide only when the active-edge set is the topology used by the update.

notation.meaning: Active nodes, edges, and coordinate blocks.

review_flags: No inspectable source supports this complete activation taxonomy and conditional-law terminology.
knowledge_statements.title: Taxonomy of randomized network activations
Zero-Probability Agent Starvation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agent with zero selection probability is permanently starved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p_i=0\), then agent \(i\) is never selected almost surely. Thus no algorithm whose only mechanism for changing agent \(i\)'s owned state is its activation can guarantee updating that state.
assumptions_latex: Only activation of agent \(i\) can change its owned state.
The stationary activation distribution has \(p_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P(I_k\ne i\ \forall k)=1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp support boundary for independent stationary single-agent activation.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Interactivation Times
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agent selected with probability p has geometric waiting times with mean 1/p.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under independent activations with \(\mathbb P(I_k=i)=p_i>0\), the number \(T_i\) of events from one activation of agent \(i\) through its next activation satisfies \[\mathbb P(T_i=t)=(1-p_i)^{t-1}p_i,\qquad \mathbb E[T_i]=p_i^{-1},\qquad \mathbb P(T_i>m)=(1-p_i)^m.\]
assumptions_latex: Activations are independent across events.
\(p_i>0\) is stationary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[T_i]=1/p_i,\qquad\mathbb P(T_i>m)=(1-p_i)^m.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-agent waiting-time law under independent stationary single-agent activation.

notation.meaning: events through the next activation of agent i

knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Weighted Agent Contribution Is Unbiased
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing a selected agent's contribution by its selection probability removes sampling bias for a prescribed aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb P(I=i\mid\mathcal F)=p_i>0\), and let \(v_i\) be \(\mathcal F\)-measurable. Then \[\mathbb E\left[\frac{\omega_I}{p_I}v_I\,\middle|\,\mathcal F\right]=\sum_{i=1}^n\omega_iv_i.\] Without \(1/p_I\), the conditional mean is \(\sum_i p_i\omega_iv_i\).
assumptions_latex: \(p_i>0\) whenever \(\omega_iv_i\) may be nonzero.
Each \(v_i\) is measurable before the activation draw.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[(\omega_I/p_I)v_I\mid\mathcal F]=\sum_i\omega_iv_i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction for unequal selection probabilities in single-agent stochastic updates.
review_flags: Importance weighting can increase variance when some selection probability is small.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Agent Activation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each event independently selects exactly one agent, and every agent has a fixed positive selection probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given agents \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), a randomized single-agent activation process is a sequence \((I_k)_{k\ge0}\) taking values in \(V\). In the independent stationary model, there is a probability vector \(p\in(0,1]^n\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\) such that
\[
\mathbb{P}(I_k=i\mid I_0,\ldots,I_{k-1})=p_i
\]
for every \(k\) and \(i\). At event \(k\), only the state owned by agent \(I_k\) is eligible to change.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
\(p_i>0\) for every \(i\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every agent is selected infinitely often with probability \(1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent categorical selection of one updating agent per event.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction for unequal agent-selection probabilities in single-agent stochastic updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(I=i)=p_i>0\), and let \(v_i\) be deterministic conditional on the pre-activation history. Then \[\mathbb E\left[\frac{\omega_I}{p_I}v_I\,\middle|\,\mathcal F\right]=\sum_{i=1}^n\omega_iv_i.\] Without the factor \(1/p_I\), the conditional mean is \(\sum_i p_i\omega_iv_i\), which generally targets a probability-weighted rather than prescribed aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing a selected agent's contribution by its selection probability removes sampling bias for a prescribed weighted aggregate.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i>0\) whenever \(\omega_iv_i\) may be nonzero.
The vectors \(v_i\) are measurable before the activation draw.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[(\omega_I/p_I)v_I\mid\mathcal F]=\sum_i\omega_iv_i.

notation.meaning: information available before the activation draw
candidate update contribution of agent i

review_flags: Importance weighting can increase variance when some \(p_i\) is small.
knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Weighted Agent Update Is Unbiased
Zero-Inclusion Block Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block that is never activated remains frozen and can prevent convergence even on a problem requiring only that block to change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathbb P(b\in B_k)=0\) for every \(k\), then the inactive-block rule gives \(x_b^k=x_b^0\) almost surely for all \(k\). Thus, for any update map satisfying \(T_b(x)=c_b\neq x_b^0\), the masked iteration cannot converge to a fixed point of \(T\).
assumptions_latex: A block \(b\) has zero inclusion probability at every event.
Inactive blocks are retained exactly.
\(T_b(x)=c_b\neq x_b^0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_b^k=x_b^0\ \text{for all }k\text{ almost surely, so convergence to a fixed point of }T\text{ is impossible}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of block coverage when one block is never activated.

notation.meaning: required fixed-point value of the omitted block

knowledge_statements.title: Random Activation-Mask Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized block update masks the residual of a full update map; the expected mask is diagonal with the marginal block-inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each \(X_b\) be a vector space and let \(P_B\) retain precisely the blocks indexed by \(B\). Applying only the active blocks of \(T:X\to X\) is equivalent to \[x^{k+1}=x^k+P_{B_k}(T(x^k)-x^k).\] If \(B_k\) is independent of \(x^k\) and \(q_b=\mathbb P(b\in B_k)\), then \[\mathbb E[P_{B_k}\mid x^k]=\operatorname{diag}(q_1I_{X_1},\ldots,q_mI_{X_m}).\]
assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_{b=1}^mX_b\), where every \(X_b\) is a vector space.
\(B_k\) is independent of the current iterate.
\(T:X\to X\) is block-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{k+1}=x^k+P_{B_k}(T(x^k)-x^k),\qquad \mathbb E[P_{B_k}\mid x^k]=\operatorname{diag}(q_bI_{X_b})_{b=1}^m.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent operator representation of simultaneous randomized block updates.

notation.meaning: block mask retaining the coordinates indexed by B
full update map before activation masking

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Block Activation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random nonempty set determines which coordinate blocks may change; in the independent full-coverage model, the sets are identically distributed and every block has positive inclusion probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) and write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\). A randomized block activation process is a sequence \((B_k)_{k\ge0}\) of random nonempty subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). At event \(k\), an update must satisfy
\[
x_b^{k+1}=x_b^k\quad\text{for every }b\notin B_k.
\]
In the independent full-coverage model, the sets \(B_k\) are independent and identically distributed, and each block has inclusion probability \(q_b=\mathbb{P}(b\in B_k)>0\). Singleton and minibatch sampling are both included.
assumptions_latex: \(m<\infty\).
\(B_k\ne\varnothing\) almost surely.
The random sets \((B_k)_{k\ge0}\) are independent and identically distributed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under independent sampling with \(q_b>0\), every block is activated infinitely often almost surely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random selection of coordinate blocks eligible for an event update.

notation.meaning: active block set at event k
marginal inclusion probability of block b

knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Sampling-Support Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infinite recurrence of every sampled edge cannot coordinate the whole network when the positive-probability edge support is disconnected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_+=(V,\{e:r_e>0\})\). If \(G_+\) is disconnected and communication is restricted to endpoints of sampled edges, no execution can transmit information between distinct components of \(G_+\). Therefore recurrence of every supported edge does not imply global network coverage or global consensus.
assumptions_latex: Communication or state coupling occurs only across the sampled edge.
The positive-probability sampling-support graph is disconnected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global information propagation and global consensus cannot be guaranteed from supported-edge recurrence alone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global information propagation when sampled-edge support is disconnected.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Activated-Edge Laplacian
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expected sampled-edge Laplacian is the weighted Laplacian of the sampling-support graph, whose nullspace identifies the components that activation can couple.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Orient each edge \(e\) arbitrarily and let \(b_e\) be its incidence vector. If edge \(e\) is sampled with probability \(r_e\), define \(L_{E_k}=b_{E_k}b_{E_k}^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[\bar L:=\mathbb E[L_{E_k}]=\sum_{e\in E}r_eb_eb_e^{\mathsf T},\qquad z^{\mathsf T}\bar Lz=\sum_{e=\{u,v\}\in E}r_e(z_u-z_v)^2.\] Its kernel consists of the vectors constant on each connected component of the positive-probability support graph.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph.
\(r_e\geq0\) and \(\sum_{e\in E}r_e=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker\bar L=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (V,\{e:r_e>0\})\text{ is connected}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebraic representation of independently sampled undirected edges.

notation.meaning: oriented incidence vector of edge e

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Edge Activation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each event independently selects one graph edge, permitting communication or updates only at that edge's endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite graph \(G=(V,E)\), a randomized edge activation process is a sequence \((E_k)_{k\ge0}\) with \(E_k\in E\). In the independent stationary model, probabilities \(r_e>0\) satisfy \(\sum_{e\in E}r_e=1\) and
\[
\mathbb{P}(E_k=e\mid E_0,\ldots,E_{k-1})=r_e.
\]
At event \(k\), communication or pairwise state modification is restricted to the endpoints of \(E_k\); all other agent states remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite and \(E\ne\varnothing\).
\(r_e>0\) for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every edge is activated infinitely often with probability \(1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random communication-link selection for pairwise asynchronous updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation-Coverage Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage may require every component within each bounded window, positive conditional window probability, or merely infinitely many activations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite components \(\mathcal C\) and active sets \(A_k\subseteq\mathcal C\), common coverage regimes are: bounded coverage, when some \(B\ge1\) satisfies
\[
\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}A_t=\mathcal C\quad\text{for every }k;
\]
persistent conditional coverage, when constants \(B\ge1\) and \(\eta>0\) satisfy
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(c\in\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}A_t\mid\mathcal F_k\right)\ge\eta
\]
for every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and \(k\); and eventual coverage, when every \(c\) belongs to \(A_k\) for infinitely many \(k\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is finite.
\((\mathcal F_k)\) contains the activation history through event \(k-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounded coverage implies eventual coverage; persistent conditional coverage implies eventual coverage almost surely under repeated conditional trials.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic and stochastic predicates ensuring recurrent activation of every component.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Distributed ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers solve local ADMM subproblems using possibly delayed consensus values. A coordinator aggregates available states, while only activated workers update their dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i=z\), initialize \(x_i^0,z^0,u_i^0\) and choose \(\rho>0\). At event \(k\), activate a nonempty worker set \(S_k\). Each \(i\in S_k\) reads a delayed master value \(z^{\tau_i(k)}\) and computes \[x_i^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x_i-z^{\tau_i(k)}+u_i^k\rVert^2\right\};\] inactive workers retain their values. After receiving the selected updates, the coordinator sets \(z^{k+1}=m^{-1}\sum_i(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k)\), and each activated worker sets \(u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\); inactive dual variables are retained. Stop when primal and dual residual tolerances hold.
assumptions_latex: Every worker is activated infinitely often and \(0\le k-\tau_i(k)\le D<\infty\).
Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, and a primal-dual solution exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs the latest \((x_1^k,\ldots,x_m^k,z^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k)\) when its prescribed residual test is met.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A bounded-delay, irregular-activation consensus-ADMM template with worker-local primal updates.

notation.meaning: Iteration index of the consensus value read by worker i.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The exact asynchronous update is variant-dependent. The supplied sections do not establish that averaging all stored states with the pre-update multipliers, followed by dual updates only at activated workers, is the intended bounded-delay ADMM scheme. A source supporting these precise aggregation and activation rules is required.
