children.title: Partial Client Participation
children.top_down_role: Optimization with sampled, unavailable, or delayed client subsets.

assumptions_latex: There are \(n\) clients with objective weights \(p_i>0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
At round \(t\), a random available or selected subset \(S_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is observed, with inclusion probability \(q_{i,t}=\mathbb P(i\in S_t)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Participation is partial when \(\mathbb P(S_t\ne\{1,\ldots,n\})>0\) for at least one round.

notation.meaning: Participating client subset at round t
Marginal inclusion probability of client i
Target objective weight of client i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random, unavailable, or delayed client subsets represented by roundwise inclusion events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partial client participation means
\[
\exists t:\ 
\mathbb P\!\left(S_t\ne\{1,\ldots,n\}\right)>0.
\]
For client quantities \(u_{i,t}\), the Horvitz--Thompson aggregate
\[
\widehat u_t=\sum_{i\in S_t}\frac{p_i}{q_{i,t}}u_{i,t}
\]
satisfies \(\mathbb E[\widehat u_t]=\sum_i p_i u_{i,t}\) when the quantities are fixed conditional on the sampling design. Without inclusion-probability correction, unequal participation can change the effective client weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Participation is partial when some communication round can omit clients because of sampling, unavailability, or delay.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial Client Participation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and inclusion-corrected aggregate are mathematically coherent and fit partial client participation, but no source is supplied for the federated formulation or its attached weighting property.

knowledge_statements.title: participation rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The participation rate is the fraction of eligible clients whose updates enter a round; its conditional expectation equals the average client inclusion probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In round \(t\), let \(E_t\) be the nonempty set of eligible clients and \(S_t\subseteq E_t\) the clients whose updates are included by the server. The realized participation rate is \(q_t=|S_t|/|E_t|\). Before selection, its conditional expected value is \(\bar q_t=\mathbb{E}[|S_t|\mid\mathcal H_t]/|E_t|=|E_t|^{-1}\sum_{i\in E_t}\mathbb{P}(i\in S_t\mid\mathcal H_t)\). Uniformly sampling exactly \(m_t\) eligible clients gives \(q_t=\bar q_t=m_t/|E_t|\).
assumptions_latex: \(S_t\subseteq E_t\) is measurable after the round's selection and response events.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[q_t=\frac{|S_t|}{|E_t|},\qquad \bar q_t=\frac{1}{|E_t|}\sum_{i\in E_t}\mathbb{P}(i\in S_t\mid\mathcal H_t).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Realized and conditional expected fractions of eligible clients participating in one round.

notation.meaning: Eligible client set in round t.
Clients whose updates are included in round t.
Realized and conditional expected participation rates.

review_flags: A federated-optimization source is required for the eligible-set denominator convention.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The formulas are valid when the eligible set and its cardinality are known under the conditioning history, but that measurability is not stated. No source establishes the eligible-set denominator or the convention that participation means updates included after response events rather than clients initially sampled.

knowledge_statements.title: client dropout during round
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within-round dropout occurs when at least one initially contacted client fails to return a valid update before aggregation; the dropout rate uses the contacted cohort as denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_t\) be the clients selected and successfully contacted at the start of round \(t\), and let \(R_t\subseteq B_t\) be those whose valid updates arrive before the aggregation deadline. Client dropout during round \(t\) occurs exactly when \(D_t=B_t\setminus R_t\neq\varnothing\). For \(|B_t|>0\), the realized dropout rate is \(d_t=|D_t|/|B_t|=1-|R_t|/|B_t|\). The aggregation cohort is \(R_t\), not the initially selected cohort \(B_t\).
assumptions_latex: An update is counted in \(R_t\) only if it is valid and received before the fixed round deadline.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D_t=B_t\setminus R_t\neq\varnothing,\qquad d_t=\frac{|D_t|}{|B_t|}=1-\frac{|R_t|}{|B_t|}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a selected client to return a valid update by the round deadline.

notation.meaning: Clients contacted successfully at the round's start.
Clients returning valid updates before the deadline.
Clients that drop out after initial contact.

review_flags: A federated-systems source is required for the selected-versus-responding cohort convention.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The set identities and dropout-rate formula are correct under the record’s definitions, and the condition role fits the leaf. A source is still required because federated literature varies on whether dropout is measured relative to selected, contacted, available, or initially responding clients.

children.title: Participation-Fairness Distortion Limitations
children.top_down_role: Objective distortions caused by nonrepresentative participation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let clients be indexed by \(i\in[M]\), let \(F_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), and let the intended federated objective be \(F_p(x)=\sum_{i=1}^M p_iF_i(x)\), where \(p\in\Delta_M\). In round \(t\), participation and aggregation induce random effective weights \(Q_t=(Q_{t,1},\ldots,Q_{t,M})\in\Delta_M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-client federated optimization with possibly nonrepresentative random participation; the definition concerns objective distortion, independently of any convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(q_i=\mathbb E[Q_{t,i}]\) for a stationary participation rule and \(F_q(x)=\sum_i q_iF_i(x)\). The participation-fairness distortion on \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is \(\mathcal D_X(p,q)=\sup_{x\in X}|F_q(x)-F_p(x)|\). For tolerance \(\delta\ge0\), the rule lies on the \(\delta\)-distortion boundary when \(\mathcal D_X(p,q)=\delta\), is admissible when \(\mathcal D_X(p,q)\le\delta\), and is participation-fair when \(q=p\), equivalently \(\mathbb E[Q_{t,i}]=p_i\) for every client.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The intended client weights define one objective, while expected participation and aggregation weights define an effective objective. Their worst-case absolute difference over the domain is the participation-fairness distortion. A rule is fair when every expected effective client weight equals its intended weight; a tolerance boundary is the level set where distortion equals the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal D_X(p,q)=\sup_{x\in X}|\sum_i(q_i-p_i)F_i(x)|\), with fairness condition \(q=p\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If every \(F_i\) is differentiable, a gradient-level analogue is \(\mathcal G_X(p,q)=\sup_{x\in X}\|\sum_i(q_i-p_i)\nabla F_i(x)\|\); it is a separate distortion metric, not generally equivalent to \(\mathcal D_X=0\).
special_cases_latex: If clients are sampled with probabilities \(\pi_i>0\) and an unbiased Horvitz--Thompson aggregation is used, then the effective mean weights can satisfy \(q_i=p_i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(|F_i(x)|\le B_i\) on \(X\), then \(\mathcal D_X(p,q)\le\sum_i|q_i-p_i|B_i\).
boundary_notes: Equality of effective and intended objectives may occur even when \(q\ne p\) if the client functions are linearly redundant.
The definition does not assert demographic fairness, equal utility, or convergence.

notation.meaning: Random effective aggregation weight of client i in round t.

review_flags: No supplied source locator supports this exact named distortion-boundary definition.
standard_field_rationale: the definition formalizes the conventional distinction between intended and effective participation-weighted objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Participation-Fairness Distortion Boundary
Participation-Induced Objective Bias
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncorrected unequal participation reweights client objectives by their participation probabilities and can move stationary points away from those of the intended objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under uncorrected participation, client \(i\)'s long-run exposure is proportional to \(p_iq_i\). Normalizing gives
\[
\widetilde p_i=\frac{p_iq_i}{\sum_{j=1}^np_jq_j},
\qquad
\widetilde F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\widetilde p_iF_i(x).
\]
Thus \(\widetilde F=F\) whenever all \(q_i\) are equal. If the \(q_i\) are unequal and
\[
\sum_i(\widetilde p_i-p_i)\nabla F_i(x)\ne0
\]
at some differentiability point \(x\), the effective and intended objective gradients differ there, exhibiting participation-induced objective bias.
assumptions_latex: The target objective is \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n p_iF_i(x)\), where \(p_i>0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
Client \(i\) has long-run positive participation probability \(q_i\), and aggregation does not correct unequal inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The effective objective is \(\widetilde F(x)=\sum_i\widetilde p_iF_i(x)\), with \(\widetilde p_i=p_iq_i/(\sum_jp_jq_j)\), rather than \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Long-run exposure model for uncorrected unequal client participation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The weights p_iq_i arise only for a specified long-run aggregation/exposure model; merely saying that inclusion probabilities are uncorrected is insufficient because round-normalized aggregation can induce different weights. The plain statement additionally claims movement of stationary points, whereas the formula establishes only a gradient discrepancy at some point.

knowledge_statements.title: Client-Level Fairness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under loss parity, a model is client-fair when the largest difference between any clients' losses is at most the chosen tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the client-loss-parity sense, define the disparity
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{client}}(x)=
\max_{1\le i\le n}F_i(x)-
\min_{1\le i\le n}F_i(x).
\]
A model \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-client-fair when
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{client}}(x)\le\varepsilon.
\]
The case \(\varepsilon=0\) requires equal loss for every client. This condition evaluates disparity across clients and is distinct from minimizing the weighted mean \(\sum_i p_iF_i(x)\), which alone imposes no bound on \(\Delta_{\mathrm{client}}(x)\).
assumptions_latex: Each client has a finite real-valued loss \(F_i(x)\) at the evaluated model \(x\in X\).
A tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is \(\varepsilon\)-client-fair in loss parity exactly when \(\max_iF_i(x)-\min_iF_i(x)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss-parity version; other federated client-fairness notions require separate statements.

notation.meaning: Loss or risk of client i at the common model

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The loss-parity condition is precise and appropriately scoped, but client-level fairness has several inequivalent meanings and no citation establishes that this version is intended here.

knowledge_statements.title: Group Representation Fairness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group representation fairness requires each group's long-run participation exposure to remain within a tolerance of its declared target share.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The realized representation of group \(G\in\mathcal G\) is
\[
R_G=\sum_{i\in G}\rho_i.
\]
For prescribed target shares \(\pi_G\), group representation is \(\varepsilon\)-fair when
\[
\max_{G\in\mathcal G}|R_G-\pi_G|\le\varepsilon.
\]
Exact representation fairness corresponds to \(\varepsilon=0\). The targets may encode population shares, objective weights, or another declared policy, but they must be fixed independently of the realized participation whose fairness is being assessed.
assumptions_latex: Clients are partitioned into nonempty groups \(\mathcal G\), and client \(i\) receives normalized long-run exposure \(\rho_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_i\rho_i=1\).
Each group \(G\in\mathcal G\) has a target exposure \(\pi_G\ge0\), with \(\sum_G\pi_G=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Group representation is \(\varepsilon\)-fair exactly when \(\max_{G\in\mathcal G}|\sum_{i\in G}\rho_i-\pi_G|\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposure-parity condition relative to explicitly supplied group targets.

notation.meaning: Partition of clients into protected or operational groups
Normalized exposure assigned to client i

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The exposure-to-target condition is internally coherent and fits the leaf, but no source supports it as the intended group-representation fairness notion; the choice and interpretation of target shares are application dependent.

knowledge_statements.title: Fairness under Unequal Availability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse-availability selection realizes target client exposure only when no client's requested marginal exposure exceeds its availability probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The unconditional exposure of client \(i\) is \(q_is_i\). Exact availability-adjusted fairness with target shares \(p_i\) and expected budget \(m\) requires
\[
q_is_i=mp_i\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
Consequently the unique marginal correction is
\[
s_i=\frac{mp_i}{q_i}.
\]
A valid policy with \(s_i\in[0,1]\) exists if and only if \(mp_i\le q_i\) for every \(i\). If this inequality fails, the target exposure is unattainable without reducing \(m\), relaxing the targets, or changing availability.
assumptions_latex: Client \(i\) is available with marginal probability \(q_i>0\), has target exposure \(p_i>0\), and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
When available, client \(i\) is selected with conditional probability \(s_i\in[0,1]\), and the expected participation budget is \(m\in(0,\sum_iq_i]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact target exposure with budget \(m\) is feasible exactly when \(mp_i\le q_i\) for every client, using \(s_i=mp_i/q_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal-exposure feasibility under unequal availability and a fixed expected participation budget.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The marginal feasibility calculation is correct for the stated per-client conditional-selection model without joint capacity constraints, but no citation supports this particular formulation of fairness under unequal availability.

children.title: Federated Local-Update Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods trading local computation against communication frequency.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F_i(x)=\mathbb E_{\xi\sim\mathcal D_i}[f_i(x;\xi)]\) for clients \(i\in[M]\). At communication round \(t\), a server holds \(x_t\in\mathbb R^d\), selects \(S_t\subseteq[M]\), and assigns aggregation weights \(a_{t,i}\ge0\) summing to one over \(S_t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural definition covering synchronous methods that perform one or more client-side updates between server communications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A federated local-update method is specified by client maps \(U_{t,i}^{(K_{t,i})}:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\), each formed by composing \(K_{t,i}\ge1\) local update operators from the common initialization \(x_t\). Participating client \(i\) returns \(y_{t,i}=U_{t,i}^{(K_{t,i})}(x_t)\) or \(\Delta_{t,i}=y_{t,i}-x_t\), and the server applies an aggregation map \(x_{t+1}=A_t(x_t,\{y_{t,i}:i\in S_t\})\). The canonical weighted-average instance is \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{t,i}\Delta_{t,i}\). Communication occurs only before the local maps and after their returned updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A federated local-update method broadcasts a server model, lets each participating client compose one or more local optimization steps, and then aggregates the resulting models or displacements. The defining feature is that several client computations may occur without intervening server communication.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For affine server aggregation, model averaging and displacement averaging are equivalent: \(\sum_i a_{t,i}y_{t,i}=x_t+\sum_i a_{t,i}(y_{t,i}-x_t)\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(K_{t,i}=1\) gives a one-local-step federated stochastic-gradient method.
Taking deterministic local solvers yields a local-optimization rather than local-SGD instance.
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing \(K_{t,i}\) changes the amount of computation per communication round without changing the number of server aggregations.
boundary_notes: Asynchronous methods require a separate model of stale initializations and arrival times.
The definition does not require convexity or guarantee that local maps approximate the global objective.

notation.meaning: Composition of K local update operators at client i.

review_flags: The supplied books discuss distributed computation but no inspected locator establishes this exact federated definition.
standard_field_rationale: broadcast-local-compute-aggregate is the conventional structural template for federated local-update methods.

children.title: Federated SGD
children.top_down_role: Federated aggregation after short local stochastic computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Federated SGD
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Federated SGD aggregates one stochastic gradient from each selected client and corrects by the client's history-conditional inclusion probability, yielding the intended objective gradient in conditional expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in X\), stepsizes \(\eta_t>0\), weights \(p_i\), and a horizon \(T\), round \(t\) samples \(S_t\). Each \(i\in S_t\) draws \(\xi_{i,t}\) and returns \(g_i(x_t;\xi_{i,t})\). The server forms
\[
G_t=\sum_{i\in S_t}\frac{p_i}{q_{i,t}}g_i(x_t;\xi_{i,t}),
\qquad
x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tG_t.
\]
Under the stated history-conditional inclusion and oracle-unbiasedness assumptions,
\[
\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal H_t]=\nabla F(x_t).
\]
Stop after \(T\) rounds and output \(x_T\), or a prespecified average of the iterates.
assumptions_latex: The parameter domain \(X\) is a real vector space, \(p_i>0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\), and the differentiable objective is \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n p_iF_i(x)\).
Before sampling at round \(t\), the history \(\mathcal H_t\) contains \(x_t\), and \(q_{i,t}=\mathbb P(i\in S_t\mid\mathcal H_t)>0\).
For every client selected at round \(t\), \(\mathbb E[g_i(x_t;\xi_{i,t})\mid\mathcal H_t,\,i\in S_t]=\nabla F_i(x_t)\), and the displayed conditional expectations exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned iterate is generated by an inclusion-corrected stochastic-gradient update satisfying \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal H_t]=\nabla F(x_t)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-local-gradient, history-conditionally inclusion-corrected version of federated SGD.

notation.meaning: Common server model at round t
Stochastic gradient computed by client i
History-conditional inclusion probability of client i at round t
Information available before round-t client sampling

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For client objectives \(F_i(x)=\mathbb E[f_i(x;\xi_i)]\), let \(g_i(x;\xi)\) be a stochastic gradient or subgradient. In round \(t\), the server broadcasts \(x_t\) to participating clients \(S_t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous one- or short-step stochastic client computation followed by a server average; no convergence assumptions are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Federated SGD with \(K\ge1\) local stochastic steps initializes \(x_{t,i}^{0}=x_t\) and, for each \(i\in S_t\), sets \(x_{t,i}^{k+1}=x_{t,i}^{k}-\eta_{t,k}g_i(x_{t,i}^{k};\xi_{t,i}^{k})\) for \(k=0,\ldots,K-1\). The server update is \(x_{t+1}=\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{t,i}x_{t,i}^{K}\), where \(a_{t,i}\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{t,i}=1\). Equivalently, \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{t,i}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\eta_{t,k}g_i(x_{t,i}^{k};\xi_{t,i}^{k})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Federated SGD starts each selected client from the current server model, performs a fixed short sequence of stochastic-gradient steps on that client's data, and averages the resulting client models. Expanding the local recursions gives the equivalent aggregate of all local stochastic-gradient increments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}=\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{t,i}x_{t,i}^{K}=x_t-\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{t,i}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\eta_{t,k}g_i(x_{t,i}^{k};\xi_{t,i}^{k})\).
special_cases_latex: Uniform aggregation uses \(a_{t,i}=1/|S_t|\).
Full participation uses \(S_t=[M]\).
immediate_consequences_latex: When \(K>1\), later stochastic gradients are evaluated at client-specific iterates rather than at the common server model.
boundary_notes: Some literature reserves the name Federated SGD for \(K=1\); this record explicitly includes the stated short-local-computation convention.
Mini-batches can replace individual samples without changing the recursion.

Client stochastic gradient or subgradient oracle.

children.title: Local SGD and Periodic Averaging
children.top_down_role: Multiple local stochastic updates between global aggregations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M\) workers maintain \(x_i^s\in\mathbb R^d\) at local-step time \(s\). Let \(g_i^s\) be a stochastic gradient and let \(\mathcal A=\{\tau_1,\tau_2,\ldots\}\subset\mathbb N\) be synchronization times.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous local SGD with periodic exact averaging and a common local-step clock.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The periodic-averaging calculus is defined by provisional steps \(z_i^{s+1}=x_i^s-\eta_sg_i^s\), followed by \(x_i^{s+1}=z_i^{s+1}\) when \(s+1\notin\mathcal A\), and \(x_i^{s+1}=\sum_{j=1}^M p_jz_j^{s+1}\) for every \(i\) when \(s+1\in\mathcal A\), where \(p\in\Delta_M\). With \(\bar x^s=\sum_i p_ix_i^s\), the mean recursion is \(\bar x^{s+1}=\bar x^s-\eta_s\sum_i p_ig_i^s\), while synchronization enforces \(x_i^{s+1}=\bar x^{s+1}\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every worker takes stochastic-gradient steps independently between synchronization times. At a synchronization time, all provisional worker models are replaced by their weighted average. The weighted mean always follows the aggregate-gradient recursion, and the worker deviations reset to zero after averaging.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x^{s+1}=\bar x^s-\eta_s\sum_i p_ig_i^s\), and \(x_i^{s+1}-\bar x^{s+1}=0\) whenever \(s+1\in\mathcal A\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a constant period \(H\), one may take \(\mathcal A=\{H,2H,3H,\ldots\}\).
special_cases_latex: \(H=1\) gives synchronized mini-batch SGD.
A single synchronization only at termination gives independent local training followed by one-shot averaging.
immediate_consequences_latex: Between synchronization times, the disagreement variables \(e_i^s=x_i^s-\bar x^s\) need not vanish.
boundary_notes: This definition uses exact synchronous averaging; decentralized mixing and asynchronous averaging are different calculi.
Unequal numbers of local steps require client-specific clocks or masking variables.
review_flags: No inspected source locator supports this exact periodic-averaging recursion in the federated setting.
standard_field_rationale: the provisional-step/averaging recursion is standard for local SGD.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-SGD Periodic-Averaging Recursion
Local SGD Dynamics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each selected client starts from the common model, takes a prescribed number of local stochastic-gradient steps, and returns its final model or displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every participating client \(i\in S_t\), initialize
\[
x_{i,t,0}=x_t.
\]
For \(k=0,\ldots,K_t-1\), independently sample local data \(\xi_{i,t,k}\) and update
\[
x_{i,t,k+1}=x_{i,t,k}-\eta_{t,k}g_i(x_{i,t,k};\xi_{i,t,k}).
\]
After completing \(K_t\) steps, client \(i\) transmits \(x_{i,t,K_t}\) or the equivalent displacement \(x_{i,t,K_t}-x_t\). The local phase itself performs no inter-client communication; synchronization is a separate aggregation operation.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Periodic model averaging replaces selected clients' local endpoints by a weighted common model after every block of local updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Interval Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication regimes are determined by whether the number of local updates between averaging events is one, uniformly bounded, or unbounded over time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A communication-interval schedule is a sequence \((K_r)_{r\ge0}\) of positive integers. It is unit-communication when \(K_r=1\) for all \(r\), bounded-period when
\[
1<\sup_rK_r<\infty,
\]
and growing-period when \(\sup_rK_r=
\infty\). Define
\[
T_R=
\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}K_r,
\qquad
R(T)=
\max\{R:T_R\le T\}.
\]
Then \(R(T)\) is the number of completed averaging events within \(T\) local updates, making the computation--communication tradeoff explicit without itself imposing convergence conditions.
assumptions_latex: Let \(K_r\in\mathbb N_{+}\) be the number of local updates between synchronization events \(r\) and \(r+1\).
Let \(T_R=\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}K_r\) denote the number of local updates completed through \(R\) communication intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Communication schedules are classified as unit, bounded, or growing according to the sequence \((K_r)\), with communication count determined by \(R(T)=\max\{R:T_R\le T\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule classification only; no convergence rate is asserted.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Update Drift Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With uniformly bounded local update directions, a client is at most eta times k times G from the synchronized model after k steps, and its maximum within-round drift is at most eta times K times G. This bound is sharp without further assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every client \(i\) and every \(k\in\{0,\ldots,K\}\), the within-round drift satisfies \[\lVert x_i^k-x\rVert\le \eta kG.\] In particular, \[\max_{0\le k\le K}\lVert x_i^k-x\rVert\le \eta KG.\] This dependence on \(\eta\), \(K\), and \(G\) is sharp under the bounded-direction assumption alone.
assumptions_latex: Each client objective \(F_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.
During one round, client \(i\) starts from \(x\) and performs \(K\) updates \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k-\eta g_i^k\), with \(x_i^0=x\).
The local directions satisfy \(\lVert g_i^k\rVert\le G\) for \(0\le k<K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x_i^k-x\rVert\le \eta kG\) for every \(0\le k\le K\); hence the worst-case within-round drift is at most \(\eta KG\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic within-round boundary under uniformly bounded local directions.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let client \(i\) own \(n_i\) examples and empirical loss \(F_i\). During round \(t\), the server sends \(x_t\) to clients \(S_t\); client \(i\) runs a local training operator \(U_{t,i}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Federated Averaging defines \(y_{t,i}=U_{t,i}(x_t)\) for \(i\in S_t\) and updates \(x_{t+1}=\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{t,i}y_{t,i}\), where \(a_{t,i}\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{t,i}=1\). When \(U_{t,i}\) consists of \(E\) local epochs of mini-batch SGD, the returned model is the endpoint of those local epochs, not an independently fitted minimizer unless the local routine is run to that condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Participation Federated Averaging
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampled client subset performs local work, while inverse-inclusion weighting makes the aggregate displacement unbiased for the corresponding full-client displacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Federated Server Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The server treats the aggregated client displacement as an update direction, smooths its first and second moments, and applies coordinatewise adaptive scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(m_0=v_0=0\). After aggregating client displacements into \(\Delta_t\), set \[m_{t+1}=\beta_1m_t+(1-\beta_1)\Delta_t,\qquad v_{t+1}=\beta_2v_t+(1-\beta_2)(\Delta_t\odot\Delta_t),\] and update \[x^{t+1}=x^t+\gamma_t\,m_{t+1}\oslash(\sqrt{v_{t+1}}+\epsilon).\] Server momentum is obtained by omitting adaptive scaling; other adaptive federated server methods replace the moment recursions or diagonal preconditioner. Output the final server iterate.

Parameters satisfy \(0\le\beta_1<1\), \(0\le\beta_2<1\), \(\gamma_t>0\), and \(\epsilon>0\).
Squares, square roots, and division are interpreted coordinatewise.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_i p_iF_i(x)\). During round \(t\), client \(i\) starts at \(x_t\) and would ordinarily use a local stochastic direction \(g_i(x;\xi)\), whose mean may differ from the global direction because the client objectives are heterogeneous.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general algebraic class of local-update methods that add a correction intended to offset client-specific drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A federated drift-correction method associates a correction field \(r_{t,i}:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) with each participating client and uses \(x_{t,i}^{k+1}=x_{t,i}^{k}-\eta_{t,k}(g_i(x_{t,i}^{k};\xi_{t,i}^{k})+r_{t,i}(x_{t,i}^{k}))\), initialized by \(x_{t,i}^{0}=x_t\). The correction is mean-aligned at a reference point \(z\) when \(\mathbb E[g_i(z;\xi)+r_{t,i}(z)]=\nabla F(z)\). Control-variate correction is the special form \(r_{t,i}=c_t-c_{t,i}\); proximal stabilization is represented by \(r_{t,i}(x)=\mu(x-x_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A drift-correction method modifies each local stochastic direction by an explicit correction field. At a reference point, exact mean alignment means the corrected expected client direction equals the global gradient. Control variates and proximal anchoring are different members of this broad family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t,i}^{k+1}=x_{t,i}^{k}-\eta_{t,k}(g_i(x_{t,i}^{k};\xi_{t,i}^{k})+r_{t,i}(x_{t,i}^{k}))\), with exact reference-point alignment defined by equality to \(\nabla F(z)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(b_{t,i}=-r_{t,i}\) yields the equivalent corrected direction \(g_i-b_{t,i}\).
special_cases_latex: \(r_{t,i}=0\) recovers an uncorrected local-update method.
\(r_{t,i}=c_t-c_{t,i}\) gives a client/server control-variate form.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact alignment at \(z\) does not imply alignment at later client iterates.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require the correction to be unbiased or guarantee reduced drift.
Server-only momentum is excluded unless it also modifies client local directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal term convexifies a rho-weakly convex client loss once its strength reaches rho, and yields strong convexity when its strength exceeds rho.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Expanding the centered quadratic shows that \(h_{i,t}\) differs by an affine function and a constant from \(F_i(w)+(\mu/2)\lVert w\rVert^2\). Consequently, if \(F_i\) is \(\rho_i\)-weakly convex, then \(h_{i,t}\) is \((\mu-\rho_i)\)-strongly convex for \(\mu>\rho_i\), convex for \(\mu=\rho_i\), and is not guaranteed convex for \(0\le\mu<\rho_i\). Thus \(\mu=\rho_i\) is the clientwise convexification boundary.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A client solve is relatively inexact when its final proximal-gradient residual is at most a prescribed fraction of the residual at the broadcast model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Client \(i\)'s returned point \(w_i^{t,+}\) is a \(\gamma_{i,t}\)-inexact solution of its round-\(t\) proximal subproblem when \[\lVert\nabla h_{i,t}(w_i^{t,+})\rVert\le\gamma_{i,t}\lVert\nabla h_{i,t}(x^t)\rVert,\qquad 0\le\gamma_{i,t}\le1.\] The case \(\gamma_{i,t}=0\) requires first-order stationarity, whereas larger values permit earlier termination. This criterion is relative to the residual at the broadcast initialization and does not itself bound distance to a minimizer without additional curvature.

The client starts its solver at the broadcast model \(x^t\).

children.title: SCAFFOLD Control-Variate Correction Family
children.top_down_role: Client and server correction variables for local drift.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: The server holds a model \(x_t\) and control vector \(c_t\in\mathbb R^d\); client \(i\) stores \(c_{t,i}\in\mathbb R^d\). Participating clients initialize \(x_{t,i}^{0}=x_t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous SCAFFOLD-type local stochastic updates with persistent client and server control variates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A SCAFFOLD local step is \(x_{t,i}^{k+1}=x_{t,i}^{k}-\eta_{t,k}(g_i(x_{t,i}^{k};\xi_{t,i}^{k})-c_{t,i}+c_t)\). After \(K_{t,i}\) steps, client \(i\) returns \(y_{t,i}=x_{t,i}^{K_{t,i}}\) and an updated control \(c_{t+1,i}=C_{t,i}(c_{t,i},c_t,x_t,y_{t,i})\); nonparticipating clients retain their controls. The server aggregates models and control increments, for example \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{t,i}(y_{t,i}-x_t)\) and \(c_{t+1}=c_t+\sum_{i\in S_t}b_{t,i}(c_{t+1,i}-c_{t,i})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SCAFFOLD corrects every local stochastic gradient by subtracting a persistent client control and adding a server control. Clients return both a model displacement and a control update; the server updates both global states, while unselected clients keep their stored controls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The corrected local direction is \(g_i-c_{t,i}+c_t\), with persistent client-control and server-control recursions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The additive drift-correction field is \(r_{t,i}=c_t-c_{t,i}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c_t=c_{t,i}=0\), the local recursion reduces to uncorrected local SGD.
If \(c_{t,i}\) exactly represents a client gradient and \(c_t\) their target-weighted mean at the same point, the corrected mean direction is globally aligned there.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method's state includes all stored client controls, including controls of currently inactive clients.
boundary_notes: The client-control map \(C_{t,i}\) distinguishes algorithmic options and must be specified by an implementation.
The definition does not assert exact variance reduction or convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: SCAFFOLD Control-Variate Correction Family
SCAFFOLD Correction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SCAFFOLD corrects each local stochastic gradient by subtracting a client control and adding a server control, then updates both controls after local work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x^0\), \(c^0\), and \(c_i^0\). In round \(t\), selected client \(i\) sets \(y_i^{t,0}=x^t\) and performs \[y_i^{t,k+1}=y_i^{t,k}-\eta\bigl(g_i(y_i^{t,k};\xi_i^{t,k})-c_i^t+c^t\bigr),\qquad 0\le k<K_i.\] It returns \(y_i^{t,K_i}-x^t\) and updates \[c_i^{t+1}=c_i^t-c^t+\frac{x^t-y_i^{t,K_i}}{K_i\eta}.\] The server aggregates the returned model displacements and control changes, then outputs its final model.
assumptions_latex: Client \(i\) has differentiable objective \(F_i\), client control \(c_i^t\), and server control \(c^t\).
The client starts round \(t\) from \(y_i^{t,0}=x^t\) and performs \(K_i\ge1\) steps with stepsize \(\eta>0\).
The server aggregates returned model and control changes with specified weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The corrected local direction is \(g_i(y;\xi)-c_i^t+c^t\), with client and server controls updated after local work.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SCAFFOLD local correction with the displacement-based client-control update.

notation.meaning: Client i and server control variates.

review_flags: original SCAFFOLD source required for exact client-control update variants and server scaling

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The corrected direction and displacement-based client-control update are coherent SCAFFOLD formulas, but exact control-update and server-aggregation conventions vary. The named algorithm requires an authoritative SCAFFOLD citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Client Control Variates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A client's new control can be computed directly from its old control, the server control, and its average model displacement during local work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the displacement-based SCAFFOLD update, client \(i\) sets \[c_i^{t+1}=c_i^t-c^t+\frac{x^t-y_i^{t,K_i}}{K_i\eta}.\] Equivalently, \[c_i^{t+1}-c_i^t=-c^t+\frac{1}{K_i}\sum_{k=0}^{K_i-1}\bigl(g_i(y_i^{t,k};\xi_i^{t,k})-c_i^t+c^t\bigr),\] because the corrected local recursion telescopes. The returned control increment is stored by the client and communicated to the server when the protocol requires control aggregation.
assumptions_latex: Client \(i\) performs \(K_i\ge1\) corrected local steps of common size \(\eta>0\) from \(x^t\).
Its old client control is \(c_i^t\), and the broadcast server control is \(c^t\).
The returned local endpoint is \(y_i^{t,K_i}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displacement-based update satisfies \(c_i^{t+1}=c_i^t-c^t+(x^t-y_i^{t,K_i})/(K_i\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Displacement representation of the SCAFFOLD client control update.

notation.meaning: Client i control variate before and after the round.
Server control variate broadcast in round t.
Initial server model and final local model.

The statement also includes a telescoping justification that should be removed once the sourced variant is established.

knowledge_statements.title: Server Control Variates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The server control is advanced by aggregating participating clients' control changes; under full participation it remains the mean of all client controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a server control \(c^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At round \(t\), receive \(\Delta c_i^t=c_i^{t+1}-c_i^t\) from each \(i\in S_t\) and set \[c^{t+1}=c^t+\alpha_t\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{i,t}\Delta c_i^t.\] Under full participation with \(a_{i,t}=1/n\), \(\alpha_t=1\), and \(c^0=n^{-1}\sum_i c_i^0\), the invariant \[c^t=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^t\] is preserved. The updated control is broadcast in the next participating round.
assumptions_latex: The server stores \(c^t\), and client \(i\) stores \(c_i^t\).
A participating set \(S_t\) returns control increments \(\Delta c_i^t=c_i^{t+1}-c_i^t\).
Aggregation weights \(a_{i,t}\ge0\) and a server control stepsize \(\alpha_t>0\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The server update is \(c^{t+1}=c^t+\alpha_t\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{i,t}\Delta c_i^t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Server aggregation of participating clients' control-variate increments.

notation.meaning: Server control variate before and after round t.
Control aggregation weight and server stepsize.

review_flags: SCAFFOLD sources use convention-dependent normalization under partial participation

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The full-participation mean invariant is correct under the stated initialization and weights, but the general alpha-weighted partial-participation update is convention-dependent and is not supported by a citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Drift-Cancellation Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proper client and server controls remove inter-client gradient disagreement exactly at synchronization; during local motion, the remaining error is bounded by gradient smoothness times displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i f_i\), where \(p_i>0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and fix a synchronization point \(x\). Suppose the client and server controls satisfy \(c_i-c=
abla f_i(x)-
abla F(x)\). The corrected client direction at a local point \(y\) is
\[d_i(y)=
abla f_i(y)-c_i+c=
abla F(x)+
abla f_i(y)-
abla f_i(x).\]
Consequently, \(d_i(x)=
abla F(x)\) for every client. If each \(f_i\) has an \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradient, then
\[\lVert d_i(y)-
abla F(x)Vert\le L_i\lVert y-xVert,\]
so cancellation is exact at synchronization and degrades only with local displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i f_i(x)\), with \(p_i>0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
\(c_i-c=\nabla f_i(x)-\nabla F(x)\).
Each \(\nabla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz when the residual bound is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_i(x)=\nabla F(x)\) and \(\lVert d_i(y)-\nabla F(x)\rVert\le L_i\lVert y-x\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SCAFFOLD-style cancellation at a synchronized model, with residual drift away from that model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic control-variate cancellation under the displayed calibration identity

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cancellation identity and Lipschitz residual bound are algebraically correct, and property fits the leaf. A specific SCAFFOLD-family source is needed to substantiate the stated calibration regime and terminology.

children.title: Federated Update Calibration Family
children.top_down_role: Corrections for unequal local work, sampling, or client weights.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Client \(i\) participates in round \(t\) with indicator \(I_{t,i}\), inclusion probability \(\pi_{t,i}=\Pr(I_{t,i}=1)>0\), target weight \(p_i\), local-step count \(K_{t,i}\), and returned displacement \(\Delta_{t,i}\in\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear correction of aggregate client displacements for sampling, target weights, or unequal local work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear federated update calibration rule chooses measurable coefficients \(w_{t,i}\) and optionally normalization maps \(N_{t,i}\) and forms \(\widehat\Delta_t=\sum_{i=1}^M I_{t,i}w_{t,i}N_{t,i}(\Delta_{t,i})\), followed by \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t\widehat\Delta_t\). Sampling calibration is exact for fixed vectors \(u_i\) when \(\mathbb E[\sum_i I_{t,i}w_{t,i}u_i]=\sum_i p_iu_i\), equivalently \(\mathbb E[I_{t,i}w_{t,i}]=p_i\) clientwise. Work calibration may use \(N_{t,i}(\Delta)=\Delta/K_{t,i}\) to convert accumulated displacement into a per-local-step quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A calibration rule transforms and reweights client displacements before aggregation. Exact sampling calibration requires every client's expected realized coefficient to equal its target weight. A separate normalization may divide by local work so updates produced by different numbers of client steps represent comparable per-step quantities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\Delta_t=\sum_iI_{t,i}w_{t,i}N_{t,i}(\Delta_{t,i})\), with exact sampling calibration condition \(\mathbb E[I_{t,i}w_{t,i}]=p_i\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(w_{t,i}=p_i/\pi_{t,i}\), then the coefficient condition holds whenever \(\pi_{t,i}>0\).
special_cases_latex: Setting \(N_{t,i}\) to the identity performs sampling-only calibration.
Full participation with \(w_{t,i}=p_i\) needs no inclusion-probability correction.
immediate_consequences_latex: A client with \(p_i>0\) and \(\pi_{t,i}=0\) cannot be unbiasedly represented by finite inverse-probability weighting in that round.
boundary_notes: Dividing a nonlinear local-training displacement by its step count does not generally make it an unbiased gradient.
Self-normalized weights usually sacrifice exact unbiasedness for a convex-combination update.
review_flags: The named umbrella family and combined calibration definition lack a verified source.
standard_field_rationale: inverse-probability weighting and per-work normalization are standard statistical calibration devices.
knowledge_statements.title: Federated Update Calibration Family
Normalized Client Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide each client displacement by its accumulated local step size. The result is an average direction whose scale does not grow mechanically with local step count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At round \(t\), client \(i\) initializes \(y_{i,0}=x_t\) and performs \(\tau_i\ge1\) steps
\[y_{i,k+1}=y_{i,k}-\eta_{i,k}g_{i,k},\qquad 0\le k<\tau_i.\]
Its displacement is \(\Delta_i=x_t-y_{i,\tau_i}=\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}\eta_{i,k}g_{i,k}\). Given a positive normalizer \(a_i=\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}\eta_{i,k}\), the normalized client update is
\[u_i=\frac{\Delta_i}{a_i}=\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}\frac{\eta_{i,k}}{a_i}g_{i,k}.\]
Thus \(u_i\) is a step-size-weighted average direction; for constant \(\eta_{i,k}=\eta_i\), it equals \(\tau_i^{-1}\sum_k g_{i,k}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_i\ge1\) and \(\eta_{i,k}>0\).
All local iterates and directions lie in the same Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_i=\Delta_i/a_i\) is a convex combination of the local directions \(g_{i,k}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization converts variable-length local model displacements into average local directions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalization follows directly from telescoping local descent steps

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The normalization definition follows correctly from the local-step recursion and matches the leaf, but no inspectable source supports its placement as a federated update-calibration concept.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Work Reweighting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weight each displacement inversely by its local steps and step size, then apply the intended client weight. This prevents extra local work from automatically increasing client influence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let client \(i\) have target weight \(p_i\), local length \(\tau_i\), constant step size \(\eta_i>0\), and displacement \(\Delta_i=\eta_i\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}g_{i,k}\). The target-weighted average of client-average directions has the representation
\[\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\left(\frac1{\tau_i}\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}g_{i,k}\right)=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{p_i}{\eta_i\tau_i}\Delta_i.\]
Hence a server step \(x^+=x-\gamma\sum_i p_i\Delta_i/(\eta_i\tau_i)\) removes the purely multiplicative influence of unequal local step counts and step sizes while retaining the prescribed client weights.
assumptions_latex: Client \(i\) uses a constant local step size \(\eta_i\) during the round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i p_i\tau_i^{-1}\sum_k g_{i,k}=\sum_i p_i\Delta_i/(\eta_i\tau_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reweighting separates intended client importance from heterogeneous amounts of local work.

notation.meaning: intended objective weight of client i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact algebraic reweighting of telescoped local updates

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The displayed representation is exact for constant client-specific step sizes, and representation is an acceptable role here. A source is required for the claimed federated local-work calibration interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Probability Correction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide each participating client’s target-weighted update by its inclusion probability. The aggregate is unbiased, provided every relevant client can be selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be a random participating set with inclusion probabilities \(q_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\). For fixed client vectors \(u_i\) and target weights \(p_i\), define
\[\widehat u=\sum_{i\in S}\frac{p_i}{q_i}u_i.\]
Then
\[\mathbb E[\widehat u]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_i.\]
This identity requires only the marginal inclusion probabilities; independence of client selections is unnecessary. If some \(q_i=0\) while \(p_i u_i\ne0\), no estimator based solely on observed participating updates can recover that missing term without additional structural information.
assumptions_latex: \(u_i\) is fixed, or conditionally fixed, when \(S\) is sampled.
\(q_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\) whenever \(p_i u_i\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widehat u]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Horvitz–Thompson correction for randomly participating clients with known inclusion probabilities.

notation.meaning: marginal inclusion probability of client i

review_flags: verify that the locator explicitly covers inverse-probability correction

knowledge_statements.title: Client-Weight Calibration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate matches the intended client-weighted target for every possible update exactly when each server coefficient times its inclusion probability equals the target client weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a random client set with \(q_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\), and let the server form \(\widehat u=\sum_{i\in S}a_i u_i\), where \(a_i\) is deterministic conditional on the sampling design. For arbitrary fixed vectors \(u_1,\ldots,u_n\), the calibration condition
\[\mathbb E[\widehat u]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_i\]
holds if and only if
\[q_i a_i=p_i\qquad\text{for every }i.\]
Thus \(a_i=p_i/q_i\). Under full participation, \(q_i=1\), this reduces to the prescribed objective weights \(a_i=p_i\).
assumptions_latex: \(q_i>0\) for every client with \(p_i\ne0\).
The coefficients \(a_i\) do not depend on the realized value of \(u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\sum_{i\in S}a_i u_i]=\sum_i p_i u_i\) for all \((u_i)\) if and only if \(a_i=p_i/q_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient coefficient calibration for an unbiased target-weighted client aggregate.

notation.meaning: server coefficient applied when client i participates

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coefficient matching follows from linearity and arbitrary test vectors

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: For fixed coefficients and arbitrary client vectors, the stated coefficient-matching condition is correct and condition is the appropriate content kind. No source is supplied for this federated calibration characterization.

children.title: Federated Client Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection and weighting mechanisms for partial client participation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: There are \(M\) clients. At round \(t\), the server observes an information state \(\mathcal H_t\), chooses a random subset \(S_t\subseteq[M]\), and aggregates returned client quantities \(u_{t,i}\in\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection and aggregation weighting for partial participation, including randomized, availability-aware, and state-dependent policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A federated client-selection mechanism is a conditional distribution \(P_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal H_t)\) on subsets of \([M]\), together with aggregation coefficients \(w_{t,i}(S_t,\mathcal H_t)\). Its inclusion probabilities are \(\pi_{t,i}=\Pr(i\in S_t\mid\mathcal H_t)\), and its aggregate is \(\widehat u_t=\sum_{i\in S_t}w_{t,i}u_{t,i}\). The mechanism is target-unbiased for weights \(p\in\Delta_M\) when, for every collection of \(\mathcal H_t\)-measurable vectors \(u_{t,i}\), \(\mathbb E_t[\widehat u_t]=\sum_i p_iu_{t,i}\); clientwise, this is ensured by \(\mathbb E_t[\mathbf1\{i\in S_t\}w_{t,i}]=p_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A client-selection mechanism specifies a conditional law over participating subsets and the weights applied to their returned updates. Its marginal inclusion probabilities describe participation. Target-unbiasedness means that, conditionally on the available history, the expected aggregate equals the desired full-client weighted aggregate for arbitrary fixed client vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\sim P_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal H_t)\) and \(\widehat u_t=\sum_{i\in S_t}w_{t,i}u_{t,i}\), with unbiasedness condition \(\mathbb E_t[\mathbf1\{i\in S_t\}w_{t,i}]=p_i\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For positive inclusion probabilities, inverse-probability coefficients \(w_{t,i}=p_i/\pi_{t,i}\) satisfy the clientwise condition.
special_cases_latex: Uniform fixed-size sampling chooses every subset of a given cardinality with equal probability.
Availability-aware selection restricts the conditional distribution to currently available clients.
immediate_consequences_latex: Selection probabilities and aggregation weights jointly determine the effective expected client contribution.
boundary_notes: Adaptive selection can be statistically dependent on past updates without violating the conditional definition.
Unbiased selection does not imply equal participation frequency or fairness under other criteria.

notation.meaning: Information available when selecting clients in round t.
Conditional inclusion probability of client i.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Client Sampling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose every fixed-size client subset with equal probability. Each client has inclusion probability m/n, and the sample mean estimates the population mean without bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\) clients and an integer \(m\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), uniform client sampling without replacement draws a subset \(S\) uniformly from all \(m\)-element subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Thus
\[\mathbb P(S=A)=\binom{n}{m}^{-1}\quad\text{for every }A\text{ with }|A|=m,\qquad \mathbb P(i\in S)=\frac mn.\]
For fixed vectors \(u_i\), the sample mean \(\widehat u=m^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}u_i\) satisfies
\[\mathbb E[\widehat u]=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n u_i.\]
assumptions_latex: \(1\le m\le n\).
The vectors \(u_i\) are fixed, or conditionally fixed, before sampling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(i\in S)=m/n\) and \(\mathbb E[m^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}u_i]=n^{-1}\sum_i u_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-size uniform sampling without replacement from a finite client population.
review_flags: verify finite-population sampling coverage at the locator

children.title: Information-Aware Client Sampling Family
children.top_down_role: Selection weighted by statistical or optimization information.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m\ge 1\) clients have differentiable local objectives \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), target weights \(p_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1\), and round-\(t\) information \(\mathcal I_t\). Let \(S_t\) be a random client subset and \(q_{i,t}=\mathbb P(i\in S_t\mid\mathcal I_t)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-client, round-based federated optimization; the definition covers adaptive statistical or optimization information but excludes purely resource-driven selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An information-aware client-sampling rule is a measurable map \(\Pi_t:\mathcal I_t\mapsto\mathcal P(2^{[m]})\) whose inclusion probabilities satisfy \(q_{i,t}>0\) whenever \(p_i>0\), and for which at least one \(q_{i,t}\) depends on an optimization-relevant statistic in \(\mathcal I_t\), such as \(f_i(x_t)\), \(\|g_{i,t}\|\), a loss decrease, uncertainty score, or an estimator of update variance. If an unbiased aggregate is required, sampled updates \(u_{i,t}\in\mathbb R^d\) are combined as \(\widehat u_t=\sum_{i\in S_t}(p_i/q_{i,t})u_{i,t}\), so that \(\mathbb E[\widehat u_t\mid\mathcal I_t,(u_{i,t})_{i=1}^m]=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i u_{i,t}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An information-aware rule assigns a conditional distribution to the participating-client subset using currently available optimization or statistical information. Every target client must retain positive inclusion probability. When preservation of the target weighted update is part of the interface, each sampled update is multiplied by its target weight divided by its inclusion probability, yielding a conditionally unbiased aggregate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_t\) is information-aware precisely through its measurable dependence on optimization-relevant \(\mathcal I_t\), with optional Horvitz--Thompson aggregate \(\widehat u_t=\sum_{i\in S_t}(p_i/q_{i,t})u_{i,t}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For singleton sampling, \(\mathbb P(I_t=i\mid\mathcal I_t)=q_{i,t}\), \(\sum_iq_{i,t}=1\), and \(\widehat u_t=(p_{I_t}/q_{I_t,t})u_{I_t,t}\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(q_{i,t}\propto p_i\|g_{i,t}\|\) gives a gradient-norm-informed rule whenever the norms are available and nonzero.
immediate_consequences_latex: Conditional unbiasedness separates information-aware sampling from any bias introduced by omitting the factors \(p_i/q_{i,t}\).
boundary_notes: Dependence only on availability, latency, energy, or bandwidth belongs to resource-aware selection unless optimization information also enters the probabilities.
The definition imposes no convergence or variance-optimality guarantee.

notation.meaning: Information available when the round-t sampling distribution is chosen.
Conditional inclusion probability of client i.

knowledge_statements.title: Information-aware client sampling
Importance-Weighted Client Sampling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse-probability weighting preserves the target mean. When at least one weighted update is nonzero, sampling in proportion to weighted update norms minimizes the second moment; when all weighted updates vanish, every sampling distribution is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_i\ge0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\), and let \(u_i\in\mathbb R^d\) be fixed. Let \(q_i\ge0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n q_i=1\), with \(q_i>0\) whenever \(p_i\lVert u_i\rVert>0\). Draw \(I\) with probabilities \(q_i\) and define
\[G=\frac{p_I}{q_I}u_I.\]
Then
\[\mathbb E[G]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_i,\qquad \mathbb E\lVert G\rVert^2=\sum_{i:q_i>0}\frac{p_i^2\lVert u_i\rVert^2}{q_i}.\]
Set \(Z=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\lVert u_j\rVert\). If \(Z>0\), the second moment is minimized by
\[q_i=\frac{p_i\lVert u_i\rVert}{Z}\]
for indices with \(p_i\lVert u_i\rVert>0\), with zero probability assigned to the remaining indices. If \(Z=0\), the target and second moment are zero, and every sampling distribution is optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(u_i\in\mathbb R^d\), \(p_i\ge0\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\).
\(q_i\ge0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n q_i=1\), and \(q_i>0\) whenever \(p_i\lVert u_i\rVert>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G]=\sum_i p_i u_i\); if \(Z>0\), the minimum second moment is attained by \(q_i\propto p_i\lVert u_i\rVert\), while if \(Z=0\), every sampling distribution is optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-client importance sampling with unbiased weighting and second-moment-optimal probabilities, including the zero-update degenerate case.
review_flags: verify that optimal importance probabilities are stated at the locator

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Aware Client Sampling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert positive client-data scores into sampling probabilities, sample clients accordingly, and inverse-weight their updates so data-aware selection does not change the intended aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given target weights \(p_i\), client vectors \(u_i\), and positive data scores \(s_i=s(D_i)>0\), set
\[q_i=\frac{s_i}{\sum_{j=1}^n s_j}.\]
Draw one client \(I\sim q\), obtain its update \(u_I\), and output \(G=(p_I/q_I)u_I\). For a minibatch of \(m\) independent draws, output the average of the \(m\) corrected vectors. Stop after the prescribed number of communication rounds and return the current server iterate. Conditional on the scores and client updates,
\[\mathbb E[G]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_i.\]
Thus data statistics alter sampling frequency without changing the target aggregate when correction is retained.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i=s(D_i)>0\) for every client with \(p_i u_i\ne0\).
Scores and updates are conditionally fixed when sampling occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[(p_I/q_I)u_I]=\sum_i p_i u_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Client sampling driven by positive data-derived scores, with inverse-probability aggregation.

notation.meaning: client i's local dataset or data summary

knowledge_statements.title: Loss-Aware Client Sampling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample high-loss clients more often while retaining exploration, then inverse-weight selected updates. Conditional unbiasedness is preserved when losses are fixed before selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At round \(t\), let \(\ell_{i,t}\ge0\) be a client loss estimate available before selection, choose \(\varepsilon>0\), and define
\[q_{i,t}=\frac{p_i(\ell_{i,t}+\varepsilon)}{\sum_{j=1}^n p_j(\ell_{j,t}+\varepsilon)}.\]
Draw \(I_t\sim q_t\), obtain update \(u_{I_t,t}\), and use \(G_t=(p_{I_t}/q_{I_t,t})u_{I_t,t}\) in the server update. Repeat until the round budget or stopping criterion is met. Conditional on the preselection history and fixed client updates,
\[\mathbb E[G_t]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_{i,t}.\]
The exploration constant ensures positive probability for every positively weighted client.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i>0\), \(\ell_{i,t}\ge0\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
The loss scores are measurable before round-\(t\) client selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{i,t}>0\) and \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=\sum_i p_i u_{i,t}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive sampling based on reported client losses, with explicit exploration and bias correction.

notation.meaning: preselection loss score for client i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: adaptive score sampling with predictable probabilities and inverse weighting
specific loss-aware federated sampling source required

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The exact loss-based probability rule requires a source. Moreover, the conditional-unbiasedness conclusion requires the candidate updates to be measurable with respect to the preselection history, which is stated informally but omitted from the formal assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Bias Correction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logged preselection probabilities and inverse weights certify conditional unbiasedness. The certificate is invalid when relevant clients have zero probability or probabilities depend on post-selection information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F_t\) contain all information available before round-\(t\) selection, and let \(q_{i,t}=\mathbb P(I_t=i\mid\mathcal F_t)>0\). For target weights \(p_i\) and \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable candidate updates \(u_{i,t}\), define
\[G_t=\frac{p_{I_t}}{q_{I_t,t}}u_{I_t,t}.\]
The verifiable identities \(q_{i,t}>0\) and
\[\sum_{i=1}^n q_{i,t}\frac{p_i}{q_{i,t}}u_{i,t}=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_{i,t}\]
certify that \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=\sum_i p_i u_{i,t}\). The certificate fails if probabilities are computed after observing selection-dependent update information or if a required \(q_{i,t}\) is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(q_{i,t}\) and \(u_{i,t}\) are \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable.
\(q_{i,t}>0\) whenever \(p_i u_{i,t}\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=\sum_i p_i u_{i,t}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conditional-expectation certificate for adaptive client-selection bias correction.
review_flags: verify conditional importance-weighting coverage at the locator

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Aware Client Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select only available clients whose total resource cost fits the round budget, optimize expected utility, and use inclusion-probability correction when preserving target weights is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At round \(t\), client \(i\) reports an availability indicator \(a_{i,t}\in\{0,1\}\), resource cost \(c_{i,t}\ge0\), and utility score \(s_{i,t}\). Given budget \(B_t\), choose a distribution \(\pi_t\) supported on subsets
\[\mathcal C_t=\left\{S:S\subseteq\{i:a_{i,t}=1\},\ \sum_{i\in S}c_{i,t}\le B_t\right\}\]
that maximizes \(\mathbb E_{S\sim\pi_t}[\sum_{i\in S}s_{i,t}]\), possibly subject to inclusion floors. Draw \(S_t\sim\pi_t\), execute those clients, and aggregate using \(p_i/q_{i,t}\), where \(q_{i,t}=\mathbb P_{\pi_t}(i\in S_t)\), when an unbiased target aggregate is required. Return the server iterate after the stopping budget is exhausted.
assumptions_latex: \(a_{i,t}\), \(c_{i,t}\), and \(s_{i,t}\) are known before selection.
\(\mathcal C_t\ne\varnothing\).
For unbiased correction, \(q_{i,t}>0\) whenever \(p_i u_{i,t}\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\in\mathcal C_t\) almost surely, and inverse-inclusion weighting preserves \(\sum_i p_i u_{i,t}\) when all required probabilities are positive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible client selection using availability, resource budgets, and optional inverse-probability correction.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constrained subset selection combined with inclusion-probability correction

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate content kind, but the proposed utility-maximizing selection model has no supporting resource-aware federated source. Optional inclusion floors and the corrected aggregation operation are also not specified fully enough to identify one exact algorithm.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At round \(t\), client \(i\in[m]\) has observable resource state \(r_{i,t}\in\mathcal R_i\), predicted participation cost \(c_{i,t}\in\mathbb R_+^k\), and availability indicator \(a_{i,t}\in\{0,1\}\). A system budget is \(b_t\in\mathbb R_+^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-client synchronous or deadline-based selection with measurable resource states; statistical representativeness is not itself required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A resource-aware client-selection rule is a measurable map \(\Sigma_t:(r_{1,t},\ldots,r_{m,t},b_t)\mapsto S_t\subseteq[m]\), possibly randomized, satisfying \(i\in S_t\Rightarrow a_{i,t}=1\) and \(\sum_{i\in S_t}c_{i,t}\preceq b_t\) almost surely. Its decision law is resource-aware when membership probabilities or the selected feasible set depend on at least one system coordinate such as latency, channel rate, energy, memory, compute capacity, availability, or deadline completion probability. More generally, \(S_t\) may solve \(\min_{S\subseteq[m]}J_t(S)\) subject to \(S\subseteq A_t\) and \(\sum_{i\in S}c_{i,t}\preceq b_t\), where \(A_t=\{i:a_{i,t}=1\}\) and \(J_t\) is a declared selection objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource-aware selection maps current system states and budgets to a feasible participating set. Selected clients must be available, and their aggregate resource consumption must satisfy every declared budget coordinate. Randomized rules qualify when their membership probabilities depend on resource state. An optimization objective may rank feasible sets, but the feasibility constraints are the defining systems interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\subseteq A_t\) and \(\sum_{i\in S_t}c_{i,t}\preceq b_t\) almost surely, with the selection law measurably dependent on resource state.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With binary variables \(z_{i,t}=\mathbf1\{i\in S_t\}\), feasibility is \(z_{i,t}\le a_{i,t}\) and \(\sum_i z_{i,t}c_{i,t}\preceq b_t\).
special_cases_latex: A single deadline budget can be represented by restricting selection to clients with predicted completion time \(\tau_{i,t}\le D_t\).
A cardinality cap is obtained from \(c_{i,t}=1\) and \(b_t=K_t\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The feasible family \(\mathcal F_t=\{S\subseteq A_t:\sum_{i\in S}c_{i,t}\preceq b_t\}\) varies with the system state.
boundary_notes: Resource-aware selection need not preserve the target client distribution; bias correction is a separate interface.
No claim is made that the predicted resource costs equal realized costs.

notation.meaning: Round-t resource state of client i.

review_flags: The supplied sources discuss distributed communication broadly but were not established as support for this exact constrained-selection definition.
A source with an explicit resource-aware client-selection formulation is needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Client-Selection Bias Correction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighting each selected client by the reciprocal of its inclusion probability yields an unbiased target aggregate, although rare clients can cause high variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the target aggregate be \(g=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i g_i\), where \(p_i\ge 0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and \(g_i\in\mathbb R^d\). Let \(S\) be a random client subset with inclusion probabilities \(\pi_i=\Pr(i\in S)>0\). The Horvitz--Thompson aggregate is \[\widehat g=\sum_{i\in S}\frac{p_i}{\pi_i}g_i.\] Regardless of dependence among client-selection indicators, \(\mathbb E[\widehat g]=g\). Thus inverse-inclusion weighting removes first-order selection bias; its variance may nevertheless be large when some \(\pi_i\) are small.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i\) is integrable for every client \(i\).
\(\pi_i>0\) whenever \(p_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widehat g]=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i g_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-probability correction for unequal client inclusion probabilities.

notation.meaning: marginal inclusion probability of client i

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-inclusion weighting claim is mathematically correct and fits the correction topic, but no inspectable citation supports the estimator or variance warning.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let the desired aggregate be \(u_t=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i u_{i,t}\), where \(p_i\ge0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and \(u_{i,t}\in\mathbb R^d\). A random subset \(S_t\) has conditional inclusion probabilities \(q_{i,t}=\mathbb P(i\in S_t\mid\mathcal F_t)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Design-based correction for nonuniform or availability-dependent participation, conditional on the current history and fixed potential client updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A client-selection bias correction is a collection of aggregation coefficients \(w_{i,t}(S_t,\mathcal F_t)\) such that, for every client \(i\) with \(p_i>0\), \(q_{i,t}>0\) and \(\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{i\in S_t\}w_{i,t}\mid\mathcal F_t]=p_i\). The corrected aggregate is \(\widehat u_t=\sum_{i\in S_t}w_{i,t}u_{i,t}\), which consequently targets \(u_t\) conditionally for arbitrary fixed vectors \((u_{i,t})_{i=1}^m\). The canonical first-order-inclusion correction is \(w_{i,t}=p_i/q_{i,t}\), yielding \(\widehat u_t=\sum_{i\in S_t}(p_i/q_{i,t})u_{i,t}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bias correction reweights each observed client update so that its expected coefficient equals that client's target objective weight. Positive inclusion probability is required for every positively weighted target client. Dividing the target weight by the conditional inclusion probability is the canonical correction and makes the aggregate conditionally unbiased for any fixed collection of client updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widehat u_t\mid\mathcal F_t,(u_{i,t})_{i=1}^m]=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i u_{i,t}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Universal conditional unbiasedness for all \((u_{i,t})\) is equivalent to \(\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{i\in S_t\}w_{i,t}\mid\mathcal F_t]=p_i\) for every \(i\).
special_cases_latex: For one sampled client \(I_t\), the corrected aggregate is \((p_{I_t}/q_{I_t,t})u_{I_t,t}\).
If \(q_{i,t}=p_i\) under singleton sampling, no numerical reweighting is needed.
immediate_consequences_latex: A client with \(p_i>0\) and \(q_{i,t}=0\) cannot be design-unbiasedly recovered from that round.
Small \(q_{i,t}\) can produce large correction weights and high variance.
boundary_notes: The condition corrects sampling bias, not bias already present in local update estimators.
Self-normalized weights generally change the exact unbiasedness property.

notation.meaning: Aggregation coefficient applied when client i is selected.

review_flags: The formula is a standard inverse-probability construction, but no inspected slot-specific source locator was supplied.
Exact support in a federated client-selection source is required.

children.title: Personalized Federated Optimization
children.top_down_role: Federated objectives retaining client-specific parameters or predictors.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: There are \(m\) clients. Client \(i\) has a parameter \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_i}\), local loss \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and weight \(p_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_i p_i=1\). Shared variables, if present, lie in \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-client optimization retaining a distinct client predictor or parameter; it includes coupled, clustered, and shared-representation formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A personalized federated optimization problem is an optimization problem of the form \[\min_{z\in Z,\,x_i\in X_i}\;\Phi(z,x_1,\ldots,x_m):=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i f_i(x_i;z)+R(z,x_1,
\ldots,x_m),\] where the feasible or regularization term \(R\) couples information across clients, while the deployed solution contains client-indexed components \(x_i\) that are not constrained to be identical. A solution is any \((z^\star,x_1^\star,\ldots,x_m^\star)\in\operatorname*{argmin}\Phi\); client \(i\)'s personalized predictor is determined by \((z^\star,x_i^\star)\). The coupling may encode proximity to a reference, task relations, clustering, or a shared representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Personalized federated optimization jointly fits client-specific parameters and any shared variable. Local weighted losses are combined with a coupling term or coupling constraint that transfers information among clients. Unlike global-model federated optimization, the deployed output retains a client-indexed component and does not require all clients to use the same complete parameter vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution object retains \((x_i^\star)_{i=1}^m\), with cross-client sharing specified by \(R\) rather than the consensus constraints \(x_1=\cdots=x_m\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Hard coupling constraints are represented by taking \(R\) to be the indicator function of a feasible coupling set \(\mathcal C\subseteq Z\times\prod_iX_i\).
special_cases_latex: Regularized personalization uses \(R=\sum_i p_i\lambda_i d_i(x_i,z)\).
Shared-representation personalization writes the client predictor as \(h_{x_i}\circ\phi_z\).
Clustered personalization restricts clients in the same learned group to share a parameter.
immediate_consequences_latex: Ordinary global-model federated optimization is the special case in which all complete client parameters are constrained to coincide.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require convexity, smoothness, or a particular communication protocol.
Independent local training with \(R\equiv0\) contains no federated coupling and is normally excluded as a degenerate case.

notation.meaning: Cross-client coupling regularizer or extended-valued constraint.

review_flags: No inspected authoritative locator in the supplied set defines personalized federated optimization at this level of generality.
A precise personalization source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Federated Personalization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each client minimizes its own loss while a quadratic penalty keeps its personalized model near a jointly learned reference model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For client losses \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), weights \(p_i\ge 0\) satisfying \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and \(\lambda>0\), regularized federated personalization solves \[\min_{w,\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_m\in\mathbb R^d}\ \sum_{i=1}^m p_i\left(f_i(\theta_i)+\frac{\lambda}{2}\lVert\theta_i-w\rVert_2^2\right).\] Here \(w\) is a shared reference and \(\theta_i\) is client \(i\)'s personalized model. The coupling penalizes deviation from \(w\) without requiring the client models to coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\), \(p_i\ge0\), and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
Each \(f_i\) is proper and bounded below.
\(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed coupled objective defines the personalized client models and shared reference.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically coupled client models with a learned global reference.
