children.title: Secure Aggregation Interface
children.top_down_role: Optimization compatibility with aggregate-only visibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Secure Aggregation Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible server update depends on client messages only through their secure sum and public metadata, never through individual plaintext updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a participating set \(S\), let client \(i\) submit \(u_i\in G\), where \((G,+)\) is an abelian group. A secure-aggregation-compatible optimization round requires the server's update to have the form \[w^{+}=\Psi\!\left(w,S,\sum_{i\in S}u_i,\xi\right),\] where \(\xi\) is public or server-side randomness. The secure aggregation interface reveals the sum and declared public metadata but no individual \(u_i\). Consequently, any server rule requiring inspection, ordering, clipping, or reweighting of individual plaintext updates must be performed before aggregation or replaced by an aggregate-computable rule.
assumptions_latex: Client messages lie in a common abelian group \(G\).
The secure protocol correctly returns \(\sum_{i\in S}u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimization update is computable from aggregate-only visibility exactly when it admits the displayed interface.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate-only server interface for federated update computation.

notation.meaning: encoded update submitted by client i
server update rule using aggregate-visible inputs

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The aggregate-only condition fits the leaf, but the exact compatibility claim and operational consequences require a secure-aggregation source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a participating set \(S\), client \(i\) holds an encoded update \(u_i\in G^d\), where \(G\) is a finite abelian group. The desired aggregate functionality is \(F_S((u_i)_{i\in S})=\sum_{i\in S}u_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized optimization-facing functionality for secure summation; implementation, authentication, and cryptographic assumptions are external.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A secure aggregation interface realizes a randomized protocol whose decoded output is \(A=\sum_{i\in S'}u_i\in G^d\) for the protocol-defined surviving set \(S'\subseteq S\), while the server-visible transcript \(V\) reveals no client-specific plaintext beyond the declared leakage \(L(S',(u_i)_{i\in S'})\), ordinarily the surviving set, public metadata, and aggregate \(A\). Formally, the interface declares correctness \(\mathbb P(\operatorname{Decode}(V)=A)\ge1-\delta_{\mathrm{cor}}\) and a simulation condition: for every permitted adversary, \(V\) is computationally or statistically indistinguishable, at a declared level, from a simulator given only \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Secure aggregation presents the optimizer with the sum of encoded updates from a specified surviving client set while hiding the individual plaintext updates according to a declared simulation-based leakage rule. The interface must state its correctness failure probability, adversary class, dropout rule, group representation, and allowed public leakage. The optimizer consumes the decoded aggregate rather than individual client vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The released optimization quantity is \(A=\sum_{i\in S'}u_i\), except with declared correctness failure probability \(\delta_{\mathrm{cor}}\), and transcript visibility is restricted by the declared simulation condition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For weighted averaging, clients may encode \((w_i u_i,w_i)\), allowing the server to recover \(\sum_iw_iu_i/\sum_iw_i\) when the denominator is nonzero.
special_cases_latex: With no dropout, \(S'=S\).
Exact integer or finite-field summation is obtained before any decoding or dequantization error is introduced.
immediate_consequences_latex: An optimizer requiring individual updates is incompatible with an aggregate-only interface unless the protocol deliberately exposes additional leakage.
boundary_notes: Secure aggregation alone does not imply differential privacy of the released aggregate.
Quantization, modular overflow, malicious-client validity, and dropout tolerance require separate declared conditions.

notation.meaning: Finite-group message domain used by the secure-sum functionality.
Clients whose inputs are included after dropout handling.

review_flags: No cryptographic secure-aggregation source appears among the supplied locator hints.
A protocol or ideal-functionality source is required for correctness and simulation clauses.

children.title: Differential Privacy Interface for Federated Optimization
children.top_down_role: Interaction between federated optimization and client- or record-level privacy.

knowledge_statements.title: Differential Privacy Interface for Federated Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript privacy under record- or client-level adjacency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\sim D'\) denote either record-level adjacency or client-level adjacency, fixed before analysis. A randomized federated mechanism \(M\), whose output includes the observable training transcript and final model, is \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-differentially private if, for every adjacent \(D,D'\) and measurable event \(E\), \[\Pr(M(D)\in E)\le e^{\varepsilon}\Pr(M(D')\in E)+\delta.\] A federated optimizer interfaces with differential privacy by bounding each adjacent unit's contribution, randomizing the communicated or aggregated updates, and accounting for privacy across all rounds under the chosen adjacency relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complete observable training mechanism must satisfy differential privacy for a fixed record- or client-level adjacency relation across all communication rounds.
assumptions_latex: The adjacency relation \(\sim\) is specified as record-level or client-level.
\(M\) includes every data-dependent output visible to the adversary.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\) and \(0\le\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) satisfies the displayed \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-privacy inequality for all adjacent datasets and measurable events.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The differential-privacy definition correctly fixes one adjacency relation and covers the observable transcript, but no privacy source is cited.

knowledge_statements.source_title: Differential Privacy Interface for Federated Optimization
knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_m)\) denote federated data and \(\simeq\) a declared neighboring relation, either record-level or client-level. A randomized training mechanism \(M\) releases a transcript or final model in measurable space \((\mathcal Y,\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central or distributed federated mechanisms evaluated by the distribution of their released transcript; adjacency must be fixed explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A federated optimization mechanism \(M\) satisfies the \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-differential-privacy interface with respect to \(\simeq\) if, for every neighboring pair \(D\simeq D'\) and every measurable event \(E\in\mathcal A\), \[\mathbb P(M(D)\in E)\le e^\varepsilon\mathbb P(M(D')\in E)+\delta.\] The optimization interface additionally declares the released object, clipping or sensitivity domain, randomness location, composition scope across rounds, and whether \(\simeq\) changes one record inside one client or adds, removes, or replaces an entire client dataset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A federated training mechanism is differentially private when the probability of every released event changes by at most the stated multiplicative and additive allowances between neighboring federated datasets. The interface is incomplete unless it identifies record-level or client-level adjacency, the released transcript, sensitivity or clipping convention, where noise is generated, and whether the privacy parameters cover one round or the entire training run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall D\simeq D',\ \forall E\in\mathcal A:\ \mathbb P(M(D)\in E)\le e^\varepsilon\mathbb P(M(D')\in E)+\delta\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The symmetric neighboring relation permits the same inequality with \(D\) and \(D'\) exchanged.
Pure differential privacy is the special case \(\delta=0\).
special_cases_latex: Record-level adjacency changes one example within one client's dataset.
Client-level adjacency changes the participation or full dataset of one client.
When only the final model is released, \(M(D)\) denotes that model; transcript privacy uses the complete observable transcript.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any data-independent or randomized post-processing of \(M(D)\) retains the same declared privacy parameters.
Secure aggregation does not replace this distributional requirement.
boundary_notes: The definition alone supplies no utility, convergence, or communication guarantee.
An unspecified adjacency relation makes numerical privacy parameters ambiguous.
review_flags: The mathematical condition is standard, but none of the supplied source locators was verified as a differential-privacy source.
A precise authoritative privacy definition and federated adjacency locator are required.
knowledge_statements.title: Differentially private federated optimization interface
client update norm bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clipping bounds every client update by the clipping radius and bounds the replacement sensitivity of a fixed-size uniform average by twice that radius divided by cohort size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For clipping radius \(C>0\), define \(\operatorname{clip}_C(u)=u\min\{1,C/\|u\|\}\) for \(u\neq0\), and \(\operatorname{clip}_C(0)=0\). Every clipped client update satisfies \(\|\operatorname{clip}_C(u)\|\leq C\). If a server averages exactly \(m\) clipped updates as \(M(u_1,\ldots,u_m)=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\operatorname{clip}_C(u_j)\), then two input batches differing by replacement of one client update satisfy \(\|M(u_1,\ldots,u_m)-M(u'_1,\ldots,u'_m)\|\leq2C/m\).
assumptions_latex: Updates lie in a real normed vector space and \(C>0\).
The aggregate is a uniform mean of a fixed cohort size \(m\geq1\).
Neighboring batches use replacement adjacency and differ in exactly one client update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|\operatorname{clip}_C(u)\|\leq C,\qquad \sup_{U\sim U'}\|M(U)-M(U')\|\leq\frac{2C}{m}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic norm and replacement-sensitivity bounds produced by federated update clipping.

notation.meaning: Radial clipping operator with radius C.
Uniform mean of the clipped client updates.
Fixed-size update batches differing by one replacement.

review_flags: A differential-privacy source is required for the clipping and replacement-sensitivity interface.
Sensitivity changes under add/remove adjacency or data-dependent aggregation denominators.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The clipping norm bound and the replacement-sensitivity bound of 2C/m are mathematically correct for a fixed-size uniform mean under replacement adjacency, and the property kind fits the leaf. No differential-privacy citation with a specific locator is supplied, so the precise adjacency and aggregation interface remains unsupported.

knowledge_statements.title: clipping-induced optimization bias
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Norm clipping generally changes the mean client update. A two-point distribution already yields nonzero bias, so the expected clipped server direction need not equal the unclipped optimization direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(C>0\) and define \(\operatorname{clip}_C(u)=u\min\{1,C/\lVert u\rVert_2\}\), with \(\operatorname{clip}_C(0)=0\). For an integrable random client update \(U\in\mathbb R^d\) having mean \(g=\mathbb E[U]\), clipping targets \(g_C=\mathbb E[\operatorname{clip}_C(U)]\), and its optimization bias is \(b_C=g_C-g\). Clipping does not generally preserve unbiasedness. Indeed, in one dimension, if \(\mathbb P(U=0)=\mathbb P(U=2C)=1/2\), then \(g=C\), whereas \(g_C=C/2\) and \(b_C=-C/2\). Thus the expected clipped server update can differ from the intended mean update even before privacy noise is introduced.
assumptions_latex: \(U\in L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{clip}_C(U)]-\mathbb E[U]\) can be nonzero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias of deterministic Euclidean norm clipping applied to random client updates before privacy noise is added.

source_witnesses.locator: Abstract and Sections 3–4, discussion and analysis of clipping bias

knowledge_statements.title: per-round privacy loss
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Per-round privacy loss is the log likelihood ratio between one round's conditional output laws on adjacent datasets, evaluated at the released output; its value on outcomes impossible under both laws is immaterial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For adjacent federated datasets \(D\sim D'\), fix a round \(t\) and an admissible public transcript history \(h\). Let \(P_t^h\) and \(Q_t^h\) be the conditional laws of the round output under \(D\) and \(D'\), respectively, on a common measurable output space, and suppose they have densities \(p_t^h\) and \(q_t^h\) relative to a common dominating measure. On \(\{y:p_t^h(y)+q_t^h(y)>0\}\), define the per-round privacy-loss function by \(\ell_t^h(y)=\log\!\bigl(p_t^h(y)/q_t^h(y)\bigr)\), taking \(+\infty\) when \(p_t^h(y)>0=q_t^h(y)\) and \(-\infty\) when \(q_t^h(y)>0=p_t^h(y)\). Its value on \(\{p_t^h=q_t^h=0\}\) may be assigned arbitrarily. If \(Y_t\sim P_t^h\), then \(L_t^h=\ell_t^h(Y_t)\) is the per-round privacy-loss random variable, defined \(P_t^h\)-almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: privacy composition across rounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under basic adaptive composition, privacy parameters add across rounds: the transcript is differentially private with total epsilon and delta equal to the corresponding roundwise sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\sim D'\), and let an interactive procedure release \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_T\). Suppose that for every round \(t\), every admissible preceding transcript \(h\), and every measurable event \(S\), its conditional mechanism satisfies \(\mathbb P(Y_t\in S\mid D,h)\le e^{\varepsilon_t}\mathbb P(Y_t\in S\mid D',h)+\delta_t\), and the same requirement holds with \(D,D'\) interchanged. Then the complete transcript mechanism \(D\mapsto(Y_1,\ldots,Y_T)\) is \(\bigl(\sum_{t=1}^T\varepsilon_t,\sum_{t=1}^T\delta_t\bigr)\)-differentially private. knowledge_statements.title: Byzantine-Robust Aggregation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic robust-aggregation contract under bounded honest dispersion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\) contain an unknown honest index set \(H\) with \(|H|\ge n-b\), and define \(\bar v_H=|H|^{-1}\sum_{i\in H}v_i\). An aggregation rule \(A:(\mathbb R^d)^n\to\mathbb R^d\) satisfies a \((b,c)\)-Byzantine-robust interface on radius \(\rho\) if \[\max_{i\in H}\lVert v_i-\bar v_H\rVert_2\le\rho\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\lVert A(v_1,\ldots,v_n)-\bar v_H\rVert_2\le c\rho\] for every choice of the remaining at most \(b\) vectors. An optimizer using \(A\) must establish honest-update dispersion compatible with this contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If honest updates concentrate around their mean, the aggregator must remain close to that mean despite any allowed Byzantine vectors.
assumptions_latex: Honest vectors satisfy the displayed radius bound.
Byzantine vectors are otherwise arbitrary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert A(v_1,\ldots,v_n)-\bar v_H\rVert_2\le c\rho\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Among \(n\) received vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\), an unknown honest set \(H\subseteq[n]\) has \(|H|\ge n-b\); vectors from \(B=[n]\setminus H\), with \(|B|\le b\), may be arbitrary and adaptive. Let \(\mu_H=|H|^{-1}\sum_{i\in H}v_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roundwise vector-aggregation interface under a bounded number of arbitrary messages; the chosen error functional must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A map \(A:(\mathbb R^d)^n\to\mathbb R^d\), possibly randomized, is \((b,\mathcal C,\mathcal E)\)-Byzantine robust if, for every honest multiset satisfying condition \(\mathcal C\) and every replacement of at most \(b\) inputs by arbitrary vectors, its output \(a=A(v_1,
\ldots,v_n)\) satisfies the declared error relation \(\mathcal E(a,\mu_H)\). A common optimization-facing relation is \(\mathbb E\|a-\mu_H\|^2\le C\sigma_H^2\), where \(\sigma_H^2=|H|^{-1}\sum_{i\in H}\|v_i-\mu_H\|^2\), with all constants, dimensional dependence, and probability levels declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Byzantine-robust aggregation rule must approximate a reference aggregate of the honest vectors uniformly over every allowed placement and value of up to the stated number of malicious messages. The interface identifies the honest-data regularity condition, corruption budget, reference center, error metric, probability level, and constants. Merely naming an aggregation rule does not specify robustness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
For all \(|B|\le b\) and arbitrary \((v_i)_{i\in B}\), \(A(v_1,\ldots,v_n)\) satisfies \(\mathcal E(A(v_1,
\ldots,v_n),\mu_H)\) whenever the honest inputs satisfy \(\mathcal C\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A high-probability contract may require \(\|a-\mu_H\|\le r(\mathcal C,n,b,d,\eta)\) with probability at least \(1-\eta\).
special_cases_latex: When \(b=0\), exact averaging is robust with zero error relative to \(\mu_H\).
Coordinatewise median, trimmed means, and geometric median instantiate different contracts under different honest-data assumptions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The optimization method may treat \(a-\mu_H\) as an aggregation error only within the declared contract.
boundary_notes: Robustness to arbitrary vectors does not imply privacy or message authenticity.
No universal finite error is possible without an adequate corruption fraction and honest-data condition.

notation.meaning: Maximum number of Byzantine input vectors.
Declared regularity condition on honest vectors.

coordinate-wise median aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sort client values separately in every coordinate and output the coordinatewise lower median. The rule is one-shot and coordinate-system dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(n\ge1\) reported updates \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\). No iterative state is initialized. For each coordinate \(j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), sort \(v_{1j},\ldots,v_{nj}\) as \(v_{(1)j}\le\cdots\le v_{(n)j}\), set \(k=\lceil n/2\rceil\), and define \(a_j=v_{(k)j}\). After all coordinates have been processed, stop and output \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_d)\). The rule acts independently in each coordinate and is therefore not invariant under arbitrary rotations of \(\mathbb R^d\); its result need not equal a geometric median.
assumptions_latex: \(v_i\in\mathbb R^d\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_j=v_{(\lceil n/2\rceil)j}\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-shot deterministic coordinate-wise aggregation using the lower-median convention.

notation.meaning: r-th order statistic in coordinate j

knowledge_statements.title: trimmed-mean aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each coordinate, remove the prescribed number of largest and smallest client values and average the remainder. Different coordinates may retain different clients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(n\ge1\) reported updates \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\) and an integer \(b\) satisfying \(0\le b<n/2\). No iterative state is initialized. For each coordinate \(j\), sort the reported values as \(v_{(1)j}\le\cdots\le v_{(n)j}\), discard the \(b\) smallest and \(b\) largest values, and set \(a_j=(n-2b)^{-1}\sum_{r=b+1}^{n-b}v_{(r)j}\). Stop after processing all coordinates and output \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_d)\). Trimming is performed independently by coordinate, so retained coordinates need not originate from the same clients.
assumptions_latex: \(v_i\in\mathbb R^d\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
\(b\in\mathbb Z\) and \(0\le b<n/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_j=\frac{1}{n-2b}\sum_{r=b+1}^{n-b}v_{(r)j}\) for every coordinate \(j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-shot coordinate-wise symmetric trimmed mean with an integer trimming count.

notation.meaning: number of values trimmed from each tail per coordinate

knowledge_statements.title: Krum aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Krum scores each reported update by its squared distances to its nearest prescribed neighbors and outputs the single update with minimum score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(n\) vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\), a Byzantine upper bound \(f\), and a fixed tie-breaking order, with \(n\ge2f+3\). No iterative state is initialized. For each \(i\), let \(N_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i\}\) contain the \(n-f-2\) indices having smallest squared distances \(\lVert v_i-v_j\rVert_2^2\), resolving ties by the fixed order, and compute \(s_i=\sum_{j\in N_i}\lVert v_i-v_j\rVert_2^2\). Choose \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_i s_i\) using the same order, stop, and output \(v_{i^*}\).
assumptions_latex: \(v_i\in\mathbb R^d\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
\(f\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(n\ge2f+3\).
A deterministic tie-breaking order is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Krum}_f(v_1,\ldots,v_n)=v_{i^*}\), where \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{i}s_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original one-vector Krum rule with squared Euclidean distance scores.

notation.meaning: nearest-neighbor index set used to score candidate i
Krum distance score of candidate i

source_witnesses.locator: Section 4, printed p. 4, definition of the Krum function; Proposition 1, printed p. 5

knowledge_statements.title: multi-Krum aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-Krum computes ordinary Krum scores, selects a prescribed number of lowest-scoring client updates, and returns their arithmetic mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\), a Byzantine upper bound \(f\), a selection count \(q\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and a fixed tie-breaking order, with \(n\ge2f+3\). For every \(i\), form the \(n-f-2\) nearest-neighbor set \(N_i\) and Krum score \(s_i=\sum_{j\in N_i}\lVert v_i-v_j\rVert_2^2\). Let \(I_q\) be the indices of the \(q\) smallest scores, with ties resolved by the fixed order. Stop and output \(q^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_q}v_i\). The cases \(q=1\) and \(q=n\) reduce respectively to Krum and ordinary averaging.
assumptions_latex: \(v_i\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(n\ge2f+3\).
\(f\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(q\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
A deterministic tie-breaking order is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MultiKrum}_{f,q}(v_1,\ldots,v_n)=\frac1q\sum_{i\in I_q}v_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-Krum variant averaging a fixed number of lowest-scoring Krum candidates.

notation.meaning: indices of the q smallest scores

knowledge_statements.title: distance-score honest-majority condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Krum's distance-score condition requires n greater than 2f+2. Under this condition, every honest candidate's score neighborhood contains at least one honest comparison; this alone is not a resilience guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\) reports contain at most \(f\) Byzantine reports, and let \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) denote the honest indices, so \(\lvert H\rvert\ge n-f\). The distance-score honest-majority condition for Krum is \(2f+2<n\), equivalently \(n\ge2f+3\) for integer \(n,f\). Assume this condition holds. Then the score-neighborhood size \(n-f-2\) is positive, and for every honest candidate \(i\in H\), any set \(N_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i\}\) of size \(n-f-2\) contains at least \(n-2f-2\ge1\) honest indices. This is a feasibility condition for the distance score, not by itself a convergence or Byzantine-resilience guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(n,f\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
At most \(f\) of the \(n\) reports are Byzantine.
\(2f+2<n\), equivalently \(n\ge2f+3\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(i\in H\) and every \(N_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i\}\) with \(\lvert N_i\rvert=n-f-2\), one has \(\lvert N_i\cap H\rvert\ge n-2f-2\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial feasibility condition underlying Krum-type nearest-neighbor scores.

notation.meaning: score neighborhood of candidate i, of size n-f-2

source_witnesses.locator: Section 4, Proposition 1, printed p. 5, condition 2f+2<n; Krum neighborhood definition on printed p. 4

knowledge_statements.title: robust update clipping
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip every client update to a fixed Euclidean radius, then compute the weighted average; an empty or zero-weight participant set causes failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given client updates \(u_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\), nonnegative weights \(w_i\), and radius \(\tau>0\), initialize the accepted weighted sum to zero and define \(C_\tau(0)=0\) and \(C_\tau(u)=u\min\{1,\tau/\lVert u\rVert_2\}\) for \(u\ne0\). For every participating client, replace \(u_i\) by \(\widetilde u_i=C_\tau(u_i)\). If \(\sum_i w_i>0\), output \(g=(\sum_i w_i\widetilde u_i)/(\sum_i w_i)\); otherwise report aggregation failure. Each submitted contribution then satisfies \(\lVert\widetilde u_i\rVert_2\le\tau\), although clipping alone does not ensure Byzantine robustness.
assumptions_latex: The updates satisfy \(u_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\), and all norms are Euclidean.
The clipping radius satisfies \(\tau>0\).
The aggregation weights satisfy \(w_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is \(g\), with every clipped contribution satisfying \(\lVert\widetilde u_i\rVert_2\le\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-client Euclidean-norm clipping before weighted server aggregation in one federated round.

notation.meaning: Raw and clipped updates from client i.
Euclidean-norm clipping map with radius tau.
Nonnegative aggregation weight of client i.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is internally coherent, uses fully delimited TeX, and fits the computational-mechanism leaf. However, no citation supports this particular clipping-and-weighted-aggregation specification or its robustness qualification.

knowledge_statements.title: anomaly-filtered aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score client updates, discard those above a declared anomaly threshold, and average the remaining positive-weight updates; reject the round if none remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given updates \(u_1,\ldots,u_n\in\mathbb{R}^d\), weights \(w_i\ge0\), an anomaly score \(S_i=S(u_i;u_1,\ldots,u_n)\in\mathbb{R}\), and threshold \(q\in\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(A=\varnothing\). Evaluate every score and set \(A=\{i:S_i\le q\}\). If \(W_A=\sum_{i\in A}w_i>0\), output \(g=W_A^{-1}\sum_{i\in A}w_i u_i\); otherwise report aggregation failure. The score, threshold-selection rule, and any data-dependent fitting of \(S\) must be fixed before evaluating the reported round or included explicitly in the algorithm specification.
assumptions_latex: All submitted updates lie in the common space \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
The score function \(S\) and threshold \(q\) are defined for the complete submitted update collection.
Weights satisfy \(w_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(W_A>0\), the filtered aggregate is \(g=W_A^{-1}\sum_{i\in A}w_i u_i\); otherwise no aggregate is returned.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic score-threshold filtering interface followed by normalized weighted aggregation.

notation.meaning: Anomaly score assigned to client i's update.
Indices accepted by the anomaly filter.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf and the generic threshold-filtering interface is mathematically defined, but no source supports this exact interface, including its threshold-selection requirement and failure behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: model-poisoning update
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model-poisoning update is a Byzantine replacement for the prescribed local update that changes the server aggregate, possibly in coordination with other attackers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) and \(B\) partition the participating clients into honest and Byzantine sets. At server state \(\theta\), the prescribed client rule produces \(u_i=U_i(\theta,D_i,r_i)\in\mathbb{R}^d\), and the server uses an aggregator \(A:(\mathbb{R}^d)^n\to\mathbb{R}^d\). A submitted vector \(v_j\in\mathbb{R}^d\) from \(j\in B\) is a model-poisoning update when it replaces the prescribed \(u_j\) and changes the aggregate, namely \(A(u_H,v_j,u_{B\setminus\{j\}})\ne A(u_H,u_j,u_{B\setminus\{j\}})\). Joint poisoning permits Byzantine clients to choose their replacement vectors coordinately.
assumptions_latex: Every honest client has a prescribed update rule \(U_i\).
All client updates and replacements lie in \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
The server aggregation map \(A\) is defined on all submitted update tuples under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The replacement \(v_j\) is model-poisoning precisely when it is submitted instead of \(u_j\) and produces a different aggregate under the stated comparison.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Update-level poisoning relative to a prescribed honest client rule and server aggregator.

notation.meaning: Prescribed update rule for client i.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition makes an actual change in the aggregate necessary for a submission to count as model poisoning. That is narrower than common intent- or adversary-based uses and may exclude malicious updates neutralized by the aggregator. A source is required to determine the intended definition.

knowledge_statements.title: backdoor poisoning objective
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Attackers choose feasible updates that preserve clean performance while minimizing loss on triggered inputs assigned to a target label.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the post-aggregation model be \(\theta^+(v_B)=\theta-\eta A(u_H,v_B)\), where Byzantine updates \(v_B\) must lie in a feasible set \(\mathcal C\). For predictor \(f_\vartheta\), trigger map \(T\), target label \(y_\star\), and loss \(\ell\), define \(L_{\mathrm{bd}}(\vartheta)=\mathbb E_{x\sim P_{\mathrm{tr}}}[\ell(f_\vartheta(T(x)),y_\star)]\). A standard targeted backdoor objective is \[v_B^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{v_B\in\mathcal C}\bigl\{L_{\mathrm{clean}}(\theta^+(v_B))+\lambda L_{\mathrm{bd}}(\theta^+(v_B))\bigr\},\qquad \lambda>0.\] The feasible set may encode clipping, norm, or protocol constraints imposed by the server.
assumptions_latex: The aggregation map \(A(u_H,v_B)\) and step size \(\eta>0\) define the next model.
The clean and backdoor losses are finite on models reachable from \(\mathcal C\).
The displayed constrained minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any \(v_B^\star\) in the displayed argmin optimizes the weighted clean-and-targeted backdoor objective subject to \(v_B\in\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained update-selection objective balancing clean behavior and targeted triggered behavior.

notation.meaning: Trigger transformation and attacker-selected target label.
Feasible set of Byzantine update tuples.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the formulation leaf, but the weighted-sum attack objective, the clean-loss tradeoff, and the sign convention in the server update are modeling choices requiring direct support. No cited source establishes this particular formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: honest-majority robustness assumption
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly more than half of the round's distinct participants must be honest. A fault bound of f together with at least 2f+1 participants guarantees this majority, but the counting condition alone does not guarantee accurate aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a round with finite participant set \(N=H\mathbin{\dot\cup}B\), where \(H\) is honest, \(B\) is Byzantine, and \(n=|N|\), the strict honest-majority condition is \[|B|<\frac{n}{2},\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad |H|>|B|.\] If an integer fault budget \(f\ge0\) is declared, the pair of assumptions \(|B|\le f\) and \(n\ge2f+1\) is sufficient to guarantee a strict honest majority for every round respecting that budget. Client identities are counted once within the round. This counting condition limits Byzantine participation but, without an additional concentration or geometric assumption on honest updates, does not by itself guarantee an accurate aggregate.
assumptions_latex: The round has a finite participant set \(N\) of size \(n\).
The sets \(H\) and \(B\) are disjoint and satisfy \(N=H\cup B\).
Each participant identity contributes at most one counted update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The honest-majority predicate holds exactly when \(|H|>|B|\), equivalently when \(|B|<n/2\); moreover, \(|B|\le f\) and \(n\ge2f+1\) are sufficient to ensure it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted per-round participant-count condition for Byzantine-robust aggregation.

notation.meaning: Set of distinct participants in the aggregation round.
Honest and Byzantine subsets of the participant set.
Declared upper bound on the number of Byzantine participants.

knowledge_statements.title: Privacy–Utility–Robustness–Communication Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The joint tradeoff is the Pareto frontier of achievable privacy, error, Byzantine tolerance, and communication cost under fixed models and conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a data model, adversary model, privacy adjacency relation, and training horizon. For every admissible federated mechanism \(M\), let \(q(M)=(\varepsilon(M),\delta(M),\mathcal E(M),\beta(M),B(M))\), representing privacy loss, expected excess risk, tolerated Byzantine fraction, and communicated bits. The attainable region is \[\mathcal R=\{q(M):M\text{ is admissible}\}.\] With smaller \(\varepsilon,\delta,\mathcal E,B\) and larger \(\beta\) preferred, the joint tradeoff frontier is the set of nondominated points of \(\mathcal R\). Any claimed numerical frontier is meaningful only under the fixed models and resource conventions.
assumptions_latex: The data, adversary, privacy, and communication models are fixed.
All metrics are evaluated over the same training horizon.
The admissible mechanism class is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The privacy--utility--robustness--communication frontier equals the nondominated subset of \(\mathcal R\).

notation.meaning: expected excess risk of mechanism M

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathfrak M\) be a declared class of federated mechanisms. For \(M\in\mathfrak M\), let \(P(M)\), \(U(M)\), \(R(M)\), and \(C(M)\) be ordered numerical measures of privacy loss, utility loss, robustness loss, and communication cost, with smaller values preferred.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-criterion comparison within a fixed problem class, threat model, privacy adjacency, utility metric, and communication accounting convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The privacy--utility--robustness--communication attainable set is \[\mathcal A=\{(P(M),U(M),R(M),C(M)):M\in\mathfrak M\}\subseteq(\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\})^4.\] Its tradeoff frontier is the Pareto-minimal subset \[\mathcal F=\{a\in\mathcal A:\nexists a'\in\mathcal A\text{ with }a'\preceq a\text{ and }a'\ne a\}.\] Thus a mechanism lies on the frontier exactly when no admissible mechanism weakly improves all four declared criteria and strictly improves at least one. Every coordinate definition, operating horizon, and admissible mechanism class is part of the tradeoff specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The joint tradeoff is the set of all privacy-loss, utility-loss, robustness-loss, and communication-cost quadruples achievable by an explicitly fixed class of federated mechanisms. The frontier consists of nondominated quadruples: improving any coordinate from such a point necessarily worsens or leaves the admissible range of at least one other coordinate. Comparisons are meaningful only when all mechanisms use the same problem, adversary, privacy, utility, and cost conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F=\operatorname{ParetoMin}(\mathcal A)\) under componentwise order, with \(\mathcal A\) determined by the declared mechanism and evaluation classes.

For fixed budgets \((\bar P,\bar R,\bar C)\), a scalar section of the frontier is \(U^
\star(\bar P,\bar R,\bar C)=\inf\{U(M):P(M)\le\bar P,\ R(M)\le\bar R,\ C(M)\le\bar C\}\).

Fixing a communication protocol restricts \(\mathfrak M\) and produces a conditional frontier.
immediate_consequences_latex: A weighted scalarization returns only supported frontier points when the attainable region is nonconvex.
Changing adjacency, corruption budget, or bit accounting changes the attainable set.

Privacy parameters with different adjacency relations cannot occupy the same coordinate without an explicit conversion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adversarial robustness boundary for distributed optimization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\) be an honest distributed optimization instance, \(A\) an aggregation protocol, and \(\mathfrak A(\theta)\) a nested family of admissible adversaries indexed by severity \(\theta\), such as corrupted-client fraction, perturbation budget, or number of malicious identities. Let \(\mathcal G(P,A,a)\) denote a declared optimization guarantee.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarantee-relative worst-case boundary; cryptographic, privacy, and detection guarantees are excluded unless explicitly included in \(\mathcal G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the robust severity set \[\Theta_{\rm rob}:=\{\theta:\forall a\in\mathfrak A(\theta),\ \mathcal G(P,A,a)\text{ holds}\}.\] The adversarial boundary is \(\partial\Theta_{\rm rob}\); for a scalar monotone severity parameter it is summarized by \[\theta^\star:=\sup\{\theta:\forall a\in\mathfrak A(\theta),\ \mathcal G(P,A,a)\text{ holds}\}.\] Severity beyond the boundary admits at least one allowed adversary that violates the declared guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The robust severity set consists of attack budgets under which the optimization guarantee holds against every allowed adversary. Its boundary is the adversarial boundary. For a scalar nested attack budget, the threshold is the supremum of robust budgets; beyond it, at least one permitted adversary defeats the guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\theta>\theta^\star\Longrightarrow\exists a\in\mathfrak A(\theta)\text{ for which }\mathcal G(P,A,a)\text{ fails},\] whenever the adversary classes are nested and the robust set is downward closed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a binary success predicate and downward-closed robustness, \(\Theta_{\rm rob}\) is an interval beginning at zero, possibly with an open or closed endpoint.
special_cases_latex: The severity parameter may be the maximum number \(f\) of Byzantine clients, an \(\ell_p\) poisoning radius, or the fraction of Sybil-controlled aggregation weight.
immediate_consequences_latex: An adversarial threshold is meaningless without specifying the adversary class, information pattern, aggregator, and optimization guarantee.
boundary_notes: The definition does not claim attainability at \(\theta^\star\).
Randomized guarantees must state whether probability is over protocol randomness, attacks, or both.
review_flags: No source locator was available for this guarantee-relative formalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial robustness boundary for distributed optimization

children.title: Byzantine Update Faults
children.top_down_role: Arbitrary or malicious optimization messages.

knowledge_statements.title: Byzantine Update Faults
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Byzantine client may send any adaptive optimization vector, unrelated to data or the prescribed algorithm, while honest clients follow the protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Byzantine update fault is present when a client \(i\in B\) may transmit an arbitrary message \(u_i^t=\phi_i^t(\mathcal H_t,\xi_i^t)\in\mathbb R^d\) at round \(t\), where \(\phi_i^t\) is unrestricted, \(\mathcal H_t\) is the observable history, and \(\xi_i^t\) permits private randomness. The message need not equal a gradient, correspond to any dataset, or remain consistent across recipients or rounds. Honest clients \(i\notin B\) follow the specified update rule. A robustness statement under this model must hold uniformly over the Byzantine set and all admissible adaptive message strategies.
assumptions_latex: A server expects one update in \(\mathbb R^d\) from each selected client.
The Byzantine set \(B\) is not constrained by the prescribed local algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(i\in B\), the transmitted update may be any adaptive vector in \(\mathbb R^d\); guarantees must therefore quantify over all such choices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message-level Byzantine fault model with adaptive, arbitrary client updates.

notation.meaning: Message sent by client i in round t

review_flags: The supplied distributed-optimization locators do not address Byzantine fault models; a Byzantine-robust optimization source is required.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition broadly matches an adaptive Byzantine message model, but no Byzantine-robust optimization source is cited. The claim that messages may differ across recipients also exceeds the stated single-server, one-update assumption unless equivocation or multiple recipients are explicitly included.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At round \(t\), honest client \(i\) would send an update \(u_{i,t}^{\rm hon}\in\mathbb R^p\) prescribed by its data, state, and protocol. A set \(B_t\subseteq[n]\) is Byzantine, and the server receives messages \(m_{i,t}\in\mathbb R^p\), possibly with recipient-dependent copies \(m_{i\to j,t}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrary-message fault model for distributed or federated optimization; computational limits and attack budgets must be specified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Client \(i\) has a Byzantine update fault at round \(t\) when \(i\in B_t\) and its transmitted message is not constrained to equal any protocol-compliant update: \[m_{i,t}\in\mathbb R^p\quad\text{may be chosen as an arbitrary function of the adversary's information and history}.\] In a point-to-point protocol, Byzantine equivocation is allowed when \(m_{i\to j,t}\ne m_{i\to \ell,t}\) for two recipients. An \(f\)-Byzantine execution satisfies \(|B_t|\le f\) for every \(t\), unless the model instead bounds the union of corrupted clients over time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Byzantine client may send any optimization vector allowed by the message space, chosen using its available information and history, rather than the protocol-compliant update. It may also send inconsistent vectors to different recipients when the communication model permits equivocation. An f-Byzantine model bounds the number of such clients according to a stated per-round or cumulative convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[i\in B_t\Longrightarrow m_{i,t}\text{ is unconstrained by }m_{i,t}=u_{i,t}^{\rm hon}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A Byzantine update can model arbitrary value faults, including fabricated gradients, model replacements, sign reversals, and protocol-dependent adaptive vectors.
special_cases_latex: An omission is representable by a distinguished no-message action if the Byzantine model includes silence.
A fixed malicious vector is a special case of an adaptive arbitrary update.
immediate_consequences_latex: Norm or unbiasedness assumptions imposed on honest stochastic updates cannot automatically be imposed on Byzantine messages.
boundary_notes: Data poisoning that still produces a protocol-compliant gradient of a corrupted objective is conceptually distinct from arbitrary message fabrication.
The definition alone supplies no robustness threshold.

notation.meaning: set of Byzantine clients at round t

review_flags: The standard arbitrary-message model is stated without an inspectable supporting source.

children.title: Data and Objective Poisoning
children.top_down_role: Optimization effects of corrupted local data or risks.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Client \(i\) has clean empirical distribution \(P_i\) on sample space \(\mathcal Z\), loss \(\ell(x;z)\), and clean objective \(F_i(x)=\mathbb E_{z\sim P_i}[\ell(x;z)]\). A poisoning map replaces \(P_i\) by \(\widetilde P_i\) in an allowed uncertainty set \(\mathcal U_i(P_i,\varepsilon_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-level interface for data poisoning: corruption acts through local risks or their oracles, rather than granting unrestricted message fabrication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The poisoned local objective is \[\widetilde F_i(x):=\mathbb E_{z\sim\widetilde P_i}[\ell(x;z)],\qquad \Delta_i(x):=\widetilde F_i(x)-F_i(x).\] For target weights \(p_i\), the induced aggregate objective is \(\widetilde F(x)=\sum_ip_i\widetilde F_i(x)=F(x)+\sum_ip_i\Delta_i(x)\). The data-objective poisoning interface is the map \[(\widetilde P_i)_i\longmapsto(\Delta_i)_i\longmapsto\widetilde F,\] together with the declared feasibility constraints \(\widetilde P_i\in\mathcal U_i(P_i,\varepsilon_i)\). Poisoning is optimization-effective on domain \(\mathcal X\) when \(
abla\widetilde F(x)
e
abla F(x)\) for some \(x\in\mathcal X\), or the corresponding declared nonsmooth operators differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data poisoning replaces clean client distributions with allowed corrupted distributions. This changes local risks by objective perturbations and therefore changes the weighted aggregate objective. The interface records the map from corrupted data laws to local objective perturbations and then to the aggregate risk. Poisoning is optimization-effective when it changes the aggregate optimization operator somewhere in the stated domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widetilde F-F=\sum_i p_i\Delta_i,\qquad \Delta_i=\widetilde F_i-F_i.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For finite datasets, replacing \(D_i\) by \(\widetilde D_i\) yields \(\widetilde F_i(x)=|\widetilde D_i|^{-1}\sum_{z\in\widetilde D_i}\ell(x;z)\).
special_cases_latex: Label flipping, sample insertion, sample deletion, and feature perturbation correspond to different choices of \(\mathcal U_i\).
Clean-data behavior is recovered when \(\varepsilon_i=0\) and \(\mathcal U_i(P_i,0)=\{P_i\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A protocol can faithfully optimize \(\widetilde F\) yet fail to optimize the clean target \(F\).
boundary_notes: Arbitrary replacement of transmitted gradients is a Byzantine update fault rather than solely data-objective poisoning.
The uncertainty set must specify the attack budget; without it, the interface imposes no adversarial limit.
review_flags: No independently inspectable source supports the exact interface definition and scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Data-objective poisoning interface
Data Poisoning Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data poisoning changes an allowed number of client examples, then lets the normal training rule propagate that change into the objective and update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(D_i=\{z_{ij}\}_{j=1}^{n_i}\), a data-poisoning interface permits an attacker to choose \(D_i'\in\mathcal A_i(D_i)\), where \(\mathcal A_i(D_i)\) is an explicitly declared admissible set, such as datasets obtained by replacing at most \(b_i\) examples. The client then forms \(f_i'(x)=|D_i'|^{-1}\sum_{z\in D_i'}\ell(x;z)\) and applies the prescribed optimizer to \(f_i'\). Thus the attack acts through \(D_i\mapsto D_i'\mapsto f_i'\mapsto u_i'\); it does not directly authorize an arbitrary objective or message beyond what some admissible \(D_i'\) induces.
assumptions_latex: Client \(i\) ordinarily forms an empirical objective from dataset \(D_i\).
An attacker may replace \(D_i\) by an admissible poisoned dataset \(D_i'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The data-poisoning interface is the map \(D_i\mapsto D_i'\mapsto f_i'\mapsto u_i'\), with admissibility enforced at the dataset level.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dataset-level attack interface, distinguished from direct manipulation of objectives or transmitted updates.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports a formal federated data-poisoning interface or poisoning budget.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The dataset-to-objective-to-update interface is coherent and definition is the correct kind, but the admissible poisoning model and example-replacement budget lack a supporting federated data-poisoning citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Poisoning Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective poisoning directly perturbs a client loss within a declared function class, without requiring that the new loss arise from modified data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective-poisoning interface permits an attacker controlling client \(i\) to replace \(f_i\) by \(\widetilde f_i=f_i+h_i\), where \(h_i\in\mathcal H_i\) and \(\mathcal H_i\) states all magnitude, smoothness, convexity, or support restrictions. The client update is then generated by the prescribed local algorithm applied to \(\widetilde f_i\). Unlike data poisoning, the interface does not require \(\widetilde f_i\) to equal an empirical risk derived from an admissible modified dataset. Unlike a Byzantine-message model, it still requires the transmitted update to be consistent with optimizing some allowed \(\widetilde f_i\).
assumptions_latex: Client \(i\) has benign objective \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\).
The attack class specifies an admissible perturbation set \(\mathcal H_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective poisoning replaces \(f_i\) by \(f_i+h_i\) for \(h_i\in\mathcal H_i\), independently of whether the perturbed objective is realizable by poisoned data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-level poisoning interface before execution of the prescribed local optimizer.
review_flags: No supplied locator establishes the intended objective-poisoning attack class or its relation to data realizability.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The function-level interface is mathematically explicit and distinguished from data and message poisoning, but its attack class and data-realizability distinction are not supported by a cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Targeted Optimization Distortion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A targeted attack succeeds when admissible poisoned objectives make a preselected point approximately optimal while satisfying the stated collateral constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde F(x)=\sum_{i\notin B}p_i f_i(x)+\sum_{i\in B}p_i(f_i(x)+h_i(x))\). A targeted optimization distortion toward \(x_{\mathrm{tar}}\) succeeds at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) when there exist \(h_i\in\mathcal H_i\) such that \(\widetilde F(x_{\mathrm{tar}})\le\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\widetilde F(x)+\varepsilon\), together with every declared collateral constraint, such as \(C(h_1,\ldots,h_m)\le\rho\). The target is attacker-selected before evaluation. Without the target condition, merely increasing benign loss or preventing convergence constitutes untargeted disruption rather than targeted distortion.
assumptions_latex: The attacker controls objectives indexed by \(B\) and chooses admissible perturbations \(h_i\in\mathcal H_i\).
A target point \(x_{\mathrm{tar}}\in\mathbb R^d\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A targeted distortion succeeds when \(x_{\mathrm{tar}}\) is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal for the poisoned aggregate while the declared admissibility and collateral constraints hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-level success predicate for steering the aggregate toward a prescribed target.
review_flags: No supplied source specifies a canonical success predicate for targeted federated optimization distortion.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The epsilon-optimality predicate is precise and condition fits the terminal container, but no source establishes it as the intended success criterion for targeted optimization distortion or supports the chosen collateral-constraint formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Poisoning Detectability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a benign world and a poisoned world produce identical observable transcripts, every detector has false-positive or false-negative probability at least one half.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\) be the law of the observable transcript \(T\) in an admissible benign world and \(P_1\) its law in an admissible poisoned world. If \(P_0=P_1\), then for every possibly randomized detector \(\delta(T)\in\{0,1\}\), with \(1\) denoting poisoning, \[P_0(\delta(T)=1)+P_1(\delta(T)=0)=1.\] Consequently at least one of its false-positive and false-negative probabilities is at least \(1/2\). Poisoning is therefore not uniformly detectable from \(T\) unless the model excludes observationally equivalent benign and poisoned worlds or supplies additional trusted information.
assumptions_latex: A detector observes a transcript \(T\) and outputs either benign or poisoned.
Two admissible worlds induce transcript laws \(P_0\) and \(P_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(P_0=P_1\), every detector \(\delta\) satisfies \(P_0(\delta(T)=1)+P_1(\delta(T)=0)=1\); uniform reliable detection is impossible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic impossibility boundary based on observationally identical protocol transcripts.
review_flags: The indistinguishability argument is standard, but no supplied locator connects it to federated poisoning detectability.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The indistinguishability calculation is mathematically correct and failure_boundary is appropriate, but no inspectable citation connects this testing boundary to admissible benign and poisoned federated transcripts.

children.title: Collusion and Sybil Attacks
children.top_down_role: Optimization consequences of coordinated or duplicated malicious clients.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\) be a set of honest physical clients, \(P\) a set of malicious physical principals, and \(I\) the identities admitted by a distributed optimization protocol. In round \(t\), identity \(i\in I\) submits a message \(m_{i,t}\in\mathcal M_t\). The server or peer network applies an aggregation map \(A_t:\mathcal M_t^{I_t}\to\mathcal Y_t\) to the messages of the participating identities \(I_t\subseteq I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-client distributed or federated optimization in which protocol-level identities need not correspond one-to-one with physical participants. The definition concerns the adversary interface, not a particular poisoning objective or aggregation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A collusion–Sybil attack interface is a tuple \(\mathfrak A=(P,S,\pi,\{K_t\}_{t\ge0})\), where \(S\subseteq I\) is the set of adversarially controlled identities, \(\pi:S\to P\) maps each identity to its controlling physical principal, and \(K_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal H_t)\) is a joint probability kernel on \(\mathcal M_t^{S_t}\), with \(S_t=S\cap I_t\), conditioned on the adversary-visible history \(\mathcal H_t\). It is a Sybil interface when \(\pi\) is noninjective, equivalently when \(\exists p\in P\) such that \(|\pi^{-1}(p)|\ge2\). It is a collusion interface when the conditional joint law need not factor by principal: for some \(t\) and history \(h\), \[K_t(dm_{S_t}\mid h)\ne\prod_{p\in P}K_{p,t}(dm_{S_t\cap\pi^{-1}(p)}\mid h).\] The effective adversarial weight in round \(t\) is \(\alpha_t=|S_t|/|I_t|\), while the physical-adversary fraction is \(\beta_t=|\pi(S_t)|/(|H_t|+|\pi(S_t)|)\). The interface exposes a collusion–Sybil boundary precisely when protocol influence is allocated by identity and \(\alpha_t\) can exceed \(\beta_t\) because one or more principals control multiple admitted identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface consists of malicious physical principals, their controlled protocol identities, a map from identities to principals, and a history-dependent joint law for their round messages. It is Sybil-capable when at least one principal controls two or more identities. It is collusive when controlled messages may be jointly coordinated rather than conditionally independent across principals. Identity-weighted aggregation exposes the boundary when the adversarial identity fraction \(\alpha_t\) may exceed the physical-adversary fraction \(\beta_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak A\) is collusion–Sybil capable exactly when coordinated kernels \(K_t\) are permitted and the control map \(\pi:S\to P\) is noninjective.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Noninjectivity of \(\pi\) is equivalent to \(|S|>|\pi(S)|\) when \(S\) is finite.
For identity-uniform aggregation, Sybil amplification in round \(t\) can be recorded by \(a_t=\alpha_t/\beta_t>1\), provided \(\beta_t>0\).
special_cases_latex: Pure collusion has injective \(\pi\) but permits a nonfactorizing \(K_t\).
A pure Sybil attack by one principal has \(|P|=1\), \(|S|\ge2\), and arbitrarily dependent messages across \(S_t\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any robustness condition stated only in terms of the number of malicious identities constrains \(\alpha_t\), not necessarily the number of malicious physical principals.
Identity authentication enforcing \(|\pi^{-1}(p)|\le1\) removes Sybil multiplicity but does not by itself remove collusion.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require malicious messages to be identical; coordinated identities may submit distinct adaptive messages.
Data-objective poisoning is separate: this interface specifies control and coordination, not how local objectives or datasets are corrupted.
No inspected source locator was supplied that canonically defines this combined interface with the stated kernel and identity-to-principal map.

notation.meaning: Set of adversarially controlled protocol identities.
Map from a controlled identity to its physical principal.
History-conditioned joint kernel governing adversarial messages in round t.
Adversarial fractions measured by identities and physical participants, respectively.

review_flags: No inspected authoritative source supports the exact combined collusion–Sybil definition.
The mathematical interface is a precise candidate formalization of the blueprint role and requires source verification.
knowledge_statements.title: Collusion–Sybil Attack Interface
Colluding-Client Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Colluding clients coordinate their updates using shared state and randomness, so their joint behavior need not factor into independent client strategies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A colluding-client interface permits a controlled set \(B\) to choose its round-\(t\) messages jointly as \((u_i^t)_{i\in B}=\Phi_t(\mathcal H_t,S_t,\xi_t)\), where \(\mathcal H_t\) is the visible protocol history, \(S_t\) is shared private state, and \(\xi_t\) is joint randomness. Each component remains attached to a distinct registered client and must satisfy any declared per-client constraint. The defining feature is that the joint law need not factor across clients: \(P((u_i^t)_{i\in B}\mid\mathcal H_t)\ne\prod_{i\in B}P(u_i^t\mid\mathcal H_t)\) may hold.
assumptions_latex: A controlled set \(B\) can communicate privately or share state.
Each controlled client submits one protocol-visible update per round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Collusion allows the tuple \((u_i^t)_{i\in B}\) to follow an arbitrary joint strategy subject only to the declared per-client protocol constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-strategy interface for multiple distinct controlled clients with shared information.

notation.meaning: Shared colluder state before round t
Update of client i at round t

review_flags: No supplied locator formalizes colluding clients in distributed or federated optimization.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The joint-strategy formulation fits a colluding-client interface and is internally consistent, but no source supports this particular information, shared-state, randomness, and per-client-constraint model.

knowledge_statements.title: Sybil-Client Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Sybil attacker uses multiple apparent client identities, allowing one controller to submit several updates and accumulate identity-based aggregation weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Sybil-client interface exists when one adversarial principal controls \(k=|S|\ge2\) logical identities and may submit an update \(u_s^t\) under each \(s\in S\) during round \(t\). The server observes separate identities but does not observe their common controller. If aggregation assigns weights \(w_s^t\) by identity, the principal's direct aggregate contribution is \(\sum_{s\in S}w_s^t u_s^t\), rather than the contribution allowed to one physical principal. The interface must specify registration, participation, and weighting constraints; otherwise the effective adversarial weight is undefined.
assumptions_latex: One adversarial principal controls a set \(S\) of registered logical client identities.
The server treats identities as separate contributors unless an identity-control rule intervenes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Sybil interface permits one principal to submit the family \((u_s^t)_{s\in S}\) through multiple apparent clients and thereby acquire identity-dependent aggregation weight.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity-level attack interface in which one principal controls multiple apparent clients.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports a formal Sybil-client model for federated aggregation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition clearly separates logical identities from their common controller and correctly notes dependence on registration and weighting rules, but it lacks a source for the federated Sybil threat model.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinated Update Manipulation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Colluders can realize a target aggregate shift precisely when that shift belongs to the weighted Minkowski sum of their individually allowed update sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For aggregation weights \(w_i\ge0\), coordinated update manipulation toward \(b\in\mathbb R^d\) is feasible when the colluders can choose \(u_i\in U_i\) jointly so that \(\sum_{i\in B}w_i u_i=b\). Equivalently, \[b\in\sum_{i\in B}w_iU_i:=\left\{\sum_{i\in B}w_i v_i:v_i\in U_i\right\}.\] This condition captures aggregate coordination even when every individual update satisfies its local admissibility test. If only approximate manipulation is required, feasibility becomes \(\operatorname{dist}(b,\sum_{i\in B}w_iU_i)\le\varepsilon\) for the declared norm and tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: Colluding clients \(B\) submit vectors \(u_i\in\mathbb R^d\).
Each vector obeys a declared individual constraint \(u_i\in U_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A desired aggregate displacement \(b\) is coordinately realizable exactly when \(b\in\sum_{i\in B}w_iU_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-round feasibility condition for jointly producing a prescribed aggregate contribution.

notation.meaning: Allowed update set for client i

review_flags: No supplied locator establishes this coordinated-update feasibility model in an adversarial aggregation setting.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The weighted Minkowski-sum equivalence follows from the declared one-round model, and condition is an appropriate content kind. A source is still required to establish that this feasibility model represents coordinated adversarial update manipulation in the target context.

knowledge_statements.title: Identity-Multiplicity Effects
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under uniform identity averaging, duplicating one update across many identities increases its weight and can force the aggregate arbitrarily close to that update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let honest updates be \(h_1,\ldots,h_n\) and suppose one adversarial principal repeats \(v\in\mathbb R^d\) through \(k\) identities. Uniform identity averaging returns \[A_k=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^n h_j+kv}{n+k}.\] Hence the principal's coefficient is \(k/(n+k)\), whereas a single identity would receive coefficient \(1/(n+1)\). Moreover \(A_k\to v\) as \(k\to\infty\). Thus an aggregator that weights identities rather than authenticated principals is not invariant under identity replication, even when all repeated update vectors are unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The server averages updates uniformly by registered identity.
There are \(n\ge1\) honest identities and \(k\ge1\) identical Sybil identities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Duplicating one update \(v\) across \(k\) identities changes its aggregate coefficient from \(1/(n+1)\) to \(k/(n+k)\), approaching one as \(k\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact multiplicity effect under uniform identity-weighted mean aggregation.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports identity-multiplicity effects in federated aggregation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The uniform-averaging formula and limiting multiplicity effect are correct, and property fits the node. No citation supports the identity-replication model or its relevance to Sybil behavior in federated aggregation.

children.title: Distributed Optimization Metrics and Stopping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Observable optimization, agreement, feasibility, and saddle-progress measures.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) be distributed primal states, possibly accompanied by dual variables \(Y\), and let \(\mathcal T\) be the target solution set. Let \(Z=(X,Y,\xi)\) denote all locally held state and auxiliary transcript information available to a certification procedure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers optimization, agreement, feasibility, stationarity, and saddle-progress certificates; computability and soundness are separated from completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed accuracy certificate is a nonnegative observable map \(C:Z\mapsto[0,\infty]\) together with a target error map \(E:Z\mapsto[0,\infty]\) and a nondecreasing calibration \(\psi\) satisfying \(\psi(0)=0\), such that \(C(Z)\le\varepsilon\) implies \(E(Z)\le\psi(\varepsilon)\) for every admissible instance and state. The certificate is exact when \(C(Z)=0\) if and only if the certified primal-dual state belongs to \(\mathcal T\). It is distributedly evaluable when agents can compute or upper-bound \(C(Z)\) using the declared local observations and a finite specified aggregation protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed accuracy certificate is an observable nonnegative quantity whose small value guarantees a small true target error. Its calibration states precisely what accuracy follows from a threshold. Exactness means that zero certificate value characterizes the target solution set. Distributed evaluability requires an explicit finite protocol using available local information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall Z\ \forall\varepsilon\ge0:\quad C(Z)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow E(Z)\le\psi(\varepsilon),\qquad \psi(0)=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A vector certificate \((C_{\mathrm{opt}},C_{\mathrm{con}},C_{\mathrm{feas}},C_{\mathrm{stat}})\) may be scalarized as \(C=\max_j C_j/\eta_j\) for declared positive tolerances \(\eta_j\).
special_cases_latex: For consensus optimization, a certificate may combine objective suboptimality at an aggregate state with \(\max_i\|x_i-\bar x\|\), provided both terms are observable or validly upper-bounded.
For a convex-concave saddle problem, a restricted primal-dual gap can serve as \(C\) on the declared bounded test sets.
immediate_consequences_latex: A stopping rule \(C(Z^k)\le\varepsilon\) is sound for the calibrated target error.
Certificate evaluation itself may consume communication and must be included in complexity accounting when non-negligible.
boundary_notes: Objective error involving an unknown optimum value is not directly observable unless a computable bound or dual certificate is supplied.
A small consensus residual alone does not certify optimality, and a small local stationarity residual alone need not certify agreement or feasibility.
Completeness, meaning that every accurate state has a small certificate, is an additional property not implied by soundness.

notation.meaning: True target error controlled by the certificate.

review_flags: No inspected source locator supports this general calibrated-certificate definition across all listed certificate types.
knowledge_statements.title: Sound observable distributed accuracy certificate

children.title: Distributed Optimization Progress Metrics
children.top_down_role: Optimization-side progress measures.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), let \(F_\star=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)>-\infty\), and let \(z\) denote the distributed state from which a candidate \(x(z)\in X\) is decoded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic minimization; the definition separates optimization progress from consensus and constraint-feasibility errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An optimization-progress certificate system is a map \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}:\mathcal Z\to[0,+\infty]\), together with a declared tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\ge0\), such that \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}(z)\) is computable from the admitted state information and \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}(z)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\) implies a specified optimization condition. Canonical choices are the objective certificate \(C_{\mathrm{obj}}(z)=F(x(z))-F_\star\) and, when \(F\) is differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(X\), the stationarity certificate \(C_{\mathrm{stat}}(z)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\nabla F(x(z))+N_X(x(z)))\). The certificate is exact when \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}(z)=0\) holds exactly at globally optimal points for the objective form, or at first-order stationary points for the stationarity form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimization-progress certificate assigns a nonnegative residual to a distributed state and declares progress adequate when that residual is below a tolerance. The objective-gap form is the decoded candidate's objective value minus the optimal value. The stationarity form is the distance from zero to the gradient plus the feasible-set normal cone. Zero objective gap characterizes global optimality, whereas zero stationarity residual characterizes first-order stationarity in the stated smooth constrained regime. Consensus and feasibility violations are not included unless explicitly incorporated into the chosen residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}(z)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\) is the declared optimization-progress certificate, with the certified property determined by the selected residual.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For unconstrained smooth minimization, \(X=\mathbb R^d\) gives \(C_{\mathrm{stat}}(z)=\|\nabla F(x(z))\|\).
For convex \(F\), the exact subdifferential residual may be written \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial(F+\iota_X)(x(z)))\).
special_cases_latex: If a valid lower bound \(L\le F_\star\) is available, \(F(x(z))-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(F(x(z))-F_\star\le\varepsilon\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The objective-gap and stationarity certificates are distinct unless assumptions relate stationarity to global suboptimality.
boundary_notes: A stationarity residual does not by itself certify global optimality for a nonconvex objective.
The optimal value or a valid lower bound may be unavailable to individual agents.

Objective-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point and an independently verified lower bound certify epsilon objective accuracy when their objective-value difference is at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F^*=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^d}F(z)>-\infty\). A pair \((x,\ell)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-objective-gap certificate if \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\), \(\ell\) is independently verifiable with \(\ell\le F^*\), and \[F(x)-\ell\le\varepsilon.\] This certificate guarantees \[0\le F(x)-F^*\le\varepsilon.\] In a distributed implementation, \(F(x)\) must aggregate all objective components evaluated at the same candidate \(x\).
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) has finite optimal value \(F^*=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^d}F(z)\).
A point \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and an independently verifiable scalar lower bound \(\ell\le F^*\) are available.
The requested tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)-\ell\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow 0\le F(x)-F^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal objective-gap certificate based on an independently verifiable global lower bound; in a distributed implementation, all objective components must be evaluated at the same candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local gradients evaluated at one common point certify smooth stationarity when their average has norm at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive integers \(m,d\), differentiable functions \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), and \(F(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)\), define \[g(x)=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\nabla f_i(x)=\nabla F(x).\] A common point \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), together with the collected local gradients evaluated at \(x\), is an \(\varepsilon\)-smooth-stationarity certificate if \[\|g(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon.\] For \(\varepsilon=0\), this is the first-order stationary condition. Gradients evaluated at different local points do not constitute this certificate without an additional relation to a reported common point.
assumptions_latex: \(m,d\in\mathbb N\) are positive integers, each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable, and \(F=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\).
Every local gradient is evaluated at the same reported point \(x\in\mathbb R^d\).
The stationarity tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left\|m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\nabla f_i(x)\right\|_2\le\varepsilon\Longleftrightarrow\|\nabla F(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order stationarity certificate for an unconstrained smooth finite-sum objective at a common network point.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Mismatch Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without additional geometry, a vanishing gradient need not imply a small objective gap; arctangent supplies a concrete smooth counterexample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(f(x)=\arctan x\), so \(f'(x)=1/(1+x^2)\) and \(f^*=\inf_x f(x)=-\pi/2\). For \(x_k=k\), \[|f'(x_k)|=\frac1{1+k^2}\longrightarrow0,\qquad f(x_k)-f^*=\arctan(k)+\frac\pi2\longrightarrow\pi.\] Thus arbitrarily accurate smooth-stationarity certificates can coexist with an objective gap bounded away from zero. Converting stationarity into objective accuracy therefore requires additional structure, such as convexity together with suitable growth information, an error bound, or a Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality.
assumptions_latex: Stationarity is measured only by \(|f'(x)|\).
No convexity, error bound, or Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|f'(x_k)|\to0\) while \(f(x_k)-\inf_x f(x)\to\pi\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing that smooth stationarity alone does not certify global objective accuracy.
